title: Five Most Important Bills' Players to Watch vs. Ravens in Week 8
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are about to enter one of the most difficult stretches of their 2026 schedule over the next several weeks, and it begins with an ultra-important conference matchup at home against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1 at 1 p.m. ET.
Coming off a much-needed bye in Week 7 , the Bills will now look to capture their third win in a row in order to keep pace in the race for the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs later on in January.
Despite receiving some worrisome injury news elsewhere on the roster , Baltimore will finally get franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson back into the fold for Sunday’s road game versus Buffalo. It's expected to provide an obvious boost to a reeling Ravens’ squad that has dropped two straight games with Jackson on the sideline due to an injured left ankle.
Prior to his injury, Baltimore was sitting at 3-1 and looked to be a legitimate Super Bowl contender under first-year head coach Jesse Minter, but it’s up for debate now . . . especially with the way the rest of the AFC North division is shaking out at the current moment.
So, with that in mind, expect Jackson and the Ravens to be extra motivated in Western New York on Sunday afternoon to right the ship.
Here are five key Bills’ players who can help prevent that nightmare scenario from happening the day after Halloween.
Through four games of the 2026 NFL campaign, Bills’ sixth-year veteran outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau seemed to be destined for greatness within Buffalo’s new 3-4 scheme under first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard this season.
Leading the league in sacks and pressures at that point in time, the sky appeared to be the limit. However, since Buffalo’s unfortunate loss to quarterback Drake Maye and the New England Patriots in Week 5, the 6-foot-6, 266-pound pass-rusher has seemingly disappeared on defense.
Yes, Rousseau had a critical game-changing blocked field goal in the team’s victory on Monday Night Football against the Los Angeles Rams on October 12, but that’s about the only noticeable thing he’s done on the field over the last two games.
The once dominant defender in September has gone missing over the last several weeks, and it’s time that he’s found again.
With quarterback Lamar Jackson likely back in the lineup this week, it’ll be imperative that Buffalo’s defense get sustained pressure on Jackson while also keeping him from running outside of the pocket.
It’ll be easier said than done, but Rousseau’s incredible length can be an extreme barrier to get around, so he’ll need to use it to his advantage when coming off the edge on Jackson.
He’ll also need to continue being a stalwart up front against the running game and Derrick Henry, who is still sixth in the NFL right now in rushing with 579 yards on the ground despite being 32 years old.
Former top-10 pick Ed Oliver has had a rough couple of years for more reasons than one.
It seemed like Oliver was on the verge of a breakout year last season following a dominant performance against, ironically, the Ravens in Week 1, but injuries ultimately derailed his 2025 campaign.
Then, devastating personal matters and more aggravating injuries clouded his summer heading into his eighth season in the National Football League, and so far his fall production on the field definitely hasn’t been what some teammates thought was about to happen for Oliver coming out of training camp .
It’s undoubtedly been a blur given all of the outstanding circumstances surrounding Oliver this year, but hopefully he can manage to find his stride at some point this season.
The former University of Houston standout is capable of being a true game-wrecker when in the right state of health and frame of mind, and that type of player is exactly what Buffalo is searching for up on the defensive front alongside budding superstars Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau this season.
If Oliver can even contribute a single game-altering play, then it could be the difference between a win and a loss for the Bills against the Ravens on Sunday. Remember, Oliver’s forced fumble late in the fourth quarter of the 2025 season opener against Baltimore was the difference-maker last September.
A similar sequence of events could be what turns the tide in Buffalo’s favor once again this November.
Outside of maybe inside linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr, no other rookie made as much noise this offseason for Buffalo than former Ohio State standout cornerback Davison Igbinosun, who the team selected in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft in April.
And, now that summertime buzz has turned into a starting role for Igbinosun opposite fellow cornerback Christian Benford over the last several weeks within Jim Leonhard’s more man-heavy scheme.
It’s been an interesting development, and Igbinosun has been holding his own so far against opposing receivers as he leads the Bills and is tied for fifth in the NFL with seven pass breakups through six games according to StatMuse .
NFL Rookie Leader in Forced Incompletions This Season: 🌰 Davison Igbinosun, Bills: 7 @OhioStateFB pic.twitter.com/XMuLRtUQyM
Now, this weekend he’ll—at least sometimes—be faced with the challenge of covering speedy Ravens’ wideout Zay Flowers, who is currently first in the AFC and seventh in the NFL in receiving yards with 608 yards and three touchdowns on 40 receptions despite playing the last three weeks with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley throwing him the ball.
It’ll be a major test for whoever is lined up opposite of Flowers, and Igbinosun will have to be up for the task whenever he’s ultimately presented with the opportunity on Sunday afternoon.
Much like the aforementioned Lamar Jackson for Baltimore, wide receiver D.J. Moore has been sidelined recently as he was just forced to miss back-to-back games for the first time in his NFL career due to a shoulder ailment that he’s been dealing with since Week 2 this season.
Moore was limited in practice all week and is listed as questionable for the game, but it still appears as if he’ll be back in the starting lineup for the Bills on Sunday if all goes according to plan.
With that in mind, it’ll be important that he gets back to the type of player he was in Week 1 against the Houston Texans when he hauled in five catches on eight targets for 100 yards and a touchdown.
Quarterback Josh Allen can’t do it all on his own—even if he still tries to sometimes—and it’ll be important for other playmakers like Moore to step up in this critical AFC matchup with the Ravens, who are currently allowing the 12th fewest yards in the NFL to opposing offenses at just 317.4 yards per game.
The Allen-Moore connection needs to come alive, especially considering that Baltimore is surrendering just 220.9 yards per game through the air heading into the critical matchup, as well.
If Allen, Moore, and the rest of the passing offense aren’t able to get things going, then running back James Cook III and Co. will have to find a way to make it work on the ground.
Considering Baltimore is just as stingy versus the pass as the run, though, it might be tough sledding.
The Ravens have allowed just 96.6 rushing yards per game so far through seven weeks of the season, and the most that the defense has given up to a single runner this fall is 98 yards to both the Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor and the Dallas Cowboys’ Javonte Williams back in September.
Since then, however, the team held Atlanta Falcons’ running back Bijan Robinson—the NFL’s leading rusher entering this weekend’s slate of games—to just 86 yards and no touchdowns back on October 11, and no other individual runner has eclipsed the 41-yard mark since then.
Needless to say, it’ll be up to Cook III to create yardage with every crease he’s given in order to keep the offense on schedule.
Like previously mentioned above with veteran wideout D.J. Moore, quarterback Josh Allen will need some help from his teammates on that side of the ball in order to come out victorious against a stout defense like Baltimore…

title: Bills Replacing Suspended Safety CJ Gardner-Johnson With Old Reliable vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have a hole in their Week 8 starting lineup due to safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson's one-game suspension for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders' tight end Brock Bowers back on October 18.
Thankfully, the Bills' depth chart features a versatile backup with 28 career starts to his credit. As such, that experienced reserve will be the starter when Buffalo hosts the Baltimore Ravens for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on November 1.
"Damar Hamlin will start at safety," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady following Friday's practice in Orchard Park.
The 28-year-old Hamlin, who became a household name as a result of suffering cardiac arrest during a Monday Night Football game on January 2, 2023, has become part of the organizational fabric.
After playing out his rookie contract, Hamlin re-signed with the Bills on one-year deals each of the past two offseasons.
Hamlin, a 2021 sixth-round draft pick, has made 59 regular season appearances for Buffalo. He's also played in seven playoff games, including a 2024 AFC Divisional Round win over the Ravens. The safety accounted for eight tackles in that game highlighted by a strip sack of Lamar Jackson.
Coincidentally, Hamlin will see Jackson again on Sunday as the Ravens confirmed he'll start at quarterback after missing three consecutive games with an ankle sprain.
Although a pectoral injury limited Hamlin to six games in 2025, he has plenty of time on task with fellow safety Cole Bishop. Following Gardner-Johnson's ejection in Week 6, he stepped in to play alongside Bishop for the remainder of the 33-30 win.
Hamlin has appeared in all six games thus far this season, seeing 151 defensive snaps across multiple roles. He's been deployed as a third safety and a nickel defensive back in Jim Leonhard's scheme.
"We've had weeks where he didn't get any reps at nickel position, and he has to go in there and play nickel. He doesn't blink, and that's kind of his personality," said Brady.
Joining the Bills' staff in 2022, Brady has been around Hamlin for all but one season in the safety's pro career.
The rookie head coach has noticed the safety's willingness and ability to take reps all throughout the secondary this year.
"That's why Damar's been here. We brought him back here because of, he has a unique skillset. He can play a bunch of different positions. He knows what to do, and he plays winning football whenever he's in there. We got all the confidence in Damar," said Brady.
On Sunday against the Ravens, Hamlin will make his 29th career start for the Bills, and Brady's just fine with that.
"Really excited for him to get to play a lot of football this week," said Brady. "He's earned it. He deserves it, and he's gonna make the most of it."

title: Bills-Derwin James Trade Lands Among NFL's Best Deadline Proposals
full_text:
Sitting at 5-1, the Buffalo Bills are among the top contenders in the NFL this season. That said, they shouldn't be content with their roster, especially with other contenders making moves.
In the NFC, the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears both bolstered up their rosters with the Seahawks adding Quenton Nelson and the Bears bringing in Jeffery Simmons . Even the San Francisco 49ers made a move, bringing back DeForest Buckner.
While none of the AFC contenders have made a huge splash just yet, it's only a matter of time. One team to keep an eye on is the Kansas City Chiefs, who could be in the market for some help at receiver. With so many moves already taking place, and others expected, Buffalo general manager Brandon Beane must be proactive and address the team's struggling secondary.
One move that could not only help Buffalo, but would also be one of the best possible traded at the deadline, according to Vinnie Iyer of The Sporting News, would be adding Derwin James in a trade with the Los Angeles Chargers . As Iyer says, the Chargers need to be sellers at the deadline following their 0-6 start and James is a perfect fit for Jim Leonhard's defense.
"The Chargers are sellers with Jim Harbaugh after starting 0-6 and needing to move some veteran players to reboot their roster. If (Khalil) Mack is the top candidate, then James would be a close second," Iyer wrote.
"The do-everything star safety has given the team many great seasons when healthy. He would thrive as the clean-up playmaker in Buffalo's defensive scheme of Jim Leonhard, filling a huge positional need while playing for a former notable NFL safety."
James is a two-time First-Team All-Pro and a four-time Second-Team All-Pro. The 17th overall pick out of Florida State in 2018 has developed into one of the more complete safeties in the league and would be an instant upgrade in Buffalo, where their trio of safeties has struggled, especially in coverage.
The Chargers won't be interested in giving up James for nothing, especially considering he just signed a three-year extension worth $75 million this offseason . James is under contract through the 2029 and despite being 30 years old, he has not slowed down when he's on the field.
For that reason, the Chargers might ask for at least one early Day 2 pick, and with Buffalo typically selecting later in rounds, they would need to sweeten the pot with a conditional pick in 2028 based on playing time and team success.
That might sound like a lot for a player nearing the end of his career, but the Bills need to capitalize on their championship window and adding James does exactly that.

title: Bills' Friday Practice Update: Questions Remain for Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore vs. Ravens
full_text:
There's no guarantee that the Buffalo Bills will have two of their primary pass-catching weapons available when the Baltimore Ravens visit Highmark Stadium on November 1.
Although it's promising that both wide receiver DJ Moore and tight end Dalton Kincaid were present at practice for the third day in a row, there's still some uncertainty surrounding their availability come game time.
While briefly addressing reporters after Friday's practice, Bills' first-year head coach Joe Brady listed Moore and Kincaid amongst those players who are officially questionable for Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff.
After participating in a limited capacity on Wednesday and Thursday, both Moore and Kincaid were on the field again during Friday's media-viewing portion of practice. As has been the case, the two players wore red non-contact jerseys, likely more as a precaution than anything else.
As for the Ravens' offense, head coach Jesse Minter confirmed that quarterback Lamar Jackson will return to the starting lineup after missing three games due to an ankle issue .
Initially spraining his AC joint in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions, Moore reaggravated the injury in Week 4 against the New England Patriots.
Marking the end of his consecutive games streak at 91 regular season appearances,  Moore was scratched from the lineup in Weeks 5 and 6 after carrying a questionable tag on the official injury report.
"The two weeks [out], it was pretty sad. I was mad at myself," said Moore on Wednesday . "Somebody put out a post on X where I was standing there watching the guys practice, that was the hardest thing about the two weeks."
With additional rest and recovery time from the Week 7 bye, Moore appears eager to return, and the Bills' offense would obviously love to have him against the Ravens.
"Obviously, we know the importance that he brings to our football team, to our offense, the toughness, the playmaking ability. It'll be nice to get him back out on the football field today," said Brady prior to Wednesday's practice.
While Moore has only 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown, his presence opens up more possibilities for the offense.
Kincaid popped up on injury report this week coming off the bye due to a chest issue. He was banged up last time out against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, but was able to finish the game.
Following a third-quarter red zone play, Kincaid was seen grabbing at his torso in apparent discomfort. He went to the locker room for evaluation, and returned as the Bills took possession with 8:01 remaining in the fourth quarter.
“Feeling good. Just how football goes. Some weeks will be worse than others, and then some weeks will feel great. But lucky and grateful enough to be able to go out there and practice," said Kincaid after Wednesday's practice (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
It seems as if the benefit of the bye week may prevent Kincaid from missing any games.
"Extra week's great. Great for everybody, honestly. Just mental, physical reset," said Kincaid, who sounded as if he intends to play.
Catching 23 of 29 targets this season, Kincaid currently leads the Bills with 315 receiving yards.

title: Bills Can't Catch Break Based on Latest Lamar Jackson Injury News
full_text:
Lamar Jackson suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 4 and has missed the past three games for the Baltimore Ravens. With the Buffalo Bills set to host Baltimore in Week 8 , Jackson's status had been up in the air leading to the weekend.
That no longer appears to be the case as all signs are pointing to Jackson being on the field against the Bills.
On Thursday, Bills On SI writer Mike Moraitis noted that Jackson was a full participant for Baltimore in practice. On Friday, he was again listed as a full participant, and then head coach Jesse Minter made it clear that they expect to see him in action on Sunday.
"We do think we'll have Lamar this week so we can go ahead and put that out there. I'm excited about that. He's had a really good week of practice. It probably ended up showing that he was full in all three days," Minter said while speaking with reporters on Friday .
"So excited about that opportunity for him to be back out again. A credit to him and the work that he put in dealing with an injury, put himself in position to be back. So that's obviously exciting for our team and open up for questions."
Jackson last faced Buffalo in Week 1 of the 2025 season, in one of the more exciting games of the year. The former NFL MVP threw for 209 yards with two touchdown passes and rushed for another 70 yards and a touchdown.
He led the Ravens to a 34-19 lead going into the fourth quarter, but Josh Allen and the Buffalo offense scored 22 points in the final 15 minutes, stealing a 41-40 win thanks to a 32-yard field goal from Matt Prater with no time remaining.
Buffalo is dealing with some injuries of their own, with DJ Moore and Ed Oliver both up in the air. Neither player has been on the field since their Oct. 4 loss to the New England Patriots, but they're trending in the right direction this week .
Moore has been dealing with a shoulder injury, while Oliver has been battling a knee issue. Both players took advantage of the bye week to get some extra rest and could be in action this weekend.
There are some concerns, however, for Spencer Brown who has been dealing with a back injury and has missed multiple practices this week. Dee Alford was limited in practice as well, with an ankle injury giving him some problems.

title: Ranking Buffalo Bills' Biggest NFL Trade Deadline Needs Under Two Weeks Left
full_text:
We are roughly two weeks from the 2026 NFL trade deadline and while the Buffalo Bills aren't seen as an overly aggressive team when it comes to the deadline, general manager Brandon Beane should be willing to make some moves.
Buffalo is considered one of the elite contenders this season, but other teams in line for a title run aren't sitting idly by. The Seattle Seahawks added Quenton Nelson to shore up their defensive line, the Chicago Bears went for a home run with defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons , and even the San Francisco 49ers improved by bringing back DeForest Buckner.
The Bills still have the talent to contend, but they need to take a page from these other teams and address some of their biggest concerns. That said, here's a look at the top four most pressing needs that Beane should be actively looking to fill.
Greg Rousseau was off to a hot start, with six sacks in the first three games of the season. Unfortunately, he's been silenced over the past three games and has been held without a sack. In fact, the pass rush as a whole has been quiet since Rousseau's explosiveness went away.
Buffalo enters Week 8 with 11 total sacks and other than Rousseau, no player has more than Bradley Chubb's 1.5. The Bills did use their first pick in the 2026 NFL draft (which was in Round 2) on T.J. Parker, but he hasn't provided a major spark. He still has plenty of upside, but they need someone who can give them a lift now, which makes outside linebacker a priority.
More concerning that outside linebacker, however, is the inside linebacker position in Buffalo. Dorian Williams is their highest-rated inside linebacker, according to PFF , earning a 64.6 through the first six games of the season. Terrel Bernard, on the other hand, is sitting at a 53.9. That's far better than rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr, who has a 40.8 currently.
The concern is whether or not the Bills will admit this is a problem. They signed Shaq Thompson to the practice squad, but have yet to activate him for a regular season game . They seem committed to Williams and Bernard, and given Bernard's salary, they might not be willing to admit there's an issue.
That doesn't mean they shouldn't add some help, because this remains one of the more problematic positions on their entire defense.
The recent signing of Tre'Davious White gives the Bills some insurance at cornerback, but that doesn't solve all their isses. While White played well for them in 2025, he was returning to a defensive scheme he knew well under Sean McDermott. Now, he joins a defense led by Jim Leonhard and as we saw when he played for the Los Angeles Rams and Baltimore Ravens in 2024, White wasn't the same without McDermott.
That doesn't mean he can't find success under Leonhard, but the Bills can't count on him to be the one to save this underperforming group. Instead, they should be actively looking for someone who can not only help now, but perhaps allow them to move on completely from Maxwell Hairston, who has gone completely into Leonhard's doghouse .
Even before C.J. Gardner-Johnson's recent suspension for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers, there were already reasons to be concerned with him. Gardner-Johnson can come up with some big plays, like when he had the interception against the Los Angeles Chargers, but he also has some big whiffs, including his two missed tackles against the Raiders before losing his cool.
What's worse is his attitude. Not only did he spit at a player, but he refused to admit he did and gave one of the worst excuses afterward , saying it was all about being competitive.
Outside of Gardner-Johnson, Buffalo is leaning heavily on Cole Bishop and Damar Hamlin, and neither are playing particularly well this season. Hamlin has the highest PFF grade of 59.1, while Bishop is struggling with a 51.3. Gardner-Johnson is in the middle, with a 55.2. Simply put, none have been living up to expectations, especially in coverage. That's a huge reason why Buffalo is currently 31st in the league in pass defense.
There are players available, with Amani Hooker of the Tennessee Titans standing out as the best option in coverage, but Beane has to be willing to pull the trigger. If he does nothing else at this deadline, adding someone who can play deep coverage would be a massive win for the Buffalo defense.

title: Rookie Defender Has Been Bright Spot in Panthers' Latest Rollercoaster Season
full_text:
On Thursday night at Lambeau Field, the Carolina Panthers fell below the .500 mark with a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Dave Canales’s club couldn’t slow down Matt LaFleur’s one-dimensional offense. While the worst ground game in the league was held under 100 yards for the eighth time in as many games, the Panthers had no answers for Packers’ quarterback Jordan Love.
Green Bay’s signal-caller hit on 30-of 41 throws for 288 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Carolina’s pass rush finished with zero sacks and zero quarterback hits, and defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero was fired by the team on Friday.
Intercepted by Zakee Wheatley ‼️ CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vOUDlt94xC
As for that one interception, it was the first of his NFL career for Panthers’ rookie safety Zakee Wheatley. Per Pro Football Focus, only Green Bay’s Evan Williams (90.6) has a higher grade at the position than Carolina’s second pick (89.8) in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL draft. The former Nittany Lion has excelled in pass coverage and is PFF’s No. 3 safety in this facet with an 83.4 grade, behind only Williams (90.1) and Seattle’s Julian Love (85.4).
Although Wheatley was inactive for the season-opener against the Bears, he has played in each of the past six games and made four starts. He ranks sixth on the club with 25 defensive stops (18 solo), one forced fumble, Thursday night’s interception of Jordan Love, and four passes defensed. He also recorded a solo tackle on special teams.
In the loss to the Packers, the five starting members of Carolina’s secondary were cornerbacks Marco Wilson (his first game with the team) and rookie Will Lee III, as well as safeties Wheatley, Nick Scott, and Tre’von Moehrig.
Wilson led the club with eight tackles, while Wheatley and linebacker Devin Lloyd were tied for second with seven stops. It marked the fifth time in six games that the 24-year-old rookie totaled at least four defensive stops in a contest.
There are certain aspects of Carolina’s defense that have improved from a year ago. Of course, the back end of this unit has certainly been hamstrung by the absences of veteran cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. And with pass-rusher Jaelan Phillips out the last two games, the Panthers failed to come up with a sack in each of those contests.
Still, Wheatley has stood out this season and looks like a Day 3 steal, which may not be a total surprise considering some post-draft evaluations of Dan Morgan’s 2026 draft class.

title: Ikem Ekwonu's Value Keeps Rising While Panthers Wait for Return
full_text:
Ikem Ekwonu hasn't played a snap for the Panthers this season, and I think I've appreciated him a little more every week he's been out. I definitely did after watching Carolina's offensive line against Tampa Bay and Green Bay.
Ekwonu is still working his way back from the torn patellar tendon he suffered against the Los Angeles Rams in January. Carolina signed Rasheed Walker after four seasons in Green Bay and put him at left tackle while Ekwonu recovered. So far, that hasn't gone very well.
Tampa Bay was probably the worst of it. Walker gave up three sacks and seven pressures, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Young didn't have much time to get comfortable that afternoon, and the Panthers ended up losing 43-13.
Four days later, Young was running around again. Green Bay pressured him on 48.9% of his dropbacks and sacked him six times. Walker was out there for all 73 offensive snaps against his old team.
Through seven games, Walker has allowed 30 pressures and four sacks, according to Core Football Labs. He's also been called for six penalties. I've seen enough to know Carolina needs better play at left tackle.
I'm not putting all of the problems up front on Walker. Taylor Moton is out for the season, Damien Lewis didn't play Thursday and Corey Bullock hurt his quad during the game. This line looks a lot different from the one Carolina expected to have, but Walker hasn't helped much either.
Dave Canales gave an update this week and said Ekwonu is “trending in the right direction.” He's doing more individual work now, which is good to hear considering the injury he's coming back from.
Canales isn't ready to have somebody go at him full speed yet, and I'm fine with that. A torn patellar tendon isn't something I'd mess around with just because the offensive line has struggled for a couple of weeks. The Panthers have already gone this long without Ekwonu.
Carolina also has some extra time before Denver comes to Charlotte on Nov. 8. Maybe Ekwonu is ready by then and maybe he isn't. I sure wouldn't mind seeing No. 79 again soon, but there's no reason to put him out there before he's ready.
Ekwonu has frustrated me plenty since Carolina took him sixth overall in 2022. His pass protection hasn't always been where it needs to be, and I've wondered at times whether the Panthers had their long-term answer at left tackle. I haven't wondered nearly as much lately.
Young has been under pressure on half of his dropbacks over the last two games. That number was 39.4% before this stretch, and his yards per attempt under pressure has fallen from 6.2 to 3.2. Watching Young deal with that much pressure has made Ekwonu's absence pretty noticeable.
Putting Ekwonu back at left tackle isn't going to fix the entire offensive line. Moton isn't walking back through the door this season, and we don't know what the group will look like by the time Denver gets here. I just know I'd rather have Ekwonu protecting Young's blind side right now.
Seven games without him have changed my mind quite a bit.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Overreaction? The Panthers' Season May Already Be Over
full_text:
Five days ago, the Panthers were 3-2 and had Tampa Bay coming to Charlotte. The Buccaneers had won one game, and I thought Carolina had a pretty good chance to get to 4-2 before heading to Green Bay four days later.
Well, that went about as bad as it could've gone. Tampa Bay beat Carolina 43-13, and the Panthers followed that with a 27-19 loss at Green Bay. They're 3-4 now, and I'll admit I'm looking at the rest of this season a lot differently than I was a week ago.
The Green Bay loss isn't the one that gets me. Carolina was on the road four days after getting beat up by Tampa Bay, and the Packers are a good football team. The Panthers actually did some things I liked in that game.
They held Josh Jacobs to 39 yards on 21 carries. That was nice to see after Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards Sunday. Chuba Hubbard had another good night with 119 yards from scrimmage, and Carolina took the ball away three times.
Getting three points off those turnovers is what hurts. Carolina had the ball three extra times and couldn't turn any of them into a touchdown. Young also took six sacks, and Green Bay eventually put the game away.
Tampa Bay is harder for me to explain. The Panthers were at home against a 1-5 team and got beat by 30. If Carolina ends up a game short of winning the division or getting into the playoffs, I have a feeling we're going to remember that one.
I've watched Young throw for 329 yards against Detroit this season. He had 287 against Atlanta, and a few weeks later he threw for 281 against Philadelphia. We haven't seen much of that lately.
Thursday was rough. Young threw for 209 yards and took plenty of hits while trying to get the ball out. Six of those plays ended with him on the ground.
Carolina doesn't have its normal offensive line out there right now. Taylor Moton is on injured reserve. Damien Lewis wasn't available against Green Bay, and then Corey Bullock hurt his quad during the game.
I had the offensive line on my list after Thursday's loss . The Panthers have more than a week before Denver, so we'll see who they can get back by then.
Hubbard hasn't been the problem. He ran for 81 yards and a touchdown Thursday and added 38 more through the air. I'd keep throwing it to him too, especially if Young is going to have defenders in his face that often.
Denver is up first on Nov. 8. Carolina gets New Orleans after that before Baltimore comes to Charlotte. The Panthers will see Tampa Bay again at the end of November.
December isn't exactly empty either. Minnesota and Pittsburgh are both on there, and Seattle comes to Charlotte a few days before Christmas.
Maybe I'm putting too much into two bad games. Carolina has played well this season, and I've seen enough from this team to know Thursday night isn't necessarily what we're going to get every week.
But 3-4 doesn't leave much room to keep finding out.
The Panthers still have their division games, which is probably the best thing they have going for them right now. They'll get another shot at Tampa Bay, and they haven't played New Orleans yet. Atlanta comes at the end of the season.
I'm looking at Denver first. Get that one and you're 4-4 with New Orleans coming up. Lose it and you're sitting at 3-5.
I'm not ready to call the season over.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Panthers Stock Report: Chuba Hubbard Rises, Bryce Young Falls After Packers Loss
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers didn't have much time to figure out what went wrong against Tampa Bay before turning around and playing Green Bay four days later. There were some things I liked Thursday night, but not enough of them as Carolina left Green Bay with a 27-19 loss.
The run defense was much better, and Chuba Hubbard had another good game. Bryce Young and the passing game struggled for the second straight week, and the offensive line had a hard time keeping Green Bay out of the backfield. The Panthers also forced three turnovers and somehow got only three points out of them.
Here's where I have the Panthers' stock after Thursday night.
Hubbard was good again Thursday night. He carried it 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown and caught seven passes for another 38 yards. That's 119 yards from scrimmage on 29 touches.
The seven catches are what caught my attention. Young was under pressure for much of the night, and there wasn't much happening downfield, so Hubbard gave him another option. I wrote about Carolina using Hubbard more as a receiver during the game , and I hope we see more of it.
I was a little worried about this matchup after Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards against Carolina on Sunday. Going from that to facing Josh Jacobs four days later didn't exactly look like a great situation for the Panthers.
Jacobs ended up with only 39 yards on 21 carries, and Green Bay had 66 rushing yards as a team. He scored twice, including once as a receiver, but Carolina didn't let him beat them on the ground.
Green Bay had plenty of success throwing the ball, especially to Christian Watson. I'm not giving the entire defense a pass here. But considering what Bucky Irving and Tampa Bay did four days earlier, I'll take what Carolina did against Jacobs.
I've liked what we've seen from Wheatley, and Thursday gave us another reason. He picked off Jordan Love in the fourth quarter for the first interception of his NFL career and gave Carolina another possession with a chance to get back into the game.
According to the Panthers' postgame numbers , Wheatley is one of five rookies in franchise history with an interception and a forced fumble through his first six games. With all the injuries in Carolina's secondary, we're probably going to see a lot more of him.
Young finished 23-of-41 for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He made a nice throw to Jalen Coker for a 26-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, but before that there wasn't much happening in the passing game.
The protection wasn't good, so I'm not putting everything on Young. There were still throws he missed, and on a few of the sacks he held onto the football too long. I gave him a C- in my postgame report card , and I'm still right around there.
We've seen Young play a lot better than this. He threw for 329 yards against Detroit, 287 against Atlanta and 281 against Philadelphia. I expected something closer to that after the Tampa Bay game, and we didn't get it.
Six sacks and nine quarterback hits aren't going to work. Green Bay pressured Young on 48.9% of his dropbacks, and there were several plays where he didn't have much time to do anything.
Carolina is pretty beat up up front right now. Taylor Moton is on injured reserve, Damien Lewis missed the Green Bay game and Corey Bullock left with a quad injury. Jake Curhan ended up playing left guard after being elevated from the practice squad.
The Panthers have some time before Denver, and hopefully that helps get a couple of guys back. I already had the offensive line on my list of things Carolina needed to work on . Watching Young get sacked six times didn't change anything for me.
This is the one that bothers me.
Carolina forced three Green Bay turnovers and got three points out of them. Jackson Kuwatch forced a fumble on the opening kickoff, Nick Scott forced another one in the second quarter and Wheatley picked off Love in the fourth.
The Panthers lost by eight. I'm not saying Carolina scores a touchdown every time Green Bay turns it over, but getting three extra possessions and coming away with three points isn't good enough. One touchdown on any of those possessions could have made the fourth quarter a lot more interesting.
Carolina is 3-4 and doesn't play again until Nov. 8 against Denver. After playing twice in five days, the Panthers have some time to get healthy and figure out what they want to change before then.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Dan Orlovsky Disagrees With Panthers Firing Ejiro Evero, But He's Wrong
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers made the surprising decision to fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday, hours after the Panthers fell to the Green Bay Packers. It is surprising not because it wasn't warranted, but because the Panthers had previously not shown that they cared enough to do something.
Firing Evero was warranted. Too many times, his players didn't look ready to play . Too many times, his decision-making boggled the mind and led to success for the opposing offense. And far too many times, some aspect of his defense completely fell off.
Dan Orlovsky couldn't believe the news, but we could.
Dan Orlovsky, former NFL quarterback turned analyst for ESPN, was in shock when he learned that the Panthers had fired Ejiro Evero. Perhaps he was a little surprised by the timing after a decent defensive outing, but this was coming after Sunday's loss to Tampa Bay.
Really surprised by this. Injuries were a huge issue—good coach https://t.co/0Ik0oGPfAK
He captioned his tweet with a claim that Evero is a "really good coach," and on ESPN, he said, "That's a good coach, man. Ejiro is a very good coach, very good coach. They're beat up in the secondary, he's a very good coach." This was after a mouth-agape stare in shock for a few seconds.
Evero is well-respected across the NFL, but there are no tangible results one can point to to back Orlovsky's point up. Evero was a good coach in Denver, which is why the Panthers poached him, and he was decent in 2023, which is why Dave Canales kept him around.
The production just wasn't there. In 2024, they set a record for the most points allowed in NFL history. In 2025, they were middle-of-the-pack in yards and points, but they had bad success rates and other advanced analytics.
This year, after bringing in Devin Lloyd, Jaelan Phillips, Bobby Okereke, Lee Hunter, Zakee Wheatley, and Will Lee, production was both too inconsistent and not good enough on the better days.
Injuries have played a role, but injuries aren't why Evero couldn't time a blitz right or get home with any amount of rushers. Injuries aren't why the defense forgot how to tackle or where to play every other week.
This was supposed to be a top-10 unit. If you'd told someone before Week 1 that the Panthers would be tied for first on October 30, they would've believed that hyped defense had delivered. It hasn't.
The defense is bottom-10 in yards per game, third-worst in rushing yards per game (bolstered by the Green Bay Packers' 32nd-ranked rushing attack), and sixth-worst in points per game.
And at some point, injuries or not, someone has to be accountable for the miscues on defense. That is, more often than not, the coordinator.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Todd Wash is Interim DC. Here are 3 Other Options Panthers Should Consider This Offseason
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are making changes after a 3-4 start to the season, firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero along with pass game coordinator Jonathon Cooley.
This comes less than 12 hours after Carolina lost its second straight game , showing lapses in defensive coverage and poor playcalling on that side of the ball. This move had to be made; the Panthers' defense has been a complete letdown when it was supposed to be the team's strength.
Even when fully healthy, Carolina was embarrassed against the Chicago Bears in Week 1, and only performed well against Deshaun Watson, and backup QBs Tanner McKee and Cooper Rush.
Now that Evero is gone, Carolina has an interim defensive coordinator. The Panthers hired Todd Wash in 2023 under former head coach Frank Reich. Wash has 20 years of coaching experience in the NFL, and 31 years of coaching experience total.
Before coming to Carolina, Wash spent time with the Detroit Lions and previously had a long stint with the Jacksonville Jaguars before that. He's coached elite players such as Aidan Hutchinson and Calais Campbell.
With a long resume to his name already, Wash will have a shot at earning the official defensive coordinator job. However, if he doesn't, then here are three names to watch in the offseason.
Scott is the defensive backs coach and defensive pass game coordinator for the Seattle Seahawks. Seattle has been one of, if not the best, defenses in the NFL for the last two seasons, and the elite secondary has been a huge piece of that.
Scott joined Seattle in 2022, which was Dave Canales' final season with the franchise before heading to Tampa Bay, so there is some familiarity.
Edwards has experience as a defensive coordinator, having served as the DC for the Minnesota Vikings, Washington Redskins, and Buffalo Bills.
Edwards is in his fourth season with the Buccaneers, currently serving as the pass game coordinator. Like Karl Scott, Edwards spent a single season with Canales. In Canales' lone season with Tampa Bay, Edwards coached the outside linebackers, so he's versatile in where he can coach on defense, and Carolina's pass rush right now looks awful based on Thursday night.
Another pass game coordinator, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, would be the dream candidate, but he'll be interviewing for head coaching jobs, not coordinator jobs.
That said, the Vikings' defense is rolling on all cylinders, and Gerald Alexander is a focal point of that staff. Minnesota currently ranks second in the NFL in pass defense, surrendering just 155 yards per game.
Alexander also has a connection to the Panthers, and it's not with Dave Canales. Alexander played for Carolina for less than a full season in 2010. As a player, he had a journeyman career, but as a coach, he's one of the league's more intriguing young options.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: 4 Players Who Will Feel the Impact of Ejiro Evero's Absence, Both Good and Bad
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers fired Ejiro Evero from his role as defensive coordinator . Pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley went with him. The change was a long time coming , and Evero did not do anything to justify more time.
However, whenever someone is fired, there are ramifications, both good and bad. Some players will benefit from a new coordinator. Others will not.
Both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are excellent cornerbacks, but Horn in particular is elite at press man coverage. He is supremely physical, so not having a coordinator who wants him to play off in a zone is going to be a huge change, and probably a really good one.
Of course, there is the caveat that Horn is on IR right now, but when he comes back, we expect he will do a little better (he was already good) with a different coordinator who might be willing to adjust to the strength of his players more often.
Ejiro Evero's 3-4 scheme was good for Devin Lloyd, who was thriving under the coordinator. The former All-Pro can succeed with anyone, but Evero was able to help bring out the best in Lloyd both in coverage and as a run defender.
We will still see him all over the field, but the importance of inside linebackers will be diluted a bit with a new coordinator. Lloyd and Bobby Okereke might not have as much production, though that doesn't mean they're worse players now.
Whether or not the Panthers will adopt a 4-3 under Todd Wash remains to be seen, but regardless, Derrick Brown is in line to perform better with Wash being elevated and taking over for Ejiro Evero. Wash was the defensive line coach, and last night, the line was actually really good in run defense, and Brown had a breakout game.
Brown has always been good, but he hasn't always thrived in Evero's system. He did make a Pro Bowl under Evero, but he had a few really excellent seasons before Evero arrived in 2023. Look for Brown to return to form soon.
When Jaelan Phillips comes back, he might be in for a very different role. Obviously, he's still going to rush the passer and set the edge, but a 3-4 system like the one Evero used is often much more favorable for edge rushers. They get more creative ways to get into the backfield.
Phillips was playing just fine under Evero, although the bar for him after a $120 million contract is much higher than that. Still, if the system changes at all, we could be looking at an even more frustrating pass rush from Phillips.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Panthers Fire Ejiro Evero After Offseason Spending Failed to Build a Top-10 Defense
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have finally moved on from defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero . After three seasons and change, the Panthers are making a change. They allowed 27 points to the Green Bay Packers after allowing 43 on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Sources: Panthers are letting go of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero.
Evero was signed in 2023 and survived the culling of the Frank Reich era, but the results never manifested. Well-regarded, the Panthers continued to try to put good personnel on the field for Evero, but it didn't work out.
After spending a ton on defense in the offseason, the Panthers' defense has been a mess, and Evero's decision-making is right in the middle of that.
The additions of Bobby Okereke, Devin Lloyd, and Jaelan Phillips were supposed to transform this unit into a top-10 group. Phillips has been hurt and the cornerback depth chart is now down to the fifth and sixth players.
Injuries have certainly played a role, but too often, Evero's units were not prepared to play. In Week 1, they were demolished by the Chicago Bears' rushing attack after having all offseason to prepare.
The only good performances this defense has in 2026 are against Cooper Rush, Deshaun Watson, and Tanner McKee. That is not exactly a who's who of quarterbacks.
In Week 7, the Panthers allowed over 250 rushing yards for the second time this season. We suspected that was the final nail in the coffin, but a short week meant they couldn't install a new defensive coordinator until now.
Then, the Panthers had some truly inexplicable mistakes on defense during another loss to the Green Bay Packers. Evero had his fifth and sixth string cornerbacks on the field on third and 13 and dialed up an all-out blitz.
Even if that had worked, it would've led to a field goal, so dropping back into coverage to make the stop would've been safer and smarter. Instead, the Packers scored a touchdown on the play. In an eight-point loss, that kind of swing looms large.
Later, on third-and-two to essentially ice the game, the Packers were likely to pass since Jordan Love was playing so well against practice squad cornerbacks and the run game wasn't working, so Evero left his cornerbacks almost 10 yards off the line in zone coverage, and the Packers converted.
BREAKING: Ejiro Evero has been relieved of his duties as the Panthers defensive coordinator, along with defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley, per the team. DL Coach Todd Wash has been elevated to interim DC, will call plays.
Going with Evero is defensive pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. The Panthers are elevating Todd Wash, the defensive line coach, to interim coordinator.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: 4 Things the Panthers Have to Fix With Extra Time After Packers Loss
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers could probably use a few days where they don't have to play football.
They just played twice in five days, lost both games and picked up a few more injuries Thursday night against Green Bay. Now they don't play again until Nov. 8 against Denver, and the timing of the break isn't bad for a team that suddenly has a lot to figure out.
Carolina looked like it was starting to put some things together a couple of weeks ago. After what we've watched against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, I'm not so sure anymore. Here are four things I'd spend some time on before the Panthers play again.
I don't know how many more cornerbacks Carolina can lose. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are already on injured reserve, and the Panthers placed Akayleb Evans on IR before the Green Bay game. Then Will Lee III injured his hamstring Thursday night and had to be carted to the locker room.
That left Chau Smith-Wade, Marco Wilson and Malcolm DeWalt IV as the three healthy corners by the end of the game. DeWalt was making his NFL debut, and Green Bay took advantage of a secondary that was running out of people. Jordan Love threw for 288 yards and three touchdowns, while Christian Watson caught eight passes for 113 yards.
I know Carolina can't just go find another Jaycee Horn sitting at home somewhere, but I'd be surprised if the Panthers don't at least look around over the next week. They need bodies at this point, especially if Lee is going to miss any time.
Carolina isn't in much better shape up front. The Panthers placed Taylor Moton on injured reserve after the Tampa Bay game, Damien Lewis missed Thursday with a knee injury and Corey Bullock left against Green Bay with a quad injury. Jake Curhan ended up at left guard after being elevated from the practice squad.
Bryce Young was sacked six times, and there were a few plays where it felt like Green Bay was on him almost immediately. Young held onto the football too long on some of them, so I'm not putting all six sacks on the offensive line. Still, it's hard to get much going when you're moving guys around up front and your quarterback is getting hit that often.
Getting Lewis back would help. Moton is going to be out for a while, so there's not much Carolina can do about that right now, but I'd like to see the Panthers come out of the extra time with some idea of what they want the offensive line to look like against Denver.
Carolina scored 30 points against Detroit, 34 against Atlanta and then went into Philadelphia and scored 25. It wasn't perfect, but I thought we were starting to see what this offense could look like when Young was playing well and Carolina stayed balanced.
Then the last two games happened. The Panthers scored 13 against Tampa Bay and 19 against Green Bay, and Thursday was especially frustrating because the defense kept giving the offense chances. Green Bay turned the ball over three times, and Carolina got only three points out of those possessions.
Some of it is the offensive line. Some of it is Young, who hasn't played particularly well the last two games. There also haven't been enough plays downfield, and at times it feels like Carolina has to work way too hard just to pick up a first down.
If I'm Dave Canales, I'm going back and looking at what was working against Detroit, Atlanta and Philadelphia and comparing it to what we're seeing now. This offense shouldn't look this different a couple of weeks later.
I liked what Carolina did with Chuba Hubbard on Thursday. Hubbard carried it 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown, but what stood out to me was the seven catches for 38 yards. He finished with 29 touches and 119 yards from scrimmage on a night when Carolina didn't have much else working.
I especially liked seeing him used more in the passing game. Young was getting pressured and there wasn't much happening downfield, so Hubbard gave him somewhere to go with the football instead of waiting for something to open up. Seven catches might be more than he'll normally have, but there's no reason Carolina can't keep using him that way.
Hubbard doesn't need 29 touches every week. The Panthers just need to make sure one of their most dependable offensive players doesn't disappear from the game plan when things aren't going well.
Carolina is 3-4 after losing twice in five days, and the Panthers look a lot different than they did after going into Philadelphia and beating the Eagles . Injuries have certainly played a part in that, and having to turn around and play Green Bay four days after Tampa Bay didn't help.
This time, they have more than four days to figure some of it out.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: 3 Major Takeaways from Panthers' Frustrating Loss to Packers
full_text:
While it wasn't a 30-point blowout, the Carolina Panthers lost in frustrating fashion once again. Thursday Night Football ended with the Green Bay Packers securing a 27-19 victory . The score is a bit deceiving, as the Packers controlled most of the night.
This is Carolina's second straight loss, moving the Panthers to 3-4, and tying them for first place with the Atlanta Falcons. So far, the NFC South is shaping up like many thought it would: a tightly contested division with no team having a winning record.
The game was ugly for Carolina; the offense was ineffective for most of the night after initially taking a 10-6 lead in the first half.
Two weeks can make a world of difference. The Panthers were riding high after winning two in a row against the Lions and Eagles, but now the team has major questions to answer.
Here are three big takeaways from the TNF loss.
Another game, and another injury to the Panthers' secondary. Carolina is literally on their last legs with this room; the injuries have now piled up more than anyone could've imagined. The Panthers' secondary injuries are as follows
Jaycee Horn: IR, torn quad
Akayleb Evans: IR, tricep, knee
Will Lee III: exited game vs. Packers, hamstring
There's still no timetable for Jackson or Horn's return, and Evans got placed on IR this week, so he'll be out for at least four weeks.
Will Lee III has been decent for the Panthers in an elevated role, showing flashes of what he can be long term with great coverage and denial. However, Carolina may not see him on the field soon, as he hurt his hamstring while trying to cover Packers WR Christian Watson.
Carolina needs to make a trade for a veteran corner; it doesn't have to be a star like Sauce Gardner, just someone who can step in and be reliable.
Young finished the night completing 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards, 1 touchdown, and 1 interception. Those aren't good numbers , but anyone who watched the game won't blame Young for struggling.
Against the Packers, Young was sacked 6 times. Furthermore, Young was pressured on 22 dropbacks, which ties his career high. The offensive line is banged up with Taylor Moton and Damien Lewis out, but this is still inexcusable considering how good Young has been when protected.
Rasheed Walker and Monroe Freeling have been major disappointments, especially Walker, who was elite in pass coverage in 2025 and allowed just five sacks.
Obviously, there are injuries. Carolina was without Jaelan Phillips on Thursday night, and has been without Nic Scourton all season.
With the injuries, the pass rush remains awful. The Panthers recorded zero sacks and zero QB hits on Thursday night. No scenario exists where Jordan Love has a clean pocket all game and the Panthers still win; it just can't happen, especially with how banged up the secondary is.
Carolina needs Phillips back sooner rather than later. Creating more pressure will help the defense in some capacity against other great QBs the Panthers will see this season.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: What Jeffery Simmons’ Opening Statement Says About Bears Trade
full_text:
Jeffery Simmons clearly understands the "why" behind the Chicago Bears landing the star defensive tackle and a 2028 fifth-round pick for a 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick, and 2027 fourth-round pick from the Tennessee Titans.
During his opening press conference with his new team, Simmons clearly outlined the same vision in being with the Bears that the front office justified for giving up such a big haul to land him.
He also gave quarterback Caleb Williams a shoutout for Chicago being great "from quarterback all the way down."
"This team believes in what they have here and they want it right now. My game, my passion, my energy, my leadership, I can only help this team even more than what it's got. This is a great team from quarterback all the way down," Simmons said .
Simmons was brought on to strengthen an already stout defense against the run. Simmons has 20 run stops this season, which should fit nicely with Dennis Allen's No. 3-ranked run defense during through Week 7.
With the defense potentially game to match Williams and Co.'s offensive output as the top-ranked passing game when Williams is suited up in uniform, this is a strong contender.
In fact, the Bears might be the most win-now roster in the league.
Another impressive aspect about Simmons' opening press conference is that he instantly understands Chicago's culture.
Specifically, Simmons understands the hate that's breed in the NFC North.
Simmons said he'd be onboard soon with the hate the team has for the Green Bay Packers, who most recently got the better of the Bears in a 31-7 rout at Lambeau Field . Green Bay and Chicago have had heated battles dating back to last December. The Bears stole the NFC North crown and then a month later Chicago stunned the Packers with an 18-point comeback in the Wild Card Round.
There's a bit more intra-divisional hate in the NFC North than the AFC South. All the teams are in the northern part of the country, for starters.
With Simmons in the Windy City, there's a clear opportunity to elevate his game. Senior defensive assistant Bill Johnson has worked with guys like Aaron Donald and Cameron Jordan in his career. Simmons approaching those two on the field would certainly justify Ryan Poles and Co. going all in for him. After paying that price, there probably won't be another significant deal before November 10.
You can ballyhoo about the assets given up, but if Simmons gets with the program, the payoff would prove this front office's worth and then some.
The talent is there. Even Simmons sees it, and he just got here.
Andrew Hughes is a freelance journalist based in Austin, Texas, who has bylines across ON SI and The Sporting News. His work has been featured in The Miami Herald, Bleacher Report, and Yahoo Sports. Andrew graduated from Brooklyn College with a degree in journalism in 2017 and has been a sports fan since 1993.

title: Giddy Describes Halas Hall Reaction to Bears Trade for Jeffery Simmons
full_text:
When Bears coaches around Halas Hall heard the news Thursday about the trade for Jeffery Simmons , it actually might have been someone in Cincinnati who had the best reaction.
Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor heard clapping down the hall and then got on Face Time with his brother, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor.
"Which, we don't normally talk until like late in the week," Press Taylor said.
Zac wore a big smile so Press assumed his brother heard the news.
"And I'm like, 'thank you,' " Press Taylor said, not realizing the real reason his brother was smiling.
" ‘No,' " Press said Zac told him. "We play the Titans this week.' '
The Bears had just removed one huge headache from the Bengals' preparation and game plan by taking Simmons away from Tennessee.
"But in all honesty, I was in the division for four years with the guy and I know it’s a nightmare," Press Taylor said of Simmons. "Twice a year it was an absolute nightmare having to deal with him, just being aware of where he is, how you’re blocking him every given play.
Newly acquired DT Jeffery Simmons at his first #Bears practice. pic.twitter.com/KUePfcc1qR
"And you know what he’s going to do. He’s a high-motor, incredibly productive terrifying guy to go against. I’m glad we’re not going against him anymore."
The Bears were beaming at Halas Hall Friday over having the player everyone else must scheme to block.  Linebacker Devin Bush was stunned when he found out about it Thursday.
"I didn't believe it at first," Bush said. "I thought it was just fake news, but after I found out it was real I was happy."
The message delivered by the front office to the team?
"We're going after it," Bush said. "We're all in."
Defensive tackle Grady Jarrett has someone playing alongside now who commands attention and, no doubt, double teams.
"I was actually telling him I was watching him on film study earlier in the week, I just like to see the tenacity he plays with, the mindset," Jarrett said. "When you're on a team that's struggling (like Tennesee was) and you've got to go out there every day you've got to make your mind up to go out and compete, I've been in that situation. It just speaks to your football character.
"And obviously the intangible things we can see, just the eye test: quickness, a combination of power, and a super smart player ... I could go on all day. He's a special player."
Cool. Here's Jeffery Simmons rushing off the edge https://t.co/xTvlwLtYgG pic.twitter.com/Ylum4fOn2W
Even special teams coordinator Richard Hightower got in on the act.
"He'll obviously have an opportunity to play field goal block like he always has," Hightower said. "He's a monster in there."
It might have been Hightower who characterized what's best about the addition of a player of this level during the middle of a season.
"We got this thing rolling now," Hightower said. "All you (Simmons) gotta do is add and come to and do what he does, no added pressure, none of that, just play ball. And that's what we're expecting from him. He's got enough pieces around him where he can just be himself. He don't need to press, any of that."
He can put the press on opposing quarterbacks, instead.
Plays like this in the Red Zone are worth a loooooottt of draft capital Jeffery Simmons is a beast pic.twitter.com/dFdLGQJbLg
"I don't know that I've had anybody that's been what I would consider this dominant," defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said. "I've had some good players, you know, that have played inside for us. David Onyemata (in New Orleans) comes to mind but I don't know that I've had anybody this disruptive."
The disruption should help everyone on defense.
"Drawing extra attention will help everybody up front," Jarrett said. "It will really help the whole defense. It will kind of dictate protection sometimes, where you're going to put people.
"So I think it's going to be super good for the whole team."
The negatives are the draft day cost and future cap considerations. All of that is something to worry about in the future. As Bush said, at this point it's all about winning now.
I still can’t believe Jeffery #Simmons is a new "Monster of the Midway." 🤯🐻⬇️ Having him destroying the middle of the line is going to be awesome. #Chicago defense has just become an absolute nightmare. 🧱🏈 #DaBears pic.twitter.com/rrHEiVRqxn

title: Khalil Mack Trade Rumor Confirms Roadblock Bears Face For Possible Deal
full_text:
If the Chicago Bears want to trade for veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack, they're going to need the Los Angeles Chargers to budge.
According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Chargers have remained steadfast in their desire not to sell at the deadline despite beginning the season with an 0-6 record.
That means the Chargers remain a roadblock — and maybe the only roadblock — for the Bears acquiring Mack.
"The Chargers have confounded teams by not engaging in trade talks," Jones said on Saturday. "The Bolts are 0-6 but are telling teams Khalil Mack isn’t available. It’s hard to envision that remaining the case over the next 10 days."
Teams are stunned because the Chargers are going nowhere this season and should be looking to sell off pieces, and especially players who are on the final year of their contracts, like Mack.
Perhaps Mack can give the Chargers a nudge with a trade request. Either way, we suspect the Chargers will change their stances the closer it gets to the deadline.
Early this week, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Bears were "connected to" interest in Mack , along with edge rusher Josh Sweat.
"Two teams I'm watching very closely are the 49ers and Bears," he said Monday. "I've heard both teams connected to several defensive players, including rushers, Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack."
Then, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said that even after the Jeffery Simmons trade, the Bears are likely still in the market for an edge rusher.
So, it's safe to assume that, at the very least, Mack is on the Bears' radar in their quest to find more help along the edge.
The Bears' defense has been solid overall and better than expected this season.
The Bears' pass-rush has been good, also, with Chicago ranking tied for eighth in the league with 19 sacks, with 10.5 of those coming from edge rushers.
But, at the very least, more depth is needed behind Austin Booker, Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat, the latter of whom has been disappointing this season. Odeyingbo is also on the shelf with a quadriceps injury and we aren't sure how much longer he'll be sidelined beyond his current injured reserve stint.
Mack would be a perfect addition for the Bears.
The future Hall of Famer has still got it with his three sacks and 16 pressures in six games, and he's coming off a season in which he posted 5.5 in 12 contests.
Mack is also quite familiar with Chicago after spending four years in the Windy City, where he has said in the past he enjoyed his time.
Ultimately, we believe it's a matter of when, not if, Mack will land back in Chicago.

title: 3 Reasons the Bears Trade For Jeffery Simmons is Different Than 2018 Khalil Mack Trade
full_text:
The Bears pulling the trigger on a trade that brought defensive game-wrecker Jeffery Simmons to Chicago on Thursday morning probably instilled a feeling of Déjà vu. The Bears shipped out two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection for the four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle (and a fifth-round pick).
That was eerily similar to the haul they gave up for an equally dominant pass rusher, Khalil Mack, just before the 2018 NFL season kicked off. They gave up two first-round picks, a third-round pick, and a sixth-round selection for Mack, a second-round pick, and a fifth-round selection.
The Bears then signed Mack to a six-year, $141 million deal that made him the highest-paid defensive player in league history. Still, he was worth every penny, as Mack was a Defensive Player of the Year finalist in 2018 and instantly turned the Bears' defense into one of the league's most feared units.
While the decision initially looked like a lopsided victory for Chicago, the tide turned after his incredible 2018 campaign. He was still great, but not nearly as dominant as injuries began to take their toll.
The team around Mack fell apart, and the Bears were stuck in mediocrity for the rest of his time in Chicago. Futility at quarterback position saw the future Hall of Fame edge rusher never win a playoff game (we don't need to talk about the one he lost in 2018) during his time in Chicago.
I still love Mack, and don't look back at his time in the Windy City as a failure by any means. Even being less than 100%, he was still their most dominant player over that span. I was a staunch supporter in bringing him back at a MUCH lower price earlier this month.
However, former general manager Ryan Pace was flat-out wrong about how close the team was to competing for a Super Bowl, and that tarnished the acquisition. They didn't achieve their goal during his time in Chicago, and Mack's hefty contract was a hindrance in that regard. There's plenty of reason to believe their most recent costly acquisition will be different this time around , though.
Mack was the cherry on top of an offseason that saw the Bears burn their salary cap like it was going out of style. They completely revamped the pass-catching room by signing Allen Robinson, Taylor Gabriel, and Trey Burton to multi-year deals.
Pace never seemed to know when to put the checkbook away in free agency. While that occasionally worked to the Bears' advantage (Akiem Hicks and Allen Robinson proved to be great additions), it usually didn't. Their hit rate was low, and the money dried up quickly.
That fact, combined with Pace's affinity for treating first-round picks like they've long been out of style, left the roster in disrepair when Ryan Poles took over. Say what you will about Poles' weak third-round hit rate and decision to hire/retain Matt Eberflus, but you can't knock him for his early-round hit rate and any overindulgence via free agency.
A major reason the Bears fell off after 2018 was that defensive coordinator Vic Fangio accepted the Broncos' head coach position the following year. Fangio has always been recognized as one of the league's premier defensive minds, and Chicago's defense struggled to maintain their level of play after he jumped ship.
While they were still near the top of the league in points and yards allowed in 2019, their numbers fell off considerably in both of Mack's final two years in Chicago before bottoming out in 2022.
Meanwhile, Chicago's current defensive coordinator, Dennis Allen, who is also considered one of the league's best, has been a head coach twice. First with the Raiders from 2012 to 2014 and then with the Saints from 2022 to 2024. Neither stint went well, and it would be shocking to see him get another head coaching gig at this stage of his career.
Allen deserves a world of credit for coaching up the Bears defense to a respectable unit despite not having anyone that opposing defenses needed to gameplan against until Kyler Gordon entered the lineup in Week 6. They now have two players to circle, and Allen should be in Chicago for the long haul if he capitalizes on the acquisition.
Pace wasn't wrong for capitalizing on the rookie QB contract window in 2018. That's what smart front offices do. The issue is that they put their chips in on the wrong guy, and didn't know whether Mitchell Trubisky would lead them to the promised land heading into the 2018 campaign.
The most important reason the Bears are much better positioned for success is that they landed a stone-cold killer at quarterback. Caleb Williams is still only scratching the surface, and he's already established himself as one of the league's best young quarterbacks .
Notably, they also found their head coach of the future. Matt Nagy looked the part in 2018, but we all saw how fast that fell apart. Ben Johnson immediately injected a shot of adrenaline into the locker room and is already being lauded as one of the league's best head coaches.
The duo instills immeasurable confidence in where they're going , regardless of how things go on the defensive side of the ball.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Former Bear and Super Bowl Champ Set to Sign with Team for Official Retirement
full_text:
Before the Chicago Bears awakening on offense in 2025 , the first year with head coach Ben Johnson and quarterback Caleb Williams working together, the early 2010's team was considered to be the best that a Bears offense had ever looked. Led by quarterback Jay Cutler, this offense featured two dynamic receivers in Brandon Marshall, for whom the Bears traded in 2012, and Alshon Jeffery, the Bears' second-round draft pick that same year.
In the 2013 season, this duo helped the Bears put up nearly 28 points per game and combined for 2,716 receiving yards and 19 touchdowns. Unfortunately, the team won only eight games that year and regressed in 2014 to win just five. Marshall was traded to the Jets the following year while Jeffery would remain with the Bears for another two years before signing with the Philadelphia Eagles, with whom he won Super Bowl LII.
Jeffery hasn't played in the NFL since 2020, but he's apparently going to officially hang up the cleats soon. While speaking to NFL analyst Kay Adams on her Up & Adams podcast, Jeffery announced that he intends to make his retirement official soon, and that he wants to retire as a Chicago Bear. "I started in Chicago, so I have to end it in Chicago," Jeffery told Adams.
As aforementioned, Jeffery did not stay with the Bears for very long. After playing out his four-year rookie contract, he spent the 2016 season playing on the franchise tag. That offseason, he signed with the Eagles on a one-year, $9.5 million deal, followed by a four-year contract extension with the Eagles worth $52 million, his last contract in the NFL.
But during those five seasons in Chicago, Jeffery was electric. He earned Pro Bowl honors in 2013 and put up back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons in 2013 and 2014. His last two years were plagued by injuries, causing him to miss 11 games, but he still racked up 1,628 yards and six touchdowns in those last two years.
In 2019, to celebrate the franchise's 100th birthday, Jeffery was named to the Top 100 Bears of all-time list , landing at No. 80. That put him at one spot ahead of former teammate Brandon Marshall.
Unfortunately for Jeffery, he may not be remembered by Bears fans quite as fondly as other former members of the team. Ahead of the Bears' Wild Card game against the Eagles in 2019 (yes, that Wild Card game), Jeffery made a comment about Chicago that rubbed its inhabitants the wrong way. "I love the city of Philadelphia," Jeffery said, "Chicago is just where I was for work."
That, plus his trash talk on the turf at Soldier Field, upset a large number of Bears fans, and by looking at the replies to Kay Adams' post of her interview with Jeffery, that anger doesn't seem to have subsided by much.
Hopefully Bears fans can remember the good that Jeffery did for this team when he does make his retirement official. He was a great receiver who suffered through what were some pretty bleak years for the Bears. He later clarified his comments, saying that he never meant to diss the city of Chicago but rather the "work environment" in his time with the Bears compared to his time with the Eagles.
With that in mind, Bears fans must admit that it's hard to disagree with what he said. The Bears were stuck in a deep rut during Jeffery's time with the team, but he almost immediately won a Super Bowl with the Eagles. Winning a championship does wonders for a team's work environment, something that the Bears may soon discover after their blockbuster trade for superstar Jeffery Simmons .
