title: Quenton Nelson Laments Inability to Escape Jeffery Simmons Ahead of Bears-Seahawks
full_text:
When the Indianapolis Colts traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks this week, the All-Pro guard figured that would be the last he would see Jeffery Simmons, at least in the near future.
However, ahead of the Week 8 contest against the Chicago Bears, Nelson finds himself in a familiar spot: lining up across from Simmons.
The Bears made a blockbuster trade with the Tennessee Titans for Simmons on Thursday, and it comes just days before Chicago and Seattle square off on Monday night in Week 8.
It hasn't been confirmed if Simmons is even playing yet, but that is the overwhelming expectation. Now, Nelson is back in a familiar spot against his old AFC South foe, which he isn't thrilled about.
"I was like, man, I can't get away from this guy," Nelson said when asked about Simmons going to Chicago ahead of his new team's matchup with the Bears. "It will be another battle against him this week."
"He's an amazing football player and competitor," Nelson added.
Nelson and Simmons have been battling twice a year since 2019, when Simmons was drafted into the AFC South with the Titans, who took him at No. 19 overall. Nelson was a first-round pick of Indianapolis the year before.
The battles have been epic and nasty at times, but there is a ton of respect between two players who are among the very best at their respective positions.
“I know I need to bring my A-game every time I line up against Quenton,” Simmons said of Nelson in the offseason. “He plays the game hard. Facing him twice a year for my last seven years, he’s been unbelievable. It’s nothing but respect for Quenton.”
Since their respective entrances into the league, both Simmons and Nelson have been elite, which only makes their battles more fun to watch.
Nelson has been a Pro Bowler in every season of his career and is a six-time All-Pro. Simmons has notched four Pro Bowls and three All-Pro nods, including his first first-team selection in 2025.
Another thing the two players have in common is they have been through a lot of losing in recent years, with the Colts and Titans having no shortage of struggles.
But the script has now been flipped for both players, as Nelson is joining the reigning Super Bowl champions who are very capable of repeating and Simmons joins a Bears team that looks like a contender after seven games.
And now, the Simmons-Nelson rivalry continues in what will be a huge game for their new teams on Monday night.

title: This Time Ryan Poles Might Really Have True Bears Defensive Multiplier
full_text:
If anything became apparent from Ryan Poles' discussion of the Bears and expectations following the trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , it's that a higher level of play is expected from the entire defense.
In particular, defensive end Montez Sweat needs to play at a higher level. Referred to by Ben Johnson as "Steady Eddie," Sweat can't just produce average, dependable football now when offensive lines are focusing on stopping a holy terror like Simmons .
"That’s why I really believe that closest path to the quarterback, to the ball, is inside, and often times that will open up some things on the outside for your guys," Poles said. "Yeah, just talking with Montez, he’s locked in, ready to go."
Sweat played with Simmons at Mississippi State in 2017 and 2018.
New Chicago Bears defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons is the only iDL to clear the 95th percentile in pressures, sacks, run stops, tackles for a loss, and QB hits over the last 3 seasons, per @SumerSports : pic.twitter.com/6Wz2LXUOH5
"This is one of his guys and I think he elevates his game, being around Jeffery," Poles said. "That’s our expectation. I think that’s the expectation he has for himself as well."
In essence, they'll be multiplying the multiplier because that is what Sweat was supposed to be.
The overall impact of having Simmons on how the Bears look on the field is going to be less gambling, big plays from their defensive line and a threat from the rush making their defensive backs better.
No matter what Vegas says, Bears are now the favorite. Super Bowl-or-bust stakes for Ben Johnson & Caleb Williams. Target on their backs & just like my #Seahawks s/o re: Quenton Nelson + not shying away from the price of chasing greatness, I bleeping love it. After watching…
Poles relayed how difficult it has been for Allen to craft a defensive plan each week, knowing he needed so much disguising and blitzing to get a rush going. Ultimately, he thinks they're better for the experience. In other words, it should make Allen better, as well.
"I think because of some of the contraints from injuries and some of the things we’ve had, you’ve seen DA shape-shift each week," Poles said. "But because of that -- and I want to shout a guy, David Epstein; he wrote a book called “How Constraints Make Us Better,” “Inside the Box,” it’s called -- because of those constraints we had to come up with really creative ways to get home and create pressure and all that.
"Now because you’ve done that and you’ve added another piece, his rolodex of things he can do for an offense just grows from here."
Just why is Jeffery Simmons the perfect fit for the #Bears defense? His burst and speed off the ball. Attributes Dennis Allen demands consistently. Like how about this play from last year as a great example? Ridiculous. pic.twitter.com/rSrCLDkCIr
Allen wasn't tipping his hand about how he can use Simmons, saying on how it's going to become a more expansive role after this week against Seattle because he'll have only a couple of practices. He did admit it's a bit like a Christmas present under the tree for him.
"Like, he got here like six o'clock last night," Allen said. "You know what I mean? So it's not like you can go in and say, we're gonna do all these crazy things.
"Let's kind of get our game plan together on what we want to try to get accomplished this week, we'll have a better feel for it next week, the following week, the following week after that and, it'll change as we go along."
Dennis Allen with Jeff Simmons: https://t.co/gjZCIpfVfP pic.twitter.com/a0WYytLV6J
Allen does know one thing others may not think about when they're dreaming of all the sacks that could come.
"I think it will help in terms of pass coverage," Allen said. "You know, if we're able to affect the interior of the pocket a little bit more, get a little bit more quick pressure on the quarterback, maybe some quick wins, I think that speeds up the process for the quarterback.
"It makes it easier for us to do some things on the back end."
They definitely can use that considering they alllow more yards per play than any defense.
The price was costly for him, even if it means in the future they'll not have first-round picks for two years.
"This changes the entire dynamic of [the Chicago Bears'] defense and what Dennis Allen wants to do." — @WWERollins on the Jeffery Simmons trade to the @ChicagoBears 💪 pic.twitter.com/t10P0r6uxC
"I don’t see it as some move that is gonna hurt us long-term," Poles said. "Is it going to bring about constaints? One hundred percent. But that’s where we have to have our processes and systems in who we extend, who we pay in free agency, hitting our draft picks. Do you move up? Do you move back? All those factors come into play.
"I feel like we’ve taken the time to really detail this out where it’s something that can help us tremendously early as well as down the road."
They can worry about the lost draft picks after they see QBs trampled and games won.
Big Jeff in the house 🏠 pic.twitter.com/DOHoR9DECB

title: Less Mobile Caleb Williams Faces Seahawks and How Bears Benefit
full_text:
The Bears coaching staff has continued walking the tight rope all year.
It's a constant battle between keeping quarterback Caleb Williams in the pocket or being so restrictive with his movement that they impede one of his greatest weapons — mobility.
It's possible the hamstring injury he had actually helped their cause and benefited the offense.
Williams has seemed to do a better job of staying with the pass play the last two weeks since returning from injury, according to what's been clocked on his time to throw. The question is whether this can continue against Seattle's Super Bowl champion defense on Monday night.  It's possible there is irony at work here and that is his hamstring actually helping his game by keeping him from excessive and hasty running. Both Williams and coach Ben Johnson sees it as something else, though.
Caleb Williams supporting a children ran lemonade stand in Madison Wisconsin before the USC Wisconsin game this past Saturday pic.twitter.com/r5FkEMpDG9
Bears coach Ben Johnson doesn't necessarily see it as the injury helping them and identified another reason.
“It's the same story that it's been for the last year and a half," Johnson said. "He's got a lot of time-on-task with some of these (offensive) concepts. Certainly, there's some things in each game plan that are a little bit unique for that particular defense, but we try to keep it consistent to where all these banked reps and the things that he's seen each play against coverage-wise.
"It does accelerate his ability to go through a progression and check the ball down if primary or No. 2's not there. We talk every week. We watch the tape, and we're looking at it. Were we able to stay in the pocket just a tick longer and deliver the ball, or did we need to break it there? Those are things that we have a good back-and-forth on because we've been pretty consistent as a coaching staff."
I owe you honesty. Chicago would be my pick to come out of the NFC today. Can’t apologize for it. Ben Johnson is in his bag, and Caleb Williams may be the most talented QB in the conference. I just lost likability points, didn’t I? pic.twitter.com/ekMBq5kqGi
Johnson does realize the benefits of a mobile QB at this point, even if it sometimes doesn't allow plays to be run the way he'd like.
"We don't want to take that magic out of his play whatsoever, and yet I do think you're seeing just a tick more of him playing on-time and on-rhythm, and I think that allows our pass catchers to come alive also," Johnson said. "We've got some dangerous weapons for him, but I think he's doing a good job finding those open guys right now."
The difference hasn't been huge and Williams is at 3.22 seconds to throw now, according to NFL NextGen Stats. That's slow but still down from earlier this season.
The Seattle Seahawks Defense just SHUT DOWN Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker - completely dominating this offense. This will be the biggest test of Caleb Williams and Ben Johnsons young careers. BIG TIME GAME COMING pic.twitter.com/gk8gStMJBK
Maybe the greatest proof of benefits from getting the ball out for Williams is how  yards after catch on throws have gone up from 5.6 last year to 6.4 this year. His percentage of on-target throws have increased dramatically from 69.8% to 79.6% per Pro Football Reference. It suggests he's throwing from a stationary position more often than trying to throw on the move outside the pocket.
Williams isn't so sure the hamstring has bottled up him in the pocket. He's just crediting teammates for making his job easier and letting him avoid running as much.
Caleb Williams is playing out of his mind this year and we all saw that last night. We’ve always seen the flashes with Caleb, but there’s been so much inconsistency. That is not the case this year. He is displaying elite QB play drive to drive. Top 5 QB in the NFL soon. pic.twitter.com/eZrMX3ffHq
Better blocking lets him stay put and get it away to receivers.
"I've felt good after our games," he said. "Obviously, I haven't maybe moved as much, so shout out to the O-line and running backs and everybody for blocking; wide receivers getting open.
"I haven't had to move as much, but I mean I've felt good moving and so these past couple days (off) have been nice, but glad to be getting back into it.”
The number of sacks Williams absorbed this year has been greater than last year through seven games, but this doesn't necessarily say his pass blocking is worse. He played in four of the seven games and has taken 12 sacks. He didn't reach the 12th sack taken until the seventh game in 2025.
This can indicate more willingness to stay with the pass play and throw from the pocket instead of getting out and running at first sign of pressure.
The bottom line has been bigger plays downfield. Averaging a career-best 8.2 yards per pass attempt puts him in elite company. Only Josh Allen (8.8), Drake Maye (8.3) and Brock Purdy (8.3) are averaging more.
It's amazing how much better numbers can look if a quarterback gets the ball in his playmakers' hands instead of his own for whatever reason.
Dan Orlovsky finally admits to being wrong about Jayden Daniel’s over Caleb Williams. 👀 #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/cHrEwiGBje

title: Kyle Monangai, Colston Loveland Injury Updates & More From Bears' Friday Practice Report
full_text:
The Chicago Bears dropped their second-to-last injury report of the week ahead of their Week 8 game against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night and it had bad news.
The Bears' Friday injury report includes a new addition in tight end Colston Loveland. This is his first appearance on an injury report this season.
We are, of course, keeping an eye on running back Kyle Monangai to see if there was any progress for him on the injury report after he didn't practice on Thursday . The Bears running back has not practiced since his injury.
Now, a look at the full injury report and everything else we know about the Bears' walking wounded.
Loveland was added to the injury report with a neck issue and was listed as a limited participant. It would appear, at least for now, that Loveland suffered his injury in practice, but that has not been confirmed.
Regardless, being a mid-week addition to the injury report is never a good sign for a player's chances of suiting up. We should know more on Saturday when head coach Ben Johnson addresses the media and the Bears put out their final injury report of the week.
If Loveland is forced to sit out, that would put the Bears in a precarious spot with Cole Kmet already out for the season.
That would push struggling rookie Sam Roush into an even bigger role, and we would also see Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail off Chicago's practice squad.
As for Monangai, another day without participation in practice keeps him on track to sit out his fourth straight game. Monangai was spotted riding a stationary bike at a practice earlier in the week, but that's about all the progress we've seen out of him.
Another bit of bad news is linebacker D'Marco Jackson going from limited on Thursday to a non-participant on Friday. That's not good for his chances of suiting up on Monday night.
The rest of the injury report was status quo. T.J. Edwards, who has been out for two weeks, and Jack Sanborn, who didn't play last week, remain on track to return.
Meanwhile, Malik Muhammad's status is up in the air after he turned in another limited session.
The good news for all of the Bears' injured players is that they have an extra day to get right with the game taking place on Monday, so perhaps they can improve enough over the weekend to get into what is a hugely important matchup against the Seahawks.

title: Bears' Jeffery Simmons Trade Grades: Not Everyone Loved Chicago's All-In Move
full_text:
The Chicago Bears pulled off a massive trade for Jeffery Simmons on Thursday and now it's time to scan around the NFL landscape to see how experts graded the trade.
As far as we're concerned, this was a fantastic trade for the Bears and we're giving it a "B+" overall.
The only reason the grade isn't higher is because the Bears will have to win a Super Bowl to fully justify giving up more for a D-tackle than any team in NFL history .
That said, Simmons checks a big box for Chicago, as the team needed both more pass-rush juice and better run defense, two things Simmons can offer at an elite level.
Now that you know what we think, let's see how experts from different media outlets view the trade. Most have a positive opinion, but there is one expert who doesn't view it fondly.
Kadlick gives the Bears a solid grade despite giving up such a big haul for Simmons.
He cautions that such a trade that sees a team give up two first-rounders could end up being a disaster, as the Indianapolis Colts have seen after the Sauce Gardner deal, but Kadlick rightly points out that the Bears are in a much better spot than Indy was.
"Is it a gamble for the Bears to ship away their next two first-round picks?" Kadlick asked. "Certainly, just look at what’s happened to the Colts after they did the same for cornerback Sauce Gardner at the 2025 deadline. That said, Chicago is in far better shape from top to bottom than Indianapolis was at this time last year, and with Simmons under contract through the ’29 season, the Bears have multiple years to make this move pay off."
The fact of the matter is, the Bears appear to have their franchise quarterback in Caleb Williams, who is ascending to elite status in 2026, and now is the time to strike while he's on his rookie deal.
Ryan Poles did just that by trading for Simmons.
The Bears score an even better grade with DeArdo and Zenitz, who also laud Chicago for making an all-in move.
"By getting Simmons, the Bears have increased their odds of winning what is arguably the NFL's hardest division, which includes the league's last unbeaten team, the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings," the CBS Sports analysts wrote. "The Bears may have won the division without Simmons, but his addition makes them the front-runner. "
"This also makes the Bears a stronger Super Bowl contender while keeping pace with the 49ers, who made a splash of their own earlier this week when they traded for DeForest Buckner," they added. "Instead of standing on the sidelines, the Bears decided to respond."
A lot has been made of the cost, and rightly so, we've never seen a team give up the kind of haul the Bears did for Simmons.
But if he helps bring a Super Bowl to the Windy City, nobody is going to bat an eye at what Chicago gave up.
Popper comes through with the lowest grade in our round-up.
"This is an ultra-aggressive move from the Bears. If it leads to a Super Bowl while Simmons is in Chicago, it will all be worth it," he said. "But anything short of a Lombardi Trophy makes this trade a huge overpay. Those are slim margins. Simmons is a game-wrecker, but we are separating the player from the process on this deal."
Because of Chicago's need and win-now situation, this grade no doubt deserves to be higher than a "D+," even when you consider how much the Bears gave up.
That said, we tend to agree with Popper here. Anything less than a Super Bowl after this trade will make it look a lot worse.
Here's how other outlets viewed the Simmons deal:

title: Bengals in Rarified Air As Double-Digit Favorites, and It Hasn’t Always Worked Out Well
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are 10.5-point favorites Sunday against the Tennessee Titans, which is a rare number for the franchise, especially of late.
In the immediate aftermath of the blockbuster trade that is sending Tennessee All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears, the line did not change.
Only once before in the Zac Taylor era have the Bengals been favored by at least 10.5 points, and it was nearly five years to the day prior to Sunday’s game.
It was Oct. 31, 2021, and the Bengals were 11-point road favorites against the New York Jets in Week 8.
And like this year, they were coming off a huge win in Baltimore that announced their presence as a Super Bowl contender.
In Week 7, 2021, the Bengals beat the Ravens 41-17 on their home field.
In Week 7 this year, the Bengals beat the Ravens 35-13 on their home field.
Cincinnati fans hope the parallel ends there.
Because in that Week 8 game at New York in 2021, Jets quarterback Mike White made his first career start and threw for 405 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-31 victory.
Sunday will mark just the 14th time the Bengals have been favored by as many as 10.5 points since 1990.
They are 10-4 in those games.
Week 8, 2017 vs. Indianapolis (-11) – Bengals 24, Colts 23
Week 7, 2016 vs. Cleveland (-11) – Bengals 31, Browns 17
Week 10, 2015 vs. Houston (-10.5) – Texans 10, Bengals 6
Week 9, 2015 vs. Cleveland (-11) – Bengals 31, Browns 10
Week 16, 2009 vs. Kansas City (-13) – Bengals 17, Chiefs 10
Week 13, 2009 vs. Detroit (-13.5) – Bengals 23, Lions 13
Week 12, 2009 vs. Cleveland (-12) – Bengals 16, Browns 7
Week 14, 2006 vs. Oakland (-10.5) – Bengals 27, Raiders 10
Week 2, 2006 vs. Cleveland (-10.5) – Bengals 34, Browns 17
Week 16, 2005 vs. Buffalo (-13) – Bills 37, Bengals 27
Week 14, 2005 vs. Cleveland (-12.5) – Bengals 23, Browns 20
Week 17, 1990 vs. Cleveland (-16) – Bengals 21, Browns 14
Week 12, 1990 vs. Indianapolis (-11.5) – Colts 34, Bengals 20
So for those who like to make a wager on the games, the Bengals are 4-10 against the spread when favored by at least 10.5 points.
Later Thursday, once the Simmons trade was made official and bettors started hammering the Bengals, the line jumped to 11.5.
Only 22 times in franchise history have the Bengals been favored by that many, with the most recent being the 17-10 win against the Chiefs in 2009.
The Bengals are 18-4 in those 22 games, but only 9-12-1 against the spread.
The Titans have been underdogs of at least 11.5 points 55 times in franchise history, going 7-47-1 in those games. That includes a losing streak of six in a row and 12 of the last 13.

title: Press Taylor Shares Zac Taylor's Hilarious Reaction to Jeffery Simmons Trade
full_text:
Chicago Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor had a fun exchange with reporters on Friday.
Taylor said he got a FaceTime call from his brother, Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor. It was uncommon for Press to receive a call from his brother on a Thursday while both coaches are game planning for their respective matchups.
Expecting some brotherly love or excitement for his success, Press was instead greeted by a smiling Zac Taylor, who said, "We play the Titans this week."  Of course, Zac was referencing the big trade involving the Chicago Bears and Tennessee Titans on Thursday that sent four-time Pro Bowler Jeffery Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks and a day-three swap.
For Press Taylor and the Chicago Bears, this immediately strengthens their already stellar run defense and dramatically improves their pass rush, as Simmons already has four sacks this season. Chicago is looking to make it back to the playoffs but faces the gauntlet of one of football's best divisions: the NFC North.
The Bengals face just as tough a challenge as the AFC North, so every game matters, and Zac Taylor has every right to be excited that Jeffery Simmons is no longer a Tennessee Titan.
He even jokingly told his brother Press, "I am going to put in a couple more passes."
It is an easy joke to make when you look at how dominant Simmons has been this season and throughout his career.  According to PFF, Simmons has the 3rd-most pressures among all interior defensive linemen and ranks as the 12th-best interior defender in football. Knowing they won't have to account for the four-time Pro Bowler on every snap, the offense can be even more dynamic and dial up an aggressive passing attack with extra time in the pocket, leading to the thrill of Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Mike Gesicki.
"I don't have to block him, but we're definitely glad he made it a little better for us with the game plan," Chase said this week.
"Two hours of anxiety last night is gone," Bengals center Ted Karras said.
That's what happens when game wreckers are no longer on the field. The Bengals look to keep the good times going with a two-game win streak and get the Jungle Rocking on Sunday as they face a young Tennessee Titans team.

title: Zac Taylor Announces Light Injury Game Status List For Titans Matchup

title: Is There an Opportunity for the Bengals to Pull Off a Massive Blockbuster Trade?
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens was massive. Now, it's time for the team to move on to their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.
With the win last Sunday, the Bengals moved to 4-2 on the season, and this week offers them a great chance to stay afloat in the fight for the top spot in the AFC North.
If the Bengals have more goals than just a divisional crown, there could be some moves made by the front office before the trade deadline that will make this team a stronger threat.
A lot of the talk about making a move for a running back has been in the headlines, but what about a trade for a tight end? One name that could possibly be on the block is Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta.
LaPorta has been at odds with the Lions as his recent comments about getting a new contract proved that the tight end is a tad disappointed.
"It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take. “I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else. So whatever.”
That sounds like a player who is ready to move on if his current team doesn't show him the respect he feels he deserves. However, Lions head coach Dan Campbell doesn't seem to think his tight end's comments are anything to worry about.
For the Bengals , tight end is a position that recently took a major hit. With the recent news that Erik All's season has been derailed by a knee injury, the Bengals could use a major talent like LaPorta, but it may be costly.
Spotrac currently has LaPorta's market value at $15 million a season for three years. LaPorta will be 26 by the time the 2027 season begins. To put that in perspective, the Dallas Cowboys signed tight end Jake Ferguson at the same age for a $50 million deal.
Getting LaPorta will come at a heavy price. Not only will the Bengals be expected to give him a new deal, but the team will probably need to trade important draft capital.
LaPorta is sixth in receiving yards for tight ends this season and has three touchdown receptions. He would obviously be a massive upgrade at the position, but would the Bengals be willing to retain him with a new deal?
A trade for LaPorta is unlikely. However, if the Bengals want to go all-in, it couldn't hurt to ask if there is a market for the talented tight end.

title: Bengals Trade Fit for Emerging Linebacker is a No-Brainer Move
full_text:
Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. have improved this season for the Bengals , but both have still struggled in certain areas, specifically with missed tackles. Together, they've missed 14 tackles in six games, indicating that linebacker remains a weakness on defense, one that could cost them later in the season. One trade candidate could fix that problem, though, as The Athletic has labeled Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley a fit for the Bengals at the trade deadline.
Henley has flashed elite play early in his career. In 2024, he recorded 147 tackles with an 8.7% missed-tackle rate, an interception, and eight passes defended, allowing a 99.1 passer rating. His 2025 season started slow due to severe illness, however, he still recorded 103 tackles with only five misses. He also had two interceptions with five passes defended.
His play in 2026 started inconsistently, but from Week 3 onward, he corrected that and continued to show the traits of an ascending player at 27 years old. He has only missed two tackles all season compared to Knight and Carters 14 combined.
With Henley in the final year of his rookie deal and the Chargers having tremendously underwhelmed this season, now is the perfect time to acquire him at a low cost.
The difficulty of negotiating a contract extension, along with a rebuild set to take place in LA, could reduce the trade compensation to as little as a fifth-round pick. The Bengals could avoid sacrificing even a fifth-rounder in next year's draft by including Shemar Stewart in the deal.
There is also a precedent for what an extension for Henley could look like. If he hits his ceiling, the ideal contract should land somewhere in the range of what Zach Baun and Azeez Al-Shaair commanded at $17-$18 million a year.
Acquiring Henley would give the Bengals, at minimum, a starting-caliber player at the linebacker spot with a high ceiling as a potential rising star.
Should the Bengals look elsewhere for a linebacker instead of Henley, there are still starting-caliber options worth the investment.
Titans linebacker Cody Barton is one example of a trustworthy player at the linebacker spot as he has remained solid at the position in his eight-year career. He has missed no more than seven tackles since 2019 and will turn 30 in November. Barton has solid coverage skills, but his 4.2% career missed-tackle rate shows he can bring down ball carriers.
Another option is Chargers linebacker Troy Dye, who has routinely served as a solid backup with special-teams experience. The team could acquire him to replace veteran Swayze Bozeman, who is currently on Injured Reserve with a fractured forearm. At 30 years old, Dye would likely fill Bozeman's role better than Jack Kiser, whom the team claimed off waivers after Bozeman's injury.
Either Barton or Dye would be cheaper than Henley in a trade and may better align with what the Bengals want to add to their linebacker room.

title: Micah Parsons Picks Bengals to Achieve AFC’s Top Regular-Season Goal
full_text:
Micah Parsons sees the Cincinnati Bengals finishing atop the AFC. The Green Bay Packers star picked Cincinnati on his Bleacher Report show when asked which team would earn the conference's first-round bye.
The Bengals improved to 4-2 with a 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Cincinnati erased a 13-0 halftime deficit by scoring 35 unanswered points, giving Parsons plenty to consider when making his prediction.
“I’m gonna say Bengals,” Parsons said in the clip. “I think they’ve been pretty much the most consistent.”
"Ja’Marr’s numbers may not be high. It’s because Tee’s been snapping,” Parsons said.
Higgins offered a strong example in Baltimore, catching six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase added five catches for 62 yards and a score, while Joe Burrow finished with 292 passing yards and four passing touchdowns.
Burrow was particularly sharp after halftime, completing 16-of-18 passes for 249 yards. That efficiency helped Cincinnati turn a two-score deficit into a comfortable road win over a division opponent.
“The Bengal defense is playing great,” Parsons said. “It’s not the same Bengals. It’s not the same. I think they low-key win the division.”
The Bengals recorded four sacks against Baltimore and held the Ravens scoreless after halftime.  Cincinnati has 21 sacks through six games, with multiple sacks in each game and at least four in four of those games.
That pass rush gives Cincinnati another way to take control when the offense needs time to find its rhythm. Against Baltimore, the defense kept the deficit manageable until Burrow and his receivers turned the game around.
The uneven start also leaves Cincinnati with something to clean up. Chasing the AFC's top seed will require more complete performances, because even an offense with Burrow, Chase, and Higgins cannot count on five touchdown drives after halftime every week.
Cincinnati returns to Paycor Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 8. A win would put the Bengals at 5-2, giving them a chance to build on their breakthrough in Baltimore and strengthen their standing in the AFC playoff race.

title: Bengals Star React to Titans Jeffery Simmons Trade Before Cincinnati Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals don't have to deal with arguably the best defensive tackle in the NFL this coming weekend, a welcome relief to members of the offense.
Tennessee sent Jeffery Simmons to the Bears today in a blockbuster move ahead of the 2026 Trade Deadline. The 2025 AP First-Team All-Pro is 10th at his position in Pro Football Focus grading this season while leading all interior linemen in ESPN pass-rush win rate and ranking fifth in pressure rate.
Ja'Marr Chase and Ted Karras spoke about the ease of the game plan Thursday, while acknowledging you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL.
"I don't have to block him, but we're definitely glad he made it a little better for us with the game plan," Chase said.
Karras did have to take him on and he is breathing big sigh of relief to not face the eighth-year star.
"Two hours of anxiety last night is gone," Karras joked. "I'm going to take a deeper look and kind of try and predict how they're going to play without them. They got good players. John Franklin-Myers has been playing at the top of his game for a long time. I remember when he was young on the Jets; he's been dangerous forever. So they got a lot of good players over there. So we got to go out and execute and win this ball game, but yeah, I mean, obviously, a dynamic player is on the Bears, so Joe Thuney has to deal with him at practice."
Cincinnati's easy schedule got a tad bit easier with the move, and they cannot afford to lose this game while pursuing the top regular season goal: The AFC's No. 1 seed.
Chase wants to see his team come out much faster than the donut they posted in the first half a few days ago.
"I think we got to look at the bright side of us playing at home," Chase noted. "That's the one thing we got to look at. We're playing at home, so we got to keep the crowd in tight for us. We got to keep the fans ready. And two is just coming out faster than what we did last week. You can't look at this game like they lost Jeffery Simmons and not still be good, you know what I'm saying? Cause they still got good players up front."
The Bengals star also pointed out his ankle is feeling fine after a full day of Thursday practice.
Cincinnati gets a chance to show that hunger at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation
full_text:

"PJ brings a lot of energy. It's really important to him," Taylor noted. "He's done a great job on special teams in his roles. He stepped into safety. So when we need to continue to rely on depth at the safety position, I feel very confident in PJ and Russ (Yeast)."

title: 'Guaranteed Super Bowl' - Bengals Pushed to Trade For Star Running Back Amidst Enticing Factors
full_text:
The Bengals need to take advantage of the Colts' fire sale.
Indianapolis is dumping talented players left and right this week following trades to send out stars like guard Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jonathan Taylor is in the sights now for many teams, and the Bengals should be one of them.
They already traded away draft capital to completely transform the defense with Dexter Lawrence, and now they could do the same for the offense with Taylor.
Former NFL offensive lineman Breiden Fehoko echoed that sentiment this week. The Bengals need to make another move and go all in on pursuing the AFC's No. 1 seed. It's the easiest path to the Super Bowl, and they have the easiest schedule left in the NFL by a wide margin.
"The Bengals can lock in a guaranteed Super Bowl if they trade for Jonathan Taylor. Teams would choose to either run a light box to defend Ja’Marr (Chase) and Tee (Higgins) or load up to stop JT. YOU CAN'T DO BOTH," Fehoko declared on X .
Our Landon Belote broke down how Taylor is posting solid efficiency running from under center this season, a potential boon to Cincinnati's struggles on that front (a great shotgun runner too), and he's been a consistent force since entering the league in 2020 (one season graded lower than 65.3 overall).
Now, he is going to be very pricey. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Tuesday that the Colts don't want to trade him, and the cost could be a first-round pick. Cincinnati has eight draft picks this coming spring, including an extra projected third-round compensation pick (99th overall).
Also, Taylor starts a new $20-plus million contract extension running next season and in 2028. Alas, that's a problem to deal with in February after making a title run. Worst-case scenario, they can release him for a $10 million cap hit and $11 million in savings during the offseason, but its much more likely they just keep him as the main running back for next season. They only have Tahj Brooks under contract.
They need to try to use that extra pick somehow. They may never get a perfect-schedule storm like this ever again and cannot pass up chances to get better in pursuit of that one seed.
"I think the owner doesn't want to trade. We have two weeks from now until the deadline," Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show. "I'm sure they don't want to trade Jonathan Taylor. And if I had to guess today, I would say I don't think they will trade Jonathan Taylor.
"But I think there are going to be teams that are interested out there that will try to have conversations, make offers, and if the Colts don't change their stance, they won't trade Jonathan Taylor. But again, I think the owner doesn't want to trade him. For the record, right now. Now, that doesn't mean it won't happen, that may just be their stance to drive up the price."
Cincinnati has to stay aggressive over the next two weeks.
They already have Lawrence as a perfect example of why they should be trading assets for firm talents. Another star add could make them clear AFC favorites.

title: Bengals' Job Sunday Just Got a Lot Easier with Titans Trading Star Defensive Tackle
full_text:
Already favored by 10.5 points Sunday against Tennessee, the Cincinnati Bengals just saw their degree of difficulty plummet further with today’s news of a blockbuster trade sending Titans’ All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears.
A first-round pick in 2019, Simmons has been voted to four Pro Bowls and earned his first first-team All-Pro selection in 2025, when he had a career-high 11 sacks.
Simmons, who also has two second-team All-Pro nods, already has four sacks this season, giving him 46.5 in his career.
Among defensive tackles, Simmons 46.5 sacks rank sixth since 2019 behind Chris Jones (64), DeForest Buckner (54.5), Aaron Donald (51.5), Cameron Heyward (48), Leonard Williams (46.5).
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor talked about facing Simmons during his Wednesday news conference.
“He’s arguably up there with all of the top guys,” he said. “I hate to rank a No. 1. He’s the opponent this week. He’s really good. He gets off the ball. He’s really difficult in one-on-one situations and double-team situations. Really good against the run. Good against the pass.
“If you’re not planning for him, you’ll have some problems.”
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was asked about Simmons as well.
“He's really big. He's really strong. He's really fast,” Burrow said. “That's usually a good combination. He's really tough. Seems to love what he does, and you put all those things together, you get Jeff Simmons.”
Simmons sacked Burrow three times in the 2021 Division Round playoff game the Bengals won 19-16.
And Simmons was instrumental in drawing double teams that allowed the Titans to sack Burrow another six times for an NFL-playoff record nine.
In 2022, Simmons punched Bengals center Ted Karras at the end of the game and drew an $11,139 fine from the league,
Today’s move changes the Bengals’ plan, but Tennessee has depth at the position.
Listed behind Simmons on the Titans depth chart is Solomon Thomas, the No. 3 overall pick in 2017. But the 30-year-old Thomas hasn’t had a sack in his last 26 games.
The starter next to Thomas will be John Franklin-Myers, a fourth-round pick in 2018 who also is 30 years old.
Franklin-Myers has 1.5 sacks in four career games against the Bengals while playing for the Jets and Broncos.

title: Can the Browns Break the Losing Streak? A Look at the Numbers Ahead of Rivalry Matchup
full_text:
After a historic 5-2 start to the season, the Cleveland Browns are once again looking to rewrite the history books this week.
Since their last win in 2003, the Cleveland Browns have not defeated the Steelers on the road in a regular season game. The last time they did it? Tim Couch led the Browns to a 33-13 win.
Let's look at the numbers to see if the Browns have a real chance to sweep their biggest rival.
Sixteen players on the Browns’ 53-man roster were not yet born the last time the Browns won a regular season game in Pittsburgh.
The Browns, led by Deshaun Watson , currently have five game-winning drives through the first seven weeks of the NFL season. This number leads the league.
However, there are some glaring numbers that stick out. Pittsburgh may go after some of these gaps and expose the current AFC North leader .
Looking at the Steelers, their games have been won primarily by their defense getting stops, with their offense narrowly getting the job done.
#Browns Jared Verse responds to Cam Heyward’s comments saying that they are going to address his comments after the last Steelers game. Verse called the #Steelers dirty and that he can’t wait to see them again after their Thursday Night win. pic.twitter.com/ZCQK4ILUuM
Despite the historic losing streak, this may be the best chance the Browns have of getting their long sought after win.
If the Browns can come out early, find a consistant source of offense, and simply score, they can look to control the game with a lead.
However, Pittsburgh's defense is one of the NFL's best. Especially when playing divisional games at home, they will be one of the toughest units Cleveland will face all season.
For Pittsburgh, they need to shut down Deshaun Watson and force him to turn the ball over.
The Biggest mistake teams have been making is letting Watson get comfortable. It isn't a coincidence that Watson is the best fourth-quarter quarterback in the NFL right now. Once he gets going, it is hard to stop him.
In the same breath, we have seen Watson get himself into holes many times before. That is why the first half will be a lot more important than people think.
The game will be decided between the Browns' offense and the Steelers' defense. On the opposite side, with Cleveland facing Aaron Rodgers, we pretty much already know what we are going to get.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: The Browns’ Uniform Combination for Sunday’s Game in Pittsburgh Isn’t a Coincidence
full_text:
With both the Browns and Steelers tied atop the AFC North at 5-2, there’s plenty on the line on Sunday , unlike in the majority of the matchups between the two teams over the last two decades, especially in matchups in Pittsburgh.
The Browns will wear orange helmets, white jerseys, and orange pants for the first-place showdown , the team announced on Thursday.
putting it on 😌 @RiddellSports | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/mphTCjkwNS
It’s the same combination Cleveland wore in their only two wins at Acrisure Stadium (previously Heinz Field), which opened in 2001: Jan. 10, 2021, in the AFC Wild Card playoff game and Oct. 5, 2003, in the regular season.
Without any actual fans in the stands due to COVID, the Browns beat the Steelers, 48-37, to advance to the Divisional Round of the playoffs.
It was a game Cleveland started off hot, as the Browns’ defense recovered a botched snap in the end zone for a touchdown on the Steelers’ first play of the game. They then took a 28-0 lead into the second quarter and led 35-10 at halftime before the Steelers tried to fight their way back in the second half.
The Browns were led by Baker Mayfield, who completed 21-of-34 passes for 263 yards and three touchdowns. Ben Roethlisberger, meanwhile, completed 47-of-68 passes for 501 yards, four touchdowns, and four interceptions. The Steelers had only 52 rushing yards compared to Cleveland’s 127 yards and two scores on the ground.
The Browns’ last win in Pittsburgh with actual fans in the stands, Cleveland took an early lead and never looked back, just like they did in 2021.
The Browns led 16-3 two minutes into the second quarter and then a 30-13 lead after three quarters before winning the game in dominant fashion, 33-13.
Cleveland was led by Tim Couch, who completed 20-of-25 passes for 208 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception, along with four carries for 11 yards and a score. William Green notched 33 carries for 115 yards on the ground.
The Browns haven’t swept the Steelers 2-0 in the season series since 1988. Aaron Rodgers is the only player on either active roster who was alive then. But it appears Cleveland is pulling out all the stops to try to do so on Sunday.
If the Browns find a way to win a game with fans in the stands in Pittsburgh for the first time in 23 years, they would not only take full command of the AFC North at 6-2, but their six wins would be Cleveland's most in a season since 2003, when the Browns went 11-6 during the regular season.
Residing in Northeast Ohio my entire life, I am a lifelong Cleveland and Ohio State sports fanatic. I fulfilled my childhood dream of graduating from The Ohio State University in 2013. I began writing about sports — specifically the Buckeyes and Cleveland Browns, Cavs, and Guardians — when I realized I could no longer play them.

title: Browns Rookie KC Concepcion Is Already Making His Presence Felt Off the Field
full_text:
KC Concepcion stole headlines this past weekend when he had his first breakout in an outing against the Tennessee Titans.
From Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Concepcion dominated, hauling in eight passes for 129 yards , helping lead the Browns' offense in a 27-24 victory. Now, on the season, the 22-year-old has 30 catches for 315 yards.
While he continues to make an impact on the gridiron, he is also doing it off.
Since arriving in Cleveland, Concepcion has used his platform to raise awareness about stuttering , an issue he has battled throughout his entire personal life.
"It feels amazing, honestly," he said on Thursday, Oct. 29. "Honestly, just having the speech impediment, fighting that battle daily, and then just seeing what I can do with my platform for people who may be going through some of the same things or people who may be going through a different adversity.
"Just me seeing those comments and me being able to inspire people all over the world, it just means everything."
#Browns WR KC Concepcion on inspiring people through his media availability sessions: "It feels amazing, honestly. Honestly, just having the speech impediment, fighting that battle daily and then just seeing what I can do with my platform for people who may be going through some… pic.twitter.com/CqmeJMlFqz
Being able to find enough success on the football field to draw eyes has given him a new audience to connect with. His willingness to speak openly about his experiences provides others an opportunity to navigate similar challenges and not feel alone.
"Being able to inspire people all over the world means everything," Concepcion said.
Posted in the late hours of Thursday, X user Steven Aquino quoted a post from the Browns, saying, "I’ve stuttered my entire life. It means the world to see a high-profile athlete do this—and have it normalized—and someone who “looks” like me."
I’ve stuttered my entire life. It means the world to see a high-profile athlete do this—and have it normalized—and someone who “looks” like me. I’m not even an NFL reporter, but I love this so much. Good on the Browns and KC Concepcion. I’d love to interview him one day. https://t.co/dgzFovDXcO
Some athletes use the national stage to promote their own brands or products, or simply continue to raise their status as performers. Concepcion, on the other hand, puts himself in compromising or uncomfortable positions just to continue to make others feel better about themselves.
That doesn't just make him a good person, but also a good teammate.
Rather than keeping his personal experiences behind closed doors, he gives people a direct, genuine look into who he is. This allows people to connect with his character and personality beyond what is seen on the field.
In a letter to @NFL general managers before the draft, KC Concepcion wrote about the type of player and person he is: “By now you’ve probably heard that I stutter. Everyone has. And look, I get it. It’s a good story. I’m not mad at it. And I appreciate the love. But every time… pic.twitter.com/LrJecMbxMu
“I have had this stutter since I can remember talking," he said, following a Scouting Combine back in the spring. "This is a part of me. This is who I am. I cannot control this. I wanna be a role model for those who may be scared to speak up, who may be afraid and not confident in themselves. I stand with you."
The Browns' future is bright, not just because they sit with a 5-2 record and top spot in the AFC North, but because the front office is building a core group of athletes who possess good character, strengthening the bond between players and the fanbase.
Concepcion and the Browns will look to keep the good vibes going this weekend when they take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a Week 8 meeting at Acrisure Stadium.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Quarterback Could Become Trade Candidate Amid Colts' Potential Rebuild
full_text:
After only seven weeks of the NFL season, the Indianapolis Colts have thrown a wrench in the league’s final 10 games. They have already traded Quentin Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, and they have more players on the trade block.
The Colts are in "sell" mode after the termination of General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor could be the next Colt to leave for a contender before the November 10 trade deadline, but they may want to consider adding a Browns player amid their fire sale.
Daniel Jones has regressed since his injury last season. In 2025, the Colts got off to a hot 8-2 start and looked poised to be one of the top seeds in the AFC. Then Jones got injured for the season and they lost their final seven games. He has four touchdown passes with seven interceptions so far this season.
The Colts may want to consider trading for Cleveland Browns’ backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders. The Browns were expected to have been playing Sanders by this point in the season, but Deshaun Watson has gone 5-2 and is shaking off rust with every passing week.
“I believe the Indianapolis Colts should trade for Shedeur Sanders immediately,” - @EvCoRadio on the Browns QB2. Should the Browns trade Shedeur? pic.twitter.com/56Dd87cYuL
Sanders would have a chance to start for the Colts, and the Browns can recoup the fifth-round pick that they used on him in 2025.
ESPN Cleveland believes that the trade for Sanders would distract the Colts’ fans from holding the front office’s feet to the fire. The fans would have someone to root for in Sanders , and if he plays well, then they could have possibly found their quarterback of the future. The Browns may be ready to trade Sanders as Dillon Gabriel comes off the injured reserve and will take up a roster spot.
Todd Monken has not “gotten there yet” in deciding on the quarterback depth chart upon Gabriel’s return. He has been heralded for his processing of the offense, but his physical talent may limit his ceiling. The Browns are in “win” mode and may not have the time to develop and evaluate Sanders.
However, trading for a quarterback like Sanders just to distract fans may be too much of a reach for the Colts. They signed Jones to a two-year contract extension last offseason, averaging $ 44 million per year. If the Colts want a quarterback on a rookie contract, then they are better off drafting one in the first round, as the class looks to be an improvement over years past, and they will have a high pick due to their record.
Jones would then use the last year of his contract to start the season, similar to what the Las Vegas Raiders are doing with Kirk Cousins. The Colts will most likely be entering next season with a new coach and general manager, and they should let those people choose their own quarterback.
It is believed that Watson earned the starting quarterback role over Sanders due to the veteran’s ability to get in and out of the huddle and line up the offense.
If Sanders did not have a great grasp of the new offense after all the offseason and training camp, then getting traded to a new team mid-season would not be in his best interest. Sanders and Watson have complemented each other all offseason, and Monken has done a great job coaching them to success. He is better off staying in Cleveland, as the Browns do not have a quarterback set for next season.
The Browns do not have to make a trade just to make a trade before the deadline. The vibes are good in Cleveland, and they may not want to disturb that in any way . The Colts have stripped the roster down to the bolts and trading for Sanders would be too little too late.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Todd Monken Makes Long-Awaited Decision on Shedeur Sanders in Browns Depth Chart
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a logjam at the quarterback position.
With controversial quarterback Deshaun Watson receiving medical clearance during the offseason and ultimately being named the starter, the rest of the Browns' quarterback room was left in limbo.
Now, after weeks of speculation on how things would shake out by the middle of the 2026 campaign, head coach Todd Monken has given an update.
On Friday, Oct. 30, just days before the Browns are set to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a Week 8 meeting, Monken announced that second-year signal caller Shedeur Sanders would retain the backup spot in the depth chart. Behind him will be Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green; however, he has yet to decide which player will serve as the emergency quarterback on game day.
Browns coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders will remain Cleveland's backup QB, but he has not yet decided whether to designate Taylen Green or Dillon Gabriel as the emergency QB on game day.
While Watson's spot seemed to always be locked down, especially considering the fact that he has the Browns sitting 5-2 and third in the AFC, where things shook out after him in the depth chart was a big talking point.
Gabriel, who was placed on the injured list before the regular season began, had previously been part of the competition for the backup role. However, when he was ruled out for the first few weeks due to a back injury, Sanders slid seamlessly into that spot.
But with Gabriel being cleared, the conversation began again on whether he would be able to be No. 2 in the depth chart.
Monken keeping Sanders in that spot, though, shows loyalty to the former Colorado Buffalo, who has reportedly been working hard in practice to keep himself sharp. Although he has not been handed the starting responsibilities, holding onto the backup spot is an important step in his development and path to seeing the field.
The Browns haven't completely ironed out the quarterback room, though, as Green and Gabriel do not know their roles just yet.
Green represents another developmental option for Cleveland, being selected in the later rounds of the 2026 NFL Draft. Gabriel, on the other hand, was taken with Sanders back in 2025. While he got a chance to be the Browns' starter last season, he didn't fare too well on the field, ultimately leading to him being benched.
All offseason, neither Green nor Gabriel was realistically considered to be the franchise's next starting quarterback.
Shedeur Sanders remains the backup QB. Todd Monken doesn't know if Taylen Green or Dillon Gabriel will be the emergency QB #Browns
Ultimately, the Browns have a deep quarterback room , and establishing roles for both Watson and Sanders for the rest of the season gives everyone involved some sort of stability and understanding of where they sit.
For now, Watson is the starter, Sanders is the backup and Gabriel and Green will likely bounce between third and fourth in the depth chart.
This weekend, the Browns will take on the Pittsburgh Steelers from Acrisure Stadium at 1:00 p.m. EST

title: What Deshaun Watson Still Needs To Do To Silence the Critics
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are one of the NFL's best teams this season.
Owning a 5-2 record through the first seven weeks of the 2026 regular season, the Browns sit atop the AFC North and rank third in the AFC at large.
To maintain such a strong start to the season, quarterback Deshaun Watson will have to keep silencing the critics as he builds a career-saving campaign. The 31-year-old has led the Browns to five game-winning drives, throwing for 1,482 yards and seven touchdowns along the way.
Here are three things that Watson needs to do to push any doubts about his game into the rearview mirror and continue leading the Browns to a playoff appearance this season:
While he has been good, consistency hasn't been on Watson's side.
After an abysmal performance in the season opener in Jacksonville, he turned the page and threw for 238 yards and two scores in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Against the Carolina Panthers a week later, Watson tossed for just under 150 yards and two touchdowns.
Such a dip in production is concerning, especially when looking to establish an offense that has plenty of young, impressionable pieces on it.
In Weeks 4 and 5, Watson yet again displayed that inconsistent approach. He threw for 268 yards, one touchdown and one interception against the Pittsburgh Steelers before dropping to 155 yards and one touchdown in a road loss to the New York Jets.
This trend of having a good game, then a relatively bad one, has followed him for nearly the entire season.
While he has turned his game on by the time the game comes to a close, consistency in the passing attack is going to be the difference maker between Watson's season being viewed as a real comeback or not.
It will also be the reason the Browns do make the playoffs or don't.
When the Browns have needed Watson the most, he has stepped up. There is no questioning that.
But you can't ignore the fact that if he had turned it on a bit earlier in the game, Cleveland wouldn't have had to fight back to put together a game-winning drive in the fourth.
The late victories are great to see, especially since they have gone Cleveland's way. All it takes, though, is a loss to end such a positive narrative.
If the Browns want to remain competitive in the AFC North and make a legitimate run in the postseason, Watson and the rest of the offense have to produce more consistent outings, instead of putting everything together when it is almost too late.
ESPN's Jeff Darlington put it best, saying that the Browns' identity right now is hard to sustain, especially later in the season.
"[Late-game wins] is their identity," Darlington said recently. The question is whether they can sustain that identity. This part of the season gets so interesting. This is a perfect example of it. Two teams sitting at the top of the division, trying to claim their identity. The question for both these teams is, ‘How real is it?’ Deshaun Watson has had late-game heroics in each of their five wins. Five fourth-quarter touchdown drives. I think the question becomes, 'Can he continue to do that?
"Can he sustain that type of late-game heroics?' I think this is a perfect barometer for both of these teams, and certainly a perfect barometer for Deshaun Watson."
Watson was known for being a mobile quarterback during his days with the Houston Texans.
However, after undergoing back-to-back Achilles injuries in Cleveland, many were concerned that he would never be able to return to such a level. Fortunately, through the first few games of the year, he has the skill set that made him such a dynamic quarterback.
Across seven games, Watson has totaled 215 yards and one touchdown on 48 carries on the ground. He is averaging just north of 30 yards rushing per game, which has complemented the offense nicely.
As long as he can keep this up, the Browns' offense will remain fluid and give them multiple avenues to slice and dice their way through a defense.
The Browns return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 1, to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers from Acrisure Stadium at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Browns Remain Behind in the Trade Market, But Here's How They Can Join The Fun
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may be out of playoff contention for the 2026 NFL season.
But the Cleveland Browns certainly are.
With the Trade Deadline looming, the Browns will look to bolster the roster on both sides of the ball to maintain a top spot in the AFC North. While both sides of the ball have a few holes to fill, the defensive line has been by far the most banged-up part of the squad.
In order to fortify the group and add to the already talented corps, the Browns should make a move for Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea.
On Thursday, Oct. 29, just two days after the Indianapolis Colts began their fire sale in the trade market, 247Sports' Easton Butler reported that the Buccaneers were fielding calls for Vea. The 6-foot-4, 347-pounder has been dominant for most of his career.
Now, at age 31, Vea is likely looking to be on a contending squad and play meaningful football when the calendar turns over to 2027.
The #Packers and the #Bengals have reportedly called the Buccaneers about DT Vita Vea again, per sources. pic.twitter.com/CJuxzKbSiF
Led by a group sporting second-year standout Mason Graham and exciting edge rusher Jared Verse , the Browns have a young, impressionable line to build around. Adding a player like Vea wouldn't shake up the locker room, but rather give them an experienced star to learn from.
Vea, across the last nine seasons, has dominated the trenches.
With two Pro Bowl selections to show for it, Vea has recorded a whopping 270 combined tackles, 83 quarterback hits, 49 tackles for a loss, 37 sacks and three forced fumbles. His height has also led to him posting 11 pass deflections as well.
Since 2021, Vea has recorded four or more sacks in a season each year , giving him the consistency that Cleveland's line would be looking for.
The biggest appeal of adding Vea would be his ability to improve the Browns' run defense, all while creating more opportunities for the young pass rushers to get into the backfield. Pairing Vea with the likes of Graham and Collins on the inside would give the Browns one of the best defensive fronts in football.
The only concern for adding a player of his status is the contract he is on.
In late August, Vea signed a contract extension with the Buccaneers, adding an extra six million to his $18 million he was already making. That means his contractual value brings him in at nearly $25 million, with another $24 million guaranteed in 2027.
The Browns would have to be willing to take on such a cap hit.
However, as the front office has shown in seasons past, they can finagle the books enough to make the deal work and spread the money out.
The recent trade of defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons to the Chicago Bears provides a useful benchmark for what the Browns should give up to land Vea.
The Bears were able to pull Simmons away from the Titans by sending two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder. That is a pretty big return for the Titans, but Simmons' 11-sack campaign in 2025 put his stock through the roof.
However, the Browns shouldn't be expected to pay that much.
Vea is good; there is no questioning that, but his value comes in at a more reasonable area. The Browns would likely have to give up two third-round picks and a fourth-round pick to pry Vea away. If they were willing to give up a second, due to the Buccaneers' demands, that could get the job done as well.
If Cleveland wants to genuinely compete by the time the regular season comes to a close, the front office should at least explore sacrificing a few draft picks at the trade deadline.
And if Vea ends up on the table, the trigger should be pulled.

title: How Jared Verse Stirred the Pot Ahead of Browns-Steelers Rematch
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a massive Week 8 rivalry matchup, with first place in the AFC North on the line. A war of words has added another layer of intensity ahead of Sunday’s matchup on Nov. 1.
The Cleveland Browns beat the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Thursday Night Football in Week 4 of the NFL season. In a chippy, back-and-forth game, the Browns defeated the Steelers on a game-winning 56-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt with 10 seconds remaining. Following the game, Browns star edge defender Jared Verse commented on the Steelers' offensive line and their style of play:
#Browns Jared Verse on the chippiness with the Steelers’ offensive line: “I was talking to them crazy. I was telling them, ‘You’re double-teaming, y’all sliding, y’all garbage.’ I don’t have any respect that plays too dirty and does too much extra stuff after the game." pic.twitter.com/9gzUMZEJh7
Verse claimed that the Steelers' offensive line played “dirty,” and while that is up to one’s interpretation, the Steelers’ locker room definitely took notice.
Cam Heyward appeared on The Rich Eisen Show ahead of the Browns-Steelers matchup on Tuesday, Oct. 27. On that episode, Eisen played the clip of Verse’s comments and asked the Steelers defensive tackle to respond:
Heyward defended his teammates and suggested Verse was whining about routine football tactics such as double-teams and chip blocks.  Verse is not a player to back down, and when he spoke to reporters Thursday, Verse had more to say.
Speaking to reporters Thursday, Verse responded directly to Heyward’s criticism. Verse made one thing clear: he is not worried about Heyward or the Steelers' offensive line:
“I’m not worried about Cam, I’m not worried about their OL, I’m not worried about anyone on their team,” - Jared Verse on the Steelers 👀👀👀 pic.twitter.com/KRdQhA2qBf
That confidence faces a significant test on the road. Cleveland has not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003, giving Verse an opportunity to help end a lengthy drought while backing up his latest comments. Verse kept his response short and simple as both teams continue to prepare for a pivotal AFC North matchup.
Ultimately, a war of words means little without results on the field. Verse has yet to record a sack through Cleveland’s first seven games of the season, and Heyward plays defense, meaning the two will not line up against each other. Both have bigger priorities Sunday, starting with disrupting the opposing quarterback.
What this back-and-forth does prove is one thing: the Browns and Steelers rivalry is very much back. Trash talk has long been part of this rivalry, but this meeting carries added weight with both teams entering at 5-2 . Both teams are focused on securing first place in the AFC North.
Now it’s time to see which team can back up its words on the field.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: Browns vs. Steelers: 5 Key Matchups That Could Decide Cleveland's Week 8 Showdown
full_text:
On the first of October, the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers faced off in the spotlight on Thursday Night Football with first place in the AFC North on the line. Exactly one month later, the two teams will do it all over again in Pittsburgh, with the division lead once again hanging in the balance.
The Steelers have not lost since the Week 4 matchup in Cleveland, and the Browns have only dropped a rain-soaked game in New York. Both teams head into the pivotal game at 5-2, with the Browns owning the tiebreaker for now. The Steelers are rolling, and the Browns will have to succeed in these five key matchups to come out of Pittsburgh with their stamp on first place.
It is cliché to point to stopping the run for a key to any game in the NFL; however, it rings true for Sunday. Jaylen Warren has rushed for over 100 yards three times this season, including 93 yards in his first matchup against the Browns. He is averaging 5.5 yards per carry this season and he can hit for a big play at any moment.
Rico Dowdle missed the first game in Cleveland, but he is back and can provide relief for Warren. The Steelers got away from utilizing Warren against the Browns, and the addition of Dowdle will help them be a more well-rounded offense.
The Browns defense has struggled giving up chunk plays against the run. The more Aaron Rodgers has to throw and take hits, the better the defense can be. The defensive line needs to plug holes and hit Warren before he can get a head of steam going downfield.
The offense finally had a good game running the ball last Sunday. Lanes were open and Judkins showed speed and strength hitting the holes. Dylan Sampson returned and shook off some rust by showing his speed on the outside. KC Concepcion even contributed on creative runs.
The rushing attack needs to be productive to keep Deshaun Watson from obvious passing downs and having the Steelers’ pass rushers feed off the home crowd to create havoc. Hopefully Todd Monken and the offense has unlocked a strategy to upstart the previously stagnant running game.
The first game between these two teams was slow going to start, then Ward picked off Rodgers and the offense came alive. The same was said last week against the Tennessee Titans and the team fed off the defensive leader’s turnover.
The Steelers’ receivers have been great this season, and they have a big-bodied tight end that provides a matchup problem. Rodgers has thrown the ball over 30 times in every game this season. He is not afraid to place the ball anywhere on the field, and the secondary has to communicate and be aware of their assignment to prevent any breakdowns. This game can come down to the turnover battle, and the Browns had two interceptions in the first matchup.
The Steelers pass rush has rattled Cleveland quarterbacks in recent years. The last time Watson played in Pittsburgh he threw a pick six to the defensive end, setting the tone for the game. Spencer Fano will have to continue his great rookie season against TJ Watt and keep Watson upright.
The ball got out of Watson’s hand faster last week in Tennessee and the offense put up 27 points. The defensive line knows that Watson has the propensity to hang onto the ball a little long and they will look to hit him hard. Monken and Watson have to take them out of the game and put the offense in manageable third downs to convert.
The Browns-Steelers rivalry matters. Todd Monken understands that. But when you prepare every week like it’s the biggest game you’ve ever played, your standard doesn’t change. The attention to detail, the focus, the weight room, rehab, practice and film study are already where…
Everyone is well aware that the Browns have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh in 23 years. Their roster is filled with rookies and second-year players, and they should not care about the failures that came before them.
“Well, it has nothing to do with our team. I mean, this year, whether it’s where we’re at record-wise, comparing the past or the history against the Steelers, it’s a divisional game," said Monken about playing in Pittsburgh. "It’s bigger because it’s obviously a divisional opponent. The fastest way to get in the playoffs is [to] win your division. ”
The youth on the roster will not have the pressure of winning in the Steel City, allowing them to play fast and free. Monken is rightfully treating this like any other game and is not letting the ghosts of teams’ past haunt the locker room.
The AFC North is up for grabs, and the Browns have the opportunity to be in first place past Week 8 for the first time since 2014. They are 2-2 on the road and 3-0 at home. If the Browns want the division to run through Cleveland, then it starts with them handling the keys to the game in Pittsburgh and changing history.

title: Will Browns Make QB Changes? Monken’s Recent Comments Leave Things Up in the Air
full_text:
Second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel is officially off the injury report and back in the lineup for the Cleveland Browns.
Gabriel, who the Browns selected in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, began the year on IR dealing with a back injury.
But how will his return shape up the quarterback room? Even Todd Monken is unsure as the question arose.
Todd Monken on how Dillon Gabriel's activation might change the QB order on Sunday: 'I haven't gotten there yet.'
Despite the young pup being available, it is no question the Browns will stick with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback.
Watson currently leads the NFL in game-winning drives with five. Currently, he is on track to get himself a brand-new deal to remain the Browns' starter after this season.
However, that is a different story. The main question with Gabriel being back with the team is where he fits.
Without the former Heisman candidate, the Browns had a nicely set depth chart with Watson as the starter, Shedeur Sanders as the backup, and rookie Taylen Green as the third string.
The reason why it worked so well was that Sanders is getting to learn from Watson as the backup, with Green as a possible option to bring in on plays the Browns want to utilize his athleticism.
Now, where does Gabriel fit? Clearly, Monken favors Sanders to be the backup, and with talks of potentially bringing in Green for designed plays, does that mean Gabriel is the fourth string?
While he will most likely slot in above Green, it does bring up another question.
Will the Browns look to deal Gabriel before the NFL trade deadline?
Let's say the Browns want to move on from Gabriel. Where could they send him and what could they get in return?
The best scenario for both parties is a situation where a team just lost their starting quarterback to injury. In that case, Gabriel would get the chance to actually compete for a starting job, and the Browns could get a slightly better package from a QB-needy team.
At the moment, a team that comes to mind would be the Philadelphia Eagles.
A potential package that could benefit the Browns could be sending Gabriel and a pick for tight end Dallas Goedert. This would fill a need of backup tight end for the Brown and Orange, while capitalizing on trading a young player.
As for now, Gabriel remains with the Browns and will find a spot to sit until something changes internally.
Who knows, maybe a team has had their eye on Gabriel since his time at Orgeon and believe in the 25 year old.
Regardless, it's time for the Browns to cut ties with the Hawaii native, who has shown disinterest in playing for the Browns. It truly does not seem like Gabriel is needed or fits on the team any longer.

title: NFL Insider Revives Maxx Crosby Trade Possibility For Cowboys Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
If the Dallas Cowboys do make a trade for an edge rusher before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, they have to swing for the fences.
That's because a minor addition isn't likely to change the fortune of a defense that has been awful this season . The problem is that elite edge rushers are rarely available, and when they are, teams are lining up down the block to acquire them and the price is high.
The Cowboys did try to pull off a blockbuster trade for Maxx Crosby back in March, but they were thwarted by the Baltimore Ravens, who ended up nixing the trade over a failed physical.
That seemed to close the door on a potential Crosby trade for the Cowboys, and that especially seemed to be the case after Crosby re-committed to the Las Vegas Raiders.
However, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero believes there is still a chance Crosby gets moved ahead of the deadline.
The reason for that has to do with the fact that Pelissero thinks the Raiders are still going to field calls on Crosby and if a big offer the likes of which the Chicago Bears sent the Tennessee Titans for Jeffery Simmons is on Raiders general manager Jon Spytek's desk, all bets are off.
"Maxx Crosby wants to be a Raider, he has no desire to leave, and he is definitely not forcing his way out. But GM John Spytek is sure to get calls over the next 10 days, leaving open the possibility of another blockbuster," Pelissero wrote .
"If a 29-year-old Jeffrey Simmons can get traded for two first-round picks and more, why can’t a 29-year-old Maxx Crosby?" Pelissero asked. "And if the Raiders were willing to trade him for that package in March, why wouldn’t they do it again now if the value is there to accelerate their rebuild?"
The Cowboys will probably have to throw a Godfather-style offer at the Raiders to get Crosby like the Bears did to the Titans in a deal that included two first-round picks and a swap of Day 3 selections.
The Ravens pulled off their March deal for Crosby after giving up two first-rounders, so that's the least the Raiders will likely take.
We say "the least" because it's possible the price has gone up since the Raiders might be less inclined to trade him because of the messy situation it would create now that Crosby wants to stay.
The Cowboys weren't willing to offer two first-rounders back in March and it's hard to know if their stance has changed since.
It's possible their stance has given how bad the Cowboys have looked on defense, but it's also possible it hasn't because of how little draft capital the Cowboys have currently. Granted, they do have first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, but Dallas has just 10 selections in total between those two years.
We tend to believe Crosby isn't going anywhere, but after seeing the Simmons deal go down, and knowing the sense of urgency Jones has expressed in recent years, never say never.
