title: Cowboys Trade Rumor From NFL Insider Lays Out Unusual Possible Deadline Strategy
full_text:
One issue the Dallas Cowboys have as they navigate the next week-plus before the trade deadline is the lack of draft capital.
Because of his wheeling and dealing in recent years, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones doesn't have a ton to operate with, with the Cowboys having just four picks in next year's draft.
Dallas does have six in the 2028 NFL Draft, but the team is missing its second-round pick and we also know that teams prefer picks that come sooner rather than later in trades.
Because of the Cowboys' lack of draft capital, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones is hearing that the Cowboys might have a "difficult" time making trades at the deadline.
He also wonders if the Cowboys might try and make a player-for-player trade instead of the typical player-for-pick deals we see.
"Jerry Jones is always down to make a deal, but sources there think a pick-for-player trade would be difficult considering what Dallas has left," Jones said on Saturday. "Player-for-player trades have always been rare in the league, but if Dallas acquires help, maybe that’s their method."
Jones has poured cold water on the notion that the Cowboys are 100% locked into making a trade.
Jones continues to say he's open to making a trade , but Jones also said it's "unlikely we'll get the opportunity from outside coming in."
More recently, Jones admitted he isn't feeling an added sense of urgency after some  blockbuster trades around the NFL and "it would have to be a dynamic situation to give up (draft) picks."
This could be posturing from Jones, but it sure seems like the Cowboys owner is accepting the reality of the situation he's in.
It takes two to tango to make a trade and the price has to be right. Jones also has to weigh how much more he wants to dump into this team knowing another trade might not fix things.
The problem with a player-for-player trade is the Cowboys are very unlikely to land the kind of substantial addition they need.
That's because the Cowboys would have to give up one of their best players to get something significant done and how many of those guys can the Cowboys even afford to give up?
The answer is not many, if any.
One player who immediately comes to mind is wideout George Pickens, who is the best combination of valuable and possibly available on Dallas' roster.
Pickens is on the franchise tag , which means he's set to be a free agent in 2027 once again unless the Cowboys tag him or extend him.
We continue to believe the latter approach won't be something the Cowboys seriously consider because paying hefty money to two wideouts will seriously hinder Dallas' ability to improve other positions.
Chances are he won't be amenable to the tag again, which could lead to a holdout situation if the Cowboys take that route. If the Cowboys do keep him on the tag again, the price will be higher and all of the money will be on the books for 2027, which will seriously hinder Dallas' cap situation.
Trading Pickens right now would be a blow to the offense, but it's not like the Cowboys are having much success with him on the team, anyway, and that's because their defense stinks.
All that said, we find it highly unlikely the Cowboys will trade Pickens during the season and if a big trade does go down, it'll involve Dallas giving up more draft capital and maybe a lesser player thrown in to sweeten the deal.

title: Troy Aikman Admits He Put Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones in Awkward Position
full_text:
Troy Aikman has been a hot topic as of late now that his furure with ESPN is in doubt. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback has become one of the most successful broadcasters in the business, but following an extension announcement for Joe Buck, Aikman's future became murky.
While discussing his plans going forward, Aikman has hinted that he wouldn't mind moving into a front office role. He even got a taste for that lifestyle this year, working as a consultant with the Miami Dolphins.
Of course, what fans really want to know is if Aikman would be interested in helping the Cowboys get back on track. The three-time Super Bowl winner said that's something that appeals to him , but he has since expressed some regret in making those statements out loud.
While appearing on The Musers , Aikman said he was answering the questions honestly, but his regret is that he put Jerry Jones in a tough situation. Jones, who is the owner and general manager of the Cowboys, has been asked about bringing in Aikman and as the former quarterback says, there's really not a good answer Jones can give at this point.
“The last thing that I want is, I was answering a question, and I think it’s really unfair to Jerry that he then has to answer these questions,” Aikman during an appearance on The Musers . “As far as, ‘Hey, would you bring Troy back, or would you have a role for him?’ I mean there’s no real good answer that he can give.”
“We briefly touched on it just because I felt that maybe I backed him into a corner that he didn’t deserve to be backed into. He didn’t ask for it. And so, we’re clear on that. He totally understood, and yet, we was very complimentary if something like that were to ever take place with the idea that we’re not having those conversations at this time.”
While many fans might be getting excited about the fact that Jones and Aikman have both kept the door open, Ed Werder isn't buying it . He doesn't believe Aikman and Jones would be "compatible" in the same front office, and it's hard to argue against that.
Jones likes to be in charge and has surrounded himself with family members who share his vision. Adding someone such as Aikman who has never been shy about speaking his mind honestly feels like a recipe for disaster.
Aikman has enough football knowledge to be wildly successful in a lead role, but Jones isn't the type of owner who would give him the free rein he would need.

title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Admits No Urgency to Keep Up With NFC Arms Race Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
Some massive trades have gone down in the NFC this week, which you would assume raises the Dallas Cowboys' urgency level to do something massive before the NFL trade deadline.
The three big trades to go down this week were the Seattle Seahawks acquiring guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts, the San Francisco 49ers trading for DeForest Buckner , also with the Colts, and the Chicago Bears pulling off a blockbuster in their trade with the Tennessee Titans for Jeffery Simmons.
All three of those trades stand to improve those teams massively and are of the ilk that the Cowboys should be looking to make for their struggling defense.
But, with just about a week and a half to go before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said those aren't leaving him with added urgency and it would take a massive opportunity for the Cowboys to part with more picks.
"Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says on 105.3 The Fan that he doesn’t feel like they need to make a trade to keep up with other teams around the league," The Athletic's Jon Machota relayed.
“It would have to be a dynamic situation to give up (draft) picks," Jones said.
Jones isn't saying anything we really didn't know already. We have always figured the Cowboys would aim super high because this team's defense isn't a minor addition away from improving.
Instead, it's going to take multiple things to fall into place. Not only do the Cowboys need a true game-changer along the edge, but Dallas also has to get healthy , which the team is in the process of doing with several players expected back in the next week or so.
Even with all that, it might not be enough. That's because Dallas also has a coaching issue with defensive coordinator Christian Parker, whose play-calling has left a lot to be desired, to put it nicely.
And defensive coaching isn't the only issue. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer hasn't done an adequate job on the offensive side of the ball, either.
In the next week-plus, Jones has got to weigh if it's worth giving up more draft capital from an already depleted stable of picks to try and save this team.
As we stand here today, we would say it isn't, but we also aren't Jerry Jones, who is almost certainly more optimistic about this team than we and the vast majority of Cowboys fans are.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Shares Reason for Excitement About Cowboys' Struggling Defense
full_text:
There really isn't much to be excited about when it comes to the Dallas Cowboys' 2026 defense.
Dallas enters Week 8 ranked dead-last against the run, 24th in points allowed per game and 20th in pass defense.
It's even hard to get excited after the Cowboys put together one of their best defensive performances in Week 7 , when they allowed 21 points to the Philadelphia Eagles, which was the Cowboys' second-fewest points allowed in a game this season.
That's because the Eagles weren't close to full strength . Philly did not have the services of quarterback Jalen Hurts or his top-two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, and Saquon Barkley wasn't healthy and was in and out of the game.
One thing the Cowboys do have going for them is the fact that their defense has gotten healthier in recent weeks, and will continue to do so in the weeks ahead.
And that has head coach Brian Schottenheimer excited for the outlook of his defense.
"You felt (DeMarvion Overshown) coming back, I thought that was great," Schotty said on 105.3 The Fan . "I think getting healthy is a big part of it."
"Overall, I think the health of this defense is what's getting us really excited," he added. "We're getting bodies back and that's huge for us."
Health has no doubt been a factor in the Cowboys' poor showing on defense in 2026, as the unit has been ravaged by injuries at almost every position.
While the edge rushers room has managed to stay healthy, Dallas has been missing players along the defensive line, at linebacker, cornerback and safety.
Jonathan Bullard has missed all but three games , but he was designated to return from injured reserve on Thursday, so he's coming back soon.
At linebacker, Overshown has missed a handful of games and Dee Winters is now hurt and is slated to miss his second game .
At cornerback, Cobie Durant has missed four contests and even new cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been banged-up. Safety has been hampered by injuries, also, with Malik Hooker, Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke all missing time.
Hooker has since returned, but Locke and Thompson are both on IR, although Locke is close after he had his 21-day practice window opened up last week.
At this point, the defense getting healthy is one of the last shreds of hope there is for this unit to improve moving forward. The other is a blockbuster trade for a game-changing edge rusher, but we know that's not something Dallas can depend on.
But even if the Cowboys can get back to full strength and acquire the edge rusher they need, there's still a coaching problem with defensive coordinator Christian Parker, and until that improves, Dallas' ceiling will remain low.

full_text:

title: 7 Cowboys Who Could Be Traded Away if Dallas Becomes Seller at NFL Deadline
full_text:
All of the talk surrounding the Dallas Cowboys has been about the team making a move to add to its roster, and more specifically, to the defense.
It's not hard to see why. Jerry Jones has said time and time again he is open to making at least one more move , and Dallas could certainly use a marquee addition to its putrid defense.
But the Cowboys are also on the brink of Jones having to wonder if it's even worth it to try and save this team with another trade at the expense of shipping off another pick or more.
At 3-4, the Cowboys are very much in the thick of things in the NFC East, but the division also stinks and Dallas isn't anywhere near being able to compete for a Super Bowl, which is the real goal.
If the Cowboys were to lose both of their next two games and fall to 3-6, could they turn around and end up selling at the deadline? Not likely, but we can't rule it out, either.
If that happens, here's seven players who could get moved.
Pickens will be a free agent in 2027 and we remain highly skeptical about the Cowboys' chances of being able to retain him long term. Even Stephen Jones has said that will be difficult to do and, quite frankly, this year has once again taught us that having two great receivers means jack if the defense isn't good.
It also feels like the relationship is starting to deteriorate a bit after head coach Brian Schottenheimer called Pickens out for his poor run-blocking, and there have been effort concerns overall.
This might be the best time to sell Pickens because teams are more desperate at the trade deadline than they are during the offseason, when there are more options.
A team like the Kansas City Chiefs might be willing to pay a hefty price for a wide receiver like Pickens who would instantly be the No. 1 in Andy Reid's offense.
Ferguson has been a total disaster for the Cowboys this season. Not only has he been a terrible blocker, but the veteran tight end has struggled with drops and has even lost a crucial fumble.
He's currently in the midst of his worst season production-wise since his rookie campaign in 2022, and Brevyn Spann-Ford is getting a push as the new TE1 as a result of his struggles.
The Cowboys are surely regretting Ferguson's contract and could look to unload at least a portion of it on a team that needs a boost in the pass-catching department at tight end.
Dallas would get some much-needed future cap relief and a draft pick to replenish their dwindling stable.
Schoonmaker is on his way out of Dallas after this season after he was demoted to TE3 in favor of Brevyn Spann-Ford, who has now seemingly ascended to TE1 with Ferguson's struggles.
Schoonmaker isn't going to garner much, and perhaps as little as a late-round pick swap, but that's better than the nothing Dallas will get when he leaves in free agency in 2027.
We could see Schoonmaker getting traded even if Dallas doesn't wave the white flag on this season. Moving the veteran would also allow Dallas to open up snaps for rookie Michael Trigg.
We had Hooker pegged as a player who could be moved either via cut or trade before the season started after Dallas made several additions to the safeties room this past offseason.
However, Hooker managed to stick and has actually found himself in a key role after P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson both landed on injured reserve.
We still find it hard to believe that Hooker's relationship with Dallas will extend beyond 2026, so trading him away is a logical move.
Not only is Overshown going to be a free agent in 2027, he is also repped by David Mulugheta and after the Micah Parsons fiasco, we don't need to tell you why that decreases Overshown's chances of re-signing in Dallas.
And, truth be told, the Cowboys shouldn't be interested in bringing him back anyway. Overshown needed to shed the injury-prone label in 2026, but he has already missed a handful of games .
Of all the players who could conceivably be traded away by Dallas at the deadline, Overshown is the one who could net the second-best return after Pickens.
Jones was brought in to compete with Terence Steele at right tackle, but Steele has been good enough to hold on to the job, leaving Jones in a backup role that has allowed him to see the playing field for 21 snaps, with 11 of those coming as an extra blocker.
The trade that saw the Cowboys give up a 2027 third-rounder and a 2027 sixth-round pick in exchange for Jones and a 2027 fourth-rounder is not looking too hot right now, to say the least.
With teams always in the market for more offensive line help, it's possible Dallas could find a suitor for Jones to regain the late-round pick the team gave up as part of the trade.
The overwhelming excite for Miller's homecoming has turned into total disgust after what has been a disastrous tenure over seven games.
Miller has not so much as tallied a single sack and has fallen well short of expectations, even for a 37-year-old edge rusher. If this continues, not only could Miller leave after this season, he may retire.
An over-the-hill edge rusher with zero sacks doesn't exactly sound attractive, but we know Miller plays a premium position, so he may still draw interest. At this point, getting a late Day 3 pick for Miller would amount to a massive win for the Cowboys.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Cowboys vs Cardinals in Week 8
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys look to do something on Sunday that they haven't done all year and win a second consecutive game. They knocked off the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 and while the Eagles were banged up, it was a still a confidence-building win for a team that needed something positive to build on.
This weekend, they face a struggling Cardinals team that is 2-1, but has lost five of their past six games. It's a golden opportunity for the Cowboys to get back into the NFC East race , but they have to face their demons to get the win.
Dallas has lost eight of their past nine games against Arizona , including a Monday Night Football showdown last year. Turning their luck around becomes far more likely if these three bold predictions come true.
The Cowboys finally stuck with the run in Week 7 and Javonte Williams rewarded them with 155 yards. This week, look for him to continue to get the ball, especially against the Cardinals who are 23rd in the league against the run .
Williams looked like the player we saw in 2025 and that should continue, especially with offensive coordinator Klayton Adams facing his previous team this week. In this first bold prediction, Williams goes for 125 yards and rushes another touchdown.
DeMarvion Overshown made his much anticipated return to action in Week 7 and he was excellent. He had six tackles, one tackle for loss, batted down one pass, and hauled in an interception. He provided the exact spark that the defense had been missing, and that was without having any time to shake off the rust.
Now that he has a full game under his belt for the first time this season, look for Overshown to continnue to shine. His presence helps as the Cowboys defense puts the pressure on Jacoby Brissett and forces two turnovers, one of which comes courtesy of Overshown.
Dak Prescott went into Week 7 facing a bit of a slump. He had just two touchdowns and four interceptions over the previous two games, both of which were losses for Dallas. He responded well in Week 7, throwing for 212 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions.
There were still some areas to clean up, specifically with his accuracy. Prescott completed just 55.6 percent of his attempts, which is below his season average of 65.2 percent . Look for him to get that number up against the Cardinals, which helps as Prescott throws for at least 300 yards with two touchdowns against the Cardinals.

title: Dallas Cowboys' NFL Trade Deadline Strategy Suggests Major Activity
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and the Dallas Cowboys have once again been linked to a handful of high-profile players with less than two weeks left to make a move.
Dallas is expected to be in the market for an impact defensive player, with a strong focus on available talent to help the pass rush.
One common name linked to the Cowboys has been Arizona Cardinals star Josh Sweat , who the team will get a good look at this weekend when they welcome the Cardinals to AT&T Stadium , while there is still a pipe dream surrounding Las Vegas Raiders superstar Maxx Crosby .

title: Broncos Week 8 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Harvey, Waddle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos unveiled their final injury report and game designations for Sunday's first-place home meeting with the Kansas City Chiefs.
Denver will officially be without safety Talanoa Hufanga for another game as he tends to a weeks-long ankle issue. The team also ruled out running back RJ Harvey, who suffered a knee injury during Thursday's practice and was considered limited . Speaking Friday, head coach Sean Payton failed to elaborate on Harvey's status.
Rookie RB Jonah Coleman is slated to see an increased workload aside -- or perhaps ahead of -- veteran starter J.K. Dobbins. Former practice-squad S Taylor Rapp will continue filling in for Hufanga, who could be back for Week 9 at Carolina.
The Broncos listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( chest ), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), left tackle Garett Bolles (hip), and defensive end Zach Allen (hamstring) as questionable to suit up against the Chiefs. Each player was limited in practice Friday; Jones' injury first popped up Thursday, while Waddle and Allen were upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) earlier in the week.
Sai'vion Jones would likely start if Allen were forced to sit. Should Waddle miss Sunday's contest or be limited in any capacity, the Broncos should make a concerted effort to get WR Marvin Mims more involved .
“Sometimes it’s coverage and then it’s trying to find those personnel groupings where we’ve got a number of guys that are healthy and playing well. So hopefully we can find those opportunities," Payton said of Mims on Wednesday.
The team will make a final decision on the questionables at least 90 minutes prior to kickoff on Sunday, when inactives are due.
Denver also listed Mims (ankle), inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) as full participants. None of these players carry designations and will play at Empower Field at Mile High. Surtain is making his return following a three-game absence.
On the other side, Kansas City ruled out defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, and listed cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed and Mansoor Delane and defensive end R Mason Thomas as questionable. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is expected to play after sitting the last two games.
One of the aforementioned players is quietly an anchor on a defense that's arguably playing the best ball in the league over the last month. That player is Malcolm Roach, who's recorded 20 total tackles, (12 solo stops), 2.5 sacks, and four passes defensed across the first seven games of the season.
Roach, who's in his first year with the Broncos, currently ranks as the 42nd-best interior defensive linemen among 126 qualifiers, according to Pro Football Focus. His 69.4 pass-rush grade is good for 25th.
Payton knows the importance of Roach to his elite defensive unit -- especially so with Allen now nursing his hammy.
“I think I would say this: he does a lot of things well," he said Wednesday. "The other thing as an NFL player, you know exactly what you’re getting that’s very helpful then when you’re putting a gameplan together. Then all the other things with his personality and you guys have been around him, he’s consistent. I think that’s important to find those type of players in your front.”

title: J.K. Dobbins Sets Record Straight on Broncos RB Controversy
full_text:
J.K. Dobbins and the Denver Broncos have obviously heard to rumors over the past week.
Dobbins's body language in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals last week was curious, and after a handful of early carries, the veteran's role gave way to rookie Jonah Coleman in the second half. Dobbins did get a goal-line carry in the second half, which he punched in from the 1-yard line, but aside from that, the Broncos mostly kept him on the bench while protecting a sizable lead.
Dobbins said there was a good reason for that, though. And he clearly doesn't appreciate the rumors that he's unhappy or that there's something greater at work to explain his diminished role last week. We've questioned it here at Denver Broncos On SI , too. We've also noted the rising trade rumors linking the Broncos to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
"We were winning pretty good, right? Weren't we?" Dobbins asked 9NEWS ' Mike Klis on Thursday in a curious exchange from his locker. "Everybody wants me to play 17 games, correct? So can you take that into account before you start saying stuff like that? Because the coaches have a plan."
Dobbins referenced his " pinky promise " with the local press this past summer, a sacred covenant vowing to appear in all 17 games this season. He played the first 10 games of last year before suffering a foot injury in Week 10 that ended his first year as a Bronco.
The Broncos not only re-signed Dobbins, but they also gave him a 4x raise on a two-year, $16 million deal this past spring. What he's saying about the coaches' plan for him holds water; the Broncos want to get a good return on their investment, so in games where they're blowing out an opponent, there's not much reason to expose him to unnecessary wear and tear.
Dobbins still takes pride in coaching the young running backs behind him on the depth chart. Dobbins has looked out for RJ Harvey, and he says that veteran leadership applies to Coleman this year, too.
"This organization has a plan for me, and I'm always there to coach my young guys," Dobbins said. "I've said this from the beginning: RJ is my rookie. And we've got another rookie in Jonah. I'm coaching them to make their plays because I want to see them succeed."
Dobbins assured local reporters that his primary motivation is to win games.
"We were up by a lot," Dobbins said. "I want to win the game, and I also want to win in the playoffs and eventually get to the Super Bowl. So, to say... No, we're winning the game."
If the Broncos were losing games and Dobbins wasn't getting starter touches, it might be a different story, he said. But the Broncos are 5-2 and coming off a brutal initial six-game gauntlet to start this season, and that high level of defensive competition goes a long way toward explaining why he's averaged a career-low 3.3 yards per carry.
"I like to consider myself a pro," Dobbins said. "Now, if we're losing, and I'm not getting the carries, s**t, I'm going to be mad as f***. Sorry, excuse my language. But if we're winning and it's working,"
All three of Denver's top running backs contributed their fair share to last week's road win over the Cardinals. Harvey took a screen pass 52 yards to the house. Coleman led the team with nine rushes for 54 yards, closing the game out with some strong running to keep the clock running, while Dobbins scored his third straight touchdown of the season.
The Broncos have a talented backfield, which is one of the reasons why their rushing offense being ranked 24th entering Week 8 is so mystifying. However, Dobbins said there's a reason for that: the quality of opposing defenses the offensive line and backs have faced.
"I mean, shoot, we've got good running backs," Dobbins said. "When I get out there—I know you guys want to bring up the numbers and me having a lower average than normal, because I always have five yards a carry—like, I just played six great defenses, all in a row."
Dobbins believes that the familiarity that Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdaniel and the Los Angeles Chargers have with him only intensified his struggles against those two defenses. Plus, the Jacksonville Jaguars were interested in signing Dobbins this past offseason, so as a matter of pride, they were focused on not letting him have a big day, in his opinion.
"To think that an NFL coach—the Seahawks coach, I was with him in Baltimore, so he knows me well," Dobbins said. "The Chargers know me well. The Jacksonville Jaguars, they wanted me in the offseason. You think they're just going to let me run it up their tails? No."
Dobbins believes the noise surrounding him and the Broncos' ground game has been "blown out of proportion." As the Broncos' schedule opens up a little bit, his theory about the strength of schedule will be put to the test.
Dobbins gets a Kansas City Chiefs defense this week that's currently ranked 13th against the run, allowing just 99.5 yards per game on the ground. Then he draws the Carolina Panthers, whose defense is in shambles after firing coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday .
The NFL trade deadline is two days after the Panthers game. Time will tell whether these Taylor trade rumors are smoke or fire, but if Dobbins wants to keep the Broncos from leaning in that direction, he'll have to make some hay over the next two games.
He's healthy, though, and with Coleman helping to shoulder some of the between-the-tackles load, Dobbins has a great opportunity to start turning the ship around. The veteran back believes there's still plenty of season left to get his numbers back up, and while that's true, the Broncos will likely be looking for assurances on that front over the next two weeks because after November 10, they won't have the freedom to make an in-season trade.
"We'll get it back above five (yards per carry)," Dobbins said. "It's a long season. I'm feeling great. The coaches are doing everything to keep me healthy, and when I'm healthy, I think I'm dangerous."
There's a reason the Broncos made Dobbins available at his locker on Thursday. The team may indeed be considering making a move ahead of the deadline, but they apparently wanted to nip the rumors surrounding Dobbins's purported dissatisfaction in the bud.
Dobbins is going to continue to start, but as I wrote earlier this week, if the efficiency isn't there, the Broncos have to be willing to lean on Coleman because the rookie's burst and twitchiness have given the rushing offense an explosive edge that has been completely lacking this season. That's been the case in the two games Coleman has received carries, anyway.
Harvey popped up on Thursday's practice report with a knee injury , so don't be surprised if Coleman again out-earns Dobbins in snap share because he's a more proficient receiver and pass protector. The Broncos have the horses in the backfield, but it's time to get more consistent production out of the group of talented players.
Dobbins may end up with more carries on Sunday against the Chiefs, but if Harvey can't go or is limited because of his injury, look for the Broncos to again rely on their fourth-round rookie.
At the very least, it'll be interesting to see how Dobbins responds against Kansas City after an awkward week. Iron always sharpens iron, but now he has something to prove.
What better way to do that than by having a big day in a game that will decide the AFC West leader at the midway point of the season?

title: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Chiefs Rematch
full_text:
The Denver Broncos entered the 2026 with a few prime objectives, the first of which is winning the AFC West.
The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training.
Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak.
The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule.
How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires.
Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time?
Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Ultimately, it's an ugly one, but a win for Denver against the Chiefs, who lack pop offensively outside of Walker
Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 5-2 : The Broncos were not good in Week 1 but have played better since. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are still a quality team but not a dominant one. I think the Broncos' defense has put its season-opening issues behind them, and the offense is showing improvement. Here's to hoping Nix plays with more confidence, Jonah Coleman makes an impact, and Marvin Mims Jr. steps up again, with the Broncos finding a way to win at home . Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 20
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 4-3 : I can't remember the last time a Week 8 game had so much on the line. The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 4-3 : The Seahawks proved that if you stop Walker, you almost completely neuter the Chiefs' offense. The Chiefs don't have the skill-position players to make you pay on a consistent basis. Denver did a fairly good job of bottling up the Chiefs' run game at the line of scrimmage in Week 1, but couldn't get Walker to the ground due to poor tackling. That won't be the case this time around. Bolstered by arguably the best home-field advantage in the league, I fully expect a rambunctious defensive performance and the Broncos to be in first place in the AFC West on Sunday night. Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 16
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 3-4 : If the Broncos want to repeat as division champs, this is the game to make it so. The Broncos have been playing better football of late, and Nix certainly looks healthier, but they have fundamental flaws, and the Chiefs are one of the teams best primed to expose them. Moving to Coleman is a welcome change and should provide a shot in the arm for the running game, but the performance of Travis Kelce and Walker against Denver's linebackers key a Chiefs win, as Kansas City finds a way to generate the explosive plays the Broncos do not. Pick : Chiefs 31, Broncos 14
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 3-4 : Nix bounced back against a terrible Arizona Cardinals defense, and the Chiefs are next. Kansas City's defense has struggled this season, so the opening is there for Nix to keep up his play. There's a chance to take the division lead in this one, but can the offense do enough, and can the defense tackle Walker and company? Denver wants to send a message that the first game was a fluke, with a 29.8% missed-tackle rate among other statistical outliers. However, Denver wins thanks to some big-time decisions from Sean Payton late, including going for a two-point conversion after a touchdown.
Pick : Broncos 32, Chiefs 24
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 3-4 : The Broncos handled the Cardinals but now must turn their attention to the Chiefs, who embarrassed them to open the season. The Broncos showed more life on offense last week, but Waddle's likely absence means Mims has to step up and contribute. The game being played in Denver may be the difference-maker, and I'm going with the Broncos to take the AFC West lead from the Chiefs' clutches. Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17

title: Broncos' Trade Interest in Jonathan Taylor is Real, Insider Claims
full_text:
Despite the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, the Denver Broncos are keeping one eye on the NFL trade market 11 days ahead of the deadline.
The Indianapolis Colts' fire sale is on; they've already dealt away All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and Pro Bowl defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. All eyes are now on star running back Jonathan Taylor, including those of the Broncos, according to NFL On Prime insider James Palmer.
"They are one of the teams, I'm told, that is monitoring the Jonathan Taylor situation. It's more than likely he stays there in Indianapolis, but they are keeping an eye there," Palmer said of the Broncos .
This isn't the first we've heard of a Broncos-Taylor connection. Before last week's game against the Arizona Cardinals, Adam Schefter linked the Broncos to Indy's Pro Bowl running back.
Entering Week 8's rematch with the Chiefs, the Broncos' run game ranks 24th in the NFL, averagin 94.9 yards per game. The Broncos believe their rushing struggles are largely attributed to the tough slate of elite defenses they faced through the first six weeks of the season, including top running back J.K. Dobbins.
There could be some truth to that, as the Broncos' ground attack finally showed some signs of life last week against the Arizona Cardinals, whose defense is not ranked high. However, there was a big outlier play in Bo Nix's 62-yard touchdown run.
Corresponding to Denver's improved rushing efficiency last week as the return of Coleman from injured reserve. He led the team in rushing and snaps , averaging 6.0 yards per carry on nine totes. Dobbins took a back seat to the rookie last week, but the veteran assured reporters on Thursday that he's not upset or dissatisfied with his current role, and cares only about winning.
Coleman certainly added a different energy and burst to the Broncos' offense, and it's likely the front office will be watching to see if the rookie and Dobbins can show some more signs of life between now and November 10 before making a decision on potentially pursuing a trade.
Sean Payton has always implemented a running-back-by-committee approach, and even though the Broncos just paid Dobbins, it's still been a rotation. If you trade for Taylor, though, you're wanting to keep him on the field and get your money's worth, but then again, putting him at the top of a committee, with the lion's share of the touches, could help preserve his health and extend his career.
Taylor would be costly, not only to acquire from the Colts, but he just signed a two-year, $44 million extension before the season started. He has a $16.1 million cap number this season. However, his cap numbers climb to $21 million and $22.98 million in 2027 and 2028, respectively.
The Broncos have a couple years left of cost control on Nix, even if they opt to sign him to an extension next offseason when he becomes eligible, so if they team was of a mind to go all-in, it could find room for Taylor. It really would come down to whether the Broncos believed Taylor would be the missing piece to put them over the top.
The three-time Pro Bowler and former NFL rushing champion is a great player, and if there's anything that coud hold back the Broncos from achieving their goals this season, it would be their bottom-10 rushing attack. Taylor would upgrade that immediately, and give Nix a proven foundation to build on.
Taylor and Dobbins are roughly the same age (27). Both will turn 28 in the not too distant future, so the Broncos would have to factor in his age and the high amount of wear-and-tear on Taylor's tires.
As we're seeing around the league, the contenders are swinging for the fences ahead of the deadline. The Chicago Bears gave up multiple first-round picks for Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, while the Seattle Seahawks just landed Nelson, and the San Francisco 49ers acquired Buckner.
The Broncos plan to be contenders now and in the future, but if they really want to capitalize on what remains of Nix's rookie contract, a big move like trading for Taylor would make sense. But it would be contingent on how the next two games unfold for Dobbins and Coleman.
If it's more rushing inconsistencies, it wouldn't shock me to see the Broncos swing for the fences on Taylor. The Broncos have two games between now and the deadline — the Chiefs this week and the Carolina Panthers next — but depending on the market for Taylor, they may not have the luxury of waiting until after Week 9 to make a decision.
That's why the Broncos are, ostensibly, monitoring the Taylor situation. Stay tuned.

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Revenge Win Over Chiefs in Week 8
full_text:
Denver Broncos fans would like to forget the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium, when the Kansas City Chiefs dominated for almost the entire game. Aside from the Broncos getting an early touchdown, there wasn't much positive about their play.
Since then, the Broncos have gotten better, though they still have areas to clean up, particularly on offense. They may not enter this Week 8 matchup with their starting lineup fully intact, though, with several players limited in practice this week .
However, the Broncos still have a chance to win their rematch with the Chiefs if they can do a better overall job of execution. The Chiefs, to their credit, have played well since Week 1, aside from a bad outing against the Seattle Seahawks last week, but they aren't a juggernaut by any means.
Still, the Broncos have to make sure that things don't go down as they did in Week 1 if they want to win this game. Let's break down three keys to winning the rematch with the Chiefs, all harkening back to Week 1 when these teams first met.
One of the top reasons the Broncos lost the season opener was that the defense had no answer for the Chiefs' most notable free-agent signing of 2026. Walker, coming off a Super Bowl MVP award, immediately made an impact, and it came at the Broncos' expense.
Walker rushed for 173  yards on 23 carries with one rushing touchdown. If you take away his longest run of 60 yards, he still made a clear impact with 113 yards rushing on the other 22 carries. He also had three catches for 18 yards and a touchdown.
While Walker is not the only player the Broncos need to be concerned about, the fact is that the defense's inability to limit him was a big reason for the season-opening loss. When Walker was able to dictate the game, the Broncos' pass rush was effectively neutralized, and it mattered not who was protecting Patrick Mahomes, whose offensive line has dealt with injury issues this season.
Part of the reason Walker dominated was that the Broncos missed too many tackles or took bad angles when defending the run. They have cleaned that up in recent weeks, but they still need to be disciplined and avoid those mistakes if they want to contain him.
If the Broncos can bottle up Walker, the Chiefs will have to pass more often, and that would give the pass rush the chance to do more damage. It won't be an easy task, as Mahomes has taken just seven sacks in seven games, but the opportunities for the Broncos' pass rush will increase if the Chiefs can't get the running game going.
It's worth noting that Travis Kelce had a 59-yard gain on a reception in Week 1, but that again goes back to the lack of discipline by the Broncos' defense. However, Kelce was otherwise quiet. Thus, while Kelce can still do good things, Walker is the player the Broncos need to focus on containing to have a chance against the Chiefs' offense.
The Broncos had two players in Week 1 who didn't get any touches on offense. Both players are coming off good performances against the Arizona Cardinals last week.
The first is Coleman, who got just 6% of the offensive snaps in Week 1 and was otherwise limited to special teams. The coaching staff relied on J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, with the former held to 36 yards on eight carries and the latter getting just three carries for 18 yards, along with four receptions for 23 yards.
Dobbins hasn't been effective since then, but Harvey has shown he can make an impact. In the meantime, Coleman has proven he should have a bigger role in the offense, particularly after rushing for 54 yards on nine carries against the Cardinals.
The Broncos need to get Coleman more involved in the offense this week. His ankle didn't appear to be bothering him last week, and his presence could do a lot to take some pressure off Bo Nix if he can be the spark in the running game.
Mims was limited in the season opener as he was recovering from a foot injury suffered in the preseason. Now, though, Mims may be poised for an increased role as Jaylen Waddle's Week 8 availability is in question due to a chest injury.
Even if Waddle is cleared to play, his snaps may be limited. That means Mims could be in line for more snaps on offense. The fourth-year receiver has shown he can still contribute on offense, as he had two catches for 53 yards last week, including a 47-yard reception that showed Nix is perfectly capable of attacking downfield.
Coleman and Mims in the mix gives the Broncos more options on offense and that could be an important step to an improved offensive showing — as could the next person we'll mention.
While not everything that happened on offense in the opener was Nix's fault, he didn't look confident. After doing all right on the Broncos' only touchdown drive, he was hesitant to take shots, regardless of the situation, and demonstrated poor pocket presence.
It led to Nix being sacked three times — the most sacks the Chiefs have had in a single game this season. In fact, the Chiefs have seven sacks on the season, so while they can get after the quarterback, they aren't doing so at a high rate.
The Broncos need to give the respect due to Chris Jones, Nick Bolton, and George Karlaftis, but one way to counter what they can do in the pass rush is for Nix to play with more confidence, as he showed against the Cardinals.
The Chiefs have given up an average of 212 yards passing to opposing offenses, so while their pass defense is effective, it's not dominant. They gave up 365 yards passing to Kirk Cousins and 257 yards passing to Sam Darnold, and neither ranks among the top quarterbacks in the NFL.
If Nix plays with confidence, he should do better than the 131 passing yards he had in Week 1, especially at home. It may be asking too much to pass for 350 yards, but if he can get 225 yards or more, that could be enough if the run game comes through and the defense does its job.
All Nix has to do is be willing and ready to take shots downfield when the opportunity is there. The Chiefs' defense does deserve respect, but it's not the dominant unit it looked like in the season opener.
The Chiefs have shown they are a legitimate playoff contender, and one shouldn't read too much into their game last week against the Seahawks. However, one also shouldn't read too much into the Week 1 matchup between the Broncos and Chiefs.
The Broncos have shown they are a better defensive team than they were in Week 1, and they are starting to figure things out on offense. Now it's time for the Broncos to prove that the season opener is long behind them and that they can get it done against a top AFC team and their strongest divisional rival.
Playing at home will help, but so will sharper defensive play, a confident QB under center, and contributions from players who saw little to no action in Week 1. And if the Broncos get the win, they will improve their odds when it comes to the playoffs, the AFC West title, and a high seed.

title: Broncos' Injury Concerns Grow as Two More Key Players Surface
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are gearing up for their Week 8 rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs . If the Broncos are going to avenge their ugly 31-10 loss in the season opener, they’ll need a little luck on the health front.
Three starters were held out of Wednesday’s practice , but things changed on Thursday, with two of those players participating in a limited role. That’s the good news; the bad news is that two new names popped up on the injury report.
Let’s take a look at Thursday’s practice report.
Harvey and Jones popping up on the injury report is concerning, especially after they were unlisted on Wednesday. Both were limited, though, so there’s no reason to fear for their Week 8 availability quite yet.
If Harvey is compromised this week, at least the Broncos have Jonah Coleman back. Coleman can pound the rock and doesn’t have to leave the field on third down because of his receiving and pass-protecting proficiency. Plus, J.K. Dobbins is more than capable of doing it all, too. Let’s hope it doesn’t come to that.
With Hufanga still not participating in practice, it’s not looking great for him this week. Friday will be the ultimate decider, but that’s why the Broncos really need Jones to take it easy on his hamstring. The thought of going against Patrick Mahomes without either of your starting safeties is enough to make any team sweat a bit.
Devon Key is healthy, and Taylor Rapp has done well in playing starter snaps since Hufanga got hurt, but the Broncos would much rather have their starters against Kansas City, or at least one of them. Jones is midway through what has easily been his best as a Bronco since joining the team in 2024.
Meanwhile, it’s great to see Allen and Waddle progress to limited on Thursday after being held out of Wednesday’s session. Both starters went down late in last week’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. Hopefully, there’s enough time for them to heal up in time for this massive Chiefs game.
Surtain remains fully on pace to return to the field this week. And the timing couldn’t be better, given the importance of this game.
If the Broncos beat the Chiefs at Mile High, they’ll take the lead in the AFC West. Dener’s road ahead is significantly easier than Kansas City’s.
The Broncos have a few toughies left on the schedule beyond Week 8, but the Chiefs still have to face the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and New England Patriots. With a win, the Broncos could have the chance to really pull away in their quest to defend their division crown and repeat as AFC West champions.

title: Courtland Sutton Rejects 'Fluke' Narrative Ahead of Broncos-Chiefs Rematch
full_text:
Few people saw the Denver Broncos' 14-win campaign coming in 2025.
Yeah, the Broncos won 10 games the year prior with a rookie Bo Nix, and made the playoffs as a wildcard team, but they were quickly eliminated from the tournament by the Buffalo Bills in Upstate New York . At that point, though, just making the playoffs was a triumph, after Denver had gone eight straight years without qualifying for the postseason.
The Broncos knew that if they were going to truly become a force to be reckoned with in the conference, they'd have to knock the Kansas City Chiefs off their eight-year perch as AFC West champions. That meant the Broncos had to take care of their own business and when they went head-to-head with the Chiefs, they had to prevail.
And prevail Denver did, sweeping the Chiefs for the first time in more than a decade. Patrick Mahomes suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 15, but Chiefs had already been eliminated from the playoffs. Several weeks before, the Broncos beat a desperate Mahomes-led Chiefs team at Mile High, signaling a changing of the guard.
The Broncos would finish the season 14-3, profitting greatly from an 11-game winning streak. Denver unseated the Chiefs as AFC West champions and earned the No. 1 playoff seed in the AFC, and even exacted some revenge on the Bills in an epic 33-30 overtime win in the divisional round.
We all know how the 2025 season came crashing to a quick and brutal end with Nix's ankle injury. But fast forward to 2026, and the Chiefs are back, sitting at 5-1 going into Week 8.
Meanwhile, the Broncos are 5-2 with the chance to pull away as division leaders if they can vanquish the Chiefs at home on Sunday . Some fans hoped that Kansas City's unraveling last year was a sign that the worm had turned, and that the Andy Reid dynasty was over, but Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton knew the Chiefs' identity was still intact.
"Honestly, they're just a really good team, well coached," Sutton said on Wednesday. "They've got a lot of talent over there. The things that they did for such a long time, that identity is still there."
At the same time, the Broncos have forged their own identity. Since Sean Payton arrived as head coach, the tide has turned against the Chiefs.
Payton snapped Kansas City's 16-game winning streak over the Broncos in 2023 with Russell Wilson as his quarterback. In 2024, the Nix-led Broncos split with Kansas City and nearly swept them, were it not for a freak blocked field-goal attempt at the end of regulation at Arrowhead Stadium.
Last year was it's own thing, with the Broncos not only sweeping their long-time division rival, but the Chiefs also missing the playoffs for the first time in the Mahomes era and only the second time since Reid became head coach. Like two ships in the night, as the Chiefs were going one way last year, the Broncos were headed the other direction, and along the way, a winning identity of their own took shape in the Mile High City.
"We know that we have put together a really good team over the past few years, and for us to get to the top of that mountain last year, we understood that we had to knock off who was already up there, and they were the team that were up there," Sutton said.
The Broncos won the AFC West crown in 2025, but according to Sutton, that hasn't changed their mindset as a underdogs. In the Broncos' quest to repeat as division champs, the Pro Bowl receiver doesn't feel like the NFL world is giving them the respect they deserve.
"For us to get that reign last year, I wouldn't say that it's changed our philosophy. I think that we have the right mindset of, 'Hey, yes, we may have won the division last year, but there still doesn't feel as if there's this respect of the Broncos are a really good football team,'" Sutton said. "I think people still think that we rode off a high and there was this fluke of what happened last year."
During the 2026 offseason, the talking points on the Broncos shifted dramatically around the NFL. They were viewed as a bona fide contender, and often ranked as one of the most talented teams in the league.
However, amid Nix's early-season slump and the offense's failure to launch, the NFL world quickly started selling their stock on the Broncos and seemingly writing them off. While it's true that the Broncos have fielded a championship-caliber offense yet, it's important to remember just how tough their initial six-game schedule was, with games against the Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Chargers, and Seattle Seahawks.
Nix and the offense didn't play consistently well, but Denver kept winning. The Broncos weathered that gauntlet at 4-2 — which was about as well as anyone expected — and after beating the Arizona Cardinals on the road last week, they're now sitting at 5-2 with the chance to get even with the Chiefs and pull ahead in the division.
"So for us, it's, 'Hey, we've got to show up each week and go show everybody and prove to ourselves that we are who we say we are at the end of the day, and that last year wasn't a fluke. It wasn't just a flash in the dark,'" Sutton said.
The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at home since Payton became the head coach. And while people may still be doubting the Broncos, Sutton and company are focused on standing their ground at home, and sending the message that last year's AFC West title wasn't an anomoly.
"It's one of those things that we have to go stand up and stand on ten toes that we are who we say we are, week in and week out," Sutton said. "And this weekend it's against the Chiefs, a divisional game."
For the first time since Nix came to town, the Broncos were blown out by the Chiefs in Week 1. That 31-10 loss stung , not only because it came at the hands of the Chiefs, but also because it was under the bright primetime lights of Monday Night Football .
The Broncos are fully aware of their failure to launch in that game, and it sounds like they're relishing the opportunity to balance the scales in their Week 8 rematch with the Chiefs.
"I know that we have the character and the fight in that locker room to go out there and perform how we want to perform," Sutton said. "We know that we didn't like how we performed last time, but with it being a divisional game, we know that we've got to show up."
Suffice it to say, this iteration of Broncos-Chiefs is going to be a heavyweight bout. The Broncos have a lot to play for, including the division lead, while the Chiefs are coming off their first and only loss of the season.
Mahomes is undefeated against the Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium, and you know he'd love to get back in the win column at Mile High for the first time since 2022, and really signal to Chiefs fans and the NFL that Kansas City is back in the AFC West driver's seat.
Nix is a different quarterback at home. He was out of sorts in that ugly Week 1 loss, but a lot of water has passed under the bridge since then, and his confidence surrounding his ankle recovery is at a season-high after romping for a 62-yard touchdown last week and connecting on several explosive passing plays.
Week 8's action is going to be an epic AFC West throwdown.

title: Broncos Have 2 Matchup Problems They Must Solve vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have a chance to take the top spot in the division if they can beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. The Seattle Seahawks opened the door by beating the Chiefs last week.
The Broncos would also benefit from the schedule, since the Chiefs already had their bye week and still have most of their toughest opponents left on the docket. The Broncos' bye comes in Week 10, so a win on Sunday would put them at 6-2 and the Chiefs at 5-2.
After that Week 1 debacle, the Broncos won't be overlooking the Chiefs, as they may have in the season opener. The Broncos have to focus on winning some key matchups that deal more with their own issues than with what the Chiefs are doing.
With that said, let’s get into the two key matchups of Week 8.
Last week, Nix vs. himself was also a key matchup , but for a different reason. Going into Arizona, it was about him regaining his confidence, which he did with a 62-yard touchdown run, a 52-yard screen-pass touchdown, and several other explosive plays .
This week, it's about finding the consistency and balance Nix hasn’t shown this season.
He still has issues with his ball placement and pocket presence, and they may never fully resolve this season. In fact, it may be part of who Nix is, which isn't exactly the picture of consistency and balance.
That's where Bo's aggressiveness comes into play. He must spread the ball around better than he has, take what the defense gives him, and take calculated risks. This isn’t to say he should go out there and be a gunslinger, but when he sees the opening deep, he should take the shot, like he did last week.
Denver can’t have Nix fall back into the shell he was in for Weeks 4-6, though Week 6 was as much due to the Seahawks' defense as it was his mental state when it came to pushing the ball. The Chiefs rank 21st in explosive pass-play rate allowed and 28th in the last four games, so Nix has no excuse if he crawls back into his shell.
Bo needs to find consistency in being aggressive, both as a runner and as a passer, as well as start carrying one strong game into another, though it could still look very different in the box score. His balance has to come from spreading the ball around more and not favoring one or two receivers, which he did improve on against the Cardinals, while still hunting for explosives without being careless and taking what the defense gives him.
This was an easy one. No player-on-player matchup is more important than the Broncos' collective tackling of Walker.
In Week 1, Denver's missed-tackle rate was 29.8% , up 25% from its historically bad 70-point game against the Miami Dolphins in 2023. Most Broncos fans didn't think defense could ever get worse than that woeful day in Miami.
On top of that, the Broncos allowed 247 yards after missed tackles, with Walker having 108 yards after contact, or 4.7 yards after contact per rush.
If the Broncos want a chance in this one, they can’t let Walker run all over them. That is stating the obvious, but Denver’s defense has done well in shutting down or limiting Patrick Mahomes, especially at Mile High, so allowing Walker to carry the Chiefs would make it much harder to walk out with the win.
Denver’s defense has also allowed a high rate of explosive runs, including over the last four games, which is alarming, since those four games don't count Walker's big Week 1 showing. The Broncos have had serious consistency issues stopping the run, and it stems from more than just bad tackling.
This game is about more than the AFC West standings; Denver's pride is also on the line. It's gut-check time for Vance Joseph's defense.

title: Broncos' First Week 8 Injury Report: Updates on Surtain, Hufanga & Waddle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos released their initial Week 8 injury report ahead of Sunday's pivotal home showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Denver listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and defensive end Zach Allen (hip) — all starters — as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) following Wednesday's session.
An earlier report indicated that Waddle suffered a re-aggravation of a prior chest issue toward the end of last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game is to be determined.
The injury occurred on a trick play that head coach and offensive playcaller Sean Payton consequently apologized for.
"Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said in his postgame press conference on Sunday. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play."
Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City.
Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action.
Elsewhere on the injury report, left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims (ankle) were considered limited, while cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were full participants.
Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health.
Of note on the Chiefs' end, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (personal/knee) did not practice on Wednesday while receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) and tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) were full goes.
In the event that Waddle is inactive on Sunday, the Broncos would be down to Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin as its primary wideouts, with Pat Bryant (ankle) still on short-term injured reserve.
Although, in this case, some (more) of the receiving work could be spilled onto running back RJ Harvey's plate, the Broncos may take the opportunity to get the ball in the hands of Mims, which Payton has repeatedly insisted remains a priority on his offensive totem pole.
“I think to his credit, whenever we ask something of him—whether it’s intermediate, down the field—he’s been really effective," he said of Mims on Wednesday. "Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are... I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.”

title: Broncos' Most Surprising Trade Candidate Is Hiding in Plain Sight
full_text:
J.K. Dobbins doesn't seem happy at the moment.
The Denver Broncos' veteran running back received a season-low 14 snaps in Week 7's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals. With rookie Jonah Coleman returning from injured reserve, Dobbins took a back seat in the desert, both in snap and touch share.
The Broncos' offense looked different with Coleman on the field , and his versatility as a receiver and as a pass protector gives Sean Payton so much more to work with. When Coleman is on the field, opponents can't be sure whether it's a run or a pass coming, while with Dobbins and RJ Harvey, defenses can play the probabilities more accurately.
In the NFL, it's good not to be predictable. The Broncos have to make the tough decision to continue ceding snaps and touches in Coleman's favor if they have any hope of digging out of being a bottom-10 rushing offense.
Dobbins doesn't appear to be taking this development well, and if he's unable to get his mind right, the Broncos could suddenly become amenable to trading him away . Several teams have serious running back issues right now — including the New York Giants, who've already orchestrated a big trade (quarterback J.J. McCarthy).
The Giants would also make a lot of sense because of head coach John Harbaugh's ties to Dobbins from their time together in Baltimore. Harbaugh drafted Dobbins in the second round back in 2020.
There are other teams in need of some running back help, including the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers, and maybe even the Carolina Panthers. Dobbins has a long injury history, and while he was dinged up early this season, he's yet to miss a game.
The one fly in the ointment of a potential Dobbins trade is his contract. The Broncos just re-signed him to a two-year, $16 million deal, but only the first year was guaranteed.
That's good and bad. It's good in that a team acquiring him via trade wouldn't necessarily be locked to Dobbins beyond 2026, unless he were to arrive and hit it out of the park.
The bad? A lot of the money gets funneled into Dobbins's 2027 contract. He goes from a $6 million cap number this year to $10 million next year, with a $7 million base salary. That's a solid deal for a mid-level No. 1 running back, but for a second guy in a rotation, it would be a drastic overpay.
Now, it's helpful that nearly half of the 2026 season is over, so the Broncos have already absorbed a good chunk of his contract, and they've already paid out his $4 million signing bonus. That simplifies things somewhat for an interested suitor that's mostly concerned with running back help this season, and less worried about 2027.
With Tyler Badie on injured reserve for three more games, the Broncos would have to really be blown away by an offer to trade Dobbins. They do have Cody Schrader on the practice squad, so if a team made the Broncos an offer they couldn't refuse, there's an immediate running back available to use on game day.
The Broncos love Dobbins. Payton values Dobbins and has given the veteran back a lot of credit for the Broncos' sudden rise in confidence and swagger last year.
Payton's appreciation of Dobbins was reflected last week against the Cardinals. On a drive in which Coleman did the heavy lifting as a runner, moving the chains on two of his three carries, Payton gave the Broncos' only goal-line carry to Dobbins, which he punched in.
However, instead of jumping up and celebrating with his teammates, Dobbins ran straight back to the Broncos' sideline and sat down on the bench. Following the game, he purportedly didn't make himself available to reporters in the locker room, further showing his frustration.
Payton is big on body language. As a leader that guys in that locker room look to, if Dobbins isn't able to get his mind right and frustration continues to show through his body language, the situation could devolve ahead of the November 10 deadline.
But I give Dobbins more credit than that. His disappointment in being rendered second fiddle last week is understandable, but I'd be surprised if we don't see a more chipper energy on Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs. Character has never been a concern with Dobbins.
Iron sharpens iron, after all, so if Dobbins doesn't want to be the No. 2 running back, it's up to him to prove it on the field. And the Broncos will give him that opportunity, provided he gets his vibe back on point.
I doubt the Broncos trade Dobbins. However, he has become as surprise player to watch, given Coleman's rise, Dobbins's antics last week, and the growing need at running back several teams have ahead of the deadline.
Dobbins is an experienced back, and he's healthy. I could see a needy team calling the Broncos, but again, it would take a serious offer to get Payton and company to give up on the veteran back.
