A: This is a great quesiton. I really do not think the Jaguars will sell low on Brian Thomas Jr., and I believe it will take something worthwhile for the Jaguars to officially give up on him. With that said, I think even if Thomas has a breakout game for the first time in a long time, he…

title: 3 NFL Trade Deadline Deals the Jaguars Should Explore Right Now in Wide-Open AFC
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The NFL trade market has heated up in a big way this week, with three All-Pros traded from the AFC South alone since Tuesday.
Whether the Jaguars will get in on the trade action remains to be seen, but it is always fun to project anyways. The Jaguars have made a number of trades since James Gladstone took over, with the Jaguars' general manager completing nine non-draft day trades involving players since he was hired.
This includes trading for Jakobi Meyers at the trade deadline a year ago, a move that instantly gave the Jaguars a boost and has paid off since. And while it was a draft-day trade, Gladstone's biggest move as general manager was the 2025 blockbuster for Travis Hunter.
James Gladstone's Player Trades
2026 5th-Round Pick, 2026 6th-Round Pick
CB Tyson Campbell, 2026 7th-Round Pick
CB Greg Newsome, 2026 6th-Round Pick
2026 4th-Round Pick, 2026 6th-Round Pick
In short, the Jaguars have been pretty agressive in terms of trades. They made a move last season with the idea of winning, and it would make sense to do the same this year. But which targets would make the most sense, and which deals could make it happen? We break it down below.
The Offer: Brian Thomas Jr.
Let's get weird? I would also think picks have to be involved, with the Jaguars perhaps sending a seventh-round pick and getting a fourth-round selection in return. Thomas would have much, much more value in terms of draft picks landed in a trade if this was just a player-for-picks deal, but adding a productive veteran like Payne would be enticing. Payne is still in his prime at 29 and is a legit difference-maker against both the run and the pass, but he is under contract for just 11 more games.
Landing Payne as a rental would likely not be ideal, even if the Jaguars would likely be able to recoup something for him in the form of compensatory draft picks in the future. But with several expiring contracts along the interior defensive line, the Jaguars could look to Payne as a defensive version of Jakobi Meyers: a productive, experienced player who can bring an instant impact and sign a deal shortly after as a result.
Letting go of Thomas will always sting a bit for the Jaguars if it does happen. That is why if the Jaguars do trade Thomas, they must get something worthwhile in return. Considering Payne's fit and talent and the need for a difference-maker insider, he would certainly qualify as worthwhile. This could help push the Jaguars' defense over the top and have a minimal impact on the offense. This wouldn't be as explosive as a Jeffery Simmons deal, but Payne could have a similar impact in terms of improving the entire unit.
The Offer: 2027 3rd-Round Pick
Another defensive tackle, and for good reason. As SI's Albert Breer noted, "The Giants and Jaguars are sniffing around on defensive tackles—Jacksonville’s looking for pieces for its defensive front in general." It makes sense considering the Jaguars have a short-term need for a spark inside, as well as a long-term need for a new centerpiece for the interior defensive line. When it comes to potentially available defensive tackle targets, Ojomo is up there with Payne while also being four years younger and still ascending as a talent.
The Jaguars' fit with Ojomo makes a ton of sense off the bat. He has been disruptive against both the run and the pass, he is young and is still getting better each season, he fits the scheme like a glove, and he would give the Jaguars a talent boost at a key position of need. The question, of course, has to do with the fact that he is in a contract year. This could impact what the Eagles do quite a bit considering the options they would have if they didn't trade Ojomo.
If the Eagles opt not to trade Ojomo, then there are only two outcomes for them ahead: signing him to a big deal to give them the most expensive defensive tackle room in NFL history, or letting him walk in free agency for what very likely could be a future third-round compensatory pick, depending on how big of a deal he signs and what other moves the Eagles make. This is exactly what happened with Milton Williams, and it is not hard to see Ojomo cashing in like he did.
If you are the Jaguars, I think you accept the fact that the Eagles' asking price would be a third-round pick today. Jacksonville could live with that depending on how they play free agency next March and depending on just how much Ojomo would improve them. He is worth the swing, though.
The Offer: 2027 5th-Round Pick
It is really easy to make the case for the Jaguars to add a guy like Budda Baker. They are hurting at the safety position, having all three of their top safeties available for just the first three games of the season. Since then, Eric Murray has missed some time, Antonio Johnson is now banged-up, and Caleb Ransaw is on injured reserve. Adding a safety would help the Jaguars quite a bit in the short-term.
Then you add in the fact that Budda Baker has been one of the NFL's best and most productive, reliable, and durable safeties of the last decade, and it is easy to see the fit. Baker played the Rams twice a year during James Gladstone's and Liam Coen's time in Los Angeles, and the 30-year-old would clearly carry a ton of respect in the Jaguars' building, while serving as a legit fit and play-maker.
The Cardinals are not going anywhere during the next season-and-a-half Baker is under contract, and he would allow the Jaguars to confidently play three-safety sets once Johnson is healthy. A trio of Johnson, Murray, and Baker would be quite the group for the Jaguars at the safety position as they look to make a run for the AFC South down the stretch of the year.

title: Jaguars-Colts Thursday Injury Report: What Does Montaric Brown's Return Mean?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars look like they are getting a big boost to their secondary in Week 8.
The Jaguars had cornerback Montaric Brown listed as a full participant in practice for the second day in a row , a sign that Jacksonville is set to get their highest-paid cornerback back on the field against the Indianapolis Colts.
But what could the potential return of Brown really mean for the Jaguars in an important Week 8 AFC South battle?
Brown has missed all but six snaps over the Jaguars' last three weeks due to the hamstring injury, which first flared up on the Jaguars' injury report in the practices leading up to Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals. While Brown was not having a stellar season before his injury, it is worth noting that the Jaguars rank No. 28 and No. 24, respectively, in EPA/Play and success rate against the pass in the three weeks since.
While Brown may not slot in as a starter right off the bat for the Jaguars, he would give them expanded depth at a critical position alongside Travis Hunter, Jarrian Jones, and Jourdan Lewis.
“Certainly, we'd have a guy who's got a lot of experience who knows our system. It'd be good to have him back out there healthy," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Thursday.
Brown did play six snaps in Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles but left after allowing a long touchdown pass to Darius Cooper in man coverage, a play that clearly showed the impact of his injury. Without Brown the next week against the Houston Texans, the Jaguars had one of their worst defensive performances in two seasons.
"I know in the Philly game, tough situation where he got hurt there in the game, but he looks good and we gain a veteran presence, and we gain a level of physicality anytime Buster's out there," Campanile said. "I think he's done a great job for us that way on the line of scrimmage, tackling, being physical, even in the coverage element of everything. So yeah, that's what we gain with him in there.”
Getting Brown back at cornerback could allow the Jaguars to do a number of things differently, including getting Hunter more snaps on offense after his dominant game against the Houston Texans. Not having Brown available was the primary reason Hunter didn't play an offensive snap in Week 4 against the Bengals, which to date is the only game in Hunter's career in which he did not take a snap on both sides of the ball.
Getting Brown back also happens at a good time for the secondary since safety Antonio Johnson did not practice for the second day in a row with an ankle injury. Johnson looks unlikely to play against the Colts, which means the Jaguars will need backups like Kaevon Merriweather and reinforcements like Brown to step up in the secondary.
“Every game's different and I think we're fortunate where we got a really good room there, and I think Kaevon [Merriweather] has done a good job coming in here as a new guy who's stepped up and given us the opportunity to have another guy that can kind of play some of those roles," Campanile said.
"I think even watching him in the last game, you see some physicality, and I think he's learning everything we're doing. He's worked really hard at it. I think Perk [Defensive Backs Coach Anthony Perkins] has done a great job with him, getting him up to speed. So, there's some other guys in that room who help us that way. Like any game, you're always adjusting.”

title: 3 Reasons the Jaguars Simply Can't Afford to Sell Low on a Brian Thomas Jr. Trade
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The NFL Trade Deadline is less than two weeks away, and there are not many more names in Jacksonville that are going to garner more attention than Brian Thomas Jr.
The reasons are simple: the former first-round pick has struggled to produce since Liam Coen was hired, making him virtually the only offensive player in Jacksonville whose numbers haven't erupted thanks to the improved offense.
The last time the Jaguars were on the field, Thomas didn't log a snap in the second half as it became clear his role was being reduced. But even with the Thomas question looming over the Jaguars ahead of the deadline, there are still a few clear reasons why the Jaguars should not simply sell low and deal Thomas for anything they can get by Nov. 10.
While it is clear that the most likely path forward for Thomas is either outside of Jacksonville or just plainly off the field in favor of Josh Cameron, Travis Hunter, and 12 personnel sets, that doesn't mean the Jaguars should diminish his value on the trade market. The Jaguars might not have much use for Thomas when it comes to this Sunday vs. the Colts or next Thursday vs. the Baltimore Ravens, but there is a reason so many receiver-needy teams are connected to him. Thomas' talent from his rookie season has not just disappeared; instead, his circumstances have. That might not directly explain the dip in production, but it is the reality of the situation.
As a result, the Jaguars can not afford to treat Thomas like some depth piece who you would be excited to land a Day 3 pick for. He isn't Tank Bigbsy or Roy Robertson-Harris. He is still a former first-round pick who is young, cheap, and not that far removed from a record-breaking 1,000-yard season. These are not reasons for the Jaguars to keep trying to make it work with Thomas, because that is all they have done since 2025, but it is a valid reason for the Jaguars to not simply deal him for whatever the highest offer is.
Thomas has genuine value in the NFL; two years ago, he would have taken a first-round pick and then some to trade for. Just because it hasn't worked out in Jacksonville doesn't mean the Jaguars should opt not to respect that value on the trade market.
The two deals that first come to mind when I think about a potential Brian Thomas Jr. deal are the Chase Claypool and Marvin Harrison Jr. deals. The Steelers traded Claypool to the Chicago Bears for a second-round pick in 2022 despite Claypool never having a 1,000-yard season in his career. Claypool, of course, went on to flame out in Chicago, but it is at least a relevant data point when it comes to a former first-round pick like Thomas.
Then there is the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. Harrison never put up the numbers in Arizona that Thomas has put up in Jacksonville, but he was still able to, somehow, net the Arizona Cardinals a second-round selection. Perhaps the Houston Texans were the only team foolish enough to give up that kind of draft ammo, but the fact that Harrison goes for such a high pick should be evidence to the Jaguars that they should not just trade Thomas for nothing.
The Jaguars are ready to go on a run in the AFC South, especially with 50% of the divison waving the white flag. That doesn't mean they should just sit on Thomas as an assett, because chances are the Jaguars would trust Josh Cameron in more situations moving forward than Thomas. But it does mean the Jaguars shouldn't just give Thomas away considering what they could do with an actual draft package.
Would a third- or fourth-rounder for Thomas help the Jaguars win a game next week? No, but it could help the Jaguars land a potential difference-maker on defense in the form of the Daron Payne, Khalil Mack, or Moro Ojomo. Could the same be said for a sixth- or a seventh-round selection? The obvious answer is no. An early pick could help the Jaguars more today than Thomas might be able to, but the same can not be said for a late-round pick.

title: Why the Jaguars Are Surprise Winners in the Jeffery Simmons Trade
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- One of the true elite players in the NFL is officially out of the AFC South as the Jacksonville Jaguars prepare their run, but that isn't the only good news from the Jeffery Simmons trade.
The Tennssee Titans followed the Indianapolis Colts' lead in a Week 8 fire sale , dealing Simmons, the NFL's best defensive tackle, to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick. With Simmons heading to the Windy City, the Jaguars are now quietly one of the biggest winners from the blockbuster.
What the Bears are getting in 29-year-old Jeffery Simmons: 🏈3x All-Pro 🏈4x Pro-Bowl selection 🏈44.5 sacks 🏈8 forced fumbles 🏈6 fumble recoveries 🏈30 pass deflections pic.twitter.com/3fOGEYklnS
Jacksonville of course benefits in a big way from the Simmons trade w hen it comes to their push for an AFC South title. Though they will still have to play Simmons when they visit the Bears in Week 13, they will not have to face him in Weeks 10 and 12 in AFC South battles with the Titans, where Simmons was their only real threat defensively. But the Jaguars are winners for bigger reasons than that.
Simply put, the Jaguars need defensive help. Front line defensive help, especially as it pertains to their depth. The Jaguars were never, ever, ever going to land Simmons in a trade for the same exact reasons they were never going to get DeForest Buckner, but Simmons landing in Chicago does eliminate the Bears from several other moves that could overlap with the Jaguars.
The Bears were, well, the logical landing spot for every single top defensive lineman, even beyond Simmons. In The Athletic's NFL Trade Deadline big board, the Bears were listed as a best fit for all nine defensive tackles/edge defenders ranked in the top-15. All nine! This includes Simmons, Buckner, but also other names like Khalil Mack , Daron Payne, and Moro Ojomo ... all names we have pointed out as fits for the Jaguars.
The @TheAthletic NFL Trade Deadline Big Board #DaBears pic.twitter.com/LQanHgAXr8
Could the Bears look to go truly all-in and still add a talent like Mack to play alongside Simmons? Never say never in the NFL, but it is clear the Bears took their absolute best shot with the Simmons trade. They are already down three draft picks, are they really going to be in a rush to send more picks? Even if it is a Day 3 pick for a player like Mack? Chances are the answer is no.
This is good news for the Jaguars, who rank in the bottom quarter of teams in both sack and sack rate despite being a top-7 team in pressure rate. The Jaguars have talented defensive ends in Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker, but they badly need to add an interior pass-rusher and some backup edge rushing talent.
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen made it clear Wednesday: the Jaguars' bed has been made when it comes to the pass-rush, at least right now. Thanks to the Simmons trade, perhaps that can change.
“I mean, expectations to me are… To me, we are who we are. That's where we're at," Coen said. "It needs to get better. It has to improve for our team to continue to ascend and go where we want to go, but I do have a lot of confidence and faith in that group.”
The Jaguars have always made sense as buyers at the deadline, at least as it relates to adding some defensive line help. So did the Bears, and the Bears had arguably more ammo to work with considering their cap situation. Now that the Bears are out of the picture, the Jaguars' urgency to make a move along the defensive line should still be high, but there should be some comfort knowing that one team is out of the running.
If the Jaguars end up adding a talent like Payne, Mack or Ojomo by Nov. 10, we can likely point back to today's trade and Chicago bowing out of contention as a big reason why. That is why the Jaguars are winners from the biggest blockbuster of the season.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Colts: Fire Sale Creates Big Opportunities
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are looking to make a run. First, they must deal with the Indianapolis Colts.
The Colts, of course, are one of the more dysfunctional teams in football. They have fired their embattled general manager and have since started stripping the team for used parts, dealing All-Pro veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner before they kick off in Jacksonville in Week 8. It also remains to be seen whether Josh Downs or Jonathan Taylor will still be on the roster by 1 p.m. on Sunday.
:I think as a team, you always respect your opponent. And the guys, especially if you've played in this league for a while or even just a year, you know how hard it is to win. And no matter who you're playing. You can look back I remember my rookie year, we were 3-14 and we beat Buffalo here," Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence said Wednesday.
"We beat Indy the last game of the season. They were trying to get in the playoffs. We were 2-14 and it's the last game of the year. You wouldn't think we had much to play for. And we came out, played great, flying around and played really well. It's the NFL. It's hard to beat any team, honestly."
So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 8 battle with the Colts playing out? We break it down below with this week's bold predictions.
Will this be the game that quiets down the hysterics around the Jaguars' pass-rush? Probably not, but I do think it will be a day where the Jaguars' pass-rush is able to get after Daniel Jones with at least four sacks. The Jaguars have hit that number just once this year in Week 1 against the Cleveland Browns, but I think the game script could surely allow for it to happen, especially when you consider the opponent.
Daniel Jones has been one of the most sacked and pressued quarterbacks in football this season, and a lot of that is due to his own doing. Now that he has lost his best offensive lineman and will likely be in a game where the score and ame flow will force him to dropback more times than the Colts would like, I think the Jaguars will get plenty of chances to get after him.
Trevor Lawrence is the Colts Killer. For as documented as Lawrence's struggles and record against the Houston Texans are, he has had the complete opposite run of success against the Colts. Lawrence is 7-2 with a 100.3 passer rating (13 TDs, 4 INTs) in his career against the Colts, his best record against any team he has faced at least three times. Only Tom Brady (12-3, .800 win pct.) has a better winning percentage against Indianapolis among all quarterbacks with at least eight starts against the Colts since the 1970 merger, per NextGenStats.
I think Lawrence continues to make his MVP case with another big game against the Colts, scoring four touchdowns in the process. Lawrence is one of only two quarterbacks (joining Joe Burrow) who have two different games with four touchdown passes this season, and I think he picks up his third against a Colts team he always seems to find success against.
It remains to be seen if Jonathan Taylor will actually be on the Colts' roster by Sunday, but it sure seems like the Colts' brass is reluctant to trade him because, well, somebody has to putt butts in the seats at Lucas Oil. Taylor is arguably the NFL's best running back and, at worst, is No. 2 behind Bijan Robinson, and he would have been the biggest threat to the Jaguars this week even if the Colts didn't start tearing everything down.
Taylor has averaged over 110 yards from scrimmage per game this season and nobody has really been able to slow him down, but I think the Jaguars will. Taylor has never had an overly productive game in Jacksonville, averaging just 49.2 rushing yards in five games at EverBank Stadium. The Jaguars curse has hit the Colts' best players for years, and I think it happens to Taylor once more in what could be his final game in Jacksonville.
Could this be a get-right game for Brian Thomas Jr? A chance for the Jaguars to showcase his value for receiver-needy teams before the trade deadline? Perhaps all of the above? Thomas has had some of his best career performances against the Colts since he was drafted in 2024, highlighted by some truly stellar highlights as a vertical threat against a secondary that just can't seem to ever run with him.
BRIAN THOMAS, JR. 85-YARD TD 📺: #INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ 📱: https://t.co/waVpO8ZBqG pic.twitter.com/bfK2p2TlaB
It feels like it has been ages since we have seen the Jaguars hit Thomas downfield; he only has two targets on deep passes this season, with one resulting in an interception after Trevor Lawrence was hit and one resulting in a pass-breakup by Patrick Surtain II. I think the Jaguars finally let a Go Ball fly toward Thomas' direction this week, and I think it ends up with him finding the end-zone. Thomas has averaged nearly 18.5 yards per catch against the Colts in his career, and this could be another day of big plays.
The Jaguars are set to start Walker Little at left tackle this week following Anton Harrison's season-ending injury, and it is quite the opportunity for Little. He played well against a much-tougher test in the form of the Houston Texans' pass-rush in Week 6, and he will now play a Colts defense that has one of the more middling and uninspiring edge groups in the entire NFL. As a result, I think Little pitches a shutout.
That is not to say I do not think Little won't allow a single pressure in an absolutely dominant performance. But I do think he will have more wins than losses, and I do not think he will allow a single Colts defender to register even a quarterback hit, let alone a sack, on Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. This is a week where Little can really prove his worth and value to the Jaguars' offense moving forward.

title: ESPN Matchup Predictor Analyzes Chiefs vs. Broncos Divisional Showdown in Week 8
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs cruised to a 5-0 start to open the 2026 NFL campaign, but they ran into a brick wall last week in a prime time showdown with the Seattle Seahawks . Before Andy Reid's squad could even blink, the Chiefs are suddenly in danger of surrendering the AFC West lead when they take on the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High tomorrow.
These division rivals have already faced off earlier this season, when Kansas City took care of business 31-10 in the regular season opener. However, the Broncos have strung together a three-game winning streak during which they have allowed fewer than 16 points per contest. Many Chiefs fans have grown increasingly concerned about the state of the offense after its horrendous three-point showing on Sunday Night Football . When opposing defenses take away Kenneth Walker, KC has struggled to get anything going and create explosive plays.
This will undoubtedly be the most pivotal game of the Chiefs' season to date. Let's dive into what the ESPN Matchup Predictor believes will transpire in this AFC West clash.
Even with a comparable record on paper, the matchup predictor still gives the Chiefs a slight edge tomorrow evening.
ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 55.7%, Broncos 44.0%.
The Chiefs have now been matchup predictor favorites in every game they've played this season.
Amid a week filled with the Chiefs being embroiled in controversy , it's important to remember that a crucial contest awaits them. They desperately need to avoid falling in their second consecutive loss and relinquishing the division lead.
Things can only trend upward for this Chiefs offense, which mustered up 213 total yards and one field goal a week ago. Now that the outside noise about Kenneth Walker's return to Seattle can be put to bed, the hope is that he and Patrick Mahomes will get back to what they were doing earlier this year.
As for Denver, much has been made about Bo Nix and his inability to move the ball downfield, but the Broncos have been winning in spite of his questionable quarterback play. His defense bailed him out time and time again in an overtime thriller two weeks ago, when the Broncos outplayed the Seahawks and won on a walk-off field goal by Wil Lutz.
Ja'Quan McMillian read this PERFECTLY. SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1igvuDtROG
It makes you wonder how a team that ranks in the bottom three of the NFL in offensive yards has a 5-2 record with several solid wins. While the Broncos look mediocre using the eye test, their record keeps proving everyone wrong.
There's no question that the Chiefs have the better offense of these two teams, but the bigger question is whether they can find their footing early or if Denver's defense will stifle it from the jump. If the Broncos can force the Chiefs into playing their brand of football and turn this into a closely contested, defense-oriented matchup, that's where things could get dicey for KC.

title: 3 Wide Receivers on the Block the Kansas City Chiefs Should Consider Trading For
full_text:
Between injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton and a lack of pass-catching depth , the Kansas City Chiefs' receiving corps has been a nightmare in 2026.
KC's offense had been able to manufacture enough points on the board to win games the first five weeks, but that positive momentum came to a screeching halt last week against the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs scored just three points and were stifled all night by the reigning champions, exposing glaringly obvious flaws that need to be addressed. With the NFL trade deadline looming on Nov. 10, time is running out for the Chiefs to make a deal and bolster their aerial attack. Unless it comes in the form of a free agent signing in Tyreek Hill , the only way Andy Reid's offense can realistically improve through the air is via a trade.
It's the time of the year when fans dream about ambitious trades that seem too good to be true. Here are a trio of players that could land in Kansas City ahead of its playoff push.
Following his 1,287-yard, 10-touchdown Pro Bowl rookie season, everything has gone downhill for Thomas since. He's become the subject of heavy trade rumors amid his ongoing decline.
The Jaguars have tried to make things work with the former LSU star, but they simply haven't found a way to get him involved. He's gone consecutive games without a catch and has three receptions in the past four contests.
A 6-foot-2, 209-pound wideout, Thomas has blazing speed in the open field and could serve as a boundary target for Patrick Mahomes with his vast catch radius. We've had him circled as a potential buy-low Chiefs trade candidate since before the 2026 campaign began, and his value won't be any lower than it is right now. By no means am I advocating for the Chiefs to pursue Thomas, though. He wouldn't necessarily be a "dumpster-dive" move per se given his younger age and the draft capital the Jags invested, but the days of him being touted as a future top-tier receiver are numbered. Additionally, Kansas City would have to convince Jacksonville to send a 24-year-old former first-round pick to a receiver-needy team they could face in the AFC Playoffs, something they'd likely be reluctant to do.
In the realm of realistic trade options, Downs probably tops the list. He has openly requested a trade out of Indianapolis and shouldn't command too steep of an asking price since he will be an unrestricted free agent this offseason. Downs' numbers this year are modest (26 receptions, 307 yards), but the advanced metrics tell a different story. He is elite at creating separation out of the slot and is one of the best pure route-runners at his position. In the Colts' Week 2 overtime loss to the Chiefs, Downs auditioned against his potential future team with a seven-catch, 72-yard outing.
Josh Downs Route Running. pic.twitter.com/nDEwFDKnUq
While Rice receives plenty of action in the slot, adding Downs to the mix would allow Eric Bieniemy to diversify his concepts. The Chiefs lack man-beaters who can consistently win one-on-one matchups in open space, and Downs would fix that problem.
He certainly wouldn't be a name that KC supporters swoon over, but Downs would be a significant upgrade over what they are currently working with. After shipping Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner out of town earlier this week, it's only a matter of time before Indy sends Downs elsewhere.
If Brett Veach wants to go all in and make one of the biggest splashes in recent Chiefs trade memory, he needs to acquire Jets wideout Garrett Wilson. Of all the receivers seemingly on the trade block, there is no doubt that Wilson is far and away the most coveted.
A three-time 1,000-yard receiver, Wilson is in his fifth season with the franchise. As he noted earlier this week in a press conference, he loves playing in New York but doesn't love it as much as winning. He'd certainly have a better chance at competing for a Super Bowl in Kansas City catching passes from a future first-ballot Hall of Famer.
"Yeah, I want to be here. I want to win games. That's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest. But I'm hopeful." - Garrett Wilson https://t.co/K8XI58FqwA pic.twitter.com/Cw79Ip03gg
The Ohio State product is a true No. 1 target and has shifted more toward a primary X receiver role after often playing in the slot in past years. Regardless of where he would line up in KC, he'd undoubtedly rank among the most dynamic weapons the Chiefs have had in the 21st century.
The asking price to land a player of Wilson's caliber — let alone one with team control until 2030 — would be otherworldly and quite uncharacteristic for Veach . But if this front office is hell-bent on making a push for another Super Bowl and maximizing its championship window, it's at least worth checking in with the Jets to see whether there's any room for negotiation.

title: Peter Woods Sees Something Special Brewing Between Chiefs’ Young Defensive Stars
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs went all in on their defensive unit during the 2026 NFL Draft, selecting defensive players with all of their top three picks. General manager Brett Veach was determined to reload and pave the way for a new generation of defenders to take over.
The crown jewel of KC's draft class was LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane, who was the franchise's earliest-ever selection on a corner. Despite battling a shoulder injury that has bothered him since the Chiefs' minicamp in June, Delane has been highly effective and shown promising traits when he's been on the field.
In last week's loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football , Delane did experience some "welcome to the NFL" moments when squaring off with Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He didn't line up with him every rep of the night and held his own at times, but JSN was certainly the toughest challenge Delane has faced in his young NFL career. The Seahawks' superstar finished the contest with 150 yards and a touchdown. Regardless of his showing last game, fellow first-round rookie Peter Woods — who was selected 23 picks after Delane at No. 29 — remains fully confident in his defensive counterpart. During his media appearance on Friday , the rookie defensive lineman discussed why he has so much faith in Delane and what the two can become as they continue to develop together.
"I'm always there for him. He's a tremendous player," Woods said about his teammate. "I trust him with the backside of me because that's what he does. I'm ready to see him continue to blossom and bloom into the player he's going to be, as well as myself. We're doing that together since we came in together."
Admittedly, it has been a quiet first six games for the Clemson product to this point. Woods has played 46.3% of the defense's snaps while rotating with Khyiris Tonga on the inside, but it hasn't resulted in much production. He currently has three solo tackles, two QB pressures, and half a sack across 190 defensive reps.
#Chiefs DT Peter Woods describes what he's learned about the Broncos rivalry. He tells @Leabonics , "If I'm being honest, I don't really like none of the teams that we play." pic.twitter.com/ZedqlfseI7
It's always difficult to judge interior linemen by statistics in a limited sample size, but Pro Football Focus grades echo this sentiment, too. Woods' 50.8 defensive grade ranks No. 96 out of 126 qualifying defensive tackles in the league, and his 43.4 run defense grade is one of the NFL's worst marks.
Even with Woods' early struggles, he has plenty to learn from veterans like Chris Jones . He talked about how he and the rest of the defensive linemen have responded after the rookie suffered his first NFL defeat. "It was rather interesting being in the locker room and listening to some of the things the leaders were reiterating about getting back on track and getting hit in the mouth and figuring out what we can do to be better," Woods stated. "I think one of the older guys gave me advice that whenever you lose a game, that's when you should look in your personal mirror most and figure out how you can benefit the team to get a win."
No matter how you spin it, Woods has been a defensive staple on a 5-1 Chiefs group at just 21 years old. As he and Delane get better and gain more experience, they could both be forces to be reckoned with for years to come.

title: Major Chiefs and Broncos Injuries Could Change the Trajectory of the AFC West
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will have an important AFC West showdown on Sunday afternoon, but both teams are approaching game day with significant and potentially game-changing injury unknowns.
After being a full participant on Wednesday, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday or Friday. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that the issue is with the same shoulder that limited Delane during training camp and preseason activities before knocking him out early in Week 1 and sidelining him through Week 2.
Delane has played nearly every defensive snap in the Chiefs' games since Week 3, including a full 100% workload last weekend in Seattle. Reid said that the team would "just see how he does here going forward." Delane was later ruled questionable, implying that he could be a true game-time decision.
Veteran cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was limited on Friday and is also questionable for Sunday's game, as is rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas. However, Reid clarified that Thomas missed Friday's practice due to a personal issue and said that he would be at the game on Sunday.
"He'll meet us there in Denver," Reid said.
The best news from the Chiefs' game day designations relates to wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), who was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before participating fully during Friday's practice. Rice was given no designation for Sunday's game, meaning that he is expected to suit up in Denver.
Rice hasn't seen the field since suffering a hamstring injury against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.
Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) participated fully on Friday and received no designation after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) was a full participant all week and also received no designation.
The only fully negative news on the Chiefs' Friday injury report is unsurprising: defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott won't play, as expected, as he works back from his ACL recovery .
Meanwhile, in Denver, the questions continue, with a pair of absences now confirmed .
The Broncos ruled out safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and running back RJ Harvey (knee), dealing a blow to each side of the ball.
Harvey is a pass-catching back who is Denver's second-leading receiver on the season, while Hufanga has two interceptions and a forced fumble in the five games he's played this year.
Defensive tackle Zach Allen (hamstring) is questionable after missing Wednesday's practice and being limited on Thursday and Friday, while wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) is also questionable after the same practice schedule.
Tackle Garrett Bolles (hip) was limited all week but was also ruled questionable for Sunday's game. On the other end of the spectrum, star Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) was a full participant throughout the team's week of practice and was given no game day designation, meaning he should make his return on Sunday.
Allen, Waddle, and Bolles are all vitally important players for Denver, with Allen operating as the keystone of the Broncos' defensive line. Waddle leads the Broncos in catches and receiving yards, while Bolles has played every offensive snap of the season so far while protecting Bo Nix's blind side.
If any of those three players can't suit up on Sunday, the Broncos could be left significantly shorthanded. If they do play, the health of Rice and Delane will become even more noteworthy for Kansas City.

title: Patrick Mahomes Voices Thoughts on Josh Simmons Situation; Optimistic About 2026 Return
full_text:
One of the more concerning storylines in what has otherwise been a strong 5-1 start to the season for the Kansas City Chiefs has been Josh Simmons' back injury. A bulging disc in his lower back has kept the left tackle off the field the entire campaign, and the team placed him on Injured Reserve last week after his recovery stalled despite a brief return to practice in limited capacity.
Up until a few days ago, there was still optimism around the fanbase regarding Simmons' situation, as the training staff reportedly doesn't believe he'll need surgery for his injury and thinks he can heal with rest. However, the perception of Simmons took a turn for the worse when Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport revealed a dispute that went down in practice. According to the report, Simmons was in a team meeting with his feet propped up. Head coach Andy Reid took exception to this, and so did quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The superstar signal-caller allegedly asked Simmons to put his feet down and told him to leave the meeting in order to get treatment.
The latest development was bound to come up when the two-time MVP spoke to the media on Wednesday. He didn't directly confirm or deny the details of the exchange, but acknowledged that difficult conversations had taken place and that the team needs to do a better job of keeping those things in-house moving forward.
"Stuff like that doesn't really bother because I'm so in the moment. I think we've had the right conversations now," Mahomes stated. "We're moving in the direction. You have to have hard conversations at some point... We've built this culture of coming together as a family, and kind of doing whatever we can to make sure that not only the player but also the person is going in the right direction. You want to keep those conversations in the building, and so that's something we'll be better at moving forward."
Patrick Mahomes was asked about the story that came out Sunday morning between him and Josh Simmons. He told @Leabonics , "You have to be able to have tough conversations so that you can have better conversations going forward." pic.twitter.com/95NrEXWX4d
Rather than a hostile back-and-forth, Mahomes insisted that this was more of an open dialogue typical of the culture Reid has built throughout his years as head coach. He made sure to clarify that there was nothing malicious about the altercation and that things like that happen fairly often in the locker room.
Mahomes' outlook is far different from the one some Chiefs fans have taken amid the growing uncertainty surrounding Simmons. With the former first-round pick yet to play this season and now facing at least four more games on IR, questions about his future in Kansas City have grown. KCSN's very own Tucker Franklin and Matt Verderame recently pondered whether Simmons has played his final game in the red and gold. That isn't the perspective Mahomes has, though. He remains steadfast in his belief that Simmons has been working hard during this recovery process and will be back to help the team at some point.
"I'm extremely confident because I've seen the work he puts in," Mahomes said, according to 96.5 The Fan . "He's doing his rehab, he's doing his work, he's doing everything he can to be back on that field. He'll have a couple weeks here now while he's on IR where he can get himself back to the physical shape that he can be in. He'll be mentally confident to go out there and be the best version of himself, when he's able to do that, he'll be back on the football field."
Much has been said about the situation, and it certainly hasn't been a good look for the Chiefs. They invested a first-round pick in Simmons in last year's draft, and he was solid when he played across his eight starts as a rookie. However, he dealt with personal issues and a wrist injury that forced him to miss extended time, and it's starting to feel like his absence in 2026 is for something beyond football as well. In the meantime, undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has been filling in at left tackle . He's stepped into a difficult role early in his career, but Simmons was drafted to help protect Mahomes for years to come. It is no secret that the Chiefs' best version of themselves includes Simmons on the blind side of KC's franchise cornerstone.
The public narrative surrounding Simmons has become increasingly negative, which is why Mahomes made sure to tread carefully with his words. While his comments don't put to rest the rumors about the tackle's long-term future in Kansas City, they do shed light on how Mahomes saw things through his own lens.

title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes React to Chiefs’ Controversial Justin Tucker Signing
full_text:
Amid Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker's ongoing struggles, the franchise made a surprising move this morning by signing Justin Tucker to the practice squad . The former Baltimore Ravens standout hasn't kicked in the NFL since the 2024 season after serving a suspension for violating the league's Personal Conduct Policy.
Many Kansas City fans thought it was well overdue for the team to bring someone in to make Butker's job less secure. However, the signing has already faced significant backlash from the media. He was cut by Baltimore in May 2025 due to a combination of his declining performance and the allegations of sexual misconduct involving 16 massage therapists . When head coach Andy Reid stepped to the podium for his press conference today , he fielded questions about Tucker for approximately five consecutive minutes. One of the more notable questions he faced was about the message Tucker's signing sends to female Chiefs fans.
"He's done his suspension. Took care of that business there," Reid responded. "I'll leave it at that for you."
Reid emphasized that he and the front office had done extensive homework on Tucker's past before they decided to offer him a spot on the practice squad. He wouldn't quite elaborate on what this "homework" entailed, but insisted the team had spoken with multiple people before making its decision.
"We try to do our homework the best way we possibly can," Reid said. "Talked to a lot of people to make sure things are okay." KC's head coach said that the team brought in three kickers earlier this week to try out for a spot. Reid believes that Tucker was the best of the bunch by a long shot. He wasn't exactly effective in his last full season when he finished with a subpar 73.3% field goal percentage (22-for-30), and it's been a while since he's kicked in live action.
If there's anything this signing does, it makes it clear that Butker's future with the team is no longer guaranteed. He's cost the Chiefs too many points in recent years for this situation to be ignored any longer. Since the start of the 2025 campaign, Butker's 15 missed kicks and extra points are the most of any player in the NFL.
Even after bringing Tucker on board, Reid maintains that he is still confident in his longtime placekicker and believes Butker's recent shortcomings stem from inconsistent form and technique rather than a mental issue. "Listen, we love Harrison. I've told you before, he's one of my favorite guys," he said about Butker. "Sometimes, things don't go quite the way you want them, and you work on that. He understands the business and how it works. We had a practice squad position open, so for security, we brought [Tucker] in and put him in that spot. Butker gets it and he knows that's part of the business."
He also confirmed that the "up-and-down" Butker will receive most of the first-team reps in remaining practices leading up to the Broncos game and that he should be the only kicker active this Sunday.
Coincidentally, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Tucker have a history that goes beyond their time spent on opposing sidelines. The two (and Travis Kelce) were famously involved in a brief pregame confrontation over warm-up space in the 2024 AFC Championship Game, where KC would advance to Super Bowl LVIII in a 17-10 victory.
While there appeared to be bad blood between the two parties at the time, Mahomes chalked it up to competition and brushed the tension aside. "We haven't had a lot of conversations because he was on the Ravens, but it wasn't like we ever had any beef," Mahomes confirmed today. "At that moment, it was just competitors being competitors. He's been a big-time kicker for a long time... At the end of the day, we're just playing a game, and you want to compete and win."
Mahomes, who has always done an excellent job avoiding controversial answers to the media, wouldn't go in-depth on his thoughts about Tucker's signing and reaffirmed his trust in the front office. "We have a lot people that have been added in and out," Mahomes stated. "I try not go get too high or low or anything. I know [Brett] Veach does a great job of bringing players in."
There was always going to be an uproar over the Chiefs signing a shunned player whose NFL career appeared to be all but over. We'll soon find out whether Tucker is ever elevated to the 53-man roster and if he'll be an outside distraction moving forward.

title: Omarr Norman-Lott Taking Next Step in Return to Chiefs From ACL Tear
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs have been paid multiple visits by the pesky injury bug this season, although Week 8 presents one bit of good news on the defensive side of the ball.
Just over a year removed from sustaining a torn ACL , tackle Omarr Norman-Lott is being designated to return from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star first broke the news on Wednesday.
The Chiefs designated Omarr Norman-Lott to return to practice today, a source told The Star.
Norman-Lott, the 63rd overall pick in last year's NFL Draft, originally suffered the knee injury during a Week 7 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders. That ended his rookie campaign after the Tennessee product logged all of 73 snaps, recording five tackles and a sack in the process.
With the door for a potential regular-season debut now propped open, Norman-Lott is set to begin a 21-day window in which the team can evaluate his progress. At any point during that period, Kansas City can move Norman-Lott to the active 53-man roster. If he isn't ready to return, he'll remain on the shelf for the rest of the 2026-27 season.
Speaking to the media two weeks ago to the day, head coach Andy Reid briefly acknowledged that the sophomore tackle was inching closer to a potential return to action in some capacity.
"He is getting better, yeah," Reid said. "He is getting better. He's out working out with the trainers and doing that, but he's getting closer.”
This process seems to have taken longer than initially thought, as general manager Brett Veach shared back in April that he expected the former second-round pick to " be ready to rock and roll " for training camp. He was technically with the team at the Missouri Western State University campus, albeit to continue rehab and keep moving along at a slower pace.
Given the presence of All-Pro Chris Jones, the offseason signing of Khyiris Tonga and the first-round NFL Draft pickup of Peter Woods, there's no imminent pressure for Norman-Lott to get back on the field quickly. He'd presumably fill the role of someone like undrafted rookie Bryson Eason once ready, but Eason's played just 18 defensive snaps in four games.
According to Pro Football Focus , Norman-Lott logged six pressures in 48 pass-rushing opportunities as a first-year player. Considering his athletic profile during college compared to the seemingly bulked-up version the Chiefs fielded early on, it'll be interesting to see what role he assumes on defense when and if he plays down the stretch.
For a team that's been ravaged by recent injuries, this is a positive midweek development for Kansas City.

title: Chiefs Put Harrison Butker on Notice With Reported Justin Tucker Signing
full_text:
Despite their 5-1 record, the Kansas City Chiefs have experienced their fair share of issues throughout the 2026-27 season thus far. Getting consistent play out of the special teams unit, particularly regarding kicker Harrison Butker, is at or near the top of the list.
Following another rough outing for the club's longtime star kicker, Kansas City is bringing in another one to light a fire under Butker. It just so happens to be someone whose resume and track record blow Butker's out of the water.
First reported by Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star on Wednesday morning, the Chiefs are bringing in former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker on a practice squad basis.
The Chiefs are signing kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad, a source tells The Star.
Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN reports that the Chiefs also worked out two other kickers, including former Los Angeles Rams man Harrison Mevis.
Speaking to the media following Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , a game in which he went 1-for-3 on field goals, Butker tipped his cap to special teams coordinator Dave Toub for having his back through some recent struggles.
"I appreciate it," Butker said. "He definitely supports me. I'm in my 10th season here. I'm very thankful to have been with him for such a long time. He's my biggest supporter and always pushing me to do my best. Every kick matters, every day at practice, every game. I've got to be better."
Butker stated his pre-game warmup leading up to Sunday Night Football "wasn't great," although he couldn't pinpoint one specific thing that led to him missing his kicks.
Harrison Butker (Kansas City) ranks dead last in field goal pts over expected at -7.69, behind Trey Smack -7.28 (Green Bay) & Harrison Mevis -6.87 (Free Agent) Leaders: Will Reichard +9.47 (Minnesota), Chase McLaughlin +8.78 (Tampa Bay) & Ka'imi Fairbairn +8.56 (Houston) https://t.co/zIndx0hYoV
Tucker, a seven-time Pro Bowler and career 89.1% kicker on field goals, trails only Los Angeles Chargers standout Cameron Dicker (92.6%) as the most accurate player ever. Still, the move isn't necessarily as clear-cut in value as it appears on the surface.
First and foremost, it's been two seasons since Tucker's even kicked in an NFL game. He was suspended 10 weeks during the 2025 offseason following allegations of sexual misconduct, deemed a violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy. That followed Tucker being released by the Ravens, the only other NFL franchise he's ever known, on May 5 of the same year.
The veteran was reinstated on November 11 , only to remain unsigned for nearly a full calendar year thereafter. Tucker did get brought in for tryouts with the New Orleans Saints, Indianapolis Colts and New York Jets during that window.
Off-the-field developments aside, the Tucker signing comes with plenty of additional questions to answer. He's now several years removed from his last Pro Bowl campaign in 2023, and he left a trail of poor results on his way out of Baltimore. Kicking in all 17 regular-season games in 2024, he converted on just 22 of 30 field goal attempts, good for a 73.3% mark.
That includes a 6-of-11 ledger from 50-plus yards, which has been an issue for Butker lately as well.
Can someone who turns 37 in a matter of weeks, hasn't played in a game in 21 months and wasn't good the last time we saw him provide enough for the move to be worth it? That all remains to be seen.
At the least, it's a message to Butker that he must improve his level of play. Otherwise, his Chiefs tenure could be on ice.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Were the Chiefs Actually Exposed in Seattle?
full_text:
Things couldn't have gone much worse for the Kansas City Chiefs in their Sunday Night Football loss against the Seattle Seahawks . Still, KC remains at the top of the AFC with a 5-1 record and a lot of football still to be played.
What questions rose to the top of the Chiefs' list of uncertainties after their first loss of the year? Let's answer a few in this week's edition of the Chiefs On SI mailbag.
After this Seattle debacle, how bad have the Chiefs been exposed? - @MrEd315
I like the phrasing of this question, and I think I may surprise some people with my answer. How badly were the Chiefs exposed on Sunday? I'm not sure they were exposed at all!
The Chiefs' flaws in that game were glaring. Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong are not a legitimate 1-2-3 trio of wide receivers, and the Chiefs know that. The Seahawks knew that.
The injuries at offensive tackle—down to OT3 on the left side and OT4 on the right—were no secret either. The Seahawks may have "exposed" the fact that if you can stop Kenneth Walker, you can stop that version of the Chiefs' offense , but we talked about that issue all week, leading up to the game.
The pass rush wasn't nearly good enough at rattling Sam Darnold, but it was the fourth game this year where they failed to record a sack; that's not a new issue either.
This whole winding road leads me to a potentially unsatisfying point: the Chiefs lost that game more dramatically than I would have expected, but not for any reasons that weren't already top-of-mind. Is that enough to soothe all of your Chief concerns? Absolutely not. But it is a silver lining, and better than losing a game for some surprising, unforeseen reason.
How would you divvy up blame for the poor offensive performance between QB play, personnel, and scheme? I feel like the QB play is not a given to be Tier 1 like it was prior to 2024. - @broccolirabe.bsky.social
Patrick Mahomes has been excellent this season, but I do think the Seattle loss included his worst game of the year . With memories of the way he's been caught "pressing" in the past as he's tried to overcome his surroundings in recent years, I think the uncertainty at offensive tackle and lack of any legitimate separation from his pass-catchers allowed Mahomes to rediscover some bad habits in Seattle .
Still, late in the game, Mahomes seemed to find his groove again before being let down by his supporting cast. The quarterback is, by far, the least of my worries.
I do think the coaching staff could have given Kenneth Walker a few more tries on the ground before completely giving up on the running game (though it was unproductive when they did try it), and I'd love to see Cyrus Allen get a longer look when none of the other pass-catchers are standing out. Ultimately, I think that the deficiencies of the players who were thrust into action on Sunday night played the biggest role of the three options presented in the question.
How do they get to 10 wins? - @joeybeckley.bsky.social
Keep playing the games. They're 5-1. They have plenty of issues to solve, and this mailbag has detailed several, but I'd be absolutely floored if they're not a playoff team with double-digit wins.
With the injuries at WR and tackle and the lack of any sort of pass rush, could the Chiefs actually do a little selling at the deadline instead of adding? - @mrproctober.bsky.social
If some team wants to acquire a non-vital piece from KC, Brett Veach should hear them out, sure. In the meantime, they're currently the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Even if that seems unlikely to hold, a 5-1 team quarterbacked by Patrick Mahomes will not and should not be "sellers" at the deadline.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: Several Young Players Drop in Week 8
full_text:
Seven weeks into the 2026 NFL campaign, the Kansas City Chiefs finally suffered their first loss . There are no moral victories in this sport, although one potential silver lining is that the defeat came at the hands of an NFC club that very well could contend for the Super Bowl once again.
In the aftermath of an ugly showing on the road, Kansas City is sent back to the drawing board prior to a critical Sunday showdown against the Denver Broncos. The club's young players will surely be asked to contribute in an AFC West clash — which ones are trending in the right and wrong directions?
Following Week 7, let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each qualifying 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott isn't included due to him currently being on the physically unable to perform list . Left tackle Josh Simmons isn't included after going to injured reserve . The same applies to running back Brashard Smith .
When you notch an interception to potentially save a touchdown, you get kudos. When you do so in a game that was bordering on getting out of hand and your return sets up the team for an end-of-half field goal try, you get mentioned in this group. Cornerback Nohl Williams' impressive season rolls on thanks to his pick of Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold in Week 7.
NOHL WILLIAMS END ZONE INT AND A BIG RETURN KCvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/K42foMAhQy
First-round corner Mansoor Delane had a couple of rough reps against last season's Offensive Player of the Year, wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba, although one was simply a remarkable throw and catch. There's no need to worry about the LSU product moving forward. His third-down pass breakup and separate nice play on Smith-Njigba on a second-and-10 in the second half provided plenty of reason for continued optimism.
Rookie pass rusher R Mason Thomas and sophomore defensive end Ashton Gillotte were both shouted out in this week's stock watch story for their performances at Lumen Field. Thomas flashed more of his ability to put pressure on opposing signal-callers, whereas Gillotte's run defense was one of the few bright spots on Sunday Night Football .
Dropping down after temporarily being bumped up a tier are undrafted rookie offensive tackle Kahlil Benson and first-round defensive tackle Peter Woods. The former had one of his worst showings as a pro, albeit against a ruthless defense, but he was partially responsible for quarterback Patrick Mahomes being pressured at a top-five rate for his career. The latter played 33 snaps, good for nearly 48% of those available, but made a minimal impact.
First-year halfback Emmett Johnson didn't receive a single carry on offense for the second time in three games, but he did make a pair of nice plays in the passing game. One was a critical catch on a seemingly lost drive, and the next was a block that allowed Mahomes to pick up a rushing first down.
Wide receivers Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen both had moments that reminded those in Chiefs circles why they have yet to break out to this point. Allen, in particular, is a fan-favorite piece who many want to see the field more, but he's occasionally had trouble even navigating plays correctly.
UDFA defensive tackle Bryson Eason logged five snaps on defense and had an assisted tackle. He doesn't play special teams, so he can't move down a tier, but he's the least-noticeable player in this group.
The split of special teams versus offensive reps for tight end Jake Briningstool is up to 84-52 in 2026. In the last three games, it's 39-23. In Week 7, it was 12-5. Among this "primary special teams tier," he's the player it's easiest to see getting a promotion with a bit more involvement in future contests. Without someone above him getting hurt, safety Xavier Nwankpa's role seems capped, which is a shame considering the juice he brings to the field.
Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa is moderately similar to Nwankpa, although his role for special teams coordinator Dave Toub is more significant as a trusted option who's also made some plays this season. Given the shuffle at his defensive position, though, an increased snap count appears unlikely.
With Simmons on IR, UDFA tackle Diego Pounds technically was active for Week 7 but didn't play a single snap. He's here until further notice, joined by fourth-round rookie corner Jadon Canady , seventh-round rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier and UDFA defensive end Jack Pyburn . Nussmeier has routinely been the club's emergency third field general, but him not getting any live reps is a good thing.

title: If Mike McDaniel Still has Smashmouth Football in Him, Now is the Time for Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 and their offense has looked lost the entire season. Los Angeles has dealt with significant injuries all season with over half of their initial 53-man roster either on injured reserve or the injury report for week six.
Los Angeles' injury luck started when starting center Tyler Biadasz went down with a significant season-ending knee injury during a joint practice with the 49ers during training camp. The Chargers were forced to shuffle the offensive line with the season less than three weeks away and plug in rookie Jake Slaughter as the new starting center.
The injury to Biadasz seems to have been the catalyst for the wheels falling off of the offense's wagon. We never got to see Biadasz in game action, he did not play any snaps in the first preseason game and was injured before the second. But the reports from that joint practice, before the injury were that the Chargers offense was handily beating up the 49ers. The reports made sense coming on the heels of the Chargers backups physically dominating the Houston Texans in the first preseason game.
"The Chargers, they out-physicaled us the entire game."- Texans head coach Demeco Ryans pic.twitter.com/6Sh456WY3q
Biadasz' going down seems to have been the one injury that the offense and offensive line could not have survived, which raises more questions about roster construction and the interior offensive line as a whole. Regardless, the interior offensive line has not been good. Unfortunately, the injury bug did not stop with the line and attacked the wide receiver room as well.
The Chargers' original six wide receivers have all dealt with injuries this season. Not one of the six has played fully healthy every week and the lack of reps and continuity has ruined the timing of the offense. The disruption in timing paired with a run game that has not been a strong point and consistent interior pressure is largely how the Chargers still have not found their groove on offense.
The past two games before the bye in week seven featured four rookie starting offensive linemen. The Chargers will get Joe Alt back this week at one of the tackle spots, assuming he takes his right tackle spot back. it is possible that second-year lineman Branson Taylor figures somewhere into the lineup but if the lineup remains the same with the exception of Alt's return, the Chargers will still be starting three rookies on the offensive line, the entire left side of the line.
The Chargers rookie offensive linemen have played better than was expected but still have their rookie shortcomings. The good news is tackle Travis Burke and guard Logan Taylor are very capable run blockers. Burke is a mountain of an offensive lineman and generates significant movement at the point of attack. Note Burke's run-blocking grade on the chart below.
OT Percentile Grades in Pass & Run Blocking pic.twitter.com/Qti6mB1CT4
The strengths of the rookies could be the key to getting the Chargers back on track offensively, or at least help them find some sort of rhythm. Los Angeles will be getting some limited reinforcements back as wide receiver Ladd McConkey and Tre Harris are both scheduled to make their returns to the fields this week against the Rams. Tight end Charlie Kolar and wide receiver Quintin Johnston both emergeed from the bye without injury designations.
The question will be how does Mike McDaniel and the Chargers adjust following the bye week? Does McDaniel have any downhill smashmouth football left in his arsenal? The Chargers rushing attack has been much more successful to the left side and between the tackles. Compared to a similar offensive system in San Francisco, the Chargers run the ball between the tackles almost 20 percent less.
Based on EPA or expected points added by personnel groupings, the Chargers most efficient run formations are in 13 personnel lining up with a running back and three tight ends followed closely by  22 personnel featuring two tight ends and a fullback.
The Chargers should line up with Charlie Kolar, Hayden Rucci and Scott Matlock on the field and run right behind Travis Burke or Joe Alt, both of whom have comparable run blocking grades.
The Rams run dime personnel packages on defense nearly 50 percent of the time, meaning they have extra defensive backs on the field and create pressure by rotating and sending different players to the line of scrimmage. If they want to give the Chargers lighter defensive personnel packages, the Chargers should lean into what strengths they have.
The Rams sent most of their starting defensive line to injured reserve. They still have Aaron Donald and he can still wreck an offensive line's gameplan but Myles Garrett will not be back yet so the focus can be on Donald.
The offense under Mike McDaniel has not gone smoothly. There is blame to go around to every corner of the team and organization. But, if the Chargers and McDaniel found positives to lean into coming out the bye, now is the time to implement them.
Based on the available personnel and data from first six weeks, ditching the higher frequency of outside zone in favor of more inside zone or gap runs may be beneficial. It does go against the Miami version of McDaniel, can he tap into his Shanahan roots as a playcaller against the Rams?
Thomas Martinez has covered the Chargers and the NFL draft since 2022. Born and raised as a Chargers fan, experienced the improbable Super Bowl run in the 94’ season as a child, survived Ryan Leaf, the Marlon McCree fumble and Nate Kaeding in the playoffs. title: NFL Trade Rumors Update Tells Unfortunate Story About Jim Harbaugh's Chargers
full_text:
It feels like a matter of time before the Los Angeles Chargers host a fire sale at the NFL trade deadline .
Nobody told Jim Harbaugh, Joe Hortiz or the Chargers, though.
Despite the stubbornness coming out of Los Angeles right now , everyone seems to agree that the Chargers will trade Khalil Mack before the deadline.
Not as likely, though just as smart, would be the Chargers trading away Quentin Johnston, getting anything in return for the obvious-feeling departure for the former first-round pick in the near future.
But exiting the bye, the Chargers have kept the messaging as positive and simple as possible despite the 0-6 record. Little is changing, and they still aren’t selling.
The Chargers might be so bad that they clutch the No. 1 pick in a year when even the Tennessee Titans are having a “down” year. They might clutch the No. 1 pick so strongly that even the “tank bowl” against Miami later this year has become less important.
But the Chargers aren’t selling yet.
So says the latest NFL trade rumors update from Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer .
“The Chargers have shut down trade inquiries for their veterans, even as the team sits at 0–6,” Breer wrote. “So while there are questions about guys like Khalil Mack and Quentin Johnston, for now, GM Joe Hortiz and coach Jim Harbaugh appear unwilling to wave any sort of white flag.”
If nothing else, this is just more reinforcement that Mack and Johnston remain the most appealing and obvious Chargers trade candidates.
At wideout, trading Ladd McConkey isn’t realistic. He’s the centerpiece of a depth chart rebuild there. They need to see more reps for guys like Tre Harris.
And on the defensive edge, letting go of Tuli Tuipulotu instead would only make sense if contract extension talks have gone absolutely nuclear. Mack leaving would mean more work for first-rounder Akheem Mesidor and others.
Other than that…the Chargers don’t really have any trade candidates. There’s a depth cornerback here or there that might interest other teams. Maybe a depth running back. But this…sort of speaks to just how bad the roster is, right?
The Chargers will change this tune ahead of the deadline. Falling to 0-7 after a date with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday is the next one to circle in red on the calendar.

title: The Case For—and Against—the Chargers Trading Away Khalil Mack
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10, at 4:00 pm ET. This week, a few teams wasted little time making deals and/or unloading veterans.
The Indianapolis Colts have been the busiest of the clubs when it comes to the latter. Earlier this week, the team sent eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and orchestrated a reunion between the San Francisco 49ers and three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. In 2020, the Colts acquired the star defender from the Niners for the 13th overall pick.
On Thursday, the Chicago Bears added 2025 First Team All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and gave up plenty to get the four-time Pro Bowler. Last season, he totaled 67 tackles, a career-best 11.0 sacks, and forced three fumbles. In seven games with the Tennessee Titans this season, he led the club with four sacks.
Speaking of leading a team in quarterback traps, ageless Khalil Mack has come up with three sacks for the last-place Los Angeles Chargers. There’s been a lot of speculation that the league’s only winless could have their own fire sale of their own when it comes to unloading players.
A playoff club each of the first two seasons under head coach Jim Harbaugh, the Bolts have lost as many games this season as they did in both 2024 and 2025. So could general manager Joe Hortiz make the 13-year veteran available in the next week or so?
13 sacks in the regular season and the first in the postseason for Tuli Tuipulotu LACvsNE on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/8fTPmVAZyw
The fifth overall pick in the 2014 NFL draft by the then-Oakland Raiders has played for three teams and been a three-time Pro Bowl performer for each. And the 35-year-old defender has moved from franchise to franchise via the trade route. The Silver and Black sent him to the Windy City in 2018, and the Chicago Bears then dealt him to the Chargers in 2022.
The resume reads 116.0 regular-season sacks, 36 forced fumbles, 13 fumble recoveries, and three interceptions—two of those returned for scores. However, the Bolts have a pair of young studs in rookie Akheem Mesidor and 2025 Pro Bowler Tuli Tuipulotu. It’s almost inexplicable that the latter has not been signed to a contract extension, and it’s hard to believe that it won’t eventually get done.
For a team in playoff contention and looking for pass-rush help, Mack makes a lot of sense and should come at a reasonable price draft-choice wise.
The veteran’s experience is certainly a plus when it comes to Tuipulotu and Mesidor in terms of what they can or have learned from him. And Mack is also not a one-trick pony as the 13-year veteran is a more-than-capable run defender. But is that enough to retain the prolific defender and not try and get something for him via trade? Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report suggests Mack could be had for a conditional fourth-round pick in 2027.
The answer appears obvious. A team like the Carolina Panthers, who have just 11 sacks in seven games and zero sacks in their last two contests, could certainly use some help. Jaelan Phillips has missed the last few games and the team was hurting in this area before he went down. The AFC West-leading and division rival Kansas City Chiefs (8 sacks in 6 games) could also use some help in this department. Stay tuned.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: The Chargers May be Hurting Themselves with Their Trade Deadline Plan
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are six games into a dumpster fire of a season. They emerge from their week seven bye with an 0-6 record and a looming trade deadline.
The Chargers have been operating under a plan where standing pat on trades was their communicated position across the NFL. The Chargers have been trying to find some positive progress on offense during this losing streak but their most recent loss in week six to the Kansas City Chiefs had them l ooking like the walking dead.
The Chargers season has been essentially lost for a month entering week eight. Teams around the NFL have been inquiring about potential trade candidates from the Chargers roster for several weeks and those calls have been focused around Khalil Mack and running back Kimani Vidal to a lesser extent.
While general manager Joe Hortiz and the Chargers front office have been rebuking trade calls, the rest of the NFL moved forward and emerging contenders aggressively made attempts to improve their rosters. The Indianapolis Colts at 2-5, fired their general manager and immediately began selling off tradeable assets to recoup draft capital. The Colts sent All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the 49ers and may not be done.
The biggest trade to hit the newswire was the Chicago Bears sending two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick to the Tennessee Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The Simmons trade was not a shocker simply because of his status as one of the best defensive players in the NFL, it was more shocking because the Titans just extended Simmons on a new contract this past offseason to a record-breaking new deal.
The trades of Buckner and Simmons directly affect the Chargers and any potential trades that could have been in the works. Both the 49ers and Bears were teams and landing spots in much of the trade rumors surrounding veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack. Mack, who is on an expiring contract and more importantly, deserves to play for a contender after he trusted the Chargers brain trust to reach the playoffs again this season and chose to re-sign with the franchise.
The teams most connected to the Chargers and a potential trade for Khalil Mack have already given up draft capital for other players on the same side of the ball. Did the Chargers wait too long to find the optimal landing spot for a respected veteran as other teams chose to go in other directions? Did they hold onto hopes for turning around a season too long to now they will get less than ideal compensation? It will be interesting to monitor as this discussion moves forward and closer to the November 10th deadline.
At the very least, NFL insider Ian Rapoport is indicating the Bears are still looking to inquire about Mack even after trading for Jeffery Simmons.
From @NFLGameDay Kickoff: With trades on the mind, we break down the chances of a Jonathan Taylor or Khalil Mack trade. pic.twitter.com/IUdx1AKnTv
There has been no indication that Mack has sought out or asked for a trade or even discussed the possibility with Los Angeles' front office. Whatever happens in the coming weeks, the Chargers should do right by Mack, whatever his preference may be.
