title: Chargers May Need to Explore Sneaky Edge Rusher Option as Trade Speculation Builds
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers could soon find themselves looking for another answer along their defensive front, especially with Khalil Mack’s future with the team up in the air. He has been the poster boy for players who could get traded before the deadline.
Of course, losing a player like Mack would leave a significant hole in the pass rush and finding someone capable of helping fill that role won’t be easy. Yet it might just be that easy, as an intriguing pass rusher could be on the move.
ESPN reporter Jeremy Fowler listed Tampa Bay edge Yaya Diaby as a top trade candidate if he is truly available. Also noting that “Tampa is not poised to pay the 2027 free agent.” He is a sneaky target for the Chargers if the defensive line depletes.
The Chargers don’t necessarily need to replace Mack with another established superstar if he eventually moves on. Finding a younger pass rusher who can develop into a bigger part of the defense could be a smarter long-term approach. Diaby brings an interesting combination of size, strength and explosiveness that could give the Bolts another weapon off the edge.
Yaya Diaby has recorded a total of 22 sacks in his career including this season. He also has put up seven plus sack seasons a couple times in his career, and recently recorded three of them in one game. These numbers don't scream elite, but they do show him as a valuable starting player.
There is also something appealing about the possibility of getting ahead of the market before other teams start looking for the same type of player. He could give them an opportunity to add talent without having to pursue one of the more expensive names that might become available. Of course, the Buccaneers would have to be willing to entertain a deal, and the asking price would need to make sense.
Diaby could be an interesting investment for a team that may soon need more production off the edge. The Chargers have a chance to get ahead of a potential problem before it becomes an immediate need. So exploring younger options could be one way to do that. Replacing what Mack brings to the defense is no small task. However, they should at least explore their options if his future becomes uncertain. Sometimes the most interesting moves are the ones that aren’t getting much attention. If the Bolts want to keep its pass rush competitive while getting younger at the position then this is a trade worth considering.
It's possible that teams just don't believe in the player at this point, but the 1-5 Bucs should absolutely look to trade YaYa Diaby. He's been pretty clearly their 4th best Edge Rusher this season, taking reps from David Walker & Reuben Bain, is a pending Free Agent, and…

title: Chargers’ Weird Mike McDaniel Decision Starting to Feel Like a Tank Job
full_text:
One could confuse the Los Angeles Chargers as a team purposely tanking for the top pick in the NFL draft right now.
Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers aren’t tanking, not really. But a real tank job wouldn’t look much different from what they have done so far.
Harbaugh’s Chargers are, after all, 0-6 and somehow getting more injured coming out of a bye week . They’re continuing to ruin Justin Herbert while Mike McDaniel gets a regression from every single piece of the offense while largely mishandling players like, say, former first-round pick Omarion Hampton.
And to top it all off, the Chargers just made a weird call with Mike McDaniel.
Maybe everyone should have seen this coming when Harbaugh and the Chargers did nothing with McDaniel to start the bye week. There wasn’t even a hint of, say, someone else taking over play-calling duties, or even getting more involved with them.
To start the week after the bye, Harbaugh even stepped to the podium and defended McDaniel while saying the coordinator would remain the play-caller of the offense.
"We're very confident in Mike and his talent, his work ethic and his ability," Harbaugh told reporters . "We continue to be."
And in the ultimate form of professional player-speak, Herbert then got to the microphone and pointed the blame not at McDaniel, but at the players themselves.
"It's not [McDaniel's} fault, it's our fault as an offense," Herbert said. "We have to do our job. It's not Mike's fault. The guys are open, plays are being made. It's on us to run, to block, to catch, to throw. It's on us as an offense."
The issues with McDaniel are many. There’s poor injury luck mixed in, as usual in Los Angeles. But his arriving and reworking Herbert’s throwing motion and/or footwork from certain formations didn’t help. Neither does trying to run his Miami-looking offense with dramatically slower, worse skill position players. And his mentioned avoidance of Hampton in favor of a middling running back rotation is another one of those weird issues he doesn’t seem to be in a hurry to fix.
And look, firing McDaniel now, or ripping away play-calling duties, would push the notorious Adam Gase into a bigger role. Maybe not ideal. Firing McDaniel now or after the season probably won’t be all that different.
Even so, just keeping McDaniel amid all these regressions and problems sends a pretty poor message to the locker room. If the players keep not buying into the message or things get even worse, it runs the risk of offering up the entire coaching staff as a sacrificial lamb after the season, not just McDaniel.
Maybe there’s no stopping that anyway. But sticking with McDaniel while "simplifying" the offense probably isn’t the fix most fans wanted to see during a bye week for an 0-6 team. That is, unless they’re fans only fixating on the No. 1 pick now, anyway.

full_text:
The winless Los Angeles Chargers , now first in the NFL draft order with no end to the suffering in sight, feel like a team with everything on the table when it comes to selling and just starting the rebuild at the NFL trade deadline.
Everything but trading Justin Herbert, of course.
Trading Khalil Mack makes sense. Offloading Quentin Johnston before rebuilding the entire wideout depth chart around Ladd McConkey does, too. One could even believe the Chargers trading Tuli Tuipulotu if contract extension talks have really gone off the rails too.

title: Why the Chargers did not Chase Quenton Nelson Despite Needing Guard Help
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 and have two games before the November 10th trade deadline. In a season that is all but lost, they should not be buyers on the trade market. They have stuck to their plan to stand pat on trades , but that could quickly change.
However, if the Chargers make any moves as buyers or sellers before the deadline, the focus should be solely on the long-term future. The two areas of need currently facing the Chargers and will be the areas in the offseason that will be hotly dicsussed, is the interior offensive line and wide receivers.
The Chargers interior offensive line is a problem. Once center Tyler Biadasz went down with the season-ending injury during training camp, the wheels came off the wagon for the Chargers offensive line. This is more of a roster-building problem overall.
The Chargers' plan was to have two lighter, faster and cheaper guards sandwiched between elite tackles and a veteran center and elevated by the scheme. Once Biadasz went down the plan came crumbling down. Short of a dramatic lineup shift , the interior will have to figure out how to keep Herbert upright.
Now rookie center Jake Slaughter, who spent the offseason working on converting to guard, jumped into the starting lineup but having Slaughter and right guard Cole Strange next to each other created a natural weak point given they were intended to be the lighter and faster guards. The interior has struggled, injuries have mounted and the Chargers have been forced to start four rookies on the offensive line in their past two games against the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs.
One of the marquis players set to hit free agency after the 2026 season is All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. If the Chargers had wanted to overcorrect and make sure Quenton Nelson does not his free agency next season, they may have tried to target him via trade simply for 2027 and beyond.
Had Los Angeles attempted to trade for him, they would have had to match the Seahawks offer, which given their current draft position would have been better but they would have had to likely negotiate a new contract with the eight-time pro bowler. Nelson's next contract, which will likely fall somewhere North of $100 million with an average annual value closer to $30 million.
The Colts fired their general manager Chris Ballard and are looking to recoup draft capital for 2027 after Ballard traded away their first-round pick in 2027 for Sauce Gardner. Could the Chargers have made a run at Nelson given their current and future needs? Yes, but utilizing that much of the cap and draft capital given the current needs of the team would have been a fool's errand.
Nelson is an awesome player and could still hit free agency in the offseason, although it is highly unlikely. The Chargers will likely be exclusively sellers at the deadline as they hope reinforcements from injury can help them find some hope before the season wraps up. General manager Joe Hortiz and the Chargers front office will have to be more aggressive in addressing the interior of the offensive line in the offseason.

full_text:

Unfortunately for Los Angeles, the bye week helped a few players get back to health, but several others have not made progress or have suffered setbacks. title: Another Intriguing Option Has Popped Up On the Trade Market for the Chargers
full_text:
The NFL trade market is beginning to heat up, and the Los Angeles Chargers could have an opportunity to add another weapon to their offense.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade. Putting an intriguing young receiver on the radar of teams looking for help through the air.
For a team looking to get more out of its passing game , Downs is a name worth keeping an eye on. The 25-year-old has already shown he can produce at the NFL level, however with his future on the Colts becoming uncertain. A change of scenery could give him the opportunity to take another step forward.
At 5-foot-9, he isn’t the biggest receiver on the field, but his game is built around quickness, route running and finding ways to get open in tight spaces. Those qualities can make a major difference when an offense needs to move the chains rather than constantly depend on explosive plays downfield.
For Justin Herbert, having another receiver who can create separation underneath could be especially valuable.
Downs has demonstrated the ability to work out of the slot, giving an offense another option on short and intermediate routes. Instead of forcing throws into coverage or waiting for longer routes to develop, Herbert could have a reliable target who helps keep drives alive.
The fit becomes even more interesting when considering how a receiver like Downs could complement the other pieces already in place. His ability to operate in the middle of the field would give opposing defenses another area to worry about, potentially opening up opportunities for teammates on the outside. Adding a player with a different skill set could make the passing attack more difficult to defend without requiring him to immediately become the focal point of the offense. Of course, any potential deal would depend on the asking price. Downs is in the final year of his rookie contract, meaning the team acquiring him would also have to consider his long-term future. Giving up valuable draft capital for a player who could leave after the season is something the front office would need to weigh carefully.
Still, there is a reasonable argument for taking that chance if the price is right. Downs is young, has established himself as a productive NFL receiver and could fill a specific role without requiring a complete overhaul of the offense.
There is no guarantee Indianapolis will move him, or that the Bolts will be among the teams pursuing him. But with the trade deadline approaching, this is exactly the type of opportunity worth monitoring. If the right deal becomes available, Downs could give Herbert another weapon and provide the offense with a dimension it would benefit from having.

title: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday’s game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful.
Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday.
If the Rams are without Shelton, they will turn to backup Dylan McMahon. McMahon has been in the system for the past two years, developing on the practice squad. This is the first year he’s spent most of his time on the active roster.
“What's been good is Dylan McMahon has done a great job this week. He's had a lot of work,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Dylan's had a lot of work this week because of the approach we've taken with Coleman. I think he's handled it really well. He's been here for a handful of years so he would be the guy that would step up.”
Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well.
Additionally, Parkinson didn’t participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game.
“He brings a lot,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. “I think he's as good as anybody in the league right now at the point of attack on the line of scrimmage. I think his ability to impact in the pass game has been tremendous. He gives you more than what I think anybody even realizes or expects.”
Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington’s back locked up in practice, which is why he’ll be listed as questionable.
On the Chargers’ side, they’ll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries.
The Rams have been managing injuries all season and Sunday will be no different. If the Rams are going to win back-to-back games for the first time this season, they’ll be relying on their depth to get by. Going up against the 0-6 Chargers, the Rams will hope that they can get by another week with key starters injured.

title: Jeffery Simmons Trade Exposes the Biggest Risk Rams Took With Myles Garrett
full_text:
This week, the NFL trade market has heated up significantly. While the Los Angeles Rams made their big moves in the offseason , the Seattle Seahawks traded for Quenton Nelson on Tuesday while the San Francisco 49ers added DeForest Buckner. A day later, the Chicago Bears made one of the biggest trades of the season when they acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.
As those teams get the benefit of seeing their big acquisitions take the field immediately, the Rams continue to wait on Myles Garrett. Garrett has spent the last six weeks on injured reserve. After reports surfaced that Garrett would return to practice this week, the Rams declined to activate his 21-day practice window.
Through every passing week, the timeline of when Garrett will actually return only seems to get further away . While Garrett initially had a reported six-week timeline, it now seems unlikely that he will return before the bye week. The Rams are traveling to the east coast next week to play on a grass field in Washington that has historically been lower quality, although upgrades have been made in recent years. The following week, the Rams have a rematch with the Cardinals. It’s possible the Rams may feel they can beat the Cardinals without Garrett.
When the Rams acquired Garrett, they gave up a future first-round pick in 2027, a star edge rusher in Jared Verse, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round pick. That’s a huge haul for a player that has yet to take a healthy snap for the team.
That haul also became the baseline for the Bears’ deal with the Titans for Simmons on Wednesday. Simmons has been an elite defensive tackle in the NFL over the past several seasons, but has been overshadowed on a struggling Titans team.
Detailing how the trade for Simmons went down, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer looked into previous trades that the Rams had made for Matthew Stafford and Garrett.
“Borgonzi’s research into the Watson, Stafford, Wilson and Hunter deals, had put a ballpark price in his head for what it might take to actually part with Simmons. He told Poles he’d need the Browns’ equivalent they got from the Rams in the Myles Garrett trade,” wrote Breer. “The Rams gave up a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, a 2029 third-round pick and star rusher Jared Verse for Garrett. Verse’s inclusion, as Borgonzi saw it, is why the 2028 pick was a second-rounder rather than a first. And the third-rounder Cleveland got was two and a half years off, devaluing it a bit.”
The Bears ended up giving away 2027 and 2028 first-round picks in addition to a 2027 fourth-round pick to acquire Simmons. While the Bears gave up a similar package for Simmons that the Rams gave up for Garrett, there is still a big difference in the deals.
On Monday, the Bears will take the field with Simmons as part of their defense. Meanwhile, the Rams are still waiting for Garrett to take a healthy snap after placing him on injured reserve before Week 2,
This isn’t to say that the Rams should have done a trade for Simmons instead of Garrett. For starters, Simmons and Garrett don’t play the same position. The Rams were already good on the defensive line with Kobie Turner,  Braden Fiske, and Poona Ford. Additionally, Simmons had just signed an extension with the Titans in June and likely wasn’t available.
With that said, it does emphasize the risk that the Rams took with Garrett. Over the past few years, when the Rams have made these types of blockbuster trades, they’ve mostly worked out. The trade for Stafford resulted in a Super Bowl win. Jalen Ramsey was an integral part of the secondary. The trade for Brandin Cooks may not have worked out as well, but he played well in 2018.
When the Rams traded for Garrett, they couldn’t have anticipated that seven games into the season, he would have played just once. However, an argument can be made that the Rams got greedy in a sense when they traded for Garrett. The Rams didn’t have a need for a pass rusher, but saw Garrett as an upgrade over Verse . It was a calculated risk, but right now, they are paying the price.
The Rams currently rank 17th in pressure rate at 39 percent and their four percent sack rate ranks 28th. That’s also while blitzing at a 28.1 percent rate, which ranks 15th. Last season, the Rams ranked second in pressure rate and ninth in sack rate with the lowest blitz rate in the NFL.
It’s hard to blame the Rams for making the trade for Garrett. However, given that they didn’t have a need at that spot to begin with, waiting until the season to make a splash might have made more sense.
By trading for Garrett in the offseason, the Rams sacrificed both future draft capital and a young pass rusher who could have continued making an impact on the defense. Instead of having the flexibility to address their needs at the trade deadline, they have been left waiting and hoping that Garrett returns to the field at some point. Right now, that doesn’t seem like a guarantee.
The Bears traded for a healthy Simmons, hoping that he can push them over the hump in a competitive NFC. However, the Bears will have an opportunity to see the impact of their investment immediately while the Rams continue to wait. The Rams took a risk trading for Garrett when they did, and right now, it has yet to pay dividends.

title: Les Snead's Trade Deadline History Reveals When Rams Could Make a Move
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams get closer to the NFL trade deadline, the anticipation of whether or not they will make a deal continues to grow. There have been some rumors that the Rams could be interested in a wide receiver. However, after the flurry of moves this week, including trades by three teams in the NFC, two of which were in the NFC West, the Rams stood pat .
It’s possible that the Rams are waiting for the market to take shape and for things to cool down. Les Snead is typically good about waiting for the right opportunity. With exactly 11 days until the trade deadline, Snead has made three trades within that time period. Given his past history, if the Rams make a trade, next week or deadline day appears to be when a move will most likely happen.
Throughout the Les Snead era, the Rams have made four trades on deadline day. However, he’s also made two trades eight days ahead of the deadline and one trade the day ahead of the deadline.
When the Rams traded for Austin Corbett and Jalen Ramsey in 2019, both of those trades landed outside of the 12-day window. In 2021, Snead’s trade for Von Miller happened on the day before the deadline. Meanwhile, when the Rams traded for Roger McCreary last year, it happened eight days ahead of the deadline.
Snead has undoubtedly been one of the more active general managers when it comes to trades ahead of the deadline. Only four general managers have made more trades than Snead and only two have made more trades on deadline day.
If the Rams do make a trade next week, Monday seems like the most realistic scenario. This is typically when the Rams evaluate their roster for the upcoming week. Outside of actual deadline day, which typically takes place on a Tuesday, Snead hasn’t made a trade within the 12-day window later in the week. While the Chicago Bears traded for Jeffrey Simmons on Thursday, that isn't typically when Snead has made his moves. It’s more realistic that he’ll wait until after the game on Sunday.
The Rams will certainly have options at the trade deadline, especially if they are looking at wide receivers . Josh Downs requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts last week and is expected to get moved. Brian Thomas Jr. is an option as well as he continues to fall out of favor with the Jacksonville Jaguars.
With the wide receiver market as hot as it is, Snead and the Rams may opt to wait to see how things shake out and for the market to cool down. While the lack of a trade this week during the NFC arms race may have been frustrating, it doesn’t mean they won’t still be buyers at the deadline. Snead may simply be waiting for the right opportunity. If the Rams don’t make a trade early next week, they may be waiting until the final days of the deadline given Snead’s history.

title: The Real Reason The Rams Are Keeping Two Kickers on Their Roster
full_text:
Earlier this week, the Los Angeles Rams brought back kicker Joshua Karty after cutting him last season. Karty was just 10-of-15 on field goals last year and 23-of-26 on extra points. He also had four kicks that were blocked.
It’s not a bad idea for the Rams to add a younger kicker on the practice squad. Brandon McManus should help add some stability to the kicking operation as a veteran. However, heading into next season, the Rams would be right back at square one in their search for a kicker.
If nothing else, Karty gives the Rams a young, promising kicker that they can hope to develop. The presence of McManus, a different long snapper, and a new special teams coordinator could be beneficial to Karty. At one point, Karty was a talented kicker. From the end of his rookie season until his two blocked kicks against the Philadelphia Eagles, Karty had made 21 consecutive field goals and was 5-for-5 on kicks of 50 yards or more. If the Rams can get that out of Karty again, it could work out.
For the time being, where Karty may provide some value is on the kickoff unit. The Rams currently rank 31st in average kickoff yards allowed per return. The Rams have allowed an average of 29.7 yards per return, which is only ahead of the Miami Dolphins. Last week, the Rams allowed returns of 36 and 42 yards on their first two kickoffs of the game. It’s something that is continuously eating at head coach Sean McVay.
“We've talked about this a lot and it has to get fixed. It's not good enough and we cannot allow ourselves to do that,” said McVay earlier this week. “I have to figure that out. It's one of those deals that’s driving me crazy. We have to figure it out and we haven't yet.”
At this point, it seems as if McVay is willing to try anything to fix the kickoff coverage unit, which may be partially why the Rams brought back Karty. Last year, Karty led all kickers in fewest yards allowed via kickoff with 17.7. That’s over 10 yards better than where the Rams are currently.
A big reason for Karty’s success on kickoff was his ability to execute a ‘knuckleball’-type kick that made it difficult for the returner to handle. This allowed the Rams’ coverage unit time to get downfield as the returner struggled to handle the ball.
these knuckleball kickoffs are leading to some comical moments of NFL returners looking like the kids in the outfield during the home run derby. pic.twitter.com/G0TeqFjpru
The knuckleball kickoff is something that the Rams executed very well last season. The Rams currently rank last in kickoff DVOA at -8.6 percent. The Rams had the fourth-best kickoff unit last year, ranking fourth. With the overall lack of speed on the coverage unit, the knuckleball kickoff could be a benefit.
Ideally, the Rams would only want to have one kicker activated on gameday. It’s not at all customary for teams to have two kickers active on gamedays. However, until the Rams can trust Karty enough in the field goal operation, it may be their only choice.
“We'll work through those things and just see how the week goes,” said McVay on Wednesday. “When you have 48 bodies and the different guys that are filling in, you have to really ask yourself, 'Okay, does that really make sense? Does it fit?' There are a lot of layers to it.”
A knuckleball kickoff from the LA Rams to start their game against the 49ers 😅 pic.twitter.com/FdLGp9dPO0
Given some of the Rams’ injuries, they do have some flexibility to create space on the 48-man roster. There is a scenario where it could work. Here’s how the gameday roster could look on Sunday against the Chargers:
Quarterback (2): Matthew Stafford, Stetson Bennett Running Back (3): Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, Dean Connors Wide Receiver (6): Puka Nacua, Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Alex Bachman, CJ Daniels Tight End (3): Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen Offensive Line (7): Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Dylan McMahon, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon, David Quessenberry, Beaux Limmer Defensive Line (5): Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis, Ty Hamilton, Larrell Murchison EDGE Rusher (5): Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart, Wesley Bailey, Desjuan Johnson, Darryl Peterson III Linebacker (4): Nate Landman, Omar Speights, Shaun Dolac, Grant Stuard Cornerback (4): Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Josh Wallace, Emmanuel Forbes Safety (5): Quentin Lake, Kam Curl, Kam Kinchens, Jaylen McCollough, Maximus Pulley Special Teams (4): Brandon McManus, Josh Karty, Ethan Evans, Jake McQuaide. Inactives (5): Ty Simpson (Emergency QB), Max Klare, Coleman Shelton (Injured), Bill Murray, Joe Cardona (Injured)
It’s very possible that the Rams wanted Jon Rhattigan to be active for special teams this week after signing him. However, with the injury to Cardona, they’ll need to use one of their two practice squad elevations on McQuaide, leaving the other available for Karty.
While unconventional, it is doable for the Rams to have two kickers active on gameday. Desperate times call for desperate measures, and for the past month, it’s been easy to hear the desperation in McVay’s voice .
The Rams have lost several games this season in which special teams have played a significant role. It’s not something the Rams can just sit back and not do anything in hopes that it gets better. Through seven weeks of the season, that hasn’t been the case. The Rams may not activate two kickers on gameday and simply keep Karty available on the practice squad. However, they have reached a point where they at least have to consider it.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Biggest Trade Deadline Need Has Become Painfully Obvious
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams near the trade deadline , it has become increasingly clear that the team needs a WR3. While they primarily operate out of 13 personnel, the Rams still use three wide receiver sets at a 55.9 percent rate. It’s true that they are set to get Davante Adams back in approximately six weeks. However, they still lack depth behind Puka Nacua should he miss more time due to injury.
There comes a point when the Rams have to stop living in the fallacy that Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield are good enough. Last season, the Rams entered the trade deadline with an obvious need at cornerback. In the NFC Championship game against the Seattle Seahawks, the Rams allowed Sam Darnold to throw for 346 yards and three touchdowns.
Throughout the season, it was painfully obvious that the Rams had a need at cornerback. However, the Rams did nothing and it cost them. That’s not a mistake that the Rams can afford to make twice, let alone in back-to-back years.
We can certainly point to times in which Atwell has stepped up. When the Rams were without Cooper Kupp in 2023, Atwell stepped up along with Nacua and played well. Atwell stepped up again in 2024 when his number was called.
However, we can’t keep living in a world from two years ago. The Rams and head coach Sean McVay have let everyone know what they think of Atwell and it isn’t as a WR2 or WR3 in the offense. Despite paying Atwell $10 million that was fully guaranteed, Atwell had six receptions total last season. This year, he has three. It’s clear that the Rams see Atwell as nothing more than a vertical clear-out player. That has value in an offense, but it’s also replaceable.
It’s fine to be hopeful for what Konata Mumpfield can be. However, right now, the Rams have to live in the reality of what he is. Despite being the de facto WR2 last week, Mumpfield had one reception for 15 yards. He has nine receptions for 142 yards on the season with a 42.1 percent targeted success rate.
Jordan Whittington is a great special teams player. With that said, the idea that he’s a Puka Nacua-lite is simply not the reality. Whittington has had opportunities. He has two receptions this season. Whittington has 42 career receptions and 38 percent of those all came during a three-game stretch in his rookie season.
Even prior to Adams getting hurt, the Rams needed a WR3 in the offense that they can rely on consistently to win over the middle. Mumpfield is averaging -0.07 EPA per target and Whittington is averaging -0.24 EPA per target. They are actively detrimental to the offense.
Among 131 wide receivers to run at least 50 routes this season, Whittington’s targeted success rate ranks 119th. Mumpfield’s 42.1 percent ranks 96th. Whittington and Atwell each have 0.05 targets per route, which ranks 130th. Mumpfield’s 0.14 ranks 99th. In yards per route run, Atwell and Whittington both rank inside the bottom-10 while Mumpfield is 95th.
It simply isn’t good enough and won’t be good enough come December and January when the games matter more. The Rams have a clear need at WR3 and if they want to properly compete for a Super Bowl, they’d be right to address it at the trade deadline.
Last week, it was reported that the Rams were exploring options at wide receiver. According to 1st and Tuna , the Rams are expected to be among the teams to make an offer for Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
It’s unclear exactly what Thomas would cost in a trade. Given his draft status as a former first-round pick and previous production, a second-round pick seems likely. At the same time, if the Jaguars simply want to move on from Thomas and don’t want to bench him, they could be willing to move off of him for less. It’s certainly a situation to keep an eye on over the next week.
Additionally, the Rams are reported to have interest in Josh Downs according to Josh Taylor.
The Raiders, Jags, Patriots, Chiefs, Rams, and 49ers are all interested in Josh Downs per sources.
While Thomas would fit the need as the Rams’ “X” receiver when Adams is out, his fit becomes a lot more complicated after that. Meanwhile, Downs would fit in the offense alongside Adams and Nacua and may only cost a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Downs may have more of a market as teams look to add a wide receiver. We’ll see if the Rams get involved. For now, the interest appears to exist.
There’s no doubt that the Rams have dealt with their share of injuries this season. Their biggest offseason addition hasn’t played since Week 1 and their other big offseason acquisition has missed the last two games. However, it can be easy to get sucked into an echo chamber during the NFL season.
RotoWire recently put together an impact index score to quantify how hard teams have been hit with injuries. The Rams ended up with a moderate score of 4.56, ranking ninth in the NFL in injury impact. However, the Rams have had $67.3 million in cap space out due to injury, which is the fifth-most. Davante Adams and Poona Ford have been the biggest contributors to that with Adams’ $28 million cap-hit and Ford’s $11.4 million.
The Rams can certainly point to injuries as being a reason they are 3-4, but not the sole reason. Every team deals with injuries. The Rams have made enough mistakes independent of injuries that have hurt their record more.
Former Rams running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples was in municipal court this week in Eugene, Oregon, as he faces charges of DUII and reckless driving stemming from an incident in April. In the incident, Samples hit a parked car and fled the scene. During the court hearing, an added charge of failure to perform your duties as a driver was added as well.
University of Oregon Football Assistant Head Coach Rashaad Samples is currently in Eugene Municipal Court facing DUII & Reckless Driving charges in relation to an April incident where he hit the parked car of local man, Steven Young, and fled the scene.
According to news reports of the hearing, the other driver claimed that Samples was blaring music and eating chips before the incident. The driver also alleged that Samples offered him $1,000 and initially refused to provide his name and insurance information before giving the fake name DeSean Jackson.
A decision was not made, but another court date of December 3 has been set. At that point, the court will decide whether Samples is eligible for DUII Diversion. If Samples were to enter and complete the program, the DUII charge would be dismissed and there would be no criminal conviction.
Samples was the Rams’ running backs coach in 2022 and left before the end of the season. Since 2024, he has been the assistant head coach and running backs coach at Oregon.
To be clear, this is only me speculating. While there had been reports that Garrett would return to practice this week, the Rams opted not to open his practice window . Given that the Rams are in Washington next week, it seems unlikely that Garrett will test his knee on that field. The Rams then play the Arizona Cardinals the following week. The Rams are likely to continue playing it safe. At this point, it’s hard to see Garrett coming back before the bye.
This isn’t to say that I’d be upset if the Rams traded for Thomas or another wide receiver. However, I do believe Downs is the best fit for what the Rams need at the position right now. They don’t have a shifty player that can be used in a variety of ways or create from the slot. In an offensive system with a better quarterback, Downs has the ability to thrive . If the Rams make a move, this is the one they need to make.
The Rams’ run game is at its best when both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams are involved . A big reason the run game got going last week was because of the mixed usage of Corum and Williams. In the weeks prior, it had been mostly Williams. Corum had 17 carries just last week. He had 19 carries in the previous three weeks combined. The Rams need to keep finding ways to get both players involved. Corum’s burst and creativity as a runner add…

title: 3 NFL Trade Deadline Deals the Rams Should Explore Right Now
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are a team who could be buyers at the NFL trade deadline . They have been rumored to be exploring options at wide receiver, but there are certainly other positions where the Rams have needs as well. It seems unlikely at this point that the Rams would make a trade until next week. However, here are three NFL trade deadline deals that the Rams should explore immediately.
Brian Thomas Jr. could certainly be mentioned here as well. Thomas would give the Rams an “X” receiver while Davante Adams is injured. However, Downs wouldn’t cost as much as Thomas and would fit into the Rams’ offense once Adams does return. The Rams are missing a reliable WR3 in the offense who they can trust when they are in 11 personnel. Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield have shown flashes, but they haven’t been consistent. Downs gives the Rams some speed, but more importantly, someone who can create after the catch and create separation with his route-running. With the Colts in a fire-sale situation and Downs requesting a trade, this is a name the Rams should be exploring. Price: 2027 fourth-round pick
Trading for a defensive lineman may not be the preferred move, but it would be a smart one. The Rams do have some depth at the position and will be asking a lot of that depth with the absences of Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. It is expected that the Rams will get Turner back at some point, but Ford is out for the remainder of the season. The Rams are going to miss Ford’s presence in the middle of their defensive line. A’Shawn Robinson is familiar with the Rams and would provide the veteran run-stopping presence that they need. Price: 2028 late-round pick
It’s hard to see the Rams exploring positions outside of wide receiver and defensive line. With that said, it may not be a bad idea to explore edge rusher , and Khalil Mack makes sense. Mack is at a stage of his career in which he wants to play for a contender. The Rams have lacked consistent pressure off the edge without Myles Garrett. While Garrett is set to return within the next few weeks, Mack would still fit the rotation with Josaiah Stewart. Adding Mack would also provide some insurance if Garrett's recovery takes longer than expected. The Rams can't afford to continue struggling to generate pressure off the edge. Price: 2028 late-round pick swap

title: Rams Trade Target Josh Downs Has an Intriguing Comparison to Sean McVay's Past
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline quickly approaching, the Los Angeles Rams continue to be a team connected to wide receivers . The Rams have been rumored to show interest in Brian Thomas Jr. and Josh Downs. While both players would fit the offense, Downs is a player who may fit the offense better once Davante Adams returns and also be a more affordable option from a draft asset standpoint.
The major concern with Downs as an option appears to be his lack of size. Downs is just 5’9, 171 pounds. The Rams already have a player built like that in Tutu Atwell and don’t use him in the offense.
With that said, just because Downs and Atwell are the same size does not mean they are the same player. Atwell wasn’t the same player as Tavon Austin in the same way that Downs isn’t the same player as Atwell. While they might be the same size, it’s lazy analysis to put them all in the same box.
Atwell is a field-stretching wide receiver who relies strictly on his straight-line speed. Austin wasn’t as complete of a receiver and was more of an explosive gadget offensive playmaker. Meanwhile, Downs is a more polished, quick-separating, high-volume slot receiver .
To put it simply, Atwell threatens defensive backs with his speed, Austin was better with the ball in his hands, and Downs wins with his ability to consistently get open. That’s a very important distinction.
If the Rams were to make a move for Downs, it shouldn’t be seen as another attempt to make an undersized wide receiver work. He’s a legitimate slot receiver who could provide something that the offense has been missing from the WR3 spot.
It’s true that McVay couldn’t get Austin or Atwell to work in his offense consistently. However, neither was the complete type of wide receiver required to succeed in McVay's offense. When a smaller wide receiver has shown the ability to be a more complete receiver, McVay has had success.
A prime example is when McVay was the offensive coordinator for the Washington Commanders. McVay got the best out of Jamison Crowder, who was also 5’9, 177 pounds. Crowder was a more complete receiver and that showed in his production with McVay.
In Crowder’s two seasons with McVay, Crowder had 126 receptions for 1,471 yards and nine touchdowns. His 847 yards in 2016 was a career-best. When Washington drafted Crowder in the fourth round in 2015, he completely changed their offense.
Crowder gave Washington versatility from the slot. However, most of his value came in the short-passing game. The Rams haven’t been able to attack the deep areas of the field this season. However, the passing game has lacked consistency at times because the Rams lack wide receivers outside of Puka Nacua who can turn short throws into big gains. With Crowder, McVay could call a screen on 3rd-and-long and it had the potential to be turned into a first down. Nacua is currently the only Rams wide receiver with that ability.
“It gives us the ability to kind of move him around and use him in a variety of ways," McVay said about Crowder at the time . "The red zone has been something that he's been used in a little bit more and normal field, jet-sweep actions. Any way that you try to get him involved, usually good things happen for us."
Here's the Crowder 55-yard TD. Beautifully blocked screen. Trent Williams, playing LG, blocked two players on this one. #Redskins pic.twitter.com/48l8HDZyaR
Stafford has struggled against the blitz at times this season because the passing game hasn’t always had answers. That was evident two weeks ago in the loss to the Arizona Cardinals. The Rams tried to dial up quick passes to Nacua and the running backs, but the Cardinals were ready for it.
Outside of Nacua and the Rams’ tight ends, the Rams have been relying on Konata Mumpfield in the short and intermediate areas of the field. Mumpfield has been fine, but he hasn’t proven to be a consistent, reliable target. Under McVay, Crowder had the ability to create space for himself and wasn’t fully reliant on the offense creating the space for him. That’s also where Downs is able to win .
Another ASS chart update! We have ASS against Man Coverage vs. ASS against Zone Coverage (per @FantasyPtsData ) On god, free my boys Garrett Wilson and Josh Downs, or I'm gonna f*cking lose it pic.twitter.com/LXPVCUgD1S
The Rams are simply lacking a complementary wide receiver who can be reliable on third down, win after the catch, and still have the ability to win deep all from the slot. Back in 2016, the presence of Crowder did that for McVay, and Downs could do the same.
That was also the last time that McVay leaned into heavy tight end sets. While the Rams operate out of 13 personnel at the highest rate in the NFL, they still operate out of 11 personnel 55.9 percent of the time. However, their -0.05 EPA per pass out of 11 personnel ranks 16th. Last year it was 0.16.
#Rams TD not too dissimilar to this one McVay called to Jamison Crowder vs the Eagles a few years ago. https://t.co/EcICkvgRcc
Adding a player like Downs at the trade deadline would give McVay a more complete wide receiver in the slot and someone he hasn’t had since Crowder. Crowder changed Washington’s offense in a positive way, and Downs could do the same for the Rams’ passing game. Teams are currently daring the Rams to beat them with speed and they haven’t been able to do it. Matthew Stafford has averaged under five air yards per attempt in back-to-back weeks.
Downs fits what McVay looks for in wide receivers. He’s versatile, wins with his route running, and can create after the catch. While he may not be a great blocker, he is a willing blocker and can be just as effective in that area as Mumpfield. It’s also at the point where the Rams need to prioritize some of the playmaking ability.
Just because Downs is the same size as Atwell does not mean they are the same players. Downs brings a skill set that the Rams are currently missing at the wide receiver spot. When McVay had Crowder in Washington, he found ways to maximize his skill set and make him an important part of the offense. There’s no reason to believe that he couldn’t do the same with Downs. His ability to create separation and explosive plays after the catch is exactly what the Rams need.
Much like Crowder, Downs uses his short-area quickness, understanding of defensive leverage, and ability to find openings against zone coverage to consistently create separation. Similar to Crowder, Downs has speed but doesn’t rely on his straight-line speed to get open like Atwell.
With the trade deadline approaching, the Rams have an opportunity to address what has been holding back their passing game this season. Downs offers many of the same qualities that Crowder had that elevated McVay’s offense in Washington. He would give Stafford another reliable target who can create separation without needing the offense to manufacture opportunities for him.

title: Rams vs. Chargers Prediction: Preview, Key Matchups, and What to Watch
full_text:
Heading into the 2026 NFL season, many would have expected Sunday’s Week 8 matchup between the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers to be between two of the best teams in the NFL. Instead, the Rams are 3-4 and struggling to find consistency and the Chargers have yet to win a game.
With that said, the Week 8 matchup against a winless Chargers team should give the Rams an opportunity to win back-to-back games for the first time this season. Over the next three weeks, the Rams are set to play the 0-6 Chargers, 1-4-1 Commanders, and 2-5 Cardinals. If the Rams can start stacking wins, they have an opportunity to get above .500 and enter the bye week in position to make a playoff run.
Nothing has gone right for the Chargers this season. After Justin Herbert connected with Quentin Johnston in the preseason game against the Rams, there was a lot of excitement about the offense's potential. However, Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel haven’t clicked and injuries to the offensive line have taken their toll.
Last week, the Rams found their offensive identity through the run game, leaning on Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. That won’t come easy against a Chargers defense that ranks seventh in EPA per rush and rushing success rate allowed this season. The Rams may need to be patient and wait for something to break.
This season, the Rams have used man-blocking concepts on 52.6 percent of their runs, which leads the NFL. They also rank sixth in yards per carry on those concepts. However, the Chargers’ defense has allowed the fifth-lowest rushing success rate to man-concept runs. Additionally, they have allowed the 12th-lowest rushing success rate against 13 personnel.
There have been times this season in which Matthew Stafford has struggled against the blitz. While the Chargers haven’t blitzed a ton this season, they have generated a 52.5 percent pressure rate when they have, which ranks second in the NFL. Henley leads the Chargers in pressures when they have blitzed. Blitzing Stafford may be the Chargers’ only chance on defense. If that’s the case, Kyren Williams and Blake Corum will need to be able to step up in pass protection.
It’s hard to believe that a team with Herbert and McDaniel ranks 32nd in EPA per pass and 29th in EPA per rush. Head coach Jim Harbaugh has said that McDaniel will continue calling plays. The Rams should be able to stop the Chargers' passing game. The key with the Rams’ defense will be stopping the run and forcing the Chargers into passing situations.
The Rams have struggled to get consistent pressure on the quarterback this season. However, they need to find ways to make Herbert uncomfortable. Herbert has been hit at a 20.4 percent rate this season, which is the highest in the NFL.
Cole Strange has allowed a 7.3 percent pressure rate, which is the ninth-highest among qualifying right guards this season. Braden Fiske has done well getting to the quarterback, and it feels like only a matter of time before Aaron Donald has a classic game. Both should have a good opportunity against the Chargers’ offensive line. The same can be said about Tyler Davis and Ty Hamilton in the run game.
While the Chargers are 0-6, this isn’t a team that the Rams can afford to overlook. The Chargers will be coming off their bye week and will have had two weeks to prepare for the Rams. It wouldn’t be surprising to see McDaniel call a similar game to what the Cardinals did two weeks ago or the 49ers early in the season. While this game could be close, the Rams seemed to find something last week. If they can lean on that and remain efficient on offense, they’ll earn a second straight win. Prediction: Rams 24, Chargers 16

title: When is Myles Garrett Actually Playing for the Rams Again? Things Are Murky
full_text:
With every passing week, the uncertainty around the Los Angeles Rams and edge rusher Myles Garrett continues to grow. Despite NFL Media’s I an Rapoport reporting last week that the expectation was for Garrett to return to practice this week, the Rams will not be activating his 21-day practice window.
Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson will not practice this week, Sean McVay said.
Ever since the Rams traded for Garrett, something hasn’t been right. Garrett first missed practice at the beginning of training camp with what was described as lower-body soreness. He missed three straight practices in early August. While he was in and out of practice for a few weeks, Garrett missed the last few weeks of training camp entirely and didn’t return until Week 1.
Garrett played in Week 1, but said after the game that he didn’t feel like himself. He was then placed on injured reserve after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery. Following the surgery, many reported a six-week timeline, calling that a worst-case scenario, and that Garrett was determined to beat that timeline.
With Garrett not returning to practice this week, his timeline continues to get extended. We are now 6.5 weeks post-surgery and Sunday will be the seventh consecutive game that Garrett has missed. Without Garrett, the Rams rank 18th in pressure rate on defense and 28th in sack rate. That’s down from being second in pressure rate and ninth in sack rate last season.
Since the beginning, the Rams have lacked transparency when it came to Garrett. They've never explained what caused Garrett’s knee injury or even what the specific injury was. Garrett has only been described as having lower-body soreness and knee swelling.
The entire situation has been murky from the jump and the Rams haven’t helped at all by providing any sort of clarity. For much of the offseason, McVay said that the team was simply erring on the side of caution. With Garrett set to miss Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers, Garrett will not have played a healthy snap for the Rams as we get into November.
At this point, it’s worth wondering when the Rams will see Garrett back on the field. The Rams are taking it week-by-week, but will it be next week on the road against the Washington Commanders? Does he come back after the bye week? Will Garrett play again in 2026?
Right now, there is no clear answer. The earliest Garrett could return is Week 9 against the Commanders, but with the Rams not even ready to open his practice window, a return following the Week 11 bye may be more realistic.
For the most part, this has been mismanagement from the Rams’ training staff and has only been emphasized by the lack of transparency. While the team and Garrett likely wanted to avoid surgery, it can be argued that Garrett should have gotten the surgery back in August. It’s also worth wondering whether the Rams did their due diligence, considering that Garrett’s knee injury popped up all the way back in training camp.
Those are all fair questions with Garrett set to be out another week and the continued lack of transparency. He’s spent almost half the season on injured reserve with no signs of coming off of it anytime soon.
The Rams traded a promising young edge rusher and two first-round picks for Garrett, and he hasn’t played a healthy snap for the team. While Jared Verse doesn’t have a sack yet this season, he does have a 10.1 percent pressure rate, which is higher than both Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey. It’s also worth noting that Verse hasn’t been a good fit and has had to adjust to the Browns’ 4-3 defense.
When the Rams traded for Garrett, the expectation was that he would be the missing piece on a Super Bowl-caliber roster. Instead, the Rams are heading into Week 8 with more questions than answers. The elite edge rusher that they traded for hasn’t played since Week 1, and even then he wasn’t healthy.
Until Garrett returns to practice, there’s no reason to believe his return is imminent or that he returns before the bye week. The question isn’t just when Garrett will play for the Rams, but whether they will ever get the player they traded for and the impact they expected from their biggest offseason acquisition. That's a concerning position for the Rams to be in, especially considering what they gave up to acquire him.

title: Rams Sign Josh Karty, Jake McQuaide in Surprising Special Teams Moves
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams continue their attempt to improve their special teams uni t. On Wednesday, the Rams signed long snapper Jake McQuaide and kicker Josh Karty to the practice squad.
Through the first seven weeks of the season, the Rams have struggled on special teams and it’s become a point of emphasis for head coach Sean McVay. The Rams currently rank 32nd in special teams DVOA and gave up two long returns as well as a fake punt against the Las Vegas Raiders.
“I have to figure that out. It's one of those deals that’s driving me crazy. We have to figure it out and we haven't yet,” said McVay when he spoke to the media on Monday.
McQuaide visited the Rams on Wednesday. He spent the first 10 years of his career with the Rams and signed with them last year after they moved on from Alex Ward. The McQuaide signing does come as a surprise, as Joe Cardona was signed in the offseason and seen as a player favored by Bubba Ventrone. While the Rams haven’t been good on special teams, Cardona has been one of the few bright spots.
Whether McQuaide replaces Cardona or is simply there to provide a veteran presence as someone McVay trusts remains to be seen. However, it would be odd for the Rams to keep two long snappers available.
The addition of Josh Karty is just as surprising. Last season, the Rams cut Karty after he had issues with timing and kicks getting blocked. Karty was 10-for-15 last year and had two field goals blocked that would have given the Rams the win against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Additionally, last week, the Rams signed kicker Brandon McManus to add some stability to the field goal unit after they moved on from Harrison Mevis. McManus went 5-for-5 on extra points last week.
It seems unlikely that the Rams would move on from McManus, but Karty gives the Rams a younger option to develop on the practice squad. Karty was seen as a talented kicker at one point. From the end of his rookie season until his two kicks being blocked against the Eagles, Karty had made 21 straight field goals and was 5-for-5 from 50+ yards during that stretch.
Another aspect of signing Karty is what he can do on kickoffs. Some have speculated that the knuckleball kickoff messed up his kicking form, but the Rams implemented it last season with Karty and had success with it.
Given some of the Rams’ issues on their kickoff coverage unit, it wouldn’t be surprising if they brought up Karty on game days or found a roster spot for him just to take kickoff responsibilities. The Rams can also hope to develop Karty with the idea that he can possibly overtake McManus at some point.
The Rams have created the best field position on kickoffs this season. Blocked FGs overshadowed what was a GREAT performance from Karty. This knuckleball on the kickoff has been a weapon for the Rams STs unit. pic.twitter.com/FbbxJN3fdw
In a corresponding move, the Rams released offensive lineman Austin Blaske. Blaske was signed as an undrafted free agent and seemed to play well during the preseason. However, with the Rams prioritizing special teams , they have opted to part ways with Blaske. The signings of Karty and McQuaide also come after the Rams bringing in Jon Rhattigan on Tuesday.
McVay has made it clear that the Rams' special teams performance isn't acceptable, and the moves to bring back McQuaide and Karty are another indication that the team is searching for answers. It's uncertain whether either player will make an immediate impact, but the Rams are certainly making an effort to improve.

He's been credentialed for events such as the NFL in Australia, NFL Draft, NFL Combine, and Senior Bowl. A graduate of Northeastern University, Blaine grew up in Montana.

title: How Jets Injuries Open Door for Raiders To Take Advantage
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are looking to end a four-game losing streak when they take on the New York Jets in Week 8.
With the trade deadline less than two weeks away, the sense of urgency for the Raiders in this game is high. Las Vegas enters this contest with injuries on both sides of the ball. The Jets are also dealing with a slew of injuries, especially on the defensive line.
Ahead of this matchup, New York ruled out nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat and listed David Bailey as doubtful. Here's why these specific injuries are significant and how the Raiders can exploit them.
We had an eerily similar conversation last week heading into Las Vegas' matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, whose defensive line was marred by injuries. Despite that, the Raiders had 17 carries for 48 yards. Ashton Jeanty was uninspiring, with eight carries for 15 yards. The 22-year-old running back has battled injuries, which have clearly hampered him throughout this season.
Last week, the Dolphins ran for 156 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets, and that was when their defensive line was healthier. With the aforementioned injuries, Las Vegas' rushing attack has a chance to produce. That said, the Raiders have yet to prove they're capable of running on anyone regardless of who the opponent is.
Cousins' kryptonite is pressure, but that shouldn't be a factor with Bailey out, who leads the Jets with 5.5 sacks. On the other hand, Las Vegas' offensive line has been poor in pass protection and run blocking.
If the 38-year-old quarterback is kept upright and has a clean pocket, he should dissect the Jets’ defense, which has intercepted one pass this season.
When assessing the coming weeks, New York's defensive line is the weakest the Raiders will face in the foreseeable future. After this week, Las Vegas faces the 49ers, Seahawks, Broncos, and Browns. If Las Vegas is unable to hold up in protection and struggles against this undermanned defense, it would be a telltale sign the Raiders could be in serious trouble.
Additionally, Cousins' job could be in jeopardy with another loss. There have already been murmurs from fans about head coach Klint Kubiak giving Fernando Mendoza a chance, so the 15-year veteran can't afford a fifth consecutive loss. With another defeat, the Raiders could look to trade Cousins and others to build up their draft capital.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Raiders Showdown With Jets
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are looking to end their current four-game losing streak before it gets worse. The New York Jets are the most beatable team Las Vegas has faced since their last win over four weeks ago. However, the Jets are far from a pushover for a reeling Raiders team.
Below are the three storylines I will be watching the most in the Raiders' road matchup against the Jets.
Las Vegas' roster has several holes that remain from past seasons. These remaining holes have been exploited by the four elite teams the Raiders have played in the past month. Those roster issues will be there for the rest of the season.
Las Vegas' coaching staff must use its solid play-calling ability to scheme around the offense's deficiencies. That is their only hope of turning things around. If they can't, their remaining opponents are simply going to do all the same things their past four opponents did.
It will be challenging, but Las Vegas' coaching staff not only has to call good plays, but they also have to call a strong game while being confident the players can execute the calls. The execution part of the equation has been missing for the Raiders' offense repeatedly during the team's losing streak.
Klint Kubiak and Andrew Janocko must put together a solid game plan that puts the offense in position to win. They have already done so; they must find a way to help the players improve their execution of those plays.
The Raiders entered the fourth quarter of Week 7 down 28-6 against Matthew Stafford and the Rams. They entered the fourth quarter of Week 6 down 23-13 to Josh Allen and the Bills. They entered the fourth quarter of Week 6 down 35-10 against Drake Maye and the New England Patriots.
Those are not competitive situations. The chances of any offense, much less one that struggles to sustain drives or score points for three quarters, realistically coming back and winning in those scenarios are nearly nonexistent.
In those situations, the defense is giving up points, and the offense is not scoring anywhere as efficiently as needed.
Las Vegas has scored a total of three points in its last four third quarters. Geno Smith and the Jets aren't as bad as they may look from the outside. Las Vegas' defense must stop the run better than they have and keep the Jets' offense in check.
But the Raiders' offense must show up before they are down by two or three possessions in the fourth quarter.
The Raiders' offense has to put up yards and stats before the game is out of reach.
The last time Las Vegas played on the East Coast at 10 in the morning on the West Coast, the Raiders looked like a team that was completely thrown off by the time difference, in addition to the Patriots simply being the better team.
It is fair to point out that their loss to the Rams was similar; they at least hung in the game against the Patriots for a quarter and a half and would have been closer if not for Matt Gay missing his first field goal of the season, giving up touchdowns immediately before and after halftime.
A lot had to go wrong against the Patriots for it to get out of hand the way it did. Having to play a football game at what feels like 10 in the morning is undoubtedly a competitive disadvantage if your opponent's body doesn't have to do the same.
They face a similar situation in their Week 8 matchup against the Jets. Kubiak believes his guys will be more prepared this time around.
“Yes. Absolutely. Just the importance of getting up, getting out of bed, getting ready to roll, and getting ready to start fast,” Kubiak said after the team’s practice on Friday.
Sunday against the Jets, especially if it results in Las Vegas' fifth straight loss, will be the most critical game of Kubiak's first season with the team. It would be just another win, but a loss would spark more questions and conversations about the team's direction this season and their future beyond it.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: 3 Raiders Who Can Shine vs. Jets on Sunday
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have lost four straight games, but not all hope is lost as they travel east to face the New York Jets.
The Jets, who have not improved much in Aaron Glenn's second season as head coach, are sitting at 2-5 and have struggled on both sides of the ball. This game is a good opportunity for Las Vegas to get back on track and move to 4-4.
If they want to do that, they'll need some players to step up and have big performances. Who are some of the Raiders who need to come up big on Sunday afternoon?
Let's break down a few players who could shine against the Jets.
Given how inefficiently Ashton Jeanty has run the football this season, there may be more carries in store for Washington.
The Jets rank 24th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game, so this game could be a big chance for the Raiders to get back on track running the football. Washington is a different style of running back than Jeanty, and he could produce more big plays on the ground.
The Raiders need to find ways to move the football and put more points on the board, and running the ball would be a good start. They should call on Washington to help.
Dean has been one of the Raiders' best playmakers all season, and he should be able to do so again in this game.
The Jets may not be able to run the ball efficiently, given Braelon Allen's ankle injury (he's expected to play on Sunday) and Breece Hall's quad injury (he's listed as questionable). This may force the Jets into being one-dimensional, so Dean can be in control of what happens.
The Raiders haven't had a linebacker as good as Dean in quite a few years, and he should continue to prove he is worth his contract against the Jets. Look for him to continue to show up in a big way.
There has been consternation about the quarterback position in Las Vegas, but Cousins remains the starter and should have the opportunity to play well this Sunday.
The Jets rank in the top five in the NFL in passing yards allowed, but they do not take the football away. Cousins has put the ball in harm's way at times this season, but he won't face a defense that poses that threat.
Fans want to see Fernando Mendoza , and for good reason. However, Cousins should put up numbers and keep Mendoza on the bench for at least another week after this game.

title: Raiders vs. Jets: 5 Players To Watch for Sunday
full_text:
For the first time in four weeks, the Las Vegas Raiders have a favorable opportunity to win a football game.
The Raiders travel to New Jersey to face the New York Jets, a feisty 2-5 team that can provide problems for opponents but is too challenged talent-wise to overcome. Las Vegas has been close in two of the last four games, nearly beating the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs at home, but getting bogged down by the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams.
Head coach Klint Kubiak needs to find a rhythm and consistency for his football team as the first-year head coach looks to spark a string of wins in the coming weeks. Here are five players to watch who could help kick off that venture.
The Raiders officially designated second-year wideout Jack Bech to return from injured reserve this week. He could play this week, bolstering Kubiak's passing game. This opens the door for much-needed assistance on third downs, where Bech has shown to be reliable, and the Raiders had initially slated him for that role.
Assuming he plays, I expect Bech to be featured in the passing game, especially on third downs. This makes the Raiders' offense much more dangerous than it already is in this area.
Miller has been one of the worst left tackles this season when it comes to pressure rate and pressures allowed, which has been disappointing considering how well he's played in past years. He needs a rebound game, or we could see some changes.
Miller has a chance to do so against the Jets this weekend, but faces a challenge against a young yet explosive pass rush duo of Kingsley Enagbare and Will McDonald IV.
Good news for the Raiders and Ashton Jeanty: the Jets are one of the worst run defenses in football, allowing 127.7 yards per game on the ground.
The run game has been horrific because of how bad the blocking is up front from the offensive line, but a "get right" game is on the table for the Raiders this week. I expect Jeanty to have one of his productive rushing games this season.
Patrick Johnson is unlikely to play this week, which means it could be another practice squad elevation for the undrafted rookie Cian Slone, who has impressed on special teams and could have a bigger role on defense this week. The Raiders will have to decide on Slone with a potential third elevation, though a good outing for the first-year defensive end from NC State could make it easy.
A big game is nearing for Maxx Crosby—I can feel it in my bones. The Raiders superstar pass rusher is again being subject to trade deadline discussions online (I would ignore that, personally), though a big week for the veteran defender could help ease some of those conversations on social media.
Crosby is one of the best in the game, and he shows it every week with his pressure rate and total pressures. The sacks will come, and could this week against a Jets offensive line that is certainly hit or miss.
