title: Sneaky Trade Opportunity Could Solve Vikings' RB Needs as Deadline Nears
full_text:
All eyes are on Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley as the NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away .
With a Packers win on Thursday night and the Bears' blockbuster deal for Jeffery Simmons just hours before, the race to the top of the NFC North is officially on. At 6-0 and currently atop the best division in football, the Vikings are expected to be buyers ahead of the deadline.
But how far will new Teasley go to keep pace with the ascending rival teams?
The Vikings don't have many holes, and where they do, the fix isn't always realistic. Minnesota has been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor at every tick of the clock as a fix for their underwhelming rushing attack. While that type of swing-for-the-fences mentality could result in a deep playoff run, it also reportedly won't come cheap .
Another name, however, has seemingly fallen out of favor with his current squad and would be a much more palatable trade if the Vikings want to inject some life into their backfield.
After rushing for nearly 1,000 yards as a rookie, Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson has become mostly an afterthought recently in 2026. He has just 14 carries over the last three games and has been outsnapped by both Rhamondre Stevenson and rookie Corey Kiner in the New England backfield.
His declining role with the Pats could make him available in a trade, and it just so happens Henderson is very, very good at something the Vikings offense desperately needs.
Henderson had four carries of 40-plus yards in 2025, or one every 45 attempts. The last Viking running back to have even one of those was Cam Akers, way back in 2024. No one really expected either Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones to be ripping off explosive runs every other game, so the team added speedster Demond Claiborne in the draft, who instead has just 13 yards on six carries .
Henderson isn't a perfect answer. He struggles in pass protection and occasionally has the vision of a bat. Still, for what would likely amount to a mid-round pick, the Vikings could add a bit of juice to their hum-drum backfield.
Teasley has yet to take part in a draft for Minnesota, so would he really deal the equivalent of a first-round pick for a running back on the wrong side of 27 in Jonathan Taylor? Possibly, but there are clearly a lot of hurdles to clear before that happens.
The team still has other needs at interior offensive and defensive line, and a deal for Taylor takes most other good options there off the table. Adding the 24-year-old Henderson on a rookie deal saves some room in the draft pick budget for other moves, including for their possible new starting guard .
Teasley would be foolish to ignore the 6-0 start and add nothing at the deadline, but how much he's willing to give up in his first year at the helm may limit what fans hope he can do. If the Vikings opt for a more budget-conscious option at running back, Henderson has more appeal than, say, an aging Tony Pollard or Kenny Gainwell.

title: Potential Jauan Jennings Trade Partner Is Emerging That Vikings Shouldn't Ignore
full_text:
Entering Week 8 with a 6-0 record, the Vikings are still on track to be buyers ahead of November's NFL trade deadline. That said, the coming days and growing trade buzz around the league could create opportunities for Minnesota general manager Nolan Teasley to trade away certain players who've overstayed their welcome , including veteran wide receiver Jauan Jennings.
Signed to a one-year, $8 million contract, Jennings hasn't been the WR3 the Vikings expected when they put pen to paper in May.
The 29-year-old wideout has recorded two catches for nine yards in his first four games, adding to the ongoing obstacles Minnesota's lukewarm offense is already trying to overcome. Sure, Jennings recorded a season-high 34 receiving yards in last week's win over the Colts, but even that might not be enough to prevent a split.
While some Vikings fans might be willing to extend the veteran's runway in town, it might be best for Teasley & Co. to strike while the iron is hot—especially with a certain WR-needy AFC team looking like a potential trade partner.
On Friday morning, Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer reported that a few teams are seeking WR help , including the Steelers ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. In the last three weeks alone, Pittsburgh has lost top wideouts Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson to injured reserve, while Ben Skowronek has been limited with a calf injury this week.
Considering what's going on in the Steel City, Teasley has every reason to call Steelers GM Omar Khan about a potential trade involving Jennings.
After all, the Steelers have the cap space ($14.5 million, per Spotrac ) to fit the former Tennessee Volunteer onto their roster, and they also have draft capital to entice the Vikings. Between the backfield, WR room, and interior offensive line, Minnesota will be looking at a lot of positions in the 2027 NFL Draft, so getting some picks back for a pending UFA they may not re-sign isn't a bad idea.
According to Spotrac, the Steelers currently hold nine picks in the next two drafts, including two selections in Rounds 3, 6, and 7 for 2027. One pick could be enough for Jennings, but the Vikings could get more by preying on the Steelers' vulnerability. A package consisting of the Cowboys' 2027 fifth-rounder and the Packers' sixth-rounder in 2028 could be squeezed out, especially if Pittsburgh thinks Jennings can return to being the 900-yard receiver he was two years ago.
Another reason why the Steelers make sense is that a trade with them lessens the chance of a revenge game this season. Pittsburgh isn't on Minnesota's schedule this year, meaning the only chance for a Jennings trade to come back to bite the Purple and Gold would be in a hypothetical Super Bowl matchup.
Of course, if the Vikings make it to football's biggest stage, trading away Jennings—regardless of the return—won't matter in the grand scheme. He clearly isn't contributing much to the Vikings' success so far, so they may as well try to get as much value as they can in a trade while seeking reliable WR help elsewhere.
Some experiments simply don't work out , and that's the nature of the football business. What matters is how teams react and adapt to certain situations. If Teasley wants to prove he's the right GM to lead the Vikings to long-term glory, it's time to turn the page on one of the team's offseason misfires and see how much they can squeeze out of the Steelers before it's too late.

title: It's Time for Nolan Teasley to Prove He's All In on Vikings as Trade Deadline Pressure Rises
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline doesn't officially hit until 4 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 10 , but contenders across the NFC are already wheeling and dealing.
The pressure is officially on for the Vikings and general manager Nolan Teasley to keep pace as teams they’re likely to battle in the playoffs start to load up. While there is still a week and a half to act, Teasley cannot afford to wait while other teams keep stacking talent.
The Vikings’ 16-10 victory against the Colts last Sunday seemingly sent up a flare to the rest of the league that Indy was open for business. Turns out, they were. The Colts traded star left guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks on Tuesday. The move filled a massive hole for Seattle as they look to keep up with San Francisco in the NFC West. The 49ers were not far behind, acquiring defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Colts that afternoon.
Then, an NFC North rival added even more pressure for Teasley and the Vikings to act as the Bears shipped off a package of two firsts and a fourth for Titans DT Jeffery Simmons on Thursday.
Needless to say, the Vikings will need to be aggressive if they want to keep up. With a sinking offense and a brutal schedule approaching, the rookie GM needs to make a splash . Thankfully, reports indicate he’s attempting to do just that.
While it was always fair to speculate that Teasley and the 6-0 Vikings would be active at the deadline, two new reports give us insight into just how wild things may get. Sports Illustrated ’s Albert Breer mentioned three specific positions of interest for the Vikings: "interior offensive line, defensive line, and running back."
Meanwhile, NFL insider James Palmer referred to Teasley as a “madman on the phones” who is “looking at everything” during Amazon Prime ’s Thursday Night Football postgame coverage. Palmer specifically mentioned running back and tight end as positions the Vikings are looking into (h/t: James Palmer)
Looking at contenders that are looking to make a move before the deadline on our @NFLonPrime postgame show. pic.twitter.com/31yoQRNGhF
Seems like the Vikings may just be calling about every player in the league at this point. Well, except kickers, of course.
Is Teasley just doing his due diligence? Is he value bin shopping?
The reports around his urgency and the team's 7-0 start tell me he’s aiming for something big. It may not be today; it may not be next week, but Teasley seems dead set on finding a way to keep up with an ever-improving group of NFC opponents.
There are two routes for a potential major Vikings trade: 1. Inject life into a sinking offense 2. Build the most insane pass rush that’s ever been assembled Don’t ignore the possibility of number two.
The Vikings are set to have needs at quarterback, running back, tight end, outside linebacker, middle linebacker, cornerback, defensive line and more next offseason. There’s certainly a fair argument that being overaggressive at the deadline may only complicate the team’s long-term challenges, but with a generational defense and the league’s last undefeated record, Teasley may see an opportunity he cannot pass up .
After all, who cares about long-term roster building if Minnesota finally experiences a Super Bowl parade in just a few months?

title: 3 Most Important Things to Watch for Vikings against Lions in Week 8 (Flores' Defense Will Be Put to the Test)
full_text:
In the words of the great Motor City poet Marshall Mathers: “If you had one shot or one opportunity to seize everything you ever wanted in one moment, would you capture it or just let it slip?” Well, so far, the Minnesota Vikings have captured six straight wins to start the 2026 season and are looking to avoid letting their next potential victory slip away this weekend.
The Vikings head east to face their divisional rival Lions on Sunday with an opportunity to build an even larger cushion within the NFC North and the conference as a whole. Here are three things to keep an eye on in a matchup that will be Minnesota’s biggest test since their Week 2 game against the Bears.
The Vikings are looking to remain alone at the top of the NFL as the league’s last unbeaten team after this weekend. A win would give Minnesota its first 7-0 start since the 2000 season. Luckily, we all know how wonderfully that turned out.
A win this weekend would give the Vikings their first 7-0 start since 2000, a year the eventually resulted in a 41-0 loss to the Giants in the NFC Championship.
While a case could be made that a loss might bring some beneficial reflection to a Vikings team looking to contend, everyone in that locker room will certainly try their best to keep their unbeaten streak alive. Minnesota has won 11 straight games dating back to last season, with their last loss coming against the eventual Super Bowl champion Seahawks on Nov. 30 of last year.  With a difficult November schedule and other conference contenders loading up before the deadline, Minnesota needs to stack as many wins as possible. A win on Sunday will make it very hard for national talking heads to ignore the Vikings much longer, even if their winning process isn’t always pretty.
The matchup between Brian Flores and Drew Petzing wasn’t one I had circled on my calendar before the season, but Detroit’s offense has seemed to fire on all cylinders early this season,  looking eerily similar to the offense that gave the Vikings fits in 2023 and 2024 (h/t: NFL Researcher). Luckily, Flores and the Vikings' defense have continued their years-long process of adjustments and improvements to become one of the league's top squads.
Lions offense since 2023 (NFL rank)... Team points per game - 29.7 (1st) Jared Goff pass TD - 115 (1st) Jahmyr Gibbs scrimmage TD - 58 (1st) Amon-Ra St. Brown rec TD - 38 (1st)
Minnesota’s defense allows the second-fewest yards (252.8) and fewest points per game (12.3). Detroit’s offense, by contrast, ranks second in the league in yards (397.3) and points per game (30.7). Safe to say Sunday should be a heavyweight matchup every time the two stacked units face off.
The Vikings offense has mostly felt like the equivalent of watching paint dry to start the 2026 season. Outside of three or four standout plays (two of which were Justin Jefferson touchdowns), there hasn’t been much to be excited about. With the Vikings entering the heftiest portion of their schedule and the Lions struggling to defend the pass, Sunday may just be their best chance to prove they can get on track.
the Minnesota Vikings are only undefeated team left on early downs this season, their offense: #32 with 29% success rate #32 with 18% of plays gain a 1st down #32 with 24.0% of plays gain 7+ yards 62% of its series reach 3rd down #1 most in the NFL
Minnesota is struggling mightily to come out strong on early downs, but with Detroit’s defense giving up a league-worst 391 yards a game, there’s reason to be aggressive out of the gate (h/t: Warren Sharp). Getting Justin Jefferson involved early and often will be crucial, especially after he had a quiet four receptions for 44 yards against the Colts last week.

title: Vikings Still Need Jakobe Thomas in Week 8 Lineup Despite Recent Safety Success
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings finally saw the safety duo of Harrison Smith and Josh Metellus step up last week against the Indianapolis Colts, but those two players have struggled to be effective during the 2026 NFL season.
In Week 7 against the Colts, Smith caught the game-clinching interception, made four tackles and recorded half a sack on his way to the team's third-best Pro Football Focus defensive grade of 84.8. Metellus tied for the team's second-most tackles with seven. Minnesota needed those defensive backs to step up, and they helped the Purple and Gold remain undefeated on the season.
However, Smith and Metellus still have disappointing PFF grades for the season. Smith has an overall grade of 43.0 and a pass-coverage grade of 41.9, while Metellus has an overall grade of 42.3 and a pass-coverage grade of 35.1.
The Vikings face a tough stretch of games ahead of them. Over the next four weeks, they face the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers. Minnesota needs to prepare its defense by planning to have rookie safety Jakobe Thomas active on Sunday.
Thomas has been inactive for each of the Vikings' first six games and has yet to play a regular-season snap since being selected in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. It is concerning that Minnesota hasn't even tried to get him involved on special teams, despite using such a high pick on him.
A six-foot-two, 190-pound defensive back, Thomas should be a player whom head coach Kevin O'Connell wants to give some experience to as a rookie. Whether it is in Brian Flores' defense or Matt Daniels' special teams unit, he needs to start getting some snaps.
In his senior year at Miami (FL), Thomas recorded 76 combined tackles, five interceptions, four tackles for a loss, 2.5 sacks, two fumble recoveries and one defensive touchdown in 16 games played. His potential alone is enough to want to see what he can do as a pro.
It is getting to the point where fans should start questioning why Thomas remains on the sidelines this season. Having a 23-year-old player the team liked enough to take at No. 98 overall in the draft not play a single snap this year is baffling, especially with Smith and Metellus struggling .
Minnesota needs to start not only developing Thomas to prepare him for the future, but the team needs to see if he can help to make the safety position more of a consistent threat since Smith and Metellus have struggled to be consistent contributors this season.

title: The Best, Worst and Most Likely Vikings Outcomes vs. the Lions in Week 8
full_text:
The Vikings are the most polarizing 6-0 team in recent memory, with a powerful defense and a forgettable offense. That formula has worked for now, but the Vikings are about to run into a buzzsaw schedule in November, with the Lions, Bills, Packers and 49ers all on the docket.
Minnesota can get off to a good start with a win against Detroit, but that's clearly easier said than done. Here are the best, worst and likeliest scenarios for the Vikings' matchup with the Lions in Week 8.
With Aaron Jones Sr. ailing, the Vikings need a big day from Mason against the surging Lions. A nagging knee issue has kept Jones out of practice this week, and if he can't go, Mason will be the only worthwhile option in the Minnesota backfield. That's some extra pressure the Vikings' offense doesn't really need right now, but maybe Mason steps up to have a career day.
The Lions are allowing more yards per game than anyone this year, and a healthy run game could open up Detroit's vulnerable passing lanes. The return of safety Brian Branch and possibly even Kerby Joseph complicate matters, but there's still no question: the Lions' defense presents an opportunity for some offensive redemption this week. Mason had a solid return to action last week, averaging 4.5 yards per carry while splitting time with Jones, but he'll need to top that performance this Sunday.
If Mason and the rest of the offense can keep pace with a scorching hot Lions offense, the Vikings have a real chance to move to 7-0.
Jared Goff is putting up MVP-type numbers this season, and the Vikings defense will face their biggest test in weeks after chewing up and spitting out Daniel Jones last Sunday. One slight problem for Goff, though, is that the Vikings are bringing extra blitzers over 70% of the time this year... and that's really not his thing.
Over the last three seasons, Goff is first in the NFL in EPA per dropback from a clean pocket. That number craters to third-worst when under pressure, however (H/T Scott Barrett). Pressure is the name of the game for defensive coordinator Brian Flores, but Goff has 14 touchdowns to zero interceptions this season, and it looks like he may be turning over a new leaf as the league's best quarterback against the blitz (H/T Sumer Sports).
The Vikings' defense likely won't let the Lions reach their season average of 30 points per game, but the Minnesota offense also mustered just 16 against the now-tanking Colts . If Goff and the Lions put up anything even close to their season averages, this could quickly turn into a double-digit loss.
The Vikings' defense will keep the team alive in every single game they play this season. Detroit will put that statement to the test this week, and it could end with Minnesota's first loss of the season.
Star running back Jahmyr Gibbs's health will be something to monitor after a DNP at Wednesday's practice, but the concerns in this game mostly lie with Kyler Murray and the Vikings' offense. After an underwhelming return to football against the Colts, head coach Kevin O'Connell and his squad will try to get things rolling in this one.
Still, the Vikings haven't scored more than 23 points since Week 1, when old man Carson Wentz was leading the offense.
This matchup figures to be a close one, and how well the offense responds after barely scraping by Indy will determine whether this season rolls on undefeated or with a blemish on the record at the hands of a division rival.

title: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into NFC North Collision vs. Lions in Week 8
full_text:
Just like that, the November gauntlet is here. Your 6-0 Vikings head to Detroit this weekend to battle the 4-2 Lions for the first time since their Christmas matchup last season. With an undefeated record and divisional seeding on the line, the stakes are certainly high.
Will this be the week that finally proves the Vikings are worthy of their record ? Will Kyler Murray and the offense finally get on track? Will the defense finally meet their match? Let’s dive into my predictions for Sunday’s massive matchup.
This may come as a shock, but Justin Jefferson has had only one 100-yard receiving game since Oct. 5, 2025 . With the Vikings’ passing game desperate for a spark against a weak Lions pass defense, Sunday may be the perfect chance to stack some yardage.
Justin Jefferson has ONE game with 100+ receiving yards in the last 389 days. His last was a 101-yard performance against the Packers last January.
Detroit’s defensive back group is shaky, to say the least.
The Lions currently allow the most passing yards per game in the NFL, averaging a whopping 291.8. The return of safety Brian Branch last week against the Packers certainly helps their case, especially if fellow safety Kerby Joseph is close behind after being cleared to return to practice. But their cornerback group should give Jefferson plenty of opportunities to gain yardage this weekend.
Ennis Rakestraw Jr. was listed as limited in practice on Wednesday , placing even more pressure on D.J. Reed.
Even though the Lions give up a ton of yardage on defense, their pass rush is not to be ignored. They’re tied with the Vikings, Bengals, Broncos, and Texans for a league-leading 21 sacks. Basically, Sunday could be a bad day to be a quarterback at Ford Field.
Star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson and former Viking D.J. Wonnum each have five sacks for the Lions so far, while rising Vikings star Dallas Turner is tied for the third-most sacks in the league with six. I predict both defensive fronts will continue to cause chaos on Sunday, and that there will be at least seven total sacks between both teams.
With the Vikings’ inconsistent interior offensive line , Kyler Murray will need to be ready to take off to keep that number from getting even higher.
There is a case to be made that a loss on Sunday would be the best thing for the Vikings with less than two weeks left before the trade deadline . Obviously, you’d love to win every game, but the lessons learned from a loss may actually set this squad up for better long-term success.
The Vikings’ defense has been stellar, but the Lions' high-flying offense presents the hardest challenge they’ve faced this year. Can the offense be trusted in its current state to step up and score points?
If not, the Vikings will likely suffer their first loss of the year and hopefully walk away with valuable lessons from the experience. If it motivates general manager Nolan Teasley to make a splash deal at the deadline , it may prove to be a good outcome in the long run.

title: Patriots Make Important Financial Move with Hunter Henry's Contract
full_text:
The New England Patriots, strapped for cash ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, have reportedly made a move to help give them some more breathing room.
According to The Boston Globe's Ben Volin , the Patriots have created $3.3 million in cap space by restructuring tight end Hunter Henry's contract. They converted half of his base salary (which was $3.575 million) into a signing bonus.
The Patriots now have $5.245 million in cap space, up from just a few days ago. Volin reported that this restructuring took place on Thursday.
They also added two void years to the contract, a deal that Henry signed before the season began. The veteran tight end agreed to a two-year, $16 million contract extension during the summer . Part of that deal included $14.5 million in guarantees and a signing bonus worth $4.2 million. Through incentives, Henry's contract can reach up to $20 million.
Henry has gotten off to a fast start with the Patriots on the field, grabbing 26 passes for 296 yards and two touchdowns. He's currently tied for the third-most receiving touchdowns by a Patriots tight end in franchise history, and needs one more to surpass Russ Francis' 28 for sole possession of third place.
He's also been a great leader for rookie Eli Raridon, who's caught two touchdowns in the TE2 role.
"I think a ton," tight ends coach Thomas Brown said this week about how Henry helps Raridon on and off the field. "Hunter helps me being around him. I think having a guy as a veteran leader, not just the experience of playing and the production, and coming off of a career year last year in season 10, but just the way in which he goes about his business. I think being able to be a leader ... starts with your example."
The Patriots can now use some of this extra cap space to potentially make a deal at the deadline. There are some big names that have already been traded at positions of need for the Patriots, like offensive guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Now with some more flexibility, they could potentially look to plug up some of the gaps on the roster.
It likely won't be adding another tight end to the roster alongside Henry. Currently, the team has Henry, Raridon, Tanner Arkin and Cameron Latu on the active roster, and Tanner Conner on the practice squad.
Henry and the Patriots will take on the Miami Dolphins in Week 8 tomorrow at 4:25 p.m. EST.

title: Predicting How Patriots, Dolphins Perform: WRs Need To Step Up ... And Fast
full_text:
The New England Patriots are currently 2-0 against their AFC East rivals. Can they make it three wins on the year this week down in South Florida?
Historically, playing against the Miami Dolphins on the road has been a tall task for the Patriots. The heat, plus struggles against a team that's either been very good or very bad, hasn't led to the best of results for New England. This year, however, should be a solid victory for the Patriots — despite the conditions.
"We have to be conditioned," head coach Mike Vrabel said this week. "I think the better that we play, the more we possess the ball, the fresher we'll stay defensively. Hopefully we get the receivers into a rotation. The backs, we rotate. I don't think that the offensive linemen will necessarily rotate. We may play a couple guys based on who's available. That remains to be seen. The edge guys, we rotate. We try to rotate along the defensive line. We like to have our best players available to help us win."
Ahead of Week 8, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
The Patriots are sitting at 4-3 by the time this is being written, and in 48 hours, should be sitting at 5-3. Yes, the Patriots will tell you this game will be just like any other, but if they take care of business, this should be an easy win. But it depends on which type of Patriots offense we get on the field.
With A.J. Brown questionable with a knee and ankle injury, plus TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an illness , we don't know just yet about how the offense will look. Can the running game bounce back and start to put together a big game? Will the passing attack look good, regardless of who's out there? That's how this game will be dictated.
Last week against the Chicago Bears, Maye had an excellent day — passing for two touchdowns and running in a third. That was against a Bears defense that's in Super Bowl conversations. Against a Miami defense that has struggled all year, the 24-year-old should have a comfortable day in the pocket, even if some starters at both offensive line and wide receiver aren't playing.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 26, Dolphins 10
I don't see the Patriots eclipsing 30+ points considering how depleted their wide receiving corps is right now. But they certainly should win this game by several scores. The Dolphins will keep it close for a bit , but the extended break for the Patriots should help them get back in the winning swing of things.
The Dolphins are not a good football team. In fact, there is an argument to be made that they are the worst in the league. Last week, Miami scraped out with its first game of the season against a lowly New York Jets squad. However, I frankly do not see a world where that happens again on Sunday.
Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has just 1,057 yards and four touchdowns through the air this season, sitting 25th and 27th in the NFL, respectively. Plus, Miami’s fifth-leading receiver, Ryan Miller, is now on New England’s practice squad.
All of that to say, the Dolphins are much better off losing this game — to continue plummeting toward an early draft pick — than they are winning it.
X-Factor: WR Efton Chism III
Plain and simple, somebody is going to have to catch the football for the Patriots on Sunday. With A.J. Brown questionable to play , plus Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on injured reserve, New England’s only healthy receivers on the active roster are Chism, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams. Chism has obvious chemistry with Drake Maye. So, with an expected increased snap share on Sunday, I expect him to be New England’s leading receiver.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 23, Dolphins 10
Sunday afternoon may be a snooze fest. Between the Patriots’ depleted offense and the Dolphins untalented offense, I do not expect many points to be put on the board. Whichever team can play cleaner, more complementary football should come out with the win. All in all, I trust Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel to instill that significantly more than I trust first-year Dolphins lead man Jeff Hafley.

title: A.J. Brown's Injury Status Going From Bad to Worse for Patriots
full_text:
FOXBORO — It feels like the New England Patriots just went through this song and dance, but it's happening again.
Wide receiver A.J. Brown — who's already missed four games this season with a high-ankle sprain — was absent from the team's final two practices ahead of their Week 8 game against the Miami Dolphins. He was limited on Wednesday with an ankle and a knee injury, and then didn't participate one day later. On Friday, he wasn't spotted during the stretching portion of practice.
Second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson was also missing as he deals with an illness.
Speaking to reporters, head coach Mike Vrabel shared that Brown will be questionable for the game.
"We'll see how he comes in tomorrow and we'll make a decision," he told reporters Friday afternoon, deflecting a question about of this is a long-term injury. "Just wasn't able to finish practice on Wednesday, and so we continue to treat him and then we'll see where he is."
It's the same knee injury, the one that's been often referred to as degenerative, that's flared up this week. Back in the summer, Eliot Wolf admitted the knee issue was something the Patriots' medical staff signed off on before making the trade. This week has been the first time Brown's been added to the injury report this season with that knee issue.
When reporters were in the locker room on Thursday, Brown wasn't seen at any point — a change from his usual pre-practice routine.
Typically, while not always, an absence on Friday doesn't bode well for the player's status on game day. That was the case for Brown. According to NFL Network, Brown's status for Sunday in South Florida remained "up in the air." For Brown, he admitted this week that he still isn't where he wants to be on the recovery of his ankle.
"Yeah, sometimes, you know, I see it, and sometimes, I'm pushing through," Brown said. "But none of that stuff even matters. I'm out here, so I'm going."
Brown missed time after suffering the high-ankle sprain in Week 1. Since then, the Patriots have gotten inspiring performances from others in the wide receiver room. But with Mack Hollins (calf) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) also on IR, it's starting to become worrisome about how thin this wide receiver room is.
Right now, the team has DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III healthy on the active roster. Kyle Dixon , Chandler Brayboy , Cameron Dorner and Ryan Miller are on the practice squad.
"We'll have one of those guys ready and I'm sure that they all are," Vrabel said on the practice squad wideouts.
"I think also we do a really good job of trying to be multiple thrughout the week," passing game coordinator Thomas Brown said Thursday. "In case we have some issues, whether it be with injuries or having to pivot in-game, we have multiple guys ready, ready to go and activate any given moment. ... It's a next man up mentality, so we have to all prepare to go and be the starter."
Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels also spoke about Brown's resumed role into New England's offense — where he's struggled to make an impact since returning. In the last two games, he's caught a total of six passes.
"He's played eight quarters in almost two months and had four practices, I think. I'm certainly in the mode of 'this is a process of building into our best football,' We've seen that with pretty much every player that's come here," McDaniels said. "There's things we can work on to do better, and certainly his health is going to be a big part of that. So, they tell us he can do A, B and C, we'll do A, B and C.
"If there's some element of thing we need to wait on, we'll do it. I love his attitude and approach; he's been here working his tail off to try to put himself in a great position to help our team."
Should he be downgraded, this will be Brown 's fifth missed game of the 2026 season — not a very good initial return on investment for a trade involving a future first round draft pick.

title: Patriots Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Rumor for New England with 2 Weeks to Go
full_text:
The NFL's trade deadline was pushed back a week this year, so the New England Patriots and 31 other teams will have until Nov. 10 to try and get deals done this season.
The Patriots , currently sitting at 4-3 and in second place in the AFC East, could end up being active on the market. Injuries across the board and potential depth issues at other places could led Eliot Wolf and Mike Vrabel to try and improve the team somehow, someway.
Aleady in this calendar year, the Patriots have made a few trades. Back in March, they shipped away Garrett Bradbury and Marte Mapu before acquiring A.J. Brown in a block buster deal with the Philadelphia Eagles three months later. During the summer, Kayshon Boutte was dealth to the Houston Texans and during roster cuts, the Patriots also sent draft picks for Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse.
So could they end up making a deal mid-season? Here's all the rumors, quotes and storylines that are surrounding the Patriots as the trade deadline looms.
The Patriots have a lot of money tied up to the interior of their defense line, with Milton Williams ($28.5 million) and Christian Barmore ($17.1 million) being paid very well for this season. But Barmore, who's played just 41.9% of the snaps this season, hasn't been someone that's been a consistent player so far.
According to SI's Albert Breer , the defensive tackle "could be had" on the trade market after falling behind Cory Durden on the depth chart. Barmore has two more years after this season on his four-year, $84 million extension he signed in 2024 before hitting the open market.
This season, the 27-year-old has six total tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble.
Could the Patriots — the team with Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on injured reserve — end up adding a wideout? ESPN reported that Indianapolis Colts wideout Josh Downs requested a trade after a pair of his teammates were shipped away on Tuesday.
Downs spent two seasons with Drake Maye at North Carolina, scoring a career-high 11 touchdowns during the 2022 season. The Patriots only have four healthy wide receivers on the active roster right now, but adding Downs for what could be a cheap deal might help elevate the passing attack.
Seven games in, Downs has 26 receptions for 307 yards.
A few days after the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears , Vrabel spoke with reporters about how the team is stacking up prior to their Week 8 game with the Miami Dolphins. One of the questions posed was about if the Patriots will be active on the phones.
His answer left the door open for a deal being made, but the head coach also didn't officially dig a potential move into the sand. Like most coach-speak, Vrabel discussed how the Patriots would make moves to try and improve the overall roster in totality, and not try to single out a certain spot that needs upgrading.
"We're going to try to do everything we can to help the team," Vrabel said. "I don't know if we will or we won't. I would imagine that we'll try to do everything that we can to help us, within reason, and makes sense for us. I don't know how you want to interpret that, but I'm sure we'll listen and talk, just like everybody else does."
Some positions that the Patriots could end up attacking are running back, offensive guard (with a myriad of injuries hitting that group), interior defensive line and some backup cornerbacks.

title: Could Patriots Trade Christian Barmore, One of Their Longest-Tenured Starters?
full_text:
With the NFL trade dealine looming over NFL facilities, front offices across the league are in abundant contact with one another to either revamp their rosters or gain capital for upcoming seasons.
The success of this year's 4-3 New England Patriots leaves them as a team that is likely to acquire players rather than move on from some. However, there is a player the Patriots could move that would make sense for the construction of New England's roster.
On Wednesday, Albert Breer reported that the Patriots could make defensive tackle Christian Barmore available for trade.
Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore is available for trade. Per: @AlbertBreer pic.twitter.com/igjLF2tVPm
In the mass of injuries New England has sustained in the first seven weeks of the 2026 season , one position group that's been nearly unaffected by injuries is the defensive tackle unit. This solid group leaves Barmore as a liable trade peice that can be used to upgrade another position or build draft capital for future seasons.
Drafted in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft, Barmore has been a centerpiece of New England's defensive rebuild in the post-Tom Brady era.
Barmore has delivered on all fronts for the high-value investment the Patriots' previous front office made on him. Prior to 2026, Barmore had four dominant seasons (he missed most of 2024 due to blood clots), where he racked up 162 tackles and 14.5 sacks in 61 games.
However, Barmore's had a slower start to 2026, and has been overshadowed in the past two seasons by free agent signing Milton Williams . Despite his three sacks, the 27-year-old has been limited to just six tackles on the season. Last year, Barmore had just 29 tackles, his least amount in a season where he played every game.
In 2026, Barmore — who is the longest tenured defensive player on New England's roster — has only played 41.9% of snaps in the season. This percentage is third most at his position, behind Williams (67.8%) and Cory Durden (50%).
The list of remaining Patriots who played for Bill Belichick: • Christian Gonzalez (2023) • DeMario Douglas (2023) • Marcus Jones (2022-23) • Rhamondre Stevenson (2021-23) • Brenden Schooler (2022-23) • Christian Elliss (2023) • Mike Onwenu (2020-23) • Hunter Henry…
Over the next two seasons, Barmore is set to make $48.2 million with an average cap hit of $24.1 million in each season. Williams will also be a large cap expenditure, as he is set to earn an average of $30.5 million from 2027-28.
If the roster stays the same in 2028, New England will have to pay a combined $98 million to Christian Gonzalez, A.J. Brown, Williams, and Barmore. That value is expected to be a quarter of the Patriots salary cap in 2028 (salary cap figures aren't announced until the months prior to that season).
While Barmore is being paid like a top defensive linemen, his production shows that he's not as valuable as his contract suggests. And defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr's decision to play Barmore less than other defensive tackles leaves him as a cap space liability.
I asked Patriots DT Christian Barmore about his reduced role earlier this week. He paused for a few seconds before saying, "I mean, I do everything my coaches tell me to do, so you got to talk to coaches about that." Here are some numbers that illustrate that reduced role: 2026… https://t.co/nvfc3CMEII
If the Patriots choose to upgrade at any other position like guard or wide receiver before the November 10 trade deadline, then Barmore may be a valuable piece to lower the price of their payment.

title: Patriots Coach Shares Heartfelt Message to Now-Released Bryce Baringer
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England cut ties with one of their last remaining Bill Belichick draft picks this week, releasing veteran punter Bryce Baringer — who was on injured reserve to begin the season.
Baringer, who had been the Patriots punter for each of the last three seasons, suffered a lower-body injury in the preseason. The Patriots then turned to Matt Haack in the final preseason game before signing Mitch Wishnowsky to their practice squad. Wishnowsky has been the punter in each of New England's seven games this season.
Special teams coordinator Jeremy Springer, speaking to reporters for the first time since the transaction, shared what Baringer meant to him since he arrived in 2024.
"Oh man, I love Bryce," Springer said Thursday. "Me and him have a really, really strong relationship. I mean. since day one, he's been a straight supporter of me and helped me so much. Just kind of get affiliated with the area, with the players. He was all for the team. He's always for the team. He works his tail off. He's a great punter. He's going to do some great things whatever team picks him up."
Baringer was drafted in the sixth round in 2023 and won the punting job out of camp. He hadn't missed a game before this season and his 10,500 total punting yards ranks fourth in franchise history. With injuries stacking up for the Patriots on IR and only a limited amount of returns allowed, it forced the Patriots hand to roll with the punter they already had.
Mike Vrabel had similar things to say about Baringer earlier this week as well.
"I certainly appreciate what Bryce has been able to do for us," he said. "Those are tough decisions. I don't think those are things that you'd necessarily take lightly. ... We just felt like this was best for us, best for Bryce, and to give him an opportunity to go punt and see if somebody needs a punter. If we would need him back and he was there, then we would want to have him back. You just make a decision with a specialist, and as long as it's going well, which I think it is, and everybody else does, you just stick with it."
The job now fully belongs to Wishnowsky this season, but that doesn't mean Baringer can't find somewhere else to punt in 2026.
"I can't say enough good things about him, Bella — his wife — their family. He's always in my back pocket, he'll be a friend from now forward," Springer said. "And in this business, who knows, I might be coaching him next year or at some point down the road, you know, we'll be linked back up together, but excited for his future. It's just like I told him the other day, I'd say it's a stage stop on your journey. Like, we all have stops. We're all going to be in different places. This is never forever in this business. So best of luck to him."
On Tuesday, Baringer took to social media to thank the Patriots , writing: "A lot of love for New England.  Friendships and memories that will last a lifetime. Looking forward to what's to come. The prize is in the journey. Isaiah 41:10."
The 27-year-old punter is in a contract season and is set to hit free agency in March of 2027.

title: Drake Maye Gives High Praise to Patriots TEs, Highlights 'Great Connection'
full_text:
FOXBORO — Drake Maye can throw it all over the field and connect with his targets anywhere he puts it. But he's been on a different level with his tight ends this season.
The New England Patriots' top tight end duo of Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon have combined for 47 targets, 38 catches, 464 yards and four touchdowns. In the Patriots' last two games, Henry and Raridon have found the end zone three times.
Naturally, Maye gave them plenty of (deserving) praise this week ahead of the team's game with the Miami Dolphins .
"I've been blessed really my whole career since I got here, with Hoop (Austin Hooper) and Hunter, to have good tight ends," Maye said Wednesday. "Obviously we lost Hoop, but now Eli's really grown into a big role. I appreciate being with a young tight end, and not really showing him the ropes, but showing him how I see things and how I've learned to see things with Hunter and Hoop back in the day.
"But really, Hunter's one of the best things for Eli that you can have in the room. He's such a veteran presence," Maye said. "He's a pro. He does everything the right way, and we've got a great connection in that room. We've got a strong room in the run game and pass game."
Henry has been a mainstay for the Patriots since Maye's gotten here. Originally signing in free agency back in 2021, Henry has put together a career in New England that's skyrocketing him near the top of all positional statistical rankings. One more touchdown, and Henry passes Russ Francis (28) for the third-most touchdowns by a Patriots tight end ever.
Raridon is much further away. New England's third round draft pick from this spring , he's worked into the offense as the second option. The skills are all there, and he's been a weapon as a blocker and with the ball in his hands after the catch. He opened the season with a touchdown against the Seahawks, and helped get the Patriots back into the game in Week 7 in Chicago.
It's a pairing that offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels says gives the Patriots' offense a lot of flexibility. That tandem should be a big part of this offense moving forward. According to Pro Football Focus, Raridon in first among all rookie tight ens in first down receptions (nine) and hasn't dropped a pass all year.
With injuries on the offense hindering some production at the wide receiver position ( Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins remain on injured reserve ), the tight ends will become more important as the Patriots go through this stretch run.
"So, they do a lot for us, and it makes it tough on defense," Maye said. "You can match us in big people and you can try to match us in little people, and we'll try to run it.
"So, there's different things that you can create, and at the same time, they're great in the passing game."

title: Drake Maye's Performance Review: How Did Patriots QB Perform in October?
full_text:
Drake Maye's Super Bowl-rebound season got off to a very disappointing start. In September, Maye threw for 485 yards, one touchdown, and six interceptions on a 62.5% completion rate. What looked to be a junior-year slump quickly turned into a comeback story in October for the New England Patriots quarterback.
In the four weeks following Maye's abymsal first three games , the third-year passer recorded 1,299 passing yards, 12 passing touchdowns, and two interceptions with a 67.9% completion rate. Maye's exceleration as a passer coinciding with the leaves falling off trees around Foxboro feels Tom Brady-like.
However, Maye's October stardom didn't start in 2026. A year ago, Maye and the Patriots marched into Buffalo and accoomplished a massive victory on the first weekend of October. The sophomore passer's 273 yards and 101.1 passer rating was the second win of a 13-1 record to finish the season.
Drake Maye vs the Buffalo Bills. 2025. pic.twitter.com/wmX8i0kdWD
With the Patriots going 3-1 in October of 2026, could the autumn breeze bring New England into another run of dominance? According to NFL Spinzone, Maye ranks first in EPA from Week 4 to 7 and is second in pass success rate in the same amount of time.
"I think we're improving. I think we're growing," Maye said Wednesday. "We're battling some injuries. We're battling some of feeling like we're there one week, then we're dipping back down and then battling penalties. The biggest thing is we're moving the football. We’ve just got to try to finish off drives, get out of our own way penalty-wise and protect the football."
When evaluating Maye's past four games, it's essential to spotlight his performance against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5 . Maye threw for 371 yards and had five total touchdowns, plus a remarkable 150.9 passer rating.
In what was arguably Maye's best performance of his career , the Patriots took down the Raiders, who entered this game with just one loss, by a score of 45-17.
"I think we're just starting up the mountain. I think you would like to think that, and we have to go and prove that, but it's a race for us to improve," Maye said after his dominant performance. "Knowing that, you would like to say everybody – especially on offense – you'd like to say that the first three weeks weren't what we wanted to put out there."
As Maye pointed out, the New England offense continued to improve week-by-week after his performance against the Raiders. Against the Jets, Maye had a three-touchdown performance and the following week, in a loss against the Bears, he threw for 321 yards and had a 117.8 passer rating.
Patriots QB Drake Maye on not overlooking the 1-5 Dolphins this week: @boston25 pic.twitter.com/m9GR8OKsst
What may be the most impressive piece to Maye's recent success is the varying weapons he's had to make the most with. In just seven weeks, the Patriots have lost their top three receivers in A.J. Brown, Mack Hollins, and Romeo Doubs to injured reserve.
New England offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has had to revitalize his offensive game plan built over the summer with a rotation of pieces they never planned to use in higher volumes. Players like Efton Chism III, Eli Raridon, DeMario Douglas, and Rhamondre Stevenson have carried the receiving game in light of receiver injuries.
With this in mind, the efficiency of New England's passing attack in October is a product of Maye's ability to adapt and McDaniels's versatile game-planning.
Brown missed practice on Thursday with a newly designated knee injury, meaning the improvisation of receiving options may continue to be a trend for Maye moving forward.
#Patriots WR AJ Brown, not spotted at practice today, is not practicing because of a knee issue that has flared up, sources say. Brown also was listed on yesterday's injury report with an ankle. Knee was added, as well, and his status for Sunday is up in the air. pic.twitter.com/WvVJl6S6J6
Maye will continue his fall campaign into November, on the first day of the month, where New England travels to Miami to face the 1-5 Dolphins.

title: Patriots Get More Bad News on A.J. Brown's Injury, TreVeyon Henderson
full_text:
FOXBORO — After a Wednesday practice where the New England Patriots had all players on the active roster present for the first time this season, Thursday brought a noticeable change. Wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson were not seen during the media-access portion of practice. Both players were active Wednesday, with Brown a limited participant and Henderson not mentioned on the injury report. For Brown, this downgrade comes a day after reports surfaced that, alongside his previous ankle injury, he is also dealing with a knee injury.
No sign of WR A.J. Brown at practice. https://t.co/iho2uHG7tY
Brown missed time last season with a knee injury that may have stemmed from a reported degenerative knee condition. New England Executive Vice President of Player Personnel Eliot Wolf acknowledged the condition after the Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick to acquire Brown in June. "It's a factor, but we examined him," Wolf told Yahoo Sports at the time . "He's got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it." Managing Brown's health has been an ongoing campaign for New England . The star wide receiver suffered a high ankle sprain in the Patriots' season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, resulting in a four-week stint on injured reserve. "Look, he's played eight quarters in almost two months and had four practices," offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. "They tell us he can do A, B, and C; we’ll do A, B, and C. And if there’s some element of things we need to wait on, then we’ll do it, so love his attitude and his approach. He’s been here working his tail off to try to put himself in a great position to help our team, and I know he’s going to do that." Brown's absence from Thursday's practice raises concerns surrounding his availability for the Patriots' Week 8 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. The Patriots have already lost wide receivers Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and Mack Hollins (calf) to IR. If Brown were to miss time, the active roster would be left with just DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III. If that's the case, the Patriots may need to consider elevating someone from the practice squad. Kyle Dixon , the 6-foot-2, 220 lb. rookie undrafted free agent from Culver-Stockton College, could be an enticing option given his physical profile. Other WR options include Cameron Dorner, Chandler Brayboy, and Ryan Miller.
For Henderson, this latest absence is another unfortunate setback in what has been an underwhelming sophomore campaign . He's coming off a performance against the Chicago Bears in which he rushed just three times for nine yards and caught two passes for 14 yards. After suffering an ankle injury late in training camp that kept him out of the season opener, Henderson injured his ankle again against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5. The injury was initially reported as a high ankle sprain, which typically requires four to six weeks of recovery. However, Henderson continued to play in the weeks that followed. Henderson was reportedly seen in the locker room but didn't dress for practice or take any questions from reporters. He was listed on the injury report with an illness. If Henderson misses time, the Patriots would likely consider elevating Lan Larison from the practice squad.

title: Finding Trade Partners: Identifying 5 Teams the Patriots Must Contact
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is approaching , and across the league transactions are piling up. With the New England Patriots being considered as a top buyer in the league, they'll be reaching out to several underperforming franchises to bolster their roster that can compete in the playoffs.
After November 10, the Patriots would only acquire players through waivers or free agent signings, making the next two weeks a big opportunity to increase the team's competitiveness through trade acquisitions.
Having one of the most injured rosters in football, the Patriots may look to several teams to increase their depth. Here are the likely partners of a mid-season trade:
It's well-known that Mike Vrabel loves reuniting with his southern roots from Tennessee. He's signed a handful of free agents that were tenured with the Titans during his time as head coach, and most recently, traded for A.J. Brown, who Vrabel selected in the 2019 NFL Draft.
It makes too much sense that Vrabel and the Patriots front office would contact their friends in Nashville to orchestrate a trade. However, Tennessee's most valuable trade asset, Jeffery Simmons, was just moved to Chicago on Wednesday morning for two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick.
With New England's depth and efficiency at defensive tackle, it wasn't likely they'd make a move for Simmons, anyway, but this move indicates that Tennessee's market is open. EDGE Jermaine Johnson II emerges as a target for New England, who can acquire the Pro Bowl sixth-year player on an expiring contract for a small price.
Other peices that Tennessee may want to move away from include RB Tony Pollard, WR Calvin Ridley, and DE Jacob Martin.
New England could dip further into the AFC South by making a trade with Indianapolis, who's shown already that they like engaging in the trade deadline. Last year, the Colts acquired Sauce Gardner at the deadline, and they've already moved on from G Quenton Nelson and DE DeForest Buckner in the weeks leading up to this year's deadline.
After firing their general manager Chris Ballard, the Colts are exploring all options around the deadline. The biggest name they have to offer is Jonathan Taylor, who is many playoff contending teams' top target ahead of the deadline.
It was reported that Indianapolis would ask for at least a first-round pick in exchange for Taylor, unless a team would include a quality running-back in the deal. With this being said, the Patriots could offer up TreVeyon Henderson — who's underperformed in his sophomore season —  and a pick outside of of the first-round for Taylor.
#Colts RB Jonathan Taylor was asked if he’s requested a trade. First answer was unclear. After a follow-up: “No. That’d be crazy to even say because we got a division opponent (coming up). …” Taylor requested a trade in 2023 amid a contract dispute before signing an extension. pic.twitter.com/5xHc1WWflh
As seen with team's like the Eagles in 2024, who acquired Saquon Barkley in free agency, and this year's Kansas City Chiefs, who have an offensive powerhouse with Kenneth Walker at the center of it, sometimes all it takes is a dominant running back to make a great team a championship winning team.
If New England is more conservative at the deadline, they may look to other Colts players such as WR Josh Downs, who played with Drake Maye at UNC , or DT Grover Stewart.
After learning of Jalen Hurts' season-ending blood clots diagnosis, the Eagles have looked past this season as an opportunity to compete. They already moved on from center Cam Jurgens and have been shopping other players for draft capital.
The Eagles and Patriots are recent trade partners as of the A.J. Brown deal in June . The clear candidate for the Patriots to pursue this time around is guard Landon Dickerson. Dickerson is a Pro Bowler who's expressed uncertainty about his future with Philadelphia.
With guard being the most injured position on the Patriots roster, Dickerson would fill a huge gap for the offense that's struggled to replace Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker. One caveat is that Dickerson's contract is expensive, especially in 2028 where his $17.7 million cap hit will coincide with the first year of Christian Gonzalez's record-breaking extension and Brown's $17.8 million cap hit.
If the Patriots were to look for a less cap expensive option from Philadelphia, they may inquire about TE Dallas Goedert, WR Hollywood Brown, or CB Riq Woolen.
The Buccaneers have had an incredibly disappointing season thus far, and may look to sell out of the 2026 season, despite being a part of a somewhat non-competitive NFC South division.
Tampa Bay can offer quality additions to the Patriots that won't have lasting consequences. Most of Tampa Bay's trade candidates have minimal contract values that are close to expiring. This makes an interconference trade between New England and Tampa Bay very likely.
The player that hits all the margins of skill, need, and contract value is Yaya Diaby. The 6-foot-4, 270-pound linebacker is in the final season of his rookie contract and has been incredible in 2026. For a Patriots team that lacks experience and depth at edge rusher, Diaby could be difference maker in the defensive front.
How did Yaya Diaby still make this sack? TBvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WGfJpnx47b
The Buccaneers will also listen to offers for defensive ends Anthony Nelson and Al-Quadin Muhammad, and DT A'Shawn Robinson.
Just like every other team listed here, the Chargers have been a massive disappointment in 2026. Coming off a playoff run that ended In New England during the Wild Card round, the Chargers are approaching factory reset mode , meaning they'll likely move on from their biggest pieces.
One player that could draw the attention of Vrabel is Khalil Mack, who comes off the edge just like Vrabel did as a player. At 35-years old, Mack is well beyond his best day as a torturing edge rusher. But just like Diaby, Mack will provide a veteran presence to the edge rushers that can also make a difference in the defense's ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks.
Like Diaby, Mack is on an expiring contract that is only worth $8 million for whichever team that trades for him. Acquiring the stud defensive end who could one day be wearing a gold jacket in Canton, Ohio makes too much sense for this hopeful Patriots team.
The Chargers, while very available, have high-interest players for New England's needs such as WR Quentin Johnston , OL Trey Pipkins III, and LB Denzel Perryman.

title: Saints Midseason Stock Report: 4 Bright Spots Amid a Disappointing Start
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints enter their bye week with a disappointing 2-5 record despite the hype around the Saints being contenders to possibly win the NFC South.
While the season has been anything but positive, the team still has bright spots on both offense and defense.
Here's a look at four players who have performed above and beyond as we reach the midseason point.
Tyler Shough hasn't been perfect, but the second-year quarterback continues to show encouraging signs of development under coach Kellen Moore .
Through seven games, Shough has completed 67% of his passes for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's also contributed 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
His pass yardage and touchdown totals are both in the top 10 as he is tied for seventh in passing touchdowns and ninth in passing yards, but for a majority of the season he was either No. 1 or No. 2 in passing yards.
Those numbers are impressive considering New Orleans' struggles establishing a consistent rushing attack and protecting its quarterback.
Despite occasional mistakes, Shough has demonstrated improved accuracy, pocket presence and command of Moore's offense.
If he continues developing and limits turnovers, the Saints should feel increasingly confident about their quarterback situation.
Wide receiver Chris Olave has shown why the Saints gave him a 4-year, $132 million extension.
Through seven games, the former first-round pick has caught 49 passes (fourth in the NFL) for 636 yards (third in the NFL) and two touchdowns, averaging 90.9 receiving yards per game.
He opened the season with four 100-yard performances in his first four games, including a dominant 182-yard outing against Detroit .
Chase Young has arguably been New Orleans' most impressive player on defense through seven games.
The former No. 2 overall pick has recorded seven sacks, establishing himself as one of the NFL's most productive pass rushers.
Out of 50 edge rushers with at least 125 pass rushes, Young ranked second with a 90.0 Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade.
Young is on pace to record over 15 sacks, potentially putting him in the conversation for Pro Bowl recognition.
Though Young draws much of the spotlight, Carl Granderson is quietly putting together a standout year as well.
Across seven contests, the experienced defensive end has registered 25 tackles alongside 5.5 sacks, highlighted by a 1.5-sack effort versus Pittsburgh .
Granderson's current trajectory puts him on track for roughly 13 sacks, setting up a potential career mark.
Combined, Granderson and Young have racked up 12.5 sacks, forming one of the few reliable highlights for New Orleans' defense.
Even with the unit's broader difficulties, his growth paired with Young gives the Saints a high-caliber pass-rush duo for the future.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Saints' 16-10 Loss to Steelers in Paris
full_text:
Hoping to build momentum ahead of their upcoming bye week after a major victory last week, the New Orleans Saints instead fell 16-10 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday in Paris, exposing several recurring issues under coach Kellen Moore .
New Orleans' offensive struggles continued as missed scoring opportunities proved costly as the Saints fell to 2-5.
From an emerging young playmaker to a disastrous rushing performance, here is a look at the good, the bad and the ugly from the Saints' disappointing loss to Pittsburgh .
One of the few bright spots in New Orleans' disappointing loss was rookie wide receiver Barion Brown's emergence.
The sixth-round pick got a chance to show his explosiveness, finishing with three receptions for 57 yards and adding another 97 yards on four kickoff returns.
His biggest offensive play came in the first half when he caught a 49-yard pass from Tyler Shough , setting up Daniel Carlson 's 38-yard field goal.
Brown also returned a kickoff 42 yards in the second quarter, setting up a possession that ended with Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele .
Despite those contributions, Brown received just three targets.
That limited involvement raises questions about whether coach Kellen Moore is maximizing one of the offense's most explosive young playmakers.
With rookie Jordyn Tyson still sidelined by a hamstring injury, Brown has a chance to become a more consistent contributor alongside Chris Olave and Vele.
New Orleans gets a vital jolt on offense from Brown's explosive speed and big-play dynamism.
Following a sluggish 281-yard performance against Pittsburgh, integrating him must become a top priority for the Saints. To fully leverage the rookie's skill set, Moore ought to scheme designed touches, vertical routes and run-after-catch opportunities for him. Given how much he has delivered on minimal opportunities, Brown has earned a larger role.
In a narrow 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh, kicker Daniel Carlson missed a crucial 52-yard field goal in the fourth quarter — his fourth failure in 11 attempts this season. This ongoing volatility in special teams poses a critical problem for the 2-5 Saints.
The fourth-quarter miss was particularly damaging because New Orleans had already wasted a promising red-zone opportunity earlier in the second half. Rather than positioning themselves to tie or take the lead with a field goal late in the game, the Saints remained trapped in a six-point deficit.
Carlson's 63.6% conversion rate stands in sharp contrast to Steelers kicker Chris Boswell , who accounted for nine points by flawlessly making all three of his field goals (from 28, 47 and 39 yards).
With three one-score defeats recorded this year, New Orleans simply lacks the margin for error to withstand repeated scoring blunders in tight contests. Carlson's continuous field goal woes add to head coach Kellen Moore's list of bye-week priorities, as unreliable special teams only exacerbate the team's offensive stalls, defensive breakdowns and turnovers.
While much of the focus has centered on Tyler Shough's growth, an inept rushing attack still severely limits the Saints' offensive ceiling.
Sunday's outing represented a new low point for the ground game.
New Orleans generated a paltry 18 rushing yards across 17 carries, resulting in an abysmal 1.1 yards per carry.
The stat line is even more damning because Shough — a quarterback whose primary role isn't to lead the run game — was the team's top rusher with just 7 yards on three carries.
It is downright appalling that primary backs Alvin Kamara (six carries, five yards) and Kendre Miller (eight carries, six yards) both logged more rush attempts than total yards gained.
This embarrassing output highlights a backfield without a true lead option, further compounded by an offensive line that failed to establish leverage up front.
Such complete non-production is intolerable at any level of football—especially when relying on a developing quarterback to sustain drive after drive.
By stifling the run, Pittsburgh's defense put the burden entirely on Shough's shoulders.
Even with Shough connecting on nearly 79% of his passes, New Orleans repeatedly stalled because it lacked offensive balance.
Unfortunately, this isn't merely a single bad afternoon.
The Saints' season-long inability to establish the run has made the offense predictable and easy for physical front sevens to counter.

title: 3 Takeaways From Saints' Loss to Steelers: Same Problems, Different Country
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints traveled across the Atlantic Ocean hoping to build momentum heading into their bye week and salvage their season. Instead, they returned home with its fourth loss in five games and it just seems like another repeating nightmare for Who Dat Nation.
New Orleans fell 16-10 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in Paris, dropping to 2-5 through seven games under second-year coach Kellen Moore . It was the NFL's first regular-season game in France.
Despite another efficient passing performance from quarterback Tyler Shough , the Saints struggled to establish their rushing attack, failed to capitalize on scoring opportunities and couldn't get off the field defensively when it mattered most.
The loss marked New Orleans' third one-possession defeat this season, reinforcing concerns about the team's ability to execute in critical situations.
Here are three takeaways from another disappointing performance from the Saints performance.
For all the attention surrounding Shough's development, New Orleans' inability to run the football continues to undermine its offense.
Sunday's performance might have been its most concerning yet.
The Saints finished with just 18 rushing yards on 17 attempts, averaging a dismal 1.1 yards per carry.
Even more alarming, Shough led the team with 7 rushing yards on three attempts. However, he is a quarterback and that is not his job.
But for Alvin Kamara (six carries for five yards) and Kendre Miller (eight carries for six yards) to have more carries than rushing yards is disgusting.
It shows the lack of life in a running back room without a primary option, compounded by an offensive line struggling to create leverage.
That level of production is unacceptable for any offense regardless of the level of play, especially one relying on a young quarterback to consistently move the ball.
Pittsburgh's defense shut down the run, forcing Shough to carry nearly the entire offensive load.
Although Shough completed nearly 79% of his passes, New Orleans could not consistently finish drives because it lacked balance.
The problems extend beyond one disappointing performance.
New Orleans has struggled to generate consistent production on the ground throughout the season, making the offense increasingly predictable against physical defensive fronts.
Because of the rushing problems, the Saints had to rely on Shough again.
Shough did everything you could ask of him, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards and a touchdown. However, one costly mistake ultimately changed the game's complexion.
Trailing 13-10 at the start of the second half, New Orleans put together a 13-play drive that moved the offense inside Pittsburgh's 10-yard line as the Saints appeared positioned to take their first lead of the afternoon.
Instead, Shough threw a pass intended for Chris Olave , which Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson intercepted at the Pittsburgh 11-yard line.
The turnover erased a scoring opportunity and let Pittsburgh respond with a field goal, extending its lead to 16-10.
The interception proved costly, but it also highlighted the impossible position Shough has found himself in because of New Orleans' offensive struggles.
Despite completing nearly 79% of his passes, the quarterback could not afford even one mistake because the Saints had virtually no rushing attack to complement him.
That is an unrealistic expectation for any quarterback, much less one still developing at the NFL level.
Shough showed he could move the football against a Pittsburgh defense, distributing the ball effectively and keeping New Orleans competitive despite a one-dimensional offensive approach.
However, his play reinforced a troubling reality: when Shough plays well, the Saints can win; when he makes one mistake, the operation unravels.
Until Moore builds a credible run game and finishes drives, Shough bears an unreasonable load and New Orleans must create an offense where its quarterback does not need to be perfect to win.
Unless the Saints give Shough a credible rushing attack and adequate protection, they risk repeating a familiar chapter in franchise history: asking a talented young quarterback to overcome problems far beyond his control, much like Archie Manning decades ago.
Daniel Carlson 's fourth missed field goal in 11 attempts this season — a 52-yarder in the fourth quarter — kept New Orleans trailing in a 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh, highlighting a critical special teams weakness for the 2-5 Saints.
The missed 52-yard attempt came while the Saints trailed 16-10 in the fourth quarter, keeping Pittsburgh's lead at six points. Carlson's 63.6% success rate contrasts with Steelers kicker Chris Boswell , who converted all three attempts (28, 47 and 39 yards) for nine points.
The fourth-quarter miss was especially costly as New Orleans had already squandered a promising red-zone drive earlier in the second half. Instead of entering the final minutes needing only a field goal to tie or lead, the Saints remained six points behind.
Carlson's kicking struggles add to head coach Kellen Moore's bye-week concerns. For a team hampered by offensive inefficiency, defensive lapses and turnovers, unreliable special teams further shrink a narrow margin for error.
With three one-score losses this season, New Orleans cannot afford missed points. Sunday's loss highlights that the Saints lack the margin for error to overcome recurring scoring mistakes in tight games.

title: Saints Fans Should Know These 3 Things About the Steelers Before Sunday
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints (2-4) enter Sunday's historic matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) at Stade de France, looking to build momentum after their 34-27 win over the New York Giants .
However, Pittsburgh presents a considerably different challenge.
Under first-year coach Mike McCarthy , the Steelers have established themselves as a competitive AFC North contender, winning four of their first six games despite an offense that has struggled to consistently produce explosive plays.
Pittsburgh enters Sunday's contest averaging 22.8 points and 320.5 yards per game, ranking 18th and 21st in the NFL, respectively. However, its defense has been considerably more effective, allowing 307.5 yards per game, the ninth-fewest in the league.
For Saints coach Kellen Moore , Sunday's matchup offers a chance to secure consecutive wins for the first time this season before the team's Week 8 bye.
Here are three things Saints fans should know about the Steelers.
While 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers continues to anchor Pittsburgh's offense with his elite ability to read defenses and capitalize on errors, the Steelers' aerial game has produced fairly modest results.
Across six games, Rodgers has completed 61.4% of his pass attempts for 1,487 yards, throwing 12 touchdowns against five interceptions.
Despite these respectable individual metrics, Pittsburgh ranks just 18th in the league through the air, averaging 221.3 passing yards per contest.
Physical wide receiver DK Metcalf gives Rodgers a dependable downfield threat capable of winning contested balls and creating opportunities on intermediate routes.
However, Rodgers' statistical split against specific zone schemes presents a critical storyline for this matchup.
NFL Next Gen Stats reveals that Rodgers has struggled against Cover 3, registering a 32.9% success rate—the third-lowest figure among qualified quarterbacks—compared to a 52.9% success rate against all other zone schemes.
This dynamic is especially relevant given that New Orleans deploys Cover 3 on 55.9% of defensive dropbacks, leading the entire NFL.
Consequently, defensive coordinator Brandon Staley must balance disciplined zone coverage with an effective pass rush to contain Pittsburgh's passing attack.
While Rodgers draws significant focus, the Steelers' ground attack could pose a greater threat to New Orleans.
Running back Jaylen Warren has rushed for 460 yards on 84 carries, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt.
His ability to gain yards after contact, identify lanes and contribute in the passing game gives Pittsburgh multiple offensive options.
That creates a difficult matchup for New Orleans.
The Saints allow 138 rushing yards per game, ranking 30th in the NFL, while Pittsburgh averages 99.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 20th.
Despite Pittsburgh's modest team average, Warren's efficiency indicates the Steelers can exploit the Saints' run defense.
While returning veteran linebacker Kaden Elliss should bolster the Saints' run defense, containing Warren remains a critical priority. Allowing Pittsburgh to establish its ground game early will open up play-action opportunities for Rodgers.
While Pittsburgh's offense has experienced inconsistencies, its defense remains the team's most reliable strength.
The Steelers enter Sunday's matchup allowing 21.3 points and 307.5 yards per game, ranking 12th and ninth in the NFL, respectively.
A key part of its defense has been its ability to defend the pass as the Steelers have surrendered just 204.3 yards per game, the eighth-fewest in the league.
Pittsburgh has also recorded 16 sacks and six interceptions through six games, contributing to a plus-three turnover differential.
Outside linebacker T.J. Watt , who has a team-high 4.5 sacks, remains one of the league's most disruptive defensive players.
Alex Highsmith provides another formidable presence on the edge, while veteran defensive tackle Cameron Heyward anchors the interior.
The Steelers also one of the league’s top cornerbacks, eight-time Pro Bowler Jalen Ramsey , giving their secondary an experienced playmaker who can create turnovers.
For Saints quarterback Tyler Shough , protecting the football will be especially important.
Shough has thrown for 1,443 yards, 12 touchdowns and five interceptions this season, but his performance against zone coverage presents a potential concern.
According to Next Gen Stats , Shough has thrown five interceptions against zone coverage this season, tied for the second-most among qualified quarterbacks.
Pittsburgh has utilized zone coverage on 82.8% of opposing dropbacks, with five of its six interceptions occurring against zone concepts.
This creates a compelling schematic test between Moore's offense and Pittsburgh's defense.
If Pittsburgh generates pressure without compromising coverage, Shough may struggle against an opportunistic unit. To build on last week's win, New Orleans will need to establish the run, avoid clear passing downs, and minimize turnovers.
