title: How Steelers Can Beat Browns' Denzel Ward
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are preparing for their most important game of the regular season so far, as they meet the Cleveland Browns in a critical Week 8 matchup. Both teams enter with a 5-2 record and a chance to show that they are legitimate contenders for the division title and in the conference.
The Steelers enter with a wave of momentum and confidence. They've won three consecutive contests, and despite some blemishes and imperfections, this team is right in the thick of things. To win this contest, however, the Steelers have to solve the Browns’ biggest strength on defense. Cornerback Denzel Ward is playing like the best CB in the NFL, and he’s going to give the Steelers’ offense fits in this Week 8 showdown.
For the Steelers, it's a challenge that a championship-caliber team can and must overcome. Thankfully for head coach Mike McCarthy and his offense, their previous matchup, plus another loss in the Browns' schedule, can give them the keys to taking down Ward and the Cleveland defense in Week 8.
There genuinely might not be a better cornerback in the NFL right now than Denzel Ward. Through seven games, he has two interceptions and six passes defended. But the most impressive thing about the five-time Pro Bowler's start is how dominant he is when targeted.
Quarterbacks have a better chance of just throwing the ball away, rather than going after Ward with a passing attempt. According to data from Pro-Football-Reference , Ward has been thrown at 39 times but has allowed just 16 completions. That's a 41% completion rate and an average of 9.6 yards per reception.
The key for the Steelers is to get wide receiver DK Metcalf going early. In their earlier meeting, the Steelers were able to produce some numbers with Metcalf, and their method for doing so was getting him the ball quickly in space via screens. On the first offensive series of that Week 4 game, the Steelers tried to send Metcalf deep on a go-ball, but it was incomplete because of Ward's coverage on the sidelines.
Next, they sent two quick screens to him later in the drive, and that's when the yards started to pick up, with 22 yards after his first two receptions. Things went quiet for Metcalf until the fourth quarter, when he and Rodgers connected for a 43-yard bomb early in the fouth quarter. That play was successful due to the bunch formation on one side, which got Metcalf away from Ward and Tyson Campbell. This way, they were able to create a one-on-one matchup in the slot between Metcalf and the Browns' nickel corner, which was an easy one for DK to win.
That's going to be a huge part of this game for the Steelers . The battle of wits between McCarthy and the Browns' defense. Getting Metcalf away from Ward is going to be crucial as they try to keep the passing game on an upward trajectory.
A team that produced impressive passing results against Ward and the Browns was, surprisingly, the New York Jets. Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson combined for 104 yards in their Week 5 contest, and they accomplished it through surprisingly simple, yet effective methods. In the likely event that the Steelers cannot avoid the matchup of Metcalf and Ward, they have to utilize plays and concepts that can create opportunity for their top receiver.
The Browns play a lot of man-to-man coverage. According to data from Sharp Football Analysis, the Browns far and away employ the most man coverage plays in the NFL, deploying it 42.4% of the time so far this season. When you have a player of Ward's caliber, it's easy to rely on that, since a majority of the time he single-handedly eliminates receivers from the board.
But the Jets countered the Browns' defensive scheme with a ton of mesh concepts. This is a fairly common play type in today's NFL, consisting of two crossing routes over the middle of the field, and the Jets had the perfect wide receiver in Garrett Wilson to take advantage. His speed across the middle, plus some strategic pick plays and rub routes, gave Wilson just enough space to get open.
Heading into Week 8, the Steelers should take a bit from the Jets' playbook. With Metcalf's speed, they have to find a way to create separation for him, something this offense continues to struggle with. These mesh concepts can, hopefully, give Metcalf some breathing room when he goes up against Ward.
It's going to be an absolute war between the Steelers and Browns in Week 8. To get past their rival and take the top spot in the AFC North, they have to win the passing battle . If they follow this guide, they will likely get the result they are looking for.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 5 Potential Options for Steelers CB Trades
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- One of the most pressing needs for the Pittsburgh Steelers is at cornerback. The trading of Joey Porter Jr. may have been justified, at least if you ask the organization, but it also left a glaring hole in the defense.
Without him, the Steelers lack a number one cornerback. Furthermore, their inability to play man-to-man coverage is beginning to be taken advantage of. The team's reliance on soft zone coverage is no longer effective, and their lack of foot speed continues to show up on film.
That's why the Steelers need to land a starting cornerback before the NFL Trade Deadline. These five defensive backs could all fill the void in Pittsburgh as they look to upgrade the secondary.
The Steelers need someone who is long and quick. They might not be able to land a player who can be a long-term option, like the top two players on this list, but they could land a seamless fit like Miami Dolphins defensive back JuJu Brents.
Brents is by no means a star on defense, but he's been quietly steady in Miami this season. At 6'3" and over 200 pounds, he's a big and physical player who can line up on the outside and make life difficult for a number two receiver.
Experienced and versatile, Charvarius Ward is an option the Steelers could bring in with little fanfare, but high expectations. Simply put, Ward has been a rock-solid cornerback his entire NFL career.
The difficult thing with Ward is that he's under contract through the 2027 season and his cap hit for next season is just under $25 million. For a starting cornerback, that's fine, but the 31-year-old is not the player the Steelers want to tie that much money to beyond 2026. If the Colts eat some of that money, there is certainly a deal to be worked out, and the Steelers could use his presence on the outside for the rest of this campaign.
42 cornerbacks recorded at least 10 pass breakups in 2025, according to SumerSports , and one name that doesn't get talked about enough is Rasul Douglas. Last year, he was one of the few bright spots on a miserable Miami Dolphins defense. He finished the 2025 campaign with 13 passes defended and two interceptions over 813 snaps.
The 32-year-old veteran is now with the Washington Commanders, and he continues to stand out. He's on a cheap, one-year contract, but plays like a starter still. He's recorded five pass breakups and an interception to begin the 2026 campaign, and he brings an edge that would fit right in with the Steelers' defense.
A Super Bowl winner with the Seattle Seahawks last season, Riq Woolen is on a one-year contract and in a losing situation with the Philadelphia Eagles. He's a monster on the outside. He's physical and specializes in one-on-one situations. Sure, he's susceptible to penalty calls, but that's nothing the Steelers haven't seen before.
For a day three pick, which the Eagles will ask for, the Steelers could land a temporary solution with championship experience.
Times are tough for the Los Angeles Chargers. They are closer to the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft than a postseason berth, and it's nearing time they reach their own fire sale.
The Steelers could swoop in and land a starting corner on the outside for the rest of this year and next season in Cam Hart, a former fifth-round pick of the Chargers. The 25-year-old would give the Pittsburgh defense precisely what they lost with the JPJ trade. Hart is 6'2" and has a long wingspan, which are tailored perfectly to being a playmaker on the outside.
And making plays is exactly what he's doing in Los Angeles, despite the team's continued struggles. Hart has posted two interceptions and six pass breakups in six games, and quarterbacks are completing 61.9% of their pass attempts when targeting him in coverage.
Most importantly, he can play man coverage with success. Playing on his rookie deal, the Steelers would be walking into another contract negotiation in the offseason, but it won't be as dramatic as the last one with a starting cornerback in Pittsburgh.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers’ Troy Fautanu Responds to Jared Verse Smack Talk
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers left tackle Troy Fautanu addressed Cleveland Browns EDGE rusher Jared Verse's comments ahead of a crucial Week 8 matchup between the two teams.
While speaking with reporters on October 29, Fautanu offered not to directly respond to Verse's claim from directly after Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 4 over Pittsburgh that the Steelers were "dirty".
"I don't know what he's talking about honestly," Fautanu said. "I got no comment, I'm just excited to play this game. We're gonna go out there and continue to play our game."
Fautanu also noted that Verse's comments have not fired him up personally and that he's approaching this week's bout with the Browns as "just another game".
"Personally not really," Fautanu said. "It's just another game, I'm gonna approach it as such, and it's a big game because it's the next game."
Fautanu's move from right tackle to left tackle this season has come with its ups and downs thus far.
The 2024 first-round pick has allowed 20 total pressures and four sacks over seven games this year as compared to 31 pressures and three sacks across 17 contests in 2025 (per Pro Football Focus ), meaning he's regressed a decent amount from a statistical perspective in pass protection.
In what was arguably Fautanu's best performance of the campaign vs. Cleveland in Week 4, though, he allowed just a single pressure and no sacks over 46 reps as a pass blocker (per SumerSports ). That included 16 snaps in which he took on Verse, and Fautanu shut him out over that span.
With both the Browns and Steelers sitting atop the AFC North at 5-2, even if the former currently holds the tiebreaker due to a 2-0 record within the division while the latter is 1-1, this week's game is among the most consequential regular season matchups between the two sides in quite a long time.
The exchange of words has only added to the rivalry and excitement for the contest too, with Cameron Heyward stating on "The Rich Eisen Show" on October 27 that Verse's comments "will be addressed," while the latter added on October 29 that Cleveland is "about to make Pittsburgh ours."
Verse has been quiet this season (zero sacks, 12 pressures per PFF ) after arriving in the trade that sent Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in June, but the Browns' defense as a whole is tied for the third-best pressure rate in the NFL at 42.7 percent (per SumerSports ) and has recorded the sixth-most sacks of any team with 20.
Cleveland sacked Aaron Rodgers five times in its victory over Pittsburgh earlier this season, and though the Steelers' offensive line has certainly improved as the year has gone along, the unit has still given up 22 sacks (tied for second-most in NFL, per SumerSports).
Limiting the Browns' pass rushers will be paramount to coming away with a victory, and Fautanu's matchup with Verse in particular is one that Pittsburgh has to gain the upper-hand in.

title: Seahawks Get Jaxon Smith-Njigba Some Help in 2027 NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are focused on the second half of the season, but they are also looking forward to the NFL draft in the spring.
It remains to be seen where the Seahawks will end up in the first round, but with a boatload of picks , they are keeping their radars wide open. One player that could make sense for them is Rutgers wide receiver KJ Duff, who was listed as the No. 17 overall pick by Seahawks contributor Tim Crean in his latest mock draft.
"No wide receiver in the NFL is more relied on than Jaxson [sic] Smith-Njigba. The Seahawks need to find him a running-mate, because he can’t continue to carry the passing game all by himself. The 6-foot-6 KJ Duffy [sic] is an interesting player here, because the big target is so different than JSN that he just might be the perfect No. 2 in Seattle," Crean wrote.
Through seven games, Smith-Njigba has 78 targets, while no other teammate of his has more than 30. His 867 yards are well ahead of everybody in the league by over 150 yards.
When it comes to the team, no other receiver has more than 200 yards on the season. Smith-Njigba getting a super majority of the receptions, targets, and yards is not a surprise given his talent, but it might help Seattle to bring in another target to take some heat and attention off of JSN.
As a huge 6-6 target, this could be a massive boost for the Seahawks when it comes to their red zone offense.
The team signed Rashid Shaheed to a 3-year, $51 million contract and made Smith-Njigba the highest-paid wide receivers in the NFL this past offseason, adding another first-round pick to that mix. That might not make sense when there are other positions of need.
The team will need to replace DeMarcus Lawrence on the pass rush unit next season, as he is headed for retirement. Getting a young pass rusher who can develop might make more sense to the team in the long run.
A player like Yhonzae Pierre from Alabama has been linked to them in the past, and he could be someone to look out for in the future.

title: Jonathan Taylor Trade Would Help Seahawks, But Here's Why It Won't Happen
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have been linked to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor as a trade target for the past couple of weeks.
The Seahawks and Colts recently agreed to a deal involving All-Pro offensive lineman Quenton Nelson , but Taylor was not part of the trade. Bleacher Report writer Alex Kay suggested a trade that would send Taylor to the Seahawks for Emanuel Wilson and second- and fourth-round picks in next year's draft.
"Bringing Taylor into the mix would significantly elevate a Seahawks ground attack that is averaging a middling 113.7 yards per game right now. That is nearly 10 yards below what the team rushed for during the 2025 campaign and almost 20 yards fewer than it averaged during its three-game postseason run," Kay wrote.
"While the move would cost the Seahawks some premium picks, upgrading Wilson to Taylor would have a transformative effect—catapulting Seattle back near the top of the Super Bowl favorites list."
The Seahawks have a chance to win a second straight Super Bowl, and they can't sit on the sidelines and let other teams make the big plays instead of them. Last year, the Seahawks acquired Rashid Shaheed from the New Orleans Saints, and that move ended up paying off big time.
This year, they have shown aggressiveness in acquiring Nelson, but it might not hurt to get an improvement at the running back position, which has been an inconsistency for the team all season long.
Trading for Taylor ensures that another team that could be competing with them in the NFC playoffs, like the Minnesota Vikings, doesn't get him. That might be the ultimate reason, which would put the Seahawks on a path to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl for a second year in a row.
Taylor is going to cost the Seahawks a pretty penny. He is under contract for $44 million over the next two years, which is far more expensive than what Kenneth Walker III cost the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks were unwilling to match a deal similar to what Walker got with the Chiefs, so it wouldn't make sense for Seattle to raise their salary standards for Taylor.
On top of that, the team should be getting Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back in the lineup at some point in the next couple of weeks. That should help the run game tremendously, which would negate the need to make a trade for Taylor, even if it is the splashy, sexy move that many football fans would love to see.

title: Seahawks Get Good Injury News on Jadarian Price, Bad News on Byron Murphy, More
full_text:
If you were hoping for more clarity with this Friday injury report, well, sometimes hope is a dangerous thing. Yes, there is some good news here for sure, and some indications this team is starting to slot back together, but in an almost equal amount we got some concerning information. Let’s comb over it and see where we stand with one practice to go.
Let’s start with the good news. Quenton Nelson (knee) and Brady Russell (wrist) remained full participants and look good to roll. DeMarcus Lawrence and Jaxon Smith-Njigba emerged from their rest days with full practices. Connor O’Toole (hamstring), Chazz Surratt (calf), Drake Thomas (ankle) and Leonard Williams (achilles) went from limited to full.
Tyrice Knight (hip) remained limited, although it’s less important if Thomas is back for the starting spot. Drew Lock (right elbow) is also still limited. The thing that’ll get your concern going, however, is Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting downgraded to limited after four straight fulls, and Byron Murphy (back) getting thrown on as a limited participant.
Hopefully, Charbonnet’s downgrade is a reflection of getting him some rest and easier days rather than a setback. It has been reported this week that Zach is expected to play. As for Murphy, it’s a question of if the injury happened during practice or was picked up on before practice started. We won’t know for sure until tomorrow, but until then, it’s uncomfortable.
Anthony Bradford (knee) was downgraded to DNP, which makes me wonder if they might be holding him out for trade purposes . Pat O’Connell (toe) got downgraded to DNP too, and Brandon Pili (back) has a new injury that put him on the sideline. Charles Cross (ankle), Velus Jones (hamstring), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), and Rashid Shaheed (knee) were out too.
The Bears have a much more peaceful injury report, but they didn’t get the motion they would have preferred today. T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (concussion) remained practicing in full, but that’s where the good news ends. Although with a brewing situation with another linebacker on that roster, that may end up being no small thing.
Malik Muhammad (toe) was still limited today, indicative of a player with a good chance to play but who may not be himself. And with all the Bears are likely to ask of him on Monday, that’s significant. Also significant is Colston Loveland (neck), added to the report today, indicating something may have happened at practice. With Kmet already out, they need Loveland.
Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was held out again, and is very likely out for this game, but that’s not the only problem for Chicago. D’Marco Jackson (ankle), estimated to be limited yesterday, didn’t practice at all today. Whether something happened between yesterday and today, or if the estimate didn’t capture his status correctly, is unknown, but that would be no small loss.
It could easily be a glorified rest day, but this is definitely worth paying attention to tomorrow when the final report comes out.

title: 3 Bold Predictions For Seahawks vs. Bears in Week 8
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears made waves this week as both pulled off massive moves ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
Seattle added three-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts to fill their biggest need on the offensive line . As for the Bears, they added to a strength as they improved their defensive line by picking up Jeffrey Simmons in a deal with the Tennessee Titans.
Now, those two should go head-to-head as the Seahawks host the Bears on Monday Night Football in Week 8. With that showdown being in prime time, there will be plenty of eyes on both teams. With the stage set, here's a look at three bold predictions for the NFC showdown.
This is an intriguing battle of strength vs. strength. The Bears are first in the NFL in rushing yardage with 1,080 yards going into this game while the Seahawks are sixth in the league in stopping the run, and are holding teams to just 3.5 yards per attempt .
Both teams will be intent on imposing their will in this one and while the Bears have been impressive, Seattle proved last week that they're still the best defense in the league when they're focused. That's the case in this prediction as Mike Macdonald and Aden Durde put a game plan together that forces Caleb Williams to beat them with his arm.
Forcing Williams to throw the ball is only the first step. Seattle has to be up to the task of slowing him down as well, because Williams is in the midst of another fantastic season. He's completing 71 percent of his attempts and has thrown just one interception.
Seattle will have more than enough confidence going against Williams after holding Patrick Mahomes to 19-of-33 passing with an interception. This week, they continue to impress as they slow Williams down and force him to throw two interceptions for the first time this season.
If Seattle's defensive strategy goes well, the Seahawks should be able to control the ball on the ground. They did this in Week 7 to the tune of 153 yards against a stingy Kansas City defense. They're again going up against a potent defense, and one that just received a boost in the form of Jeffrey Simmons.
That said, Seattle added Quenton Nelson , who knows Simmons well from their time in the AFC South. Nelson shores up the only weakness on the offensive line and in this final prediction, he helps clear the way for Seattle's running backs to rush for 150 yards as Brian Fleury plays a brilliant ball-control offense.

title: Seahawks' Dark Side Defense Facing Injuries at Bad Time Before Bears
full_text:
Through seven weeks into the 2026 NFL Season, the Seattle Seahawks (4-3 ) have one of the best, if not the best, defenses in the NFL. The Dark Side Defense has been the reason why the team remains one of the best teams competing for a Super Bowl title . Among the key reasons for their elite potential are their dynamic star players and a roster full of productive playmakers.
​Even the great defenses have some limits. The Seahawks’ defense has some injury concerns that could play a factor on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears (5-2). The Bears will be one of the most talented offenses the Seahawks will face this season. There isn’t a question of whether the Seahawks can beat the Bears, but are they healthy enough?
​Just a few days after humiliating the Kansas City Chiefs , the Dark Side Defense has some concerns with injuries. The Dark Side Defense has seven players with legitimate concerns on Thursday’s injury report. Among the biggest are defensive tackle Leonard Williams (Achilles), Tyrice Knight (hip), edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle).
​Nwosu didn’t participate in Thursday’s practice , leaving him with some serious doubt about not playing Monday night against the Bears. He is one of the more consistent pass rushers along the edge for the Dark Side Defense. Another consistent pass rusher for the Seahawks is Williams from the interior. He has a potentially scary injury that could be tough for him to play through, even if he feels great.
​Another factor is Thomas potentially returning to the Seahawks after missing two games. The player that replaced him, Knight, is also seeing some injury concerns. He has played great stepping in as a starter, but his availability is a concern. His backups in Chazz Surratt (calf), Patrick O’Connell (toe) and Connor O’Toole (hamstring) also become a concern after being limited in Thursday’s practice.
​The Bears aren’t the most productive offense they’ll face up to this point in the season. Chicago, however, has scored the sixth-most points in the league, averaging 25.7 points per game. The Bears are also second in the league in total yards per game (393.3). One of the big reasons is their rushing offense being first in rushing yards with 1,080. The Bears have utilized D’Andre Swift as a dynamic weapon.
​Seattle is coming off a game where they held the league’s best rusher in Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III to 36 yards on 14 carries. The Seahawks faced a limited Chiefs’ offense in Week 7, but the Bears are a lot more explosive with their passing game, with quarterback Caleb Williams, wide receiver Luther Burder and Rome Odunze. The Seahawks have opposing offenses to short-yardage situations, but they’ll have to take away the deep passing game the most.

title: Six Players the Seahawks Should Note from College Football Week 8
full_text:
Throughout the College Football Season, we’ll be monitoring top performers who might be available to the Seattle Seahawks in the 2027 draft . We’ll focus on players that play positions that are likely, or at least possibly, going to be one the team considers going after. This should give us a chance to spotlight players that the team targets well ahead of time.
Over the last few weeks, I’ve felt the energy shift in how this QB class is perceived. Despite his rawness, lack of experience, and wild moments, Drew Mestemaker has a good amount of Josh Allen in his game. It was a big moment for the Longhorns, coming off two straight losses and staring at a potential three-score blown lead. Brown’s 157 rushing yards preserved the win and helped push him into the conversation concerning this upcoming draft. Texas routinely produces quality NFL running backs, and Raleek looks like the next one. Onward and upward.
It’s not easy to cook up a realistic scenario where the Seahawks draft a defensive lineman in the first round, but David Stone is worth the thought. Oklahoma puts Stone in A-gap a fairly decent amount, so he might be able to provide NFL caliber nose tackle snaps while also being a worthy three-tech. 7 tackles and 1.5 sacks against Mississippi State is turning heads.
This isn’t the season Oregon thought they would have back in August. Their high-powered offense can’t score, so it’s left to their defense to desperately fight to keep them in it. We haven’t talked much about UCLA this draft season, but Omosigho has been turning in some very strong performances lately to change that. Rotating between playing off-ball and on the edge, Sammy’s 6 tackles, 2 sacks, fumble recovery, and whopping 7 pressures are eye popping, and should be worth a lot of consideration in a few months.
I really like this safety class, and hopefully the Seahawks do too if they need to replace Julian Love. Bowen is far from a headliner in this group, but after 7 tackles and a big interception to help the Sooners notch a victory, as well as a 82.7 PFF grade, he’s worth a strong look. You could do a lot worse with a day three pick, when he’ll probably get selected.

title: What Should the Seahawks Do With Anthony Bradford?
full_text:
The making of an omelet requires the breaking of a few eggs. And in the case of the Seattle Seahawks trading for Quenton Nelson , those eggs have come in the form of a third round pick, a fifth round pick, and ten million dollars in 2026 cap commitments. There’s a fourth egg as well that is less obvious, but worth considering, in the form of Anthony Bradford.
Mike Macdonald laid it out during yesterday’s press conference. Quenton Nelson will take up the left guard position, and Grey Zabel is going to right guard. This means Anthony Bradford is hitting the bench. It’s probably the best decision the team could make right now, although I have serious concerns about it, but it leaves Bradford in an unfortunate spot .
Bradford is a little more than four months away from hitting the open market as a free agent. The next ten games plus postseason was going to go a long way in determining his value on his next contract. For him to get benched at this juncture is tragic for him, after the work he did helping this team win a super bowl last season. I can’t help but feel for him.
Because of this, I wonder if the Seahawks might turn around and flip Anthony Bradford between now and the trade deadline. Such a move could recoup the fifth rounder the team gave up in the Nelson trade, leaving just the third, which likely gets recouped as well if Nelson walks in free agency in March. There’s nearly two weeks to find a suitor for him.
It’s also a chance to do right by Anthony, who deserves a chance to start right now, and is good enough to do so despite his shortcomings. Also keep in mind the nature of the upcoming 2027 draft class, which looks excellent so far, so giving up some depth for another shot at that class is a reasonable risk. If Beau Stephens is ready to be a backup, then it makes sense.
I’m concerned about the Grey Zabel element of this switch-up . I’m old enough to prefer my right guards to be road graders who can overwhelm with strength, and I don’t see Zabel as being that. Combine that finesse skillset with his lack of experience on the right side, and I could see this being a bumpy transition. Maybe bumpy enough to get Bradford back onto the field.
So maybe you hold onto him just because of that. Even if that doesn’t happen, an injury is always in play, and holding onto Bradford bails you out if either guard goes down. We got a decent look at Stephens over the last month, and he doesn’t look ready to fill in. Ultimately, this team is trying to win it all this season, and that’s worth a lot more than a day three pick.

title: The Biggest Position of Need for Seahawks in 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are trading away draft picks to acquire Indianapolis Colts offensive lineman Quenton Nelson , but the team is still holding on to its first-round pick.
The Seahawks have a boatload of picks to work with in next year's draft , where they will be looking to add some youth to their pass rush unit.
"Dante Fowler Jr. hasn't appropriately replaced Boye Mafe for the Seattle Seahawks. Uchenna Nwosu is also on an expiring contract. Expect GM John Schneider to invest heavily at pass rusher again this coming offseason," NFL Draft On SI contributor Justin Melo wrote.
The Seahawks have a lot of experience at the pass-rushing positions, but free agency is going to come sooner rather than later for several of them. Uchenna Nwosu is not under contract for the 2027 season, and neither is DeMarcus Lawrence, who announced his retirement at the end of the season, meaning he won't be back next year either.
Dante Fowler Jr., the No. 3 overall pick in the 2015 NFL Draft, has stepped in to replace Boye Mafe, who left in free agency for the Cincinnati Bengals, but he is not off to a great start in his Seahawks career. Fowler has managed to record just one tackle in seven games so far for the Seahawks.
Players like Boubacar Traore from Notre Dame and Yhonzae Pierre from Alabama could make sense for the Seahawks, depending on where they end up in the first round and where these prospects line up on the big board at the end of April.
Needless to say, the Seahawks should be looking at pass rushers on each day of the draft, as bringing in talent across the board should help them, not just on defense but on special teams as well.
Injecting some youth into the unit could backfire if the Seahawks find the wrong people, but Seattle has always built through the draft. That is how they are going to continue to evolve as they seek another Super Bowl title.

title: Seahawks Have 'Best Defense in Football' Entering Matchup vs. Bears
full_text:
Similar to the Legion of Boom in the 2010s, the current Seattle Seahawks' "Dark Side" defense is only growing in infamy around the NFL as they continue to strike fear in opposing offenses.
There was no better example of that than in Week 7, when the Seahawks handed the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs offense their worst-ever performance in primetime. Kansas City didn't have a single snap in the red zone, totaled just 213 yards and picked up 11 first downs. Running back Kenneth Walker III, who entered the game averaging 133 rushing yards per game, finished with 14 carries for 36 yards.
After losing three of its previous four games, Seattle's defense is riding high into a Monday night game against the Chicago Bears in Week 8. The Bears are well aware of the caliber of defense they're facing.
Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was asked on Wednesday about his thoughts on facing the Seahawks after how they shut down the Chiefs. Williams gave Seattle's defensive unit a lot of credit, but also welcomed the challenge.
“Obviously, that’s the best defense in football right now, for stats-wise and players and scheme,” Williams said. “So, it’s going to be fun for us; it’s going to be a challenge for us, and we accept that challenge. We gotta go out there, we gotta execute, we gotta do our part.
“They do a good job with punching the ball out, interceptions — I think they’re second in the league or something like that with the amount of turnovers that they’ve had … They’re fully equipped over there to do whatever they need as a defense and as a team, and so like I said, it’s going to be a fun challenge for us.”
Seattle's defense is allowing the fewest total yards per game (233.9), the fewest passing yards (144.4) and the sixth-fewest rushing yards (89.4) through seven games. They rank fourth in points allowed per game (17.9) and are tied for the second-most takeaways (12).
The Seahawks are essentially dominating in every area, and Bears head coach Ben Johnson is well aware of how difficult it will be for his offense to move the ball.
“I think they do a great job affecting the quarterback, number one. Up front, they’ve got good rushers, and they’re able to get [to] and affect the quarterback without having to pressure a whole lot in passing downs,” Johnson said. “So, when you’re able to do that with just four rushers, I think it’s really hard to get guys open with a lot of space. They’re doing a phenomenal job taking away explosive plays in the passing game, and it’s hard to stay on schedule consistently and march it down the field and score in the red zone on these guys, and that’s what they try to make you do.”
The potential All-Pro defensive line duo of Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy II are two of the main culprits in what Johnson is describing, and it's further amplified by the edge rushers. Linebacker and defensive back Nick Emmanwori is emerging as one of the most unique players in the league, and he's adding a whole new dimension to the Seahawks' pass rush.
“You combine that with the fact that it’s hard for a lot of offenses to even get started — the number of three-and-outs on tape is pretty astonishing as well,” Johnson added. “It’s hard to run the ball; hard to throw the ball, and it’s going to take a team effort here to win this one this week.”
The Seahawks (4-3) and Bears (5-2) kick off at 5:15 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 2, at Lumen Field. Both teams made blockbuster trades this week, with Seattle adding All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and the Bears picking up All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , adding further intrigue to the matchup.

title: 49ers Fans' Bye Week Cheer Guide: Who to Root For Around the NFL
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers ' Week 8 bye couldn't come soon enough as I was about to sign to the practice squad as a wide receiver. I mean, 33-year-old Dad-bod fits the age criteria and the drop off can't be much from what we saw last Sunday in Atlanta.
All jokes aside, hopefully the boys get healthy this weekend before they take on the team that left the Bay for the Vegas lights.
Here are three games to keep your eye on.
The Minnesota Vikings are now gaining respect around the NFL as the only team left without feeling defeat. The Vikings (6-0) travel to Detroit (4-2) to take on the Lions #1 passing offense. Tale of two stories in this one, as it'll be good (Lions offense) vs good (Vikings defense) and bad (Lions defense) vs (Vikings offense).
A Lions win here would help the 49ers NFC Standings as this would be a division loss for the Vikings.
This will be an interesting matchup in the stands, without the 49ers, Raiders, Cowboys, and Steelers as the visiting team. What jersey will everyone be wearing while attending the game?
Nonetheless, the Chargers (0-6) will be fresh off a bye and still winless. I know Jim Harbaugh is pressing for the Chargers to sneak out a win. Mike McDaniel and Justin Herbert will need to be on the same page and not look like the 28th total offense that they are.
Sure, the Rams got "back on track" last week in Las Vegas, but that was against the league's 30th-ranked total defense. The Chargers aren't a world beater by any means, but they come in twice as good, ranked 15th.
Finally, we are back to a great Monday Night Football matchup. Regardless of who wins or loses, the 49ers will benefit.
While the Bears on paper may be a bigger threat to the 49ers because of Chicago's offense and their resurging defense, they are not in division. It's as simple as that.
Seahawks falling to 4-4 would give the 49ers a three-game lead over the second-place NFC West team and provide some space for error, like the loss to the Atlanta Falcons. Plus, the last thing the 49ers need is for the Seahawks to win this game and start playing with that arrogant confidence similar to their Super Bowl run a season ago.
With the 49ers on a bye, hopefully you get to enjoy some stress-free football, besides your fantasy team of course. Make sure to put the Lions, Chargers, and Bears on your Week 8 cheer card.

title: The 4 Worst-Performing 49ers at the Bye Week
full_text:
With the San Francisco 49ers on their Bye Week , it makes for the perfect time to review who their worst performers have been this season. Let's dive in.
By far, kicker Eddy Pineiro has been the worst 49ers player this season. It's been astonishing to see after he was a hero last season when the 49ers finally moved on from Jake Moody.
Pineiro has missed three of his nine field goal attempts this season for a 66.7% conversion rate. But his most egregious performance has come on extra-point attempts.
He's missed 21 of 25 attempts, for an 84% conversion rate. Pineiro has the yips this season and has shown zero signs of getting himself out of it.
It's only a matter of time before he costs the 49ers a game. The one saving grace is that, of all the 49ers who needed the Bye Week, it was Pineiro.
He can use this time away to reset his mind. Usually, the yips is a mental issue, so by being away, Pineiro can forget all of his woes and bounce back for the second half of the season.
What a frustrating player wide receiver Jacob Cowing has been. Most of his issues have been as a punt returner, where he oddly fields punts around the five-yard line rather than letting the ball bounce into the end zone.
Cowing has cost the 49ers valuable field position on numerous occasions this season. His worst play this year was in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.
Cowing was fielding a punt in the first quarter, and rather than calling an obvious fair catch, he elected to field the punt, allowing a Seahawks player to force a fumble.
Seattle would recover the ball with perfect field position and would score a touchdown shortly thereafter. Cowing has been a negative factor for the 49ers.
Whenever Deebo Samuel gets healthy, they need to have him be the return specialist instead of Cowing. Otherwise, they will make games much more difficult to win.
Cornerback Jack Jones was so bad this season that the 49ers chose him as the player to release when they officially acquired DeForest Buckner.
Jones couldn't make a single positive play after a pretty solid Week 1 outing. The final straw was when he was a penalty machine in the 49ers' loss to the Atlanta Falcons. The 49ers will no longer be subjected to his errant play.
It's not that Nick Bosa has been a bad performer this season. In fact, in the two games he's played, he's been good. However, it's because he's only played two games that he's been a "bad" performer.
Rather, he's been a massive disappointment, so he gets an asterisk in this list. Bosa cannot be relied upon when he returns because it's likely he will get hurt again. He's such a letdown.

title: 49ers TE George Kittle Teams Up With Novartis For Prostate Cancer Awareness
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle has teamed up with Novartis, the NFL's first-ever pharmaceutical partner, to raise awareness of prostate cancer and encourage men to take action through blood-test screening.
"My family connection to prostate cancer comes from my grandpa, my dad's dad. He had prostate cancer about eight to ten years ago and thankfully survived it. He has since passed away, but that was simply due to old age," shared Kittle in an interview with 49ers on SI .
"When he passed, I started talking to my dad more about my grandpa and his experience with prostate cancer. It was around the same time I started talking with Novartis about a potential partnership, so the two things went hand in hand. It was a strange connection at just the right time.
"I learned that one in eight men will test positive for prostate cancer, which I think are incredible odds. I had no idea that was the case."
Kittle's aim with this campaign is to encourage open conversations with friends and family about getting a blood test. Novartis states that "prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer death among men in the United States".
He wants to encourage people to be more open about the subject and help break down the stigma surrounding it, ultimately encouraging them to speak to a doctor if needed.
"To an extent, I think things are getting better [with more awareness]. More people are becoming aware and wanting to learn more," shared Kittle.
"But, like I said, I've never really had a conversation about it with my friendship group. We never talked about it until I started working with Novartis and brought it up. I asked my friends, 'Have you guys ever thought about this?' and they said no.
"I told them they should maybe have a conversation with their dads and bring it up with them. It's a pretty simple blood test.
"I think we're possibly getting past the taboo, but at the same time, you still have friends who say, 'I'm good. I don't need that. I don't need to talk about it.'
"It's like, 'Hey, man, I just want what's best for you. I want you to live a long life so we can go and play plenty of golf together.' So, if you need to get a blood test, just go and get one. It's pretty easy."
The campaign highlights the importance of early detection and encourages men to find out more at RelaxItsaBloodTest.com . Novartis states that "early detection leads to a greater than 99% relative 5-year survival rate."
Kittle followed up with some powerful words, highlighting the importance of awareness, early detection and supporting those affected by cancer: "We're all in this life together, and I'd much rather help as many people as I can than just focus on doing things on my own.
"If I can spread a little awareness and encourage a few guys who otherwise wouldn't get tested to go and have a blood test that might save their lives, then I think that's absolutely worth working with Novartis for.
"It's something that affects all of us, so we just want to spread awareness and keep people up to date with current developments and what's going on."

title: These Big Surprises are the Reason the 49ers are 6-1 at the Bye
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers don't have a game this week, as they're in the middle of a much-needed Bye . That makes it the perfect time to look at the four biggest surprises from their season so far. Let's dive in.
All offseason, fans portrayed the 49ers' offensive line as one of the worst units in the NFL. They were pounding the table for the team to sign or draft an offensive lineman to boost the position.
The 49ers didn't add anyone worth noting to the position, so it was believed that the offensive line would be putrid this season. The reality is that the offensive line was always fine.
Sure enough, they're proving that not only are they fine, but they're a stout unit. They didn't allow a single sack of Brock Purdy through the first four games of the season.
That had only happened four other times in the NFL since 1990. It was insane to see how great they were in pass protection, and it hasn't let up much.
Purdy has dropped back to pass 232 times and has only been sacked seven times and pressured 62 times. The 49ers' offensive line allows the lowest pressure rate (26.7%) in the NFL.
They have played a significant role in the 49ers' 6-1 start. Who could've foreseen that coming, especially after they were scrutinized in the past year.
Unlike the offensive line, which was undeserving of their criticism, the 49ers' safeties were absolutely valid for theirs. It was easily the worst position on the 49ers entering the 2026 season.
Ji'Ayir Brown was a known liability who was never getting any better. Malik Mustapha forgot how to tackle and take proper angles last season. Marques Sigle showed a lot of promise, but struggled in pass coverage.
Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris had his work cut out for him with this group. And boy, has he made a difference. All of the safeties have performed admirably well this season.
Brown isn't playing lights out, but he hasn't been anywhere close to the issue he was last season. Mustapha looks like a ferocious tiger out there. He's taken off.
And before Sigle got hurt, he was playing incredibly well-rounded. He took the proper next steps that were needed. The safeties look immaculate this year, and it's taken the 49ers' defense to another level.
It's uncommon for the 49ers to receive massive gains from their rookies. However, this year's draft class has been giving them amazing contributions.
Gracen Halton has been a stud, Jaden Dugger is extremely versatile, Romello Height is hitting his stride, and Kaelon Black adds a new dynamic to the offense.
Just imagine if De'Zhaun Stribling were healthy. The 49ers' rookies have been awesome this year and are playing a key role in the team's success so far.
It's not surprising to see Brock Purdy perform well. He's proven to be a really good player before, but this season, he's clearly taken it up a notch,
He looks way more comfortable this season than he has in any other. Part of that is thanks to his offensive line playing great, but even when the protection or play breaks down, he's cool as a cucumber.
Purdy has also been delivering a bunch of dimes this season, mostly to Mike Evans. His hot start has fueled MVP narratives, which is ridiculous considering it's early in the season for that topic.
In any case, Purdy has been sharp. He looks improved this year by playing within himself, and that has allowed the 49ers' offense to thrive.

title: The 49ers Would be Foolish not to Go All In for a Wide Receiver
full_text:
The 49ers are 6-1, they just added DeForest Buckner, and they’re sitting in their bye week. On paper, it’s a team ready to chase a championship. But the receiver room tells a different story, and the Nov. 10 trade deadline is the last chance to fix it.
The Falcons Game Was a Warning
San Francisco’s first loss of the year, 29-20 in Atlanta, came with only four active wide receivers. The offense gave the ball away four times, two of them Brock Purdy interceptions. A team with a healthy receiver room doesn’t play that way. That game showed what happens when the Niners lose even a little depth at the position.
Mike Evans has been everything the 49ers hoped for when they signed him. He has 27 catches for 420 yards and three touchdowns in six games, and Kyle Shanahan has talked openly about how much he trusts him. But he’s been dealing with injured ribs and Achilles tendinitis, which kept him out of the Falcons game. John Lynch said this week that the goal is to calm the Achilles down and that Evans is making progress.
Maybe he comes back strong for Week 9 against the Raiders. But Achilles problems have a way of lingering, and Evans is in his 13th season. Planning a title run around his health is risky.
Deebo Samuel was off to a great start in his return to San Francisco. In four games, he caught 16 of 20 targets for 206 yards and three touchdowns, and he added nine carries for 78 yards. Then he hurt his hamstring against the Seahawks and has been out since. Shanahan says he has a chance to return in Week 9, but “a chance” isn’t a plan.
De’Zhaun Stribling looked like a star in the preseason. The No. 33 pick put up seven catches in a single half against the Titans, and Purdy raved about him. Then he hurt his ankle in Week 1 and missed at least a month on injured reserve. He’s a rookie, and rookies are going to be inconsistent in December and January, especially in the playoffs. Stribling should be part of this team’s future, not the main reason it wins now.
The Seahawks are the defending champions, and their defense has owned this team lately. They beat the Niners 13-3 in Week 18 last season and then 41-6 in the divisional round. The Niners did win 32-29 in Seattle in Week 5, but it took two fourth-quarter scoring drives, and it cost Deebo his hamstring.
San Francisco will probably see Seattle again in the playoffs. Against a defense that good, the offense needs receivers who can win one-on-one and run every route. Being deep isn’t enough.
Garrett Wilson is the best fit I can think of. He’s 37-for-51 for 444 yards and three touchdowns on a bad Jets team, and he can win from any alignment. Evans is a big-bodied red zone threat, and Deebo is a gadget player who needs the ball in space. Wilson would be the true No. 1 who runs the full route tree, and Purdy would have a target he can trust on third down.
He’d also solve next year’s problem. Evans is 33 and Deebo has missed time again. Wilson is the long-term answer.
Wilson isn’t cheap. He’s reportedly making around $30 million a year, and the Jets will want a first-round pick. I’d give them one. My offer is a 2027 first-rounder plus a mid-round pick, something like a third. I wouldn’t include Stribling or any young starters. The Niners’ draft picks matter less than the title window they have right now.
This roster has elite players at several spots, a quarterback who’s playing well and a coaching staff that knows how to win. The one thing that can derail it is the receiver room. If Evans’s Achilles flares up in January or Deebo’s hamstring doesn’t hold, the Niners will be trying to beat Seattle with a rookie and a thin group behind him.
The deadline is Nov. 10. If the front office passes on a move like this, it’ll be a mistake.

title: Honest Assessment of the 49ers' Rookies at the Bye Week
full_text:
With the San Francisco 49ers sitting at the bye week, it is a good chance to look back at how the rookie class has done and what to expect from them after getting a chance to reset.
Stribling has been out since Week 1. While Kyle Shanahan did not name a specific date, he was always expected to miss at least 10 weeks, and Shanahan noted that closer to December is the expectation. The big question is what role he can step back into that late in the year.
Height is fifth amongst rookies in pass rush snaps. However, he is sixth in pressures and 10th in pass rush win rate, so he is playing a touch below expectations. Height had a career-high five pressures in Week 6, but followed that up with zero pressures the next week. He needs to string together a more consistent pass rush.
Black has 57 rushes for 233 yards. He averages 8.1 rushing attempts for 33 yards per game. He is averaging 4.1 yards per attempt, and his success rate is 58%. Last year, Brian Robinson averaged 4.3 yards per attempt with a 54% success rate. He averaged 5.4 attempts for 23.5 yards per game. Black has been a slight upgrade, which is all that the team asked for in his rookie year.
Halton is third amongst rookie interior rushers in pass-rush snaps. He is tied for second in pressures and second in pass-rush win rate. He is outshooting expectations. The only question is how much run-game presence he can bring.
Carver Willis has not played, but Connor Colby has struggled in the past few weeks. They might call on Willis to start after the bye.
Prysock made his defensive debut with two snaps in Week 7. After cutting Jack Jones, he is next in line to play the dime role.
Dugger is 27th amongst defensive rookies in snaps, ninth amongst linebackers. He is seventh among rookie linebackers in run stops. The only question is how much more they plan to put on his plate.
Cruz has mostly been inactive this year as it is a red-shirt season.
Thompson is a UDFA, but the rookie has 91 snaps and has excelled in the run game.

title: The 49ers Should Trade a First-Round Pick for a Proven Difference-Maker
full_text:
The 49ers traded a fourth-round pick for DeForest Buckner this week. That was a good first move.
It should not be the only major move the 49ers make before the trade deadline, as Matt Maiocco thinks it will be. Because it wasn't really a major move. It was a shrewd, cost-effective move for a player who's past his prime. Plus, he might not be on the team next season. He will be a free agent.
And the other contenders aren't done making big-time trades. The Bears just sent two first-round picks to the Titans for Jeffery Simmons, who might be the best defensive tackle in the NFL right now.
In addition, they've been linked to Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack, who probably will get dealt before the deadline. The Bears are all-in for 2026. They're mortgaging their future to win this season, something the 49ers haven't done yet. They're keeping their options open.
Meanwhile, the Seahawks and Vikings seem to be making trade offers for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, who singlehandedly could tip the balance of power in the NFC if he lands on one of those teams.
And then there's Maxx Crosby, who probably will get traded to a contender if the Raiders lose their next two games, which seems likely. Their opponents will be the Jets and the 49ers.
The 49ers can't just sit back and watch other teams trade for all the best players on the market. They have to be aggressive, too. Because this season is their best opportunity to win a Super Bowl with their current corps of players that happens to be the oldest corps among the legit contenders.
Sure, the 49ers were the best team in the NFL in September and October, but other teams are improving, and they're extremely banged up. Mike Evans has Achilles tendinitis. And if he tears that Achilles, the 49ers, as currently constructed, would be cooked.
Fortunately for the 49ers, they have their first-round picks for 2027 and 2028, and should be eager to trade them for the right player. Because the future doesn't matter. Those picks are expendable. The only thing that matters is winning the Super Bowl this season and not wasting another golden opportunity with an elite roster.
The 49ers aren't good at drafting in the first round anyway. In 10 years, the only first-round picks who have gotten second contracts from the 49ers are Nick Bosa and Brandon Aiyuk. The 49ers would have been better off had they traded all their first-round picks from the past decade for proven veterans.
But the 49ers haven't traded a first-round pick for a veteran since Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch joined the organization in 2017. That's the biggest difference between them and the Rams, who have a Super Bowl ring largely because they trade their first-round picks almost every year. They traded two first-round picks for Jalen Ramsey and won the Super Bowl shortly after.
Lynch should be on the phone right now with the Jets, offering two firsts and a fourth for wide receiver Garrett Wilson. Whatever it takes. Get it done.
And if the Jets simply refuse to trade him, the 49ers should call up the Raiders and trade two firsts for Maxx Crosby. He's not a wide receiver, but he still would fill a need and would be better than any pass rusher the 49ers would draft with one of those late first-round picks.
Get serious, 49ers. If you do nothing else and you don't win the Super Bowl, someone should get fired.

title: The Case for and Against the 49ers Going All-In on a Big Trade
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers made a big splash for DeForest Buckner , but they still have two weeks to go until the trade deadline. They also did not spend much in terms of draft capital on the trade, and while they took a chunk of salary, they are not tied to him beyond this year. So, they could still make another big move in the coming weeks.
Reports are that while the team is going to explore more moves, they might be similar to Keion White last year, and not quite like Christian McCaffrey. There is an argument to be made for both sides.
The 49ers' biggest need was defensive tackle. They were not getting Alfred Collins back this year, so they needed defensive tackle more than other positions. While they are injured at other spots, they are expected to get most of their players back.
Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are expected to be back by the bye week, and De’Zhaun Stribling will be back this season. Trading for a wide receiver would force one of them out of the picture or force the team to cut someone like Jordan Watkins.
That would be to add a receiver like Brian Thomas Jr . or Jerry Jeudy, who are both having bad seasons. A trade for Garrett Wilson would likely cost something similar to Jeffery Simmons, which seems like a lot.
At edge rusher, Nick Bosa is expected to be back soon, and Mykel Williams is a former top-15 pick. If they added a big-name edge rusher, the development of rookie Romello Height would be stalled.
The same would be said at left guard or cornerback. If Connor Colby struggles or Nate Hobbs fails to replace Jack Jones, the team would turn to Carver Willis and Ephesians Prysock. They would delay their progress with any big additions.
Adding depth gives them a chance to protect themselves if they come along slowly while also giving their youth chances to take steps.
Obviously, an all-in move that pushes these two to the sides has its benefits as well. Playoff experience is underrated, and adding a veteran who is either hungry for a ring or knows how to win one could be what the team needs.
Will they go over the top, will they make a small move, or will they stand pat?

title: The 49ers Might Not Make Another Big Move Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
After a 6-1 start, the San Francisco 49ers enter their Week 8 bye looking to bolster their roster for a playoff run with Super Bowl 61 aspirations.
The 49ers went all in, trading a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for two-time All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
Fans and media have speculated that the 49ers will continue this aggressiveness and attempt to trade for New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson or Los Angeles Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack; yes, these players are game changers, but the 49ers can find answers within.
The 49ers' biggest concern is at wide receiver after a fast offensive start to the season stalled in the last couple of weeks due to injuries at the position.
Last week against the Atlanta Falcons, the wide receiver struggles boiled over, and a 49ers wide receiver didn’t have a single catch until the second half. The Niners were without Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson.
On Tuesday, head coach Kyle Shanahan said the three wide receivers will have a chance to return after the bye week, making it unnecessary to trade for Wilson , especially with recent developments from receiver Jordan Watkins. The 49ers will also get back first-round pick De’Zhaun Stribling, who will return at the end of the season.
Wilson’s four-year, $130 million contract kicks in next season, affecting the 49ers' future salary cap. This move would be the opposite of the 49ers' move to get Buckner on a one-year rental; it would be a long-term investment.
The 49ers have also been in trade speculation around Mack. This move would improve the defensive front but would also stunt the development of an already crowded unit.
The 49ers' current edge rushers are Keion White, Mykel Williams, Romello Height, and Nick Bosa, who has dealt with an injury this season, but Shanahan said Tuesday he has a chance to be back after the bye week.
The only justifiable reason the 49ers should trade for Mack or any other edge rusher is if there is still concern about Bosa’s injuries.
Another position that hasn’t been mentioned in trade speculation but should be reviewed in the bye week is cornerback. In the last two games without Upton Stout, the 49ers allowed 257 passing yards, up from their season average of 224.
Stout is expected to be back after the bye week, but his absence revealed a glaring hole at cornerback.
Ashtyn Davis and Jack Jones, whom the 49ers released to make roster space for Buckner, replaced Stout, and both struggled.
If another 49ers starting cornerback gets injured again, they will be in a similar spot as the last couple of weeks. Right now, the backups are rookie Ephesians Prysock, Davis and Nate Hobbs, who is currently on injured reserve with no designation.

title: Cheap Alternatives to 49ers' Splashy Trade Targets
full_text:
While the San Francisco 49ers made a big swing for DeForest Buckner, it did not cost much draft capital. There are a few other big names that fans want the team to add over time before the trade deadline. However, there could also be some strong alternatives that could be had for a cost lower than Buckner. Who are the day-three trade values?
Dickerson is a three-time Pro Bowler; he is signed beyond this year, and he is still 28 years old. The Philadelphia Eagles traded Cam Jurgens for a second-round pick, and they probably view Dickerson in higher regard. The 49ers can give a massive pick for a player with injury concerns, or they can send a day-three pick or a pick swap for Bredeson.
Bredeson is also 28; he has 60 career starts, and he is also signed through 2027. This is a strong alternative.
Thomas has a 1,282-yard season under his belt, and he is still 24 years old. Still, he is averaging less than a yard per route this year and is going to cost a second-round pick .
Johnston does not have the same ceiling, but he has back-to-back 700-yard seasons. He is averaging 1.07 yards per route run, so a slight step above Thomas this year. The Chargers are 0-6, and Johnston is set to hit free agency this year. A former first-round pick could cost a sixth-round pick for the 49ers. The 49ers can see how good of a fit he is and either let him walk or look to extend him. At the trade cost, it is worth exploring.
Mack is the name that 49ers fans want the most. Still, a lot of teams want Mack, and the bidding war for an aging rental might get out of hand. Armstrong is also in the last year of his deal on a 1-4-1 Commanders team.
He is six years younger than Mack and had 5.5 sacks last year, the same number as Mack. Armstrong has 34 sacks in his nine-year NFL career and is a good run defender. The 49ers need depth behind Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams. The addition of Armstrong fills the role at a better draft cost.

title: Buccaneers Have One Distinct Advantage Over Falcons
full_text:
Zac Robinson spent two seasons as the offensive coordinator for the Atlanta Falcons. Since joining the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the offseason, it's taken some time for Robinson to fully understand the new tools he has to work with in Tampa Bay.
Although Robinson's tenure didn't get off to the roaring start he imagined as the 2026 season has gone on, we've begun to see glimpses of what he's capable of when it comes to running an efficient offense that plays to the strengths of the roster.
In the Buccaneers' two victories this season against the Cowboys (24-16) and Panthers (43-13), Robinson did a tremendous job of sticking with what worked.
The fact that he managed to scheme up a plan of attack in Dallas with UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels as his starting quarterback proves he has the flexibility to alter his approach depending on who he has available on a given day. The same could be said for how he attacked the Panthers' defense with Mayfield still recovering from a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.
Although the 43-point outburst against the Panthers last weekend was impressive, nine of those came directly from the defense or special teams. Still, Robinson's group was responsible for 34 of those points, and they managed to do it with just 64 yards passing.
The Bucs' run-first approach in this game established dominance at the line of scrimmage while featuring all three running backs — Bucky Irving, Kenneth Gainwell, and Sean Tucker — in different roles. With 258 rushing yards total, it's safe to say that Robinson was wise to stick with the run. This approach also helped to take some stress off Mayfield, who was surely battling through plenty of discomfort.
After the Panthers lost to the Packers on Thursday night, the Bucs have a golden opportunity to make up ground on the two teams ahead of them in the standings when they face off with the Falcons this Sunday at Raymond James Stadium.
Not only is the Buccaneers' defense absolutely humming coming into this game, but the team finally has a bit of momentum following their domination in Carolina last week. The Falcons have a ton of weapons, especially on offense, but the Buccaneers will have one key advantage heading into this matchup — familiarity.
Robinson knows each of the Falcons' best offensive players, RB Bijan Robinson, QB Michael Penix, WR Drake London and TE Kyle Pitts extremely well. He knows their strengths, weaknesses (aside from Bijan, who seemingly has none), tendencies and preferences. That means he also knows what looks give them the most trouble.
This could be hugely advantageous to the Buccaneers, as it would be wise for Todd Bowles to include Robinson in plenty of defensive meetings this week to ensure that the Bucs' defensive game plan is tailored specifically for the opponent they are facing.
Thanks to Zac Robinson's time in Atlanta, the Falcons are an opponent they should know inside and out. And in the NFL, you better capitalize on every advantage you have.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Tampa Bay on Nov. 1.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Falcons Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a must-win game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season.
It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta:
Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons.
The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air.
The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again.
While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball.
That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week.
Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it.
The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense.
Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers.
I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year.
Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice.
It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing.
Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air.
I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James.
This is among the closest prediction slates we've had all year. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Tampa Bay on Nov. 1.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Good News and Bad News Before Falcons Game
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play a crucial game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.
With a Carolina Panthers loss on Thursday night against the Green Bay Packers, the Bucs remain just 1.5 games out of the division lead. If Tampa Bay wins on Sunday against the Falcons, they'll be within half a game of the NFC South crown.
The Bucs lost their game at home to the Falcons last year during the infamous "3rd & 28" scenario, but they beat the Falcons on the road to begin that season. They had a lot of help from their rookie wide receiver that year, but one year later, that wideout won't be available for Tampa Bay during this matchup.
Todd Bowles confirmed that wide receiver Emeka Egbuka will be out for Sunday.
Egbuka was a big contributor in Tampa Bay's win against the Falcons last year, but he won't be playing in this game. Egbuka suffered a concussion against the Pittsburgh Steelers and appeared to clear protocol on Thursday, shedding a black non-contact jersey for his regular one, but he wasn't participating at all on Friday.
Egbuka has also been dealing with a foot injury on top of his concussion. Bowles said Friday that Egbuka cleared concussion protocol, but that his foot is still injured.
Tackle Luke Goedeke, meanwhile, was out last week against the Carolina Panthers with a calf injury and he did not participate in the first two days of practice. He did participate in this last day of practice this week, and Bowles said that he has a chance to play on Sunday, which is very encouraging for the Bucs — Goedeke has been an excellent right tackle this season.
If Goedeke can't go, though, Ben Chukwuma will fill in for him instead. Chukwuma filled in for Goedeke against the Panthers last week, and he played well — Bowles praised his effort the following Monday. He'd be up again to replace Goedeke, and if Goedeke cannot go, the team would certainly feel good about his abilities heading into Sunday.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium Nov. 1. They won't have their star wideout, but they could have one of their best offensive linemen.

title: Bucs Finally Have a Huge Advantage Against Falcons Nobody is Talking About
full_text:
Tampa Bay has always been a hot spot for transplants from up north. With that, those people have brought their fandom for other teams to the community that boasts three professional sports teams of their own.
That has been obvious for years whenever you tune into Tampa Bay Buccaneers home games.
While plenty of Bucs fans make up the crowd, over the years, there has consistently been a large contingent of opposing fans in the stands.
It's becoming an issue that has brought frustration amongst Tampa Bay fans, and that couldn't have been clearer than when the Pittsburgh Steelers fans practically took over Raymond James Stadium.
However, in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons, the Bucs will likely have an advantage in the stands.
Despite Atlanta being relatively close to Tampa compared to numerous other organizations, their fanbase is not known to travel well, and those Atlanta natives don't make up a large portion of those who have moved to the area or visit during the cooler months of the year.
It should align with the Bucs having their most fans in the stadium this season. That is big for a team that can live and die by momentum.
Fans and crowd noise can carry a team to victory, and the Buccaneers will be hopeful that their fans bring it on Sunday as they search to start 2-0 in the division and continue their midseason turnaround.
It's the most important game up to this point in the season. With the Panthers losing to the Packers on Thursday night, the Bucs could find themselves right at the top of the division if they beat the Falcons on Sunday.
With a win, the Bucs, Falcons, and Panthers would all have three wins on the season, but the Bucs would be 2-0 in the division. There is nothing quite like the NFC South.
There is a ton on the line this week, so the fans must bring the atmosphere to help the players on the field continue their recent surge of great play at every level.

title: Buccaneers Have a Major Problem Nobody Expected This Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' passing offense is averaging 150.4 yards per game. That is the worst in the entire NFL and is certainly not what fans and the organization had in mind this season when thinking about the offense.
There are a lot of factors as to why this aspect of the game has been so disappointing. Baker Mayfield missed three games due to a dislocated thumb, you had undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels filling in and the offensive line has struggled to keep either quarterback upright to make plays.
However, there are too many good players in this offense for the passing attack to be this poor. Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr., Ted Hurst III, Tez Johnson and Cade Otton have simply not been getting the football enough, and that is both on the quarterbacks and offensive coordinator Zach Robinson.
One thing the Bucs have been doing well under Zac Robinson is running the football. The team is coming off one of the best team rushing performances in franchise history, and head coach Todd Bowles even went so far as to say the run game is their calling card.
"I mean, I think that's our calling card. We play a lot better when we run the ball very successfully, whether we're home or on the road," Bowles said. "We haven't had much success at home, running the football or winning at home, but we've got to turn that around and win a home game."
Robinson has also said that this offense needs to be established through the run game.
"Yeah, if we can do that every week, that would be outstanding," Robinson said. "You always want to be able to establish a run and be able to have things that play off of the run game. Then, there [are] going to be weeks where, shoot, you might not have as many run opportunities and you're going to get back on track. That's the nature of the NFL — everything is week to week. If we can play like that, it'll definitely help us out in the long run."
Time will tell if we do see legitimate improvement in the passing game going forward. But it seems like right now the team is content to be a run-first offense and take shots in the passing attack when they can.
